title: Berufsfortbildungswerk des DGB: David M., Betriebsrat und ver.di-Listenführer in Leipzig wehrt sich gegen seine fristlose Kündigung
content:
„…

Das ist der wunde Punkt – und der Grund, warum ich meinen Fall politisiere. Aufsichtsratsvorsitzender ist der DGB-Vize Stefan Körzell. Der DGB fordert starke Betriebsräte und gute Arbeit. Das muss dann auch im eigenen Unternehmen gelten. Es gibt im bfw durchaus Geschäftsbereiche, in denen die Zusammenarbeit besser funktioniert. Aber bei uns im Osten gab es erhebliche Konflikte. Wenn Beschäftigte erleben, dass kritische Interessenvertretung so zum Risiko wird, braucht sich niemand über ihr Misstrauen wundern. Dazu kommt der Druck in der gesamten Weiterbildungsbranche. Die Träger hangeln sich von Ausschreibung zu Ausschreibung. Der Preiswettbewerb wird auf dem Rücken der Beschäftigten ausgetragen (…) Mein Ziel ist die Wiedereinstellung, ganz klar. Ich möchte eine starke Interessenvertretung sein und auch diesen Job weitermachen

…“ Aus dem

Interview von Niki Uhlmann in der jungen Welt vom 26.10.2026


 („Betriebsrat gefeuert: »Mein Ziel ist die Wiedereinstellung«“) – siehe mehr daraus und dazu:


Kein Vergleich, keine Rücknahme. Leipzig: DGB-Berufsfortbildungswerk lehnt vor Gericht Einigungsvorschlag des fristlos gekündigten Betriebsrats David M. ab 


„

Es gibt keine Einigung zwischen David M. und seinem ehemaligen »Arbeitgeber«, dem Berufsfortbildungswerk (BFW) – einer gemeinnützigen GmbH des Deutschen Gewerkschaftsbundes. Beim Gütetermin am Arbeitsgericht Leipzig trugen am Dienstag beide Seiten ihre Standpunkte zur fristlosen Kündigung von David M. vor. Dieser hatte nach seiner Entlassung am 15. September eine Kündigungsschutzklage eingereicht.


Rund 15 Unterstützer aus dem Umfeld des Gekündigten zeigten sich solidarisch und begleiteten ihn und seinen Anwalt Lukas Münch zum Gütetermin. Nicht alle erhielten einen Sitzplatz im Gerichtssaal. Diejenigen, die nicht sitzen konnten, wurden von der Richterin angehalten, draußen zu warten. M. arbeitete seit 2022 bis zu seiner Kündigung im September als Sozialarbeiter in der Resozialisierung von Strafgefangenen und engagierte sich als Betriebsrat und Gewerkschafter in der Verdi-Tarifkommission. (…)


Ralf Krawetzke, Leiter des Personalmanagements des BFW, begründete vor dem Arbeitsgericht die Entlassung: Laut Auffassung des BFW sei die fristlose Kündigung dadurch gerechtfertigt, dass David M. Spesenbetrug begangen habe und anschließend versucht haben soll, diesen zu verschleiern, indem er eine Kollegin gebeten haben soll, für ihn in der Angelegenheit zu lügen. Krawetzke zufolge habe der Betriebsrat der Kündigung zugestimmt; zudem sei von einem »Vertrauensverlust« gegenüber David M. die Rede gewesen.


Lukas Münch, Anwalt von David M., entgegnet den Vorwürfen des BFW, dass »fiktive Abrechnungen« von Bahnfahrkarten im Unternehmen seit Jahren bekannt und geduldet worden seien, unter anderem, um die Prozesse in der Buchhaltung zu vereinfachen. Der Verteidigung von M. lägen dafür mehrere E-Mails als Belege vor. Den Schritt der fristlosen Kündigung als »Ultima Ratio« empfinde Münch daher als unverhältnismäßig, auch vor dem Hintergrund, dass es seit Beginn des Arbeitsverhältnisses keine Abmahnungen gegen David M. gegeben habe.


Auf die Frage der Richterin, ob die Parteien zu einer Einigung bereit wären, erklärte Münch, dass er und sein Mandant forderten, die außerordentliche Kündigung zurückzunehmen. Statt dessen seien sie bereit, eine Abmahnung ohne Schuldgeständnis zu akzeptieren. Ralf Krawetzke machte dagegen in knappen Worten deutlich, dass weder die Forderung von David M. und seinem Anwalt noch eine andere Form der Einigung für das BFW in Frage komme. Da es wegen der starken Differenzen zwischen David M. und seinem ehemaligen »Arbeitgeber« nicht zu einer Einigung kam, setzte die Richterin einen Verhandlungstermin für den 23. April 2027 an

…“

Artikel von Amelie E. Höcker, Leipzig, in der jungen Welt vom 28.10.2026

 


Betriebsrat gefeuert: »Mein Ziel ist die Wiedereinstellung«


„

Berufsfortbildungswerk des DGB: Ein Betriebsrat wehrt sich gegen seine Kündigung. [Sie sind dieses Jahr in den Betriebsrat des Berufsfortbildungswerks des DGB, bfw, gewählt und wenig später gekündigt worden. Warum?]


Im Kündigungsschreiben steht keine Begründung. Zu den Vorwürfen äußere ich mich vor dem Prozess nicht öffentlich. Aber das Vorgehen spricht für sich: Die Kündigung kam am zweiten Tag meines Jahresurlaubs. Dass ich vier Wochen lang in China und schlecht erreichbar sein würde, war lange bekannt. Da ich den Braten schon gerochen hatte, habe ich rechtzeitig Rechtsschutz …

author: Nadeine Asbali
title: I’m a Teacher. The Bell Antisemitism Report Will Silence My Pro-Palestine Pupils
content:
If you’ve seen the news in the past week or so, you’d be forgiven for believing that antisemitism is the single most pressing issue facing British education today. All schools in England have been told they must consider antisemitism a distinct form of harm after recommendations from

a review

 by former Ofsted chief Sir David Bell were

accepted by the government

last week. 


As a secondary school teacher of ten years, I can’t help but feel like we aren’t being told the full story here. Bell is hardly an impartial figure, given his membership of a pro-Israel, anti-BDS

academic charity

 and the

anti-Muslim comments

 he made during his tenure as Ofsted head. Then there’s the report’s widely-shared finding that “almost three in five” Jewish pupils have experienced antisemitism at school. This would be a sobering statistic about any minority group, but it

just doesn’t stand up to scrutiny

. The report even admits that the “low sample size of 92 students who identify as Jewish should be treated with caution”.


The Bell review uses the controversial

International Holocaust Remembrance Alliance (IHRA)

definition of antisemitism – which states that calling the state of Israel a racist endeavour or comparing Israel’s actions to that of the Nazis constitutes anti-Jewish hate – and calls on schools to adopt it. In other words, anti-Zionism equals antisemitism. A

2025 survey

 found that 45% of British adults agreed with the statement “Israel treats the Palestinians like the Nazis treated the Jews”, so by this definition, almost half the British population are raging antisemites. Amongst young people, the figure was as high as 60%. 


Now, I teach in a very Muslim borough of east London and my pupils are, to put it mildly, extremely passionate about the Palestinian cause. They attend rallies with their parents on the weekend, wear pin badges on their backpacks and have watched a campaign of genocide against children like themselves livestreamed through their phones for the past three years. 


I have never witnessed any genuinely anti-Jewish statements, and I’m not alone in that experience amongst colleagues. Schools are not the cesspits of antisemitic hate that the media and government would have us believe, and young people are far more capable of nuanced debate than they are given credit for. But none of that seems to matter, because under the IHRA definition, criticism of Israel or rejection of Zionism is enough to constitute antisemitism – and therein lies the problem. Is this about supporting Jewish children or is it about silencing support for Palestine altogether?


The most troubling thing about the Bell review is that it masquerades as concern for Jewish pupils and teachers whilst actually functioning as a continuation of the government’s

ongoing clampdown

 on pro-Palestine expression in all areas of public life. The

report seems more concerned with banning Palestine badges and ensuring teachers are ‘politically impartial’ when it comes to the state of Israel than it does about what sort of support should be extended to victims of anti-Jewish discrimination. 


The idea that teachers should be trained specifically on antisemitism, as a form of hate entirely distinct from all other types of bigotry, speaks to a hierarchy of discrimination in the UK. Some forms of prejudice are embedded in the very system itself – consider the Prevent duty placed upon all teachers that

disproportionately impacts Muslim children

 – while others get immediate government attention and resourcing. 


My fear is that the Bell recommendations will pressure schools into cracking down on pro-Palestine expression at the cost of tackling genuine racism – and that’s before you consider the impact on underpaid and overstretched teachers having yet another priority to add to their overflowing lists when there are still young people to support and lessons to teach. 


Free speech and equality for all will likely go out the window in favour of blanket bans on all discussions of Palestine in the classroom – and undoubtedly this will have a disproportionate impact on Muslim pupils and staff. Given that Prevent referrals for wearing pro-Palestine items have

risen in recent years

, those already facing heightened suspicion and even criminalisation are likely to be further targeted.


It feels particularly sinister that this move to essentially outlaw criticism of Israel and solidarity with Palestinians – from condemning the Israeli …

author: CNT Santander
title: Accidente ferroviario en Toledo
content:
En plena actividad de las diferentes tareas de la Huelga General, nos sorprende la noticia del accidente ferroviario ocurrido en Ursa, Toledo, dejándonos el corazón totalmente devastado.


Con los sucesos de Adamuz latentes en la memoria, vemos como un nuevo accidente ferroviario se cobra vidas de personas anónimas que iban a trabajar . Son alrededor de 50 personas fallecidas y 179 heridas, pero todo está muy reciente, por lo que no se sabe aún con seguridad las verdaderas consecuencias de este accidente ferroviario. El suceso involucra a un tren de alta velocidad de RENFE que ha embestido a un tren Iryo que estaba detenido, obstaculizando la vía, provocando que varios vagones de ambos trenes descarrilaran terraplén abajo. Son 540 personas, aproximadamente, quienes iban en ambos trenes.


Seguiremos atentas a las noticias para saber qué ha ocurrido realmente e instaremos a que se depuren responsabilidades en esta tragedia en el momento pertinente, y a que se pongan todas las herramientas posibles para que la seguridad ferroviaria sea una prioridad para las empresas mencionadas.


Ahora es momento, únicamente, de lamentar las personas fallecidas, de apoyar a las personas heridas y a todas sus familias en este duro proceso.


Recordamos el teléfono de atención para consultas relacionadas con las personas que acudían en el tren: 900 10 10 20, no para cualquier consulta.


Desde CNT Santander enviamos todo nuestro afecto y apoyo en estos duros momentos.

title: The Psychiatric Drug Epidemic Livestream – Mad in Brasil
content:
Mad in Brasil presents the tenth edition of its annual international seminar, The Psychiatric Drug Epidemic. It will take place on October 28, 29, and 30 in Rio de Janeiro, Brazil, and will be livestreamed in English and Spanish.


On October 29 and 30, they will be joined by Birgit Valla from Mad in Norway, Monique de Mol from Mad in the Netherlands, Josef Witt-Doerring from the U.S. and Robert Whitaker from Mad in America, as well as guests from various parts of Brazil for our panel discussions.


October 29, morning session, starts 8 AM EDT


10:00 – 12:00 – PANEL: CONTEMPORARY INITIATIVES IN DEMEDICALIZATION AROUND THE WORLD


Robert Whitaker (Mad in America) – Contemporary Initiatives for Demedicalization Around the World (Opening Lecture)


Moderator: Paulo Amarante (LAPS/ENSP – CEE/Fiocruz)


October 29, afternoon session, starts 11:30 PM EDT


1:30 PM – 2:30 PM PANEL: A BEGINNER’S GUIDE TO WITHDRAWAL FROM PSYCHIATRIC MEDICATIONS


Josef Witt-Doerring (former FDA, TaperClinic – USA)


Moderator: Robert Whitaker (Mad in America)

Mussolini continues to tower above and parliament crawls at his feet more than ever.

Full powers have been granted with the care of servants who compete with each other in degradation. Mussolini had said, “give them to me or I’ll take them”, and no one had the dignity to answer, take them from us, but don’t force us to play the part in a comedy of the bosses, when we are servants and are pleased to be so.

The socialists themselves have not understood that they cannot remain with dignity in an assembly that functions under the terror of the baton, or of dissolution, and where opposition can only be a farce.

Dictatorship triumphs: a dictatorship of adventurers without scruples or ideals, which came to power and remains there due to the disorientation of the proletarian masses and the anxious avarice of the bourgeois class in search of a saviour. But everyone feels that the situation is such that it cannot last, and the most enlightened conservatives, while paying due homage to the masters of the hour and revealing with every word the fear that dominates them, demand the restoration of the “liberal state”, that is, a return to constitutional deception.

The method by which Mussolini came to power does not allow deception, and this is what torments the innocent souls of the conservatives.

Mussolini, if he manages to consolidate his power, will do no more and no less than any other minister would: he will serve the interests of the privileged class, and will charge for his services. But he won’t make anyone believe that he arrived in government by the will of the people. His tyranny is too recent for him to be able to hide its origin: perhaps for this reason his murky conscience advises him to appeal to God!

We do not want to deal with the new government’s plans and intentions, whether new or old, sincere or otherwise. It’s always the same habitual rehashing of old lies, the old attempt to repair a collapsing house with a coat of paint.

For us, the only important change is this: we were enemies of government because government is no more than the armed defender of all social injustices, the creator of new injustices, the enemy of freedom, the material obstacle along the path of civilization. And we were enemies of fascism because it is a movement intended to defend bourgeois privileges, to impede the ascent of the proletariat, to choke out any aspiration towards a society more just and free; and it used brutal, ferocious and vile means to achieve its goals.

Now government and fascism have become the same thing, and are made up of the same personnel: there is therefore no longer the possibility of hesitation as there was when those two forces of oppression seemed to oppose each other.

Simplified situation: so much the better. So much the better if this can serve to reunite all the forces of progress in the struggle against triumphant barbarism.

author: Kari Thompson
title: The First-Ever California State Workers’ Strike
content:
State workers went on a one-day unfair labor practice strike across California October 21, with picket lines in Sacramento, San Francisco, Los Angeles, and other cities. They're demanding better pay, affordable health care coverage, and flexibility to work from home.


This was the first strike in the history of SEIU Local 1000, which represents about 100,000 government employees, ranging from accountants to custodians to nurses at state offices, hospitals, and prisons.


They have been working without a contract since July 1. Some 5,000 employees were

excluded

 from striking.


Governor Gavin Newsom’s “return-to-office” mandate went into effect this past summer. It requires workers to be in the office four days per week—even though workers report there isn’t enough space for all of them.


Workers argue the return-to-work policy compounds the lack of pay increases. Being forced back into the office is “more than just a pay cut,” said Jonah Paul, who works for the Employment Development Department in Sacramento. ”It’s a huge reduction in quality of life.


“Telework is a stopgap for a lot of problems our society is not willing to address,” Paul said: “the cost of childcare, and insane commutes. Telework becomes a catch-all solution for a grueling life.”


ZERO RAISE


Last year, Local 1000 agreed to a pay freeze to help the state meet a budget shortfall. This summer, however, workers were supposed to see raises. But they got zilch.


The union is asking for a 20 percent raise over three years to catch up, especially given increased state revenue over the past two years.


Though Local 1000 and the state have met several times to negotiate a new contract, the union says CalHR, the bargaining representative for the state, has not been negotiating in good faith. It filed unfair labor practice charges with the state Public Employment Relations Board against CalHR for delaying negotiations and failing to respond to proposals.


“When I first started working for the state 10 years ago, for the most part CalHR would throw us a bone,” said steward Giovanni Martinez, a state worker in Sacramento. “This is the worst bargaining cycle I’ve witnessed. They don’t want to budge on a lot of stuff. Newsom takes us for granted, and the people he’s appointed in CalHR are the same way.”


Under previous leadership, the union

kicked in $1 million

 to help Newsom fight a recall campaign in 2021. Members question why a governor they supported doesn’t have their backs now.


STRIKE SCHOOLS


Members of Local 1000 have been organizing over the past few months to increase membership numbers. Activists have been approaching nonmembers at their own worksites to ask them personally to join the union, and calling others on the phone.


Stewards did their best to increase communications across the membership, though they were hampered by limited updates from the official Bargaining Unit Negotiating Committee.


Paul said that three years ago, the local offered “strike schools” to members, but these were more about discouraging members from planning for a strike. This time, he said, strike schools emphasized that the decision to strike was one for members to make, building membership numbers along with enthusiasm for walking out together.


In a strike authorization vote held from September 9 to October 7, 96 percent voted “yes” to walk out.


On the final day of the vote, the union held informational pickets to encourage participation in the vote. One picket happened to be next door to a building where Newsom was giving a speech.


With just a half-hour’s notice, stewards and other union leaders managed to get members together to cover every entrance of the building and make enough noise that Newsom had to comment on it during his event.


Despite this pressure from members, there was no last-minute deal to avert the strike, as happened 10 years ago under Governor Jerry Brown.


“For a lot of folks this is their first strike—this is mine,” Martinez said. ”We didn’t want to walk off the job—we have a good relationship with our supervisors—but we had no choice.”


WORLD’S FOURTH-LARGEST ECONOMY


Strike participation appeared strong, with thousands of workers joining rallies and marches in cities across the state. Striking workers in the state’s capitol shut down multiple blocks with a march from CalHR headquarters to the capitol building.

author: Marx-lover
title: The Cornell Case and the Left's Betrayal of Itself
content:
Here's an article about the feminist reaction to the "Cornell 7" case that has been in the news recently (October 2026). A version of it was published in "Compact." (The hyperlinks have been deleted, unfortunately.) The general point is that contemporary feminism has become an albatross for the left, and is also contributing to destructive social and cultural trends.

In the 1960s, feminists demanded that women and men have legal equality, that women be treated as mature adults who are free to make their own choices be it with regard to sex or their careers, that patriarchal paternalism be dismantled. In the 2020s, feminists demand that women be constantly protected against men, that patriarchal paternalism be resurrected, that women be legally treated as not responsible for decisions they’ve made because, in certain contexts, only men have agency. And men, they argue, are inveterate misogynists, abusers, and rapists, so the agency they manifest is almost invariably malign.

The reaction to the “Cornell 7” case is the latest example. A remarkable wave of hysteria has swept liberal and left culture, from mass media and social media to university campuses. Misandry is drenching the discourse; mobs are going after anyone who questions the dominant narrative; the guilt of the accused is automatically assumed, because the accused are men and men are by definition guilty. Is it any wonder that millions of men in recent years have turned away from the left—which seems to hate them—and fallen into the clutches of the far-right and the “manosphere”?

Consider what has transpired. Far from condemning the wildly irresponsible comments of public figures like Governor Hochul and Attorney General Letitia James, which treat as established fact accusations made in a civil lawsuit, leftists themselves, including Alexandria Ocasio-Cortez and Zohran Mamdani, have talked as though the case has already been decided. This is despite the highly ambiguous evidence that has been presented, much of which tends to exonerate the alleged perpetrators of the “gang-rape.” Not only is presumption of innocence thrown out the window; it is obvious that even if the accused end up being found innocent, most liberals and leftists will remain sure of their guilt.

Lynch mobs have been out for blood. A few weeks ago, it was easy to find thousands of people “liking” public demands to kill the accused. Even innocent bystanders were victimized. The campaign of overwhelming harassment to which the journalist Michael Tracey has been subjected for questioning the “guilty until proven innocent” narrative led to his father receiving “thousands of nonstop crazed texts/calls/voicemails” threatening him with brutal violence. The current owners of Tracey’s childhood home were “inundated” with “crazed threats,” and received suspicious packages at their house. Friends and family of the accused men were harassed by thousands. So was the family of an innocent man who happens to have the same name as one of the accused.

Since liberals and leftists are refusing to stand up for decency and the rule of law, it is left to conservatives to do so—which enables them to claim the moral high ground against “lunatic” leftists and thereby score political points. It turns out that many conservatives take women more seriously as (potentially) responsible adults and moral agents than most leftists do.

Feminist moral panics may seem well-intentioned in that they’re allegedly motivated by concern for the safety of women, but these episodes illustrate the extent to which the (so-called) “left” has been corrupted and co-opted by neoliberal dynamics, particularly in the era of social media. The atomized, polarized, siloed, anti-intellectual, narcissistic soundbite culture of social media—itself a reflection of capitalist tendencies—has helped produce a liberal-left that dehumanizes others, reflexively assumes the worst of men, exploits controversies for social media clout, and contributes to the very social breakdown that leftists rightly attack neoliberalism for engendering. After all, a feminism that teaches women to hate and fear men, and to view themselves as being on a higher moral plane, doesn’t exactly promote healthy relationships. It exacerbates gender wars and culture wars, thus, again, gifting the right wing with talking points and grievances to rally around.

author: Wajd
title: CPJ outraged by Egypt court conviction of journalist Lina Attalah, order of Mada Masr’s closure
content:
The Committee to Protect Journalists condemns the conviction of Lina Attalah, editor-in-chief of the independent Egyptian news outlet Mada Masr, on charges of running an unlicensed website, and calls on Egyptian authorities to reverse the ruling, release the journalist immediately, and end their escalating campaign against independent journalism.

Mada Masr, among the first and few of Egypt’s independent media outlets, and a vital source of critical reporting, has long faced pressure from Egyptian authorities over its journalism. The outlet reported on Tuesday that the New Cairo Misdemeanor Court fined Attalah 3 million Egyptian pounds (about US$54,000), ordered the closure of the outlet, and the confiscation of its equipment. Attalah was subsequently taken into custody, and two Egyptian lawyers confirmed to CPJ that she will remain in custody until the fine is paid.

“The conviction of Lina Attalah and the order to shut down Mada Masr represent a devastating blow to press freedom in Egypt and a direct message aimed at dismantling independent media in the country,” said CPJ Regional Director Sara Qudah. “Attalah and Mada Masr are among the most prominent voices in Egypt’s independent media landscape, providing critical reporting on issues of public interest that might otherwise go unreported. If Egypt can put in custody one of its most respected editors and shut down her newsroom, no independent journalist in the country is safe. Attalah must be released immediately, and Mada Masr must be allowed to keep reporting.”

According to reports from the hearing, journalists were not allowed to stay in the courtroom during critical stages of the proceedings. The defense was reportedly prevented from presenting key procedural requests, including requests to submit documents and hear witnesses. Attalah’s objection to the appointment of a lawyer she had not chosen was reportedly disregarded, before the court announced its verdict amid protests from her legal team. Such reported restrictions raise serious concerns about transparency, due process, and the right to a fair hearing.

“This was a farcical and highly exceptional trial that lacked the most basic rules of a fair trial and squandered Lina’s legal rights and those of her defense team,” Lobna Darwish, advocacy director at the Egyptian Initiative for Personal Rights, whose lawyers are part of Attalah’s defense team, told CPJ.

Mada Masr had repeatedly sought an operating license from Egyptian authorities, with applications rejected or left unanswered. Prosecuting its editor over this unresolved licensing process risks turning administrative regulation into a mechanism for suppressing independent media.

The ruling also comes amid a wider crackdown on Egyptian journalism, including the arrests of six journalists from investigative platform Matsadaash. The cumulative effect is to intimidate reporters, restrict public-interest investigations, and further erode the space for independent reporting.

In CPJ’s 2025 Annual Prison Census, Egypt was listed among the top jailers of journalists globally, with 18 journalists behind bars, and with continued retaliatory arrests of journalists and their family members. As of late October, 25 journalists are behind bars, the highest number since 2021.

The Egyptian Public Prosecutor’s Office did not respond to CPJ’s email seeking clarification on the legal basis for Attalah’s detention, the court’s rejection of defense requests to submit documents and call witnesses, and the exclusion of a Journalists Syndicate representative from the hearing.

title: Silivri açıklarında bulunan cansız bedenin batan geminin 2'nci kaptanına ait olduğu belirlendi
content:
İstanbul – Silivri açıklarında Alsu isimli gemiyle çarpıştıktan sonra batan Tuğberk İmamoğlu isimli gemide bulunan 9 mürettebatı arama çalışmaları sırasında dün bulunan cansız bedenin geminin 2'nci kaptanı Rahmi Temel’e ait olduğu belirlendi. Cenazesi ailesi tarafından Adli Tıp Kurumu'ndan alınan Temel'in 31 Ekim'de İzmir'de toprağa verileceği öğrenildi.

Silivri açıklarında 2 Eylül'de Alsu isimli gemiyle çarpıştıktan sonra batan Tuğberk İmamoğlu isimli gemide bulunan 9 mürettebatı arama çalışmaları sürüyor. Çalışmalar sırasında suda, kimliği henüz belirlenemeyen erkek cesedi bulundu. Ceset, kesin ölüm nedeni ve kimliğinin belirlenmesi için Adli Tıp Kurumu'na götürüldü.

Cansız beden geminin 2'nci kaptanına ait çıktı

Adli Tıp Kurumu'nda yapılan incelemelerde, suda bulunan cesedin Tuğberk İmamoğlu isimli geminin 2'nci kaptanı Rahmi Temel'e ait olduğu belirlendi. Cenazesi ailesi tarafından Adli Tıp Kurumu'ndan alınan Temel'in 31 Ekim'de İzmir Karşıyaka’da Hacı Mustafa Beşikçioğlu Camii’nde öğle saati kılınacak namazın ardından toprağa verileceği öğrenildi.

Rahmi Temel’in abisi Remzi Temel, "Çok elim bir deniz kazası sonucu 10 denizcimiz Marmara’da sulara gömüldü. Bugün 57’nci günde bir naaş çıkarıldı. Bugün çıkarılan ikinci naaş benim kardeşimin. Diğer 8 kişi aranıyor. Aileler çadırlarda bekliyor. Zor şartlarda, ümitsizce, çaresizce bekliyorlar. Herkes bir yakınına ulaşmak için canla başla bütün duruma katlanıyor, bütün güçlükler ve zorluklar içinde bekliyorlar. Bizim için sevindirici olmadı, üzücü oldu. Ben bugün haberi aldıktan sonra başımdan aşağı kaynar su dökülmüş gibi oldu. Ama en azından bir naaşa kavuşmanın da bir rahatlığı olacak, bir mezarımız olacak. Onun için buradayız, cenazemizin verilmesini bekliyoruz. Dün gemide bulunduğunu söylediler. Biz akşam haber aldık. Kimlik tespiti bugün yapılıp haber verildi. 1 gün sonrada kimliğini öğrendik. Silivri açıklarında 35 kilometre uzağında bu olay olmuş. Marmara çukuru denilen derin bir yerde. Diğer kazazedelerin de kurtarılmasını, çıkarılmasını diliyorum, inşallah çıkarılır. Ailesi ve 2 kızı var perişan. İzmir'de oturuyorlar. Şimdi buradan bir süre sonra İzmir'e gideceğiz. Perişan olmamak elde değil. Bin de bir de olsa bir ümitle bekliyorsunuz ama bugün kayıp bulundu denmesi sevinç yerine daha büyük bir üzüntü yaratıyor" ifadelerini kullandı.

Gemide aranan mürettebattan Abdulbaki Mirzaoğlu’nun dayısı Recai Yılmaz, "Tuğberk İmamoğlu gemisinde çalışan aşçıbaşı Abdulbaki Mirzaoğlu’nun dayısıyım. 4 senedir bu şirkette gemilerde aşçıbaşı olarak çalışıyordu. 7 ay sonra 48 yaşında son emekli olacaktı. 8 çocuk babası. Ailesi de gemide çalışmasına razı değildi. Çünkü çocukları babalarını görmeden büyüyordu ve haklı da çıktılar. Deniz işçileri böyle bir yaşamı hak etmiyor. Bunların hak ve hukukları daha çok korunmalı, sahip çıkılmalı diye düşünüyorum. Denizde, gemide veya geminin yan tarafında deniz dibinde arama yapılıyor. Biz aile olarak da kısa zamanda 10 aileydik, 9'a düştük. 9 aile de çadırda Silivri'de bekliyoruz. Bu hava şartlarında orada bekliyoruz" dedi.

31 yıldır emeğin sesi olan Evrensel, gücünü sadece okurlarından alıyor. Emeğin sesinin daha gür çıkması için sen de güç ver.

title: 15 gazeteci anlattı: Çatışmasızlık Kürt gazeteciliğini nasıl değiştiriyor?
content:
Medya ombudsmanı Faruk Bildirici, 29 Ekim'de yayımladığı “Çatışmasızlık hali ‘bölge’deki gazeteciliği nasıl dönüştürüyor?” başlıklı yazısında, Kürt meselesi etrafında gelişen çatışmasızlık sürecinin bölgedeki gazeteciliğe etkilerini ele aldı.


22 NİSAN KÜRT GAZETECİLER GÜNÜ


"Kürt gazeteciler baskılara rağmen hakikatin izinde"


22 Nisan 2026


Diyarbakır, Van ve bölgenin farklı kentlerinde çalışan 15 gazetecinin görüşlerine yer veren Bildirici, çatışmaların azalmasının gazetecilere yeni çalışma alanları açtığını, ancak basın özgürlüğüne yönelik sorunların devam ettiğini aktardı.


Çatışma haberlerinden toplumsal sorunlara


Bildirici, 1990'lı yıllarda gazetecilerin hedef alındığı dönemi hatırlatarak bölgedeki gazeteciliğin uzun yıllar çatışmaların, operasyonların ve hak ihlallerinin gölgesinde geliştiğini belirtti.


PKK'nin silahlı güçlerini çekmesiyle oluşan çatışmasızlık ortamının özellikle Kürt gazeteciler açısından yeni olanaklar yaratabileceğini ifade etti.


Faruk Bildirici: Tutuklu Kürt gazetecilere çifte standart uygulanıyor


27 Kasım 2023


Gazeteci Abdurrahman Gök, çatışmasızlığın kalıcılaşması durumunda gazeteciliğin güvenlik odaklı gündemden toplumsal hafızaya, haklara ve yaşam koşullarına daha fazla yönelebileceğini söyledi.


ANKA Diyarbakır Temsilcisi Ahmet Ün ise çatışmaların sona ermesiyle kırsal alanlarda haber yapmanın kolaylaşabileceğine; çiftçilerin, işsizlerin, emeklilerin ve yoksul kesimlerin sorunlarının daha görünür olabileceğine dikkat çekti.


Kürt gazetecilerin öldürülmesi İstanbul'da protesto edildi


26 Ağustos 2024


Güneydoğu Gazeteciler Cemiyeti Başkanı Felat Bozarslan da yeni dönemin göç, ekolojik tahribat, kadınların sorunları ve gençlerin gelecek kaygısı gibi konuların daha kapsamlı işlenmesi için fırsat sunduğunu belirtti.


“Çatışmasızlık basın özgürlüğü anlamına gelmiyor”


Gazeteci Hatice Kamer, bilgiye erişim olanaklarının artmasına rağmen doğru ve güvenilir bilgiye ulaşmanın zorlaştığını, ekonomik koşullar ve mesleki risklerin gençlerin gazetecilikten uzaklaşmasına neden olduğunu anlattı.


İrfan Aktan ise Kürt meselesine ilişkin haberlerde bazı engellerin kısmen aşılmasına karşın eleştirel gazetecilik üzerindeki siyasi ve hukuki baskıların devam ettiğini vurguladı.


Bakırhan MA ve JINNEWS'i ziyaret etti: Kürt gazeteciler büyük bedeller ödedi


22 Nisan 2024


Sürece yönelik eleştiriler de baskı altında


Gazeteci Mahmut Oral, barış sürecinin geleceğine ilişkin belirsizliğin gazeteciliği etkilediğini belirtti.


Oral'a göre hem iktidara hem de sürecin diğer siyasi aktörlerine yöneltilebilecek eleştiriler, gazetecilerin “süreç bozgunculuğu” suçlamasıyla karşılaşma kaygısını artırıyor.


Mezopotamya Ajansı muhabiri Zeynep Durgut da barış gazeteciliğinin güçlenmesi için öncelikle basın üzerindeki engellerin kaldırılması gerektiğini ifade etti.

Μπορεί και να έχουμε γνωριστεί καθώς πολλοί από εμάς είμαστε γονείς που τα παιδιά μας πάνε στα σχολεία του Πειραιά. Μοιραζόμαστε έτσι κι αλλιώς την ίδια δύσκολη καθημερινότητα.

title: Dress code Halloween
content:
Le 31 octobre, c'est Halloween – la fête des morts. Généralement ils reviennent exiger des bonbons ou des sorts. Le 17 octobre, le gouvernement a choisi les sorts. Résultat : on vient de quitter l'époque contemporaine et, depuis, Bismillah, c'est les ténèbres. Mais ces ténèbres, elles sont super drôles.


Jamais autant de créatures multiformes n'avaient déferlé dans nos insurrections. Il nous a fallu analyser cet étrange phénomène. Alors on a invité deux experts des ténèbres joyeuses : le philosophe Norman Ajari et l'essayiste Pacôme Thiellement. La brèche entre les mondes vient de s'ouvrir, elle n'est pas près de se refermer. C'est la première fois que la révolution s'apparente à la chorégraphie du Thriller de Michaël Jackson. Si le Gilet Jaune de 2018 s'est ajouté au k-way noir de 2016, désormais : c'est l'intégralité du multiverse qui se fait costume. Il n'est pas certain que, dans cette immense Battle d'aura avec le gouvernement, ce soient la police qui ait le meilleur déguisement. Joyeux Halloween.


00:00 Intro : le gouvernement va-t-il lâcher ses bonbons ?


03:21 Après le k-way noir et le Gilet Jaune, quel sens donner aux déguisements de la GenZ ? La police est-elle un déguisement ? Qui va gagner la battle d'aura ?


05:33 Watchmen et les superhéros : piller comme on se costume. À force de nous faire bouffer des franchises commerciales de superhéros, il fallait bien qu'ils s'incarnent !


10:55 : De l'histoire suprémaciste des vengeurs masqués du Klu Klux Klan à leur renversement aujourd'hui. S'identifier aux méchants de l'histoire pour prendre de court la police.


12:37 Pourquoi est-on passé du Joker à Batman ?


14:26 Choisir son super-héro : dans un carnaval on s'en fout. Retour sur le carnaval historique : il doit faire peur.


16:29 La lettre du prêtre Walchelin du XI° siècle et l'origine du géant Hellequin. Du carnaval aux danses macabres en passant par les orgies dans les cimetières.


19:34 Une blague fantôme.


20:08 L'auto-mise en scène des manifestants sur Instagram.


22:08 Du riotporn à la contre-offensive anti-journalistique des jeunes avec leurs portables.


24:08 Ridiculiser la presse mainstream.


25:09 Travailler depuis les vaincus de l'histoire, plutôt que des enfants à naître. Qui sont nos morts ?


29:19 La porte entre les morts et les vivants est ouverte.


29:09 Laisser Quentin D. là où il est.


30:04 Commercer avec les morts


33:40 Des nouvelles de Louise Michel. La générosité des vaincus.


34:14 Les « statues de con »


36:47 Un poème de Louise Michel, « Chant de mort à mes frères », 1871.


37:22 Le 31 octobre vengera-t-il les spectres du passé mais aussi ceux des futurs empêchés ?


38:20 La « répartition inégalitaire de l'avenir ».


40:07 André et Raphaël Glucksmann, qui est le plus mort ?

author: PETA-Team
title: Tierpark Neumünster: PETA kritisiert halbherzige Neuausrichtung mit heimischen Wildtieren
content:
Update vom 29. Oktober 2026


Künftig weniger

 „

exotische Tiere

”

im Tierpark Neumünster


Laut Medienberichten will der Tierpark Neumünster in Zukunft vor allem heimische Wildtiere zur Schau stellen. Viele der dort gehaltenen „exotischen“ Tiere, darunter der 26-jährige Eisbär Vitus, sollen künftig andernorts untergebracht werden.


Wir von PETA Deutschland begrüßen die geplante Abgabe exotischer Tiere als Schritt in die richtige Richtung, da wir die schlechten Haltungsbedingungen im Tierpark seit Jahren kritisieren. Damit die Tiere eine Chance auf ein besseres Leben haben, muss bei der Vermittlung der Tiere sichergestellt werden, dass sie nicht in ungeeignete Privathaltungen oder andere fragwürdige Einrichtungen gelangen.


Allerdings sollten auch heimische Wildtiere wie Elche, Wisente und Luchse nicht in Gefangenschaft leben müssen – selbst weitläufige Waldgehege können ihren komplexen Bedürfnissen nicht gerecht werden.


Wir fordern deshalb, dass der Tierpark künftig ausschließlich als Auffangstation für beschlagnahmte und aus schlechter Haltung gerettete Tiere dient.


Update vom 13. Juli 2026


Eisbärin Larissa ist eingeschläfert worden


Die Eisbärin Larissa wurde am 10. Juli 2026 im Tierpark Neumünster getötet, da sich ihr gesundheitlicher Zustand altersbedingt verschlechtert hat. Mit 36 Jahren galt sie laut dem Tierpark als die älteste Eisbärin der Welt. Larissa zeigte, wie viele Eisbären in Zoos, deutliche Verhaltensstörungen. Wir von PETA Deutschland hatten bereits 2022 ein Video veröffentlicht, in dem zu sehen ist, wie sie über längere Zeit immer wieder dieselben wenigen Meter am Beckenrand auf und ab lief.


Aufgrund ihrer traurigen Lebensgeschichte fordern wir erneut ein Ende der Eisbärenhaltung in Zoos und setzen uns mit einer Petition an das Bundeslandwirtschaftsministerium dafür ein, die Zucht der Tiere auslaufen zu lassen.


Originalbeitrag vom 22. Juni 2023


Video: Erschreckendes Tierleid im Tierpark Neumünster


Seit Jahren erhalten wir bei PETA Deutschland regelmäßig Hinweise von Whistleblower:innen auf Tierleid im Tierpark Neumünster. Im April 2023 dokumentierten wir daraufhin selbst vor Ort schlechte Haltungsbedingungen und

Verhaltensstörungen

 bei mehreren Tieren im

Zoo

, die nach unserer Einschätzung auf seelisches Leid hinweisen. Wir haben daher Strafanzeige gegen den Tierpark erstattet.


Verhaltensgestört: Eisbären laufen immer hin und her


In einem Video ist zu sehen, wie die

Eisbärin

 Larissa am Beckenrand immer wieder ziellos wenige Meter auf und ab läuft. Auch ihr Partner Vitus schwimmt die immer gleichen kleinen Kreise. Larissa und Vitus sind beide seit April 2017 in dem winzigen, heruntergekommenen Gehege in Neumünster eingesperrt. Die Verhaltensstörungen der beiden Eisbären sind seit Jahren bekannt und wurden uns seit 2018 wiederholt gemeldet, teilweise auch mit Videomaterial.


„Das Eisbärenpaar zeigt sehr auffällige Verhaltensstörungen. Einer läuft hin und her […] und der andere schwimmt im Pool in einem kleinen Radius im Kreis stundenlang.“

Whistleblower-Meldung vom Juli 2022


„ […] wir haben heute den Tierpark in Neumünster besucht und sind nachhaltig schockiert, unter welchen Bedingungen die Tiere dort gehalten werden. Die Eisbären […] laufen in einem sehr kleinen Gehege immer wieder verstört denselben Weg und wirken höchst apathisch. Das Gehege ist verwildert, verschmutzt und das Wasser im Schwimmbecken der Tiere ist so grün, dass man nicht hine[i]n sehen kann.“

Whistleblower-Meldung vom August 2018


Das Eisbären-Gehege ist beengt und heruntergekommen.


Die ausgeprägten Verhaltensstörungen der Eisbären werden heruntergespielt und „besondere Gerüche“ und ein angeblicher „Hormonüberschuss“ dafür verantwortlich gemacht.


Namhafte Fachleute sind überzeugt, dass Eisbären in Gefangenschaft nicht artgerecht gehalten werden können, da die Diskrepanz zwischen den Bedingungen in ihrem natürlichen Lebensraum und denen im Zoo zu groß ist. [1, 2] Obwohl die Folgen der viel zu kleinen Gehege in Zoos bekannt sind, werden die Tiere weiterhin in diese Leid verursachende Umgebung hineingezüchtet. In freier Natur wandern Eisbären jedes Jahr Hunderte bis Tausende Kilometer. Können sie sich nicht artgemäß bewegen, entwickeln sie auffällige Verhaltensstereotypien, die sich in sich ständig wiederholenden Bewegungsabläufen zeigen. Schon mehrfach veröffentlichte PETA

Videomaterial

, das schwere Zwangsstörungen bei den Tieren belegt.


Weitere verhaltensgestörte Tiere im Tierpark …

author: Αντώνιος Δημόπουλος και Λουκάς Σταμέλλος
title: Ενοχή των αστυνομικών για κακουργηματικά βασανιστήρια στον Β. Μάγγο πρότεινε η εισαγγελέας
content:
Σύνδεσμος δημοσίευσης:

Ενοχή των αστυνομικών για κακουργηματικά βασανιστήρια στον Β. Μάγγο πρότεινε η εισαγγελέας


Την ενοχή των κατηγορούμενων αστυνομικών για τα βασανιστήρια σε βάρος του Βασίλη Μάγγου στο Αστυνομικό Μέγαρο Βόλου, καθώς και για το αδίκημα της έκθεσης, πρότεινε η εισαγγελέας του Μικτού Ορκωτού Δικαστηρίου Καρδίτσας, κατά την 21η δικάσιμο, την Πέμπτη 29 Οκτωβρίου 2026.


Η εισαγγελέας έκρινε ότι οι σοβαρές σωματικές βλάβες του Βασίλη Μάγγου, μεταξύ των οποίων έξι κατάγματα πλευρών και κάκωση στο ήπαρ, προκλήθηκαν από τη βία που υπέστη κατά τη μεταφορά του και την παραμονή του στην Αστυνομική Διεύθυνση, μετά τον ξυλοδαρμό του έξω από τα δικαστήρια του Βόλου στις 14 Ιουνίου 2020.


Επικαλούμενη τις ιατρικές γνωματεύσεις και τις μαρτυρικές καταθέσεις, απέρριψε τους ισχυρισμούς ότι οι κακώσεις προϋπήρχαν ή είχαν προκληθεί αποκλειστικά από τα χτυπήματα έξω από τα δικαστήρια.


Ως προς τη στοιχειοθέτηση των βασανιστηρίων κατά το άρθρο 137Α του Ποινικού Κώδικα, υποστήριξε ότι αποδείχθηκε και ο ειδικός σκοπός της τιμωρίας του Μάγγου. Συνέδεσε τη βία με το ιδιαίτερα πολωμένο κλίμα που είχε διαμορφωθεί μετά τη μεγάλη κινητοποίηση κατά της καύσης απορριμμάτων στην ΑΓΕΤ, την προηγούμενη ημέρα, και με την αντίληψη των αστυνομικών ότι είχε πληγεί το γόητρο της αστυνομίας.


Ιδιαίτερη αναφορά έκανε στον εξευτελισμό που περιέγραψε ότι υπέστη ο Μάγγος, ως στοιχεία της πρόκλησης όχι μόνο σωματικού αλλά και ψυχικού πόνου.


Διαβάστε επίσης:


Η υπεράσπιση ενός βασανισμού


Για την επικίνδυνη σωματική βλάβη κατά τη μεταφορά με το αστυνομικό όχημα, πρότεινε την ενοχή των δύο αστυνομικών που βρίσκονταν δίπλα του και την αθώωση του συνοδηγού για τη συγκεκριμένη πράξη. Για τη βία εντός του Αστυνομικού Μεγάρου πρότεινε την ενοχή όλων των αντίστοιχων κατηγορουμένων.


Για το αδίκημα της έκθεσης, επισήμανε ότι η σοβαρή κατάσταση της υγείας του ήταν εμφανής στους αστυνομικούς, οι οποίοι τον άφησαν αβοήθητο παρά το αίτημά του να μεταφερθεί στο νοσοκομείο.


Τέλος, πρότεινε την αθώωση των κατηγορουμένων για την παράνομη κατακράτηση, θεωρώντας ότι η σχετική αρμοδιότητα ανήκε στον αξιωματικό υπηρεσίας.


Η δίκη συνεχίζεται με τις αγορεύσεις των συνηγόρων.

Ακολουθεί ολόκληρη η αγόρευση της Εισαγγελέα:


Προτού ξεκινήσω να παραθέτω τι προέκυψε κατά την κρίση μου, οφείλω να αναφερθώ στο κλίμα την περίοδο που λάμβαναν χώρα τα περιστατικά. Ο Βόλος είναι βεβαρημένος περιβαλλοντικά […] έχουμε διαδηλώσεις, ψηφίσματα, τοποθετήσεις συλλογικά και ατομικά πολιτών.


Στις 13/6/2020 έχουμε μια μεγάλη διαδήλωση έξω από το εργοστάσιο της ΑΓΕΤ Ηρακλής. Διαμαρτύρονται για τη μόλυνση της ατμόσφαιρας. Στην πορεία αυτή δημιουργούνται εντάσεις. Έχουμε σίγουρα μια κακή εκτίμηση από την πλευρά της αστυνομίας. Τραυματίζονται 5 αστυνομικοί […] κάποιοι εξ αυτών νοσηλεύονται στο Γενικό Νοσοκομείο Βόλου. Πρωτοφανές και όχι σύνηθες γενικά να τραυματίζεται κόσμος και δη αστυνομικοί σε μια επαρχιακή πόλη. Έγιναν κάποιες συλλήψεις, μετά από διώξεις από μελέτη οπτικού υλικού, και είχαμε δύο συλληφθέντες. Ένας ο κ. Θ.Σ. [σ.σ.: μάρτυρας στη δίκη εδώ] και μια γυναίκα. Γίνεται συγκέντρωση στις 13/6 το βράδυ. Κλίμα πολωμένο.


Τη 14η Ιουνίου [2020] προσέρχονται στον εισαγγελέα οι συλληφθέντες […] Κυριακή, δεν συνεδριάζει το δικαστήριο […] και ο συλληφθείς επιστρέφει στο αστυνομικό μέγαρο. Έξω από το δικαστικό μέγαρο έχει συγκεντρωθεί ένα πλήθος κόσμου για διαμαρτυρία και συμπαράσταση στους συλληφθέντες. Υπάρχει και αστυνομική δύναμη. Ο Θ.Σ. εξέρχεται από το δικαστικό μέγαρο για να μεταχθεί στο αστυνομικό τμήμα. Με το που εξέρχεται –και αυτά τα λέμε με σχετική ασφάλεια γιατί έχουμε εικόνα [βίντεο]– ο Βασίλης Μάγγος έρχεται, δεν είναι στο πλήθος των συγκεντρωμένων, έχει αφήσει το μηχανάκι του και είναι στη μέση και διαμαρτύρεται φωνασκώντας έντονα και σηκώνοντας τα χέρια του προς τη μεριά των αστυνομικών. Ο 6ος κατηγορούμενος, κ. Παζαράς, υποδεικνύει τον κ. Μάγγο και κινούνται αστυνομικοί εναντίον του. Ο κ. Μάγγος οπισθοχωρεί… Είναι οι 3 πρώτοι κατηγορούμενοι που καταφέρουν τα χτυπήματα… Ο κ. Μάγγος κάνει κάποιες κινήσεις αποτρεπτικές και όχι επιθετικές. Γονατίζει και χειροπεδείται. Οδηγείται σε όχημα. Μέσα είναι ο 4ος κατηγορούμενος, κ. Μόναχος, και συνοδηγός ο κ. Σκρίμπας και πίσω οι 3ος και 4ος κατηγορούμενοι, Μπακογιάννης και Μπαλαμώτης. Οι ενέργειες των αστυνομικών είναι επιθετικές και άγριες. Αντιδρά ο κ. Μάγγος αλλά αντιδρά και άλλος κόσμος. Επικαλούμαι την κατάθεση του μάρτυρα Ταταριώτη… και της κυρίας που ήταν κατηγορούμενη… Αντιδρούσαν ακόμα και οι ταξιτζήδες …

author: EDRi
title: EDRi-gram, 29 October 2026
content:
What has the EDRi network been up to over the past few weeks? Find out the latest digital rights news in our regular newsletter. In this edition: Celebrating end-to-end encryption, and the digital justice community in Europe and beyond

We’re still riding the high from October milestones showcasing the strength of our community. We had the pleasure of greeting many of you in person and online for #PrivacyCamp26 two weeks ago to discuss the origins of technology and how to pivot from conversations around “sovereignty” to meaningful, community-led self-determination. If you weren’t able to make it but you’re curious about the conversations, you can rewatch the livestream of some of the panel discussions.

Then, on October 21, we celebrated Global Encryption Day, highlighting end-to-end encryption as a crucial foundation to our right to safe and secure communication online and to life as we know it. Thanks to our members and partners, our message of protecting encryption was visible across several European capitals – from the metro trains of Prague to key landmarks in Berlin, Paris and Dublin with mobile “encryption trucks”. We also worked with European Sex Workers Alliance and Féministes contre le cyberharcèlement to raise awareness on the importance of safe and secure communications for sex workers as well as womens’ rights. You can read more about the action in this edition, and stay tuned for more updates coming soon on our social platforms.

Yet another win for digital rights this month came with the news of Norway’s data protection authority imposing a fine of 92 million Norwegian crowns (roughly EUR 8.8 million) on Microsoft’s adtech unit Xandr for unlawfully sharing ​Grindr users’ sensitive data with thousands of advertisers.

While we’re bolstered from the wins and community spirit, there’s a lot more to resist and much work to be done. We are still reeling from the EU governments’ final position on the Digital Omnibus on Data, which amongst other unsavoury things, will to allow companies to use our data to develop or use their AI systems if it serves a ‘legitimate interest’ – without us knowing or accepting. This is a blank cheque for tech corporations to indulge in outrageous data grabs and exploit potentially sensitive information about us.

Earlier this week, the European Commission also announced a revamp of Frontex, EU’s border agency, that is set to double its budget and expand its role in deportations and surveillance. Not only will this turn Frontex into EU’s ICE equivalent, the new Regulation also wants to allow Frontex to be able to monitor social media for information that may forecast people’s movements at EU borders. Let alone leading with solidarity and care, the EU seems intent on violating people’s freedom to move and to express themselves. Keep your eyes out for an analysis of the new proposal from the Protect Not Surveil coalition.

title: Ephéméride des luttes : 29 octobre
content:
Le 29 octobre de l'éphéméride des luttes résonne des noms de Luca, Leon, Sergio, Rocco et de toutes celles et ceux qui ont lutté dans le passé, pour que la mémoire de leurs luttes ne soient pas ensevelies sous la poussière du présent.


1390 :

 Premier procès en sorcellerie à Paris, lors duquel Jeanne de Brigue est condamnée au bûcher.


1901 :

 Aux USA, l'anarchiste Leon Czolgosz est exécuté sur la chaise électrique pour avoir assassiné le président des Etats-Unis William McKinley le

6 septembre

.


1916 :

 A Montevideo en Uruguay, parution du premier numéro de '

El Hombre

', hebdomadaire anarchiste de combat.


1947 :

 A Milan, la Volante Rossa attaque un siège du nouveau parti fasciste, le MSI, reconstitué un an à peine après la 'chute' du fascisme.


1952 :

 La conférence de presse de Charlie Chaplin est perturbée par l'Internationale Lettriste.


1964 :

 En Bolivie, c'est le premier des trois jours de grève générale décrétés par la Centrale Ouvrière Bolivienne. L'armée mènera une répression féroce et sanglante et finit par renverser le président et à s'emparer du pouvoir.


1972 :

 Des militants du groupe palestinien Septembre Noir détournent un avion de ligne ouest-allemand et obtienne la libération de trois autres de leurs militants.


1974 :

 A Florence, au cours du braquage d'une banque, deux militants des Nuclei Armati Proletari (NAP), Luca Mantini et Sergio Romeo, sont tués après un échange de coups de feu avec la police, et deux autres (Pasquale Abatangelo et Pietro Sofia) sont arrêtés après avoir été blessés au cours de la fusillade.


1975 :

 A Rome, le groupe 'Lutte Armée pour le Communisme' tire plusieurs coups de feu sur un rassemblement fasciste, tuant l'un d'entre eux.


1977 :

 - A Cagliari en Sardaigne, des molotov sont lancés sur un répétiteur téléphonique.


 A Turin, le jeune militant autonome Rocco Sardone meurt dans l'explosion de la bombe qu'il s'apprêtait à déposer contre un concessionnaire Audi.

 En France, les prisonniers des NAPAP (Noyaux Armés Pour l'Autonomie Populaire) mettent fin à leur grève de la faim.


1980 :

 A Caluire-et-Cuire, le groupe révolutionnaire 'L'Affiche Rouge' attaque un convoi de fonds d'une agence BNP.


1981 :

 Mort de Georges Brassens.


2004 :

 A Athènes, Lutte Révolutionnaire fait sauter deux fourgons pénitentiaires qui devaient aller garder la prison de Korydallos.


2012 :

 Sur la ZAD de Notre-Dame-des-Landes, on est en pleine opération 'César' : grande journée d'affrontements contre la police autour de la Saulce.


2014 :

 A Mesolongi en Grèce, un groupe de personnes détruit de nombreux véhicules de police devant un commissariat suite à l'agression de deux anarchistes par la police un peu plus tôt.


2016 :

 - A

Marseille

, une manifestation de 300 personnes

investit un bâtiment vide

 de la rue Briffaut pour y créer un centre social.


 A Cukurca en Turquie, le PKK kurde a attaqué une base de l'armée turque au mortier, tuant trois soldats et en blessant cinq autres.

 A Oullins, en banlieue lyonnaise, un cocktail molotov est lancé sur le commissariat de police depuis une voiture en mouvement.

author: WoMin
title: From Mombasa to Yaoundé, the vision and the demand is for reparative justice
content:
Through WoMin’s work alongside African women organising against extractivism, against the drivers of the climate crisis and its impacts, the destruction of the commons through false solutions, unjust energy transitions (and generally a world order that serves a minority over the global majority), we have been asking: what is the full range of impacts and costs in the face of environmental and climate impacts? Who and whose work absorbs these impacts and costs? And what would repair mean from the perspective of women, their communities and the ecosystems they care for and are cared for at the frontline of the climate crisis, where centuries of continued systems of accumulation by dispossession and destruction meet?


Our experience shows us that reparations cannot simply be another form of compensation. They must confront the very systems producing the harm – extractivism, odious and illegitimate debt, colonial legacies, patriarchy, racism, and corporate power promoting more false solutions whose aim is not climate justice but profit. Reparations must indeed offer us all a real chance to build Pan African feminist futures that centre care, including the restoration of the commons, and the conditions that make life possible.


Connecting the “c-words” – colonialism to climate reparations


The recent

African Symposium on Climate Reparations

 in Mombasa, Kenya, started on that same note: “there is no “c-word” that we cannot bring into conversations on climate reparations”, argued a comrade in his opening remarks. And indeed, the current

climate disorder

1

 is a historical process, and Colonialism (the c-word that in other climate justice spaces some shy away from) is part and parcel of it. As is, we argue at WoMin, capitalism. What is more, not only do climate reparations need to address colonialism and neocolonialism, but also the solution to the climate crisis will not be found within capitalism. Or as Audre Lorde put it, “… the master’s tools will never dismantle the master’s house. They may allow us temporarily to beat him at his own game, but they will never enable us to bring about genuine change.”


Not only we need our own tools, but also a broad alliance, as broad, yet united in principles and analysis, as broad and urgent is the task ahead. And the symposium offered an important space to bring together many working for reparations across the continent and in the diaspora, in conversations navigated along four main tracks: rights of nature and ecosystems stewardship; finance, debt and tax justice; law and human rights; and lived realities from frontline communities.


And the timing matters. We are entering the Decade of Justice and Reparations for Africans and People of African Descent, while the debt crisis in Africa continues to exponentially grow and deepen climate vulnerability, false climate solutions continue to expand, further threatening the commons millions of Africans depend upon for their everyday subsistence, and the African Court considers an Advisory Opinion on States’ obligations in the climate crisis.


As powerful expressed in an

open letter

 which emerged from the symposium, a Pan African position and action plan for climate reparations is urgent, but it cannot be constructed only through states, legal and financial tools. Those at the frontlines absorbing the costs of extractivism, ecological destruction and climate disruption have to shape what counts as harm, what constitutes repair, and what must stop. And importantly, we need to organise at all levels the collective power to make repair possible.


African women united for climate justice and reparations


This was the task of the 4th

Women’s Climate Assembly

 (WCA) in Yaoundé, Cameroon, held in early October under the theme, “Our lands, our voices: African women united for climate justice and reparations!”. The Assembly convened over 75 women community leaders, activists, feminist organisations, civil society groups and allies from twelve countries including Burkina Faso, Cameroon, Côte d’Ivoire, the Democratic Republic of Congo (DRC), Guinea-Conakry, Liberia, Namibia, Niger, Nigeria, Sierra Leone, Senegal, and Zambia.

They used them sustainably. So we ask our ancestors to guide us during this Assembly, so that peace and food …

author: Semhal Meles Zenawi
title: Ethiopia: Elections, Constitutional Change, and Genocidal Violence
content:
In November 2020, a war erupted in the Ethiopian region of Tigray. Six hundred thousand to a million civilian lives are estimated to have been lost. Amongst the many war crimes and crimes against humanity committed during the two-year war was genocide against Tigrayans. Abiy Ahmed has on several occasions insisted that the catalyst for war was his intolerance for voluntary disassociation and the exercise of the right to vote. 


The National Electoral Board of Ethiopia (NEBE) postponed the 2020 election several times, but the final “indefinite” postponement under the cover of COVID-19 breached the constitutionally set term limit. Then NEBE chair Birtukan Mideksa’s claim that COVID-19 introduced public health imperatives that overrode those of democracy was unconvincing given the government’s non-enforcement of other measures such as lockdowns or even social distancing, and its farcical claim of having developed a “homegrown” cure. 


Following a public outcry over the “corona-clouded power grab”, four prescriptive options for a “constitutional route to postponement” were presented to a curated array of government-aligned opposition by the then minister of justice, now minister of foreign affairs, Gedion Timothewos. The exercise was met with derision, even by its hand-selected participants. An equally performative constitutional “tribunal” was held, but that too failed to foster agreement over the legality of the postponement and the legitimacy of the government following the expiration of its term. 


Having catalysed constitutional chaos, Mideksa set about facilitating Ahmed’s bypassing of various laws and bylaws to dissolve the Ethiopian People’s Revolutionary Democratic Front (EPRDF) and establish the Prosperity Party (PP). Beyond legal and procedural controversies, the move to reconstitute the EPRDF drew criticism for its intent. Abiy’s desire to dissolve the EPRDF and

“Medemer”

 (amalgamate) its constituent and affiliated parts was viewed by many as an initial step towards constitutional remaking and a reversal of multinational federalism.


The dissolution of the EPRDF ended the “reformist” coalition known as Team Lemma that propelled Abiy Ahmed to its chairmanship and Ethiopia’s prime ministership. In August 2020, Lemma Megersa, after whom Team Lemma was named, was removed from the Prosperity Party and as Minister of Defence for opposing the EPRDF’s amalgamation. The PP’s establishment was so ad hoc that it remains unclear if Megersa had actually joined the PP before he was booted out.


The relationship between the erstwhile allies came under strain as early as 2019 and was indicative of a wider rift between Abiy Ahmed and his Oromo base over the meaning of “reform” and its alignment with the demands of the protests that spurred Team Lemma’s rise. Ahmed positioned himself as an Oromo populist championing the cause of the Oromo farmer and, more broadly, seeking the “proper implementation of federalism”. Once in power, he started to appeal to a form of “pan-Ethiopian” nationalism which hoped to homogenize national identity and recentralize Ethiopia’s governing structures. Many in Ahmed’s Oromo base viewed the turn as a betrayal of the cause. Even before Megersa’s political downfall, suspicions over Ahmed’s intentions ignited a still-raging conflict with the Oromo Liberation Army. 


For a time, Abiy managed to force together the antagonistic nationalisms by offering a shared enemy – Tigrayan supremacy. Once considered the champion of the “national question”, the Tigray People’s Liberation Front (TPLF) was recast as the primary impediment to its “proper implementation”, while maintaining its long-held position as the primary impediment to the return of a unitary institutional setup. “Tigrinya speakers” became “daytime hyenas” on whom the country’s many political and social crises could be scapegoated. 


The TPLF opposed the postponement of the election and refused to recognize the federal government once its constitutionally set term was over. Unfortunately, the TPLF did not lodge an official challenge to the postponement through its seats in both chambers of parliament. Instead, it retreated into Tigray to shore up its base and made plans to hold a regional election within constitutionally set limits.


Both the dissolution of the EPRDF and the postponement of the elections drew widespread criticism from divergent opposition groups. Still, the TPLF’s concerns were dismissed as the mere disgruntlements of …

author: Wini Omer
title: It’s not the refugees, it’s the austerity measures!
content:
A Sudanese journalist, with whom I worked for two years at the same newspaper, told me when I contacted him to check on his situation after the last wave of attacks against refugees in Libya: “We are trapped in our homes. We can’t leave. I didn’t send my kids to school since the beginning of this wave of violence. The situation is difficult beyond imagination.”

The Sudanese who left Sudan seeking refuge in Libya, amid very violent clashes that started in April 2023 and continue to this moment, are facing violence, danger, and hatred in what was supposed to be a safe refuge. But this reality is not exclusive to Sudanese refugees, and the violence is indifferent to other nationalities who are fleeing conflicts, war, and instability at home: Ethiopians, Eritreans, and refugees from the Central African Republic.

In Libya, African refugees faced waves of violence, the latest in June this year. Despite competing for power, Libya’s rival authorities in the east and west have united in stoking anti-migrant rhetoric and launching a violent campaign of mass detention and expulsions against migrants and refugees, as a recent

Human Rights Watch report

 has indicated.

In Egypt, a

crackdown campaign

 led by security forces, accompanied by social media hate speech against Sudanese and Syrian refugees, intensified on the ground, blaming them for the rise in living costs, mainly rents, groceries, and basic life needs. As a result of systematic brutality, between January and June 2026,

12 Sudanese passed away in Egyptian detention centers

 and police cells, including a child of 17. Refugees processed for deportation are forced to sign voluntary return declarations.

Sudan hosts one of the largest refugee and asylum-seeker populations in Africa, mainly South Sudanese, Ethiopians, and Eritreans, who currently face detention and

forced deportation

 from the capital, Khartoum, to refugee camps close to the borders with their countries of origin, after the Sudanese Armed Forces (SAF) regained control of the capital. This step was taken following a growing political rhetoric that profiled them as criminals and blamed them for the Rapid Support Forces (RSF) controlling Khartoum. Accordingly, they were deported to refugee camps in White Nile State, Al-Gadarif State, and Kassala State, camps that lack all basic human needs and restrict freedom of movement and the right to work. Many South Sudanese mothers were deported while their children were not allowed to accompany them, leaving them in limbo.

Such rhetoric, mainly produced and shared by pro-SAF individuals and platforms, provides the military establishment with a popular cover to reproduce its symbolic authority. It is also used by some actors within the army as a tool to bolster its legitimacy against the Rapid Support Forces, portraying it as the guardian of national sovereignty and the representative of the “authentic Sudanese” against the “foreign threat.” This reflects a deeper attempt to regain control over the state and society at a moment of total collapse of political and legal frameworks.

For many of these refugees, especially the Eritreans, returning is not an option, considering the human rights situation in Eritrea. But according to media reports, both Eritrea and Sudan are

complicit in the repatriation of civilians from Sudan

 back to Eritrea.

Whether it is the systematic violence against Sudanese refugees on the continent, or the deliberate violence against African refugees in Sudan, these incidents reflect one broader reality in which violence is used and reproduced either by state actors or by the citizens of the host countries to whom the refugees sought safety within the African continent. This reality raises a critical question about how to understand such incidents, the politics behind them, and why we are seeing them now.

Shifting the blame

Have the refugees led to the economic crises in Egypt, Libya, or Tunisia? Or are these crises a direct result of the state’s social and economic policies?

In Egypt, the last ten years have witnessed a high level of dependence on debt; Egypt has become one of the IMF’s largest borrowers, while social expenditure, including social protection, health, and education, has shrunk, accompanied by political oppression. Those debts have been invested in projects lacking a developmental dimension, such as

the new administrative capital

 project, which is expected to cost up to $300 billion by the time it’s finalized …

author: ROAPE
title: The sports commercializers are in town
content:
Two recent stories from Kenya reflect the rapid growth, rising ambitions, and increasing commercialization and professionalization of East Africa’s sports sector.


In the first, Helios Sports and Entertainment Group, a private equity firm focused on the continent, teamed up with Zaria Group, fronted by former NBA executive

Masai Ujiri

, to build a $294 million sports and entertainment hub in Nairobi. Then, Oscar-winning actress Lupita Nyong’o

announced

 she was investing in Nairobi City Thunder, which plays in the Basketball Africa League (BAL).


A few days later, reports said Nyong’o’s investment in Nairobi City Thunder may kickstart further investment in the BAL and sports in Kenya. This was followed by

more bullish coverage

 of

further investment

. What do we make of all this? What analytical language and tools do we have to observe and account for these significant on-ground events and dynamics?


One thing is clear: sports and commerce in East Africa are forming ever closer ties in countries such as Kenya and Uganda, across sectors, from rugby, boxing, basketball, and football to athletics, golf, badminton, and motocross, and, lately, e-sports. Major companies, often foreign, attach their brand assets to

competitions

,

leagues

, events, teams, and

sports


champions

, with a wide range of promotional messages, causes, and sector representation (banking, insurance, telecommunications,

betting

 and real estate, food and beverages, and tires).


The media in these two countries run numerous pieces every month about sports sponsorship partnerships that are signed, announced,

renewed

, and upgraded (for example, in financial commitment). Weekends in Kampala and Nairobi during sports season are packed with competitions and events (including community and charity events), and the media again

reports

 on them, naming the sponsors prominently.


TV live coverage is increasing; viewers can join in for free or pay a fee (for example, to follow

boxing

 in Kampala or

rugby

 in Nairobi). Ugandan newspapers Daily Monitor and New Vision, or sports news website

Kawowo Sports

, for example, are full of articles, week after week, with headlines, pictures and stories about sport aspirations, achievement, triumphs, records, trophies, medals and rewards,

players’

 pride,

moves

 and

signings

, or various aspects of

fandom

. Thus, there is not just sports buzz (including participation among viewers/fans) but also commercial and media (including social media) interest.


Political

, including diplomatic, buzz also exists, with the governments of

Kenya

 and

Uganda

 regularly joining initiatives and events in varying roles and capacities, including supporting the hosting of major sports 

events

, national teams and champions competing at international events, and so on. Officially launching sports events and welcoming home athletes from competition elsewhere also get solid

media


coverage

, with officials, sponsors, national flags, and fans joining in. Representatives of international sports federations; prominent, popular, or small but growing international sports competitions; or well-known global sports leagues, clubs, and personalities visit their counterparts to talk, inspect, plan,

announce

, and so on.


Relatedly, both countries are also undertaking significant 

venue 

construction 

and repair. This is related especially to football (the upcoming AFCON 2027, hosted with Tanzania) but also to other sports (such as paddle), or other formats and purposes, such as

multi-function

 sports facilities for rent for leisure or competitive activity (non-professional competitions, for example), or sports venues in the

education

 sector for schoolchildren and students’ recreational and competitive activities.

Hamz

 Stadium in downtown Kampala is one

example

.


Significantly, the facilities upgrade and sport events, participation, commerce, and fandom buzz are also evident in viewing venues: the entertainment

bars

 and

clubs

 (even a

cinema

 venue) that

broadcast

 sports events, especially football (from the EPL to the World Cup and AFCON), some of them almost throughout the entire week; say, from Tuesday in EPL-heavy weeks; or the

venues

 (clubs, bars, shopping malls) that host live sports such as

boxing

 (professional and

celebrity

 fights) or

martial arts

.


These trends, dynamics, and transformations are part of the wider

African Sports Economy

 (ASE), as they …

author: Simon Ramapuputla
title: Cosatu to campaign for ANC and SACP
content:
Cosatu has pledged to campaign for both the African National Congress (ANC) and the South African Communist Party (SACP) in the upcoming local government elections, warning that its political support will not prevent it from confronting either party if workers’ interests are undermined.


SACP candidates will be contesting the local government polls on 4 November, independently of the ANC for the first time since 1994.


The position emerged from the federation’s 15

th

 national congress, which was held from 12 to 14 October after its

first attempt in September collapsed

. In her first formal press statement as the newly elected general secretary, Zingiswa Losi said the congress reaffirmed Cosatu’s historic mission to organise and mobilise the working class, defend workers’ rights and advance a programme of democratic transformation towards socialism.


The federation’s decision to support both the ANC and SACP followed consultations among affiliates. Losi explained that the unions had adopted positions intended to influence the national congress, which ultimately passed what the leadership called a “super resolution” to support both parties.


The motion to back the SACP was championed by one of Cosatu’s largest affiliates, the National Health and Allied Workers’ Union (Nehawu). Losi defended Nehawu and the right of affiliates to consult their constituencies and bring their positions to the congress. She maintained that they had not acted improperly and that the decisive outcome was the congress’s collective resolution supporting both the ANC and SACP. Cosatu’s demands regarding local government, labour rights and public services would apply to both parties. she said.


Congress resolutions


The agenda of Cosatu’s congress involved discussions on the future of organised labour amid mass unemployment, poverty, inequality and rising living costs. The congress acknowledged the need to rebuild Cosatu’s organisational strength and reverse the trend of declining membership in parts of the private sector.


Cosatu’s declared priority is to rebuild workplace structures, organise un-unionised and precariously employed workers, strengthen collective bargaining and to improve accountability among affiliates.


One of the federation’s key proposals is a workers’ cost-of-living index to inform wage negotiations and government policy. Losi argued that economic progress should not be measured simply by declining inflation or headline growth, but by whether workers and their families could afford to live with dignity. “What it costs for workers to live must inform the bargaining strategy,” she said.


The proposed index would assess the weight of food, transport, electricity and healthcare costs on household budgets. Cosatu wants wage negotiations to take into account what money workers have left after meeting essential expenses, particularly when salary increases fail to keep pace with inflation.


The federation is also calling for an expanded basket of zero-rated goods, affordable basic services and the implementation of National Health Insurance to ease the cost of medical care.


Cosatu urged consumers and government to support locally produced goods, arguing that stronger domestic production can help protect manufacturing jobs. The federation maintains that economic growth must translate into employment and improved living standards rather than leave workers trapped in poverty.


Cosatu’s general secretary, Zingiswa Losi campaigning for the ANC in Khayelitsha recently. Photo from Zingiswa Losi’s Facebook page


Cosatu criticises the composition of GNU


While continuing to support the ANC, Cosatu still criticised the composition of the government of national unity, particularly the inclusion of the Democratic Alliance, citing differences over policies such as national health insurance and the national minimum wage. The federation argued that rebuilding the tri-partite alliance with the ANC and SACP must not require workers to accept policies that undermine their interests.


Newly elected president, Mike Shingange stressed that Cosatu’s electoral support was not unconditional. “It doesn’t mean when we campaign and vote for you, and you undermine the interests of the workers, that we’re not going to come for you. We will,” he said.


Shingange said Cosatu would not remain silent if either political partner failed to honour commitments to workers. He warned that their conduct in government could influence the federation’s …
