author: EDRi
title: What the new Convention on Decent Work in the Platform Economy means for workers – and what’s next for implementation
content:
In June 2026, the International Labour Organisation (ILO) adopted a new Convention on Decent Work in the Platform Economy. Following in the footsteps of the EU’s Platform Work Directive, this Convention extends data protection rights for platform workers and contains innovative provisions to protect against the adverse effects of automated decision-making globally. But this is only the beginning. In this article, EDRi member Privacy International explores what’s next for ratification, implementation and the future of regulating worker surveillance in the EU and around the world.

By Privacy International (guest author) · October 29, 2026

On 12 June 2026, the International Labour Organisation (ILO) adopted Convention C193 on Decent Work in the Platform Economy. This is a landmark piece of legislation as the first global legally binding instrument regulating the platform economy and addressing the impact of technology on the world of work.

The Convention represents a significant step forward for workers’ rights around the globe. It reflects the growing consensus that digital platform workers need more adequate protection from abusive and exploitative employment practices. It also reflects the need to regulate the use of automated decision-making (ADM) in the workplace affecting platform workers, an issue Privacy International has developed a set of recommendations on.

Covering similar ground to the EU’s Platform Work Directive, the Convention contains provisions on: fairer compensation, extension of access to certain social protections, the right to collective bargaining, improved occupational health and safety standards, and data protection rights to access, rectify and erase their personal data.

Crucially, the Convention recognises the need for greater transparency in algorithmic management. Section X requires companies to inform workers about the use of automated systems in monitoring their performance, allocating tasks and making decisions affecting their work and access to work. It also gives workers the right to request written explanations of significant automated decisions, as well as request review of decisions that negatively impact them. While more is needed, this sets a new global standard and expectation, codifying the reality that platform workers are indeed workers – rather than merely contractors with platforms as the intermediaries.

The next step is ensuring that governments properly implement and adequately enforce the Convention. While the Convention provides historical gains for workers, the text is not perfect; some language around the automated decision-making provisions default to vague terms. For instance, rather than hard-edged requirements, States are only obliged to ‘take appropriate measures’ to ensure responsible use of ADM, and worker access to written explanations pertains only to ‘significant’ decisions. As the deadline for transposition of the Platform Work Directive nears, this fight for strong implementation of platform workers’ rights will spread around the world.

As States approach national implementation, they must ensure that they clearly articulate the nature of those ‘appropriate measures’ in a bold and ambitious way.

At minimum, States should push for platforms to provide explanations of decisions to workers by default, rather than just ‘upon request’. Explanations should also be specific and personalised to the worker, specifying the data and parameters on which decisions are based, and how an alternative outcome could have been reached. States should also consider how platforms can give workers and their representatives access to APIs, sandboxes or source code to understand for themselves how the algorithms work.

It is also essential that references to classification of employment not be interpreted to undermine the Convention’s practical effectiveness; all workers in the platform economy, regardless of their employment status, should enjoy the rights afforded by the Convention.

Governments, platforms and the ILO should engage directly with workers, union representatives and civil society to develop effective legislative frameworks and adequate enforcement that best serve the rights and interests of workers. The ILO should also revisit a non-binding recommendation that was meant to be adopted alongside Convention C193. The draft Recommendation provided more detail on issues like transparency and explainability, giving essential guidance to Member States and …

author: Kate Sharpley
title: Barry Pateman: An Appreciation
content:
It’s important to appreciate those who have come before us. I first met Barry through Albert Meltzer, probably at a bookfair. I’d learned to trust that if Albert thought well of someone, he was probably right.

Barry was an impressive man, physically and mentally, with the sort of self-deprecating humour instantly recognisable to anyone brought up in a British working class environment. And he was able to talk to people, without the sort of academic language that can be so off-putting.

The times I saw him were few and far between but they were always memorable. Barry was brimming with ideas, whether about anarchist history, theory and practice, sport or wider culture. Like Albert he had a high regard for the autodidacts – especially those miner militants whose self-education far outstripped those who had had a university education. He was good company.

It was perhaps telling that I learned of Barry’s death a few days after returning from Ron Marsden’s funeral. Both had been intimately involved in the tension between organising as anarchists and remaining accessible to ordinary people. It’s a tension that runs through most of the anarchist organising and groups that I have been part of in my life, and one I kept promising Barry I would write something about – the organisations that can never get above Dunbar’s number[1] in membership without splitting, the affinity groups claiming to be membership organisations, the strategies designed for different times, the insights from Stuart Christie’s autobiography about affinity groups. Sorry, mate, life always seemed to get in the way, I am way too easily distracted….

He was generous with his time and his thoughts. He had many strings to his bow – as you would expect from someone who admired those self-educated working class militants – as was so warmly described by the guy who knew him from the New Zealand Cricket Museum at the memorial service.

Barry would regularly talk about how militant young miners from South Yorkshire were interested in the Direct Action Movement, during the height of the 1984-5 strike. But as they weren’t fully formed anarchists, DAM couldn’t accept them, despite their hard won experience of class struggle. It was this discussion that led DAM to become the Solidarity Federation (alongside other struggles like the Ardbride dispute 1986-87). Unfortunately, with a fabulous sense of timing, SF’s orientation towards labour movement militants happened at exactly the time the pool of labour movement militants shrank, following the catastrophic defeats of the 80s and early 90s. Barry saw the effects of these defeats first hand, as the mutual aid of the strike gave way to desperation and the destruction of former mining areas by a vengeful government. There were successes, most notably the Workmates group on the privatised part of the Tube, but that also swerved the same organisational question by staying independent – it wasn’t part of SF and as far as I know no one outside the originators ever joined SF. The arguments around SF’s industrial strategy, of building trust and organisation in a workplace and then tackling issues from that base are not new[2] – but the obstacles to winning over new people to an anarcho-syndicalist project through this activity remain substantial.

One of the commitments of the KSL has always been to uncover the motivations and actions of the unknown militants, who didn’t leave piles of writings for posterity. Barry was assertive that we hear the true voices of our forebears, not mediated by what we think now and what we want to bolster our own current views. We are much richer for that approach. The histories published by KSL are accessible to the general reader. The context is there. The achievements are many: Recognising the importance of Guillamon’s work on the Spanish revolution and ending the myth of the spontaneous uprising in 1936, achieved without any groundwork. And his work on the early 20th century movement and Emma Goldman stands out.

He kept looking for ways to spread the ideas of anarchism, and always in an outward-facing way. Whether through solidarity with strikers and others in struggle, through engaging with younger anarchists, or through the achievements of the Kate Sharpley Library he was always ready to share his experiences and knowledge and improve our understanding. To be an anarchist is hard, there’s a lot to live up to, and it’s important to understand the ways in which we all contribute. Barry was …

author: James Crump
title: Dockworkers From 100 Ports to Disrupt Military and Energy Supplies to Israel
content:
Dock and port workers from 17 countries will disrupt and block exports to Israel on Friday, with workers joining from countries including Italy, Mexico, Turkey, the US, Morocco and India.


Representatives from more than 100 ports will participate in the international day of action on 30 October, calling for an end to Israel’s genocide against Palestinians and “US-Israeli wars of aggression”.


The Palestinian BDS National Committee (BNC)


announced on X

 that workers will take action by “peacefully disrupting and blocking the transfer of military, energy and other dual-use supplies to Israel, including by refusing to handle such supplies”.


Workers will also pressure governments to impose a full military embargo on Israel and end “trade, economic and academic relations serving its illegal occupation and apartheid”.


Explaining the day of action, the BNC said that Israel’s “criminal wars” are “exacerbating the cost of living and economic crises worldwide”.


“Military budgets are swelling in the colonial West, while families and workers struggle with the cost of health, housing, transportation, and education. Our struggles are interlinked,” it stated.


A further 17 Palestinian trade unions and federations have endorsed the action, stating: “Our struggle for justice in Palestine is inseparable from the global struggle against systemic racism, militarisation, exploitation, climate devastation and all forms of oppression.”


The day of action comes a year after dockworkers in Italy

blocked the ports

 of Genoa and Livorno, with unions closing schools and stopping transportation as part of an Italy-wide general strike in response to Israel preventing the

Global Sumud Flotilla

 from reaching Gaza in 2025.


The flotilla was the largest ever naval mission to attempt to deliver humanitarian supplies to Gaza, with around 20 vessels carrying delegates from at least 44 countries.


The flotilla was subject to drone attacks before being illegally intercepted by Israel in international waters. Those on board were detained and have accused Israeli forces of subjecting them to human rights abuses including assault, degrading treatment, and the withholding of medical care.

author: By L. Cam Anderson, Contributor
title: How The Proud Boys Lost Their Name
content:
West Palm Beach, FL – On Sept. 26, the film “American Martyrs” premiered at the Kravis Center’s Cohen Pavilion in West Palm Beach, Florida. 


The subject of the film, presented by the far-right media outlet Gateway Pundit, was the Proud Boys – specifically the “seditious five,” whom a federal jury found guilty of seditious conspiracy to stop the presidential transfer of power for their role in the Jan. 6, 2021 storming of the U.S. Capitol.


The official poster for the film, promoted by Enrique Tarrio and Gateway Pundit on X ahead of its premiere. Note that Zachary Rehl, first on the left in the lineup, is AI-generated.


The five Proud Boys presenting the film were chairman Henry “Enrique” Tarrio, Ethan Nordean, Joe Biggs, Zachary Rehl and Dominic Pezzola. In reality, the actual fifth member of the “seditious five” is Jeremy Bertino, not Pezzola, who pleaded guilty and testified against the others during their trial. 


In August 2025, Bertino appeared on an episode of Tarrio’s Substack podcast titled “Kiss of Judas,” where the “government star witness” allowed the permanently sunglasses-clad chairman to humiliate him for the twelve people who liked the post. Despite this entreaty to re-enter the flock, Bertino did not make the cut as an “American martyr.”


Besides Tarrio, who received a full pardon, the others had the sentences commuted by executive order during President Donald Trump’s first day back in office on Jan. 20, 2025. 


The film premiere, held less than four miles from Trump’s Mar-a-Lago Club, was graced by numerous right-wing characters, including leading “Stop the Steal” figure and former New York City Mayor Rudy Giuliani,

QAnon digital warrior

 and former U.S. Army general Michael Flynn and convicted fraudster George Santos.


Led by right-wing media figure Lara Logan, the event opened at 7 p.m. with an open bar that overlapped with a 10-minute window set aside for “prayer, national anthem and pledge.”


After the 80-minute film concluded, the Gateway Pundit presented Tarrio with a Gateway Pundit-branded award created specifically for the occasion recognizing him “as an American Martyr and Hero.”


“It’s not an Emmy,” Tarrio wrote on X two days later. “But it’s so much better.”


[Source: Enrique Tarrio on X]


Despite the obvious connections to the Proud Boys organization, the premiere lacked any of the recognizable branding belonging to what it depicted as a persecuted “drinking fraternity.”


Even on Tarrio’s person, the golden cock and abbreviated name have given way to the branding for his streaming outfit, “War Boys,” which has gained a whopping 700 followers on Rumble since the channel was created in April last year.


And on Tarrio’s merch website – where the Afro-Cuban now in his 40s markets just about any idea as apparel, including a t-shirt reading “Enrique Tarrio Eats Cream Pies” with an AI illustration of Tarrio licking an over-sized cream pie – reveals a distinct absence of Proud Boys related merchandise.


[Source: Enrique Tarrio on X]


Tarrio’s ability to capitalize on Proud Boys merchandising, which once characterized his merch store, hit a setback last year when a D.C. Superior Court judge awarded the brand to a historically-Black church following a years-long legal battle set in the wake of the 2020 Presidential election.


At the beginning of 2025, the Metropolitan African Methodist Episcopal (MAME) church was the only place one could purchase official Proud Boys merchandise, re-branded to signify Black pride, with proceeds going toward the church’s community justice fund.


In April 2025, the church’s hold on the brand was tested on the Hudson Valley Proud Boys, who were sued in the Southern District Court of New York for their continued usage of the Proud Boys branding and merchandising.


The court reached a default judgment against the Hudson Valley Proud Boys, a chapter associated with Tarrio, earlier this year on April 8, awarding MAME $75,000 for trademark infringement and nearly $200,000 in attorney’s fees.


The judgment against the Hudson Valley Proud Boys is only a small part of the church’s pursuit to be fully compensated in the amount awarded by the court, which continues to be a major struggle to this day and sees all related parties continue to be wrapped up in the ongoing court battle.


On the night of Dec. 12, 2020, the streets of Washington were thronged with black shirts and red caps.

title: On en a marre - en Suisse aussi!
content:
Wir haben es satt. Alle am 31. Oktober nach Zürich in den Kreis 4.


Seit drei Jahren offener Genozid. Kriege überall. Bilder von Polizei und Faschist*innen, die Hand in Hand die Jugend ihrer Länder verstümmeln.

 La police mutile les lycéen-s!

 Unterdrückung, Polizeistaat und Faschismus, so sichbar wie schon lange nicht mehr.


An diesen Punkt sind wir nicht ohne Grund gekommen. Denn die Herrschenden nutzen ihre Macht, um die Ressourcen dieser Welt nach ihrem Kalkül einzusetzen. Das heisst, das Geld geht ins Militär, anstatt in die Schulen. Das heisst das Geld geht in KI, anstatt in den Klimaschutz. Das heisst das Geld wird in die Polizei investiet, anstatt in antipatriarchale Projekte. Das heisst offene Grenzen für Kapital und geschlossene Grenzen für all diejenigen, die durch die Kriege des Kapitals ihre Lebenswelt verlieren. Kurz, der Status Quo ist nicht einfach so passiert.

Die Herrschenden haben sich - wenn auch nicht als homogener Block - für ihn entschieden.


In der Summe haben sie den Krieg der Pflege und Care, die Polizei der Gerechtigkeit, KI der Ökologie und Genozid der Erinnerung und

Reparation

 vorgezogen haben. Hervorheben wollen wir dabei auch, dass die genannten Probleme nicht isoliert betrachtet werden können. Die Herrschenden finanzieren ihre Kriege und Genozide mit dem Geld, dass dann anderswo fehlt.

Es ist ein und dieselbe Rechnung.

 Und aus eigener Tasche bezahlen sie es sicher NIE! Aka, wir alle bezahlen es. In der heilen Schweiz immerhin (noch) nicht mit unserem Leben. Und die Verantwortlichen sitzen tagtäglich vor unseren Nasen. Was eine Gesamtscheisse! Zum Glück findet der Kampf dagegen gerade wieder Wege in die Festung Europa.

The kids are alright after all!


Wir lehne dabei das Narrativ ab, es handle sich einach um Schüler*innenproteste. Erstens geht es schon lange nicht mehr um "Protest" es geht um Konfrontation und die Weigerung, sich zu unterwerfen.

Der Geist des Aufstands geht um in Europa.

 Zweitens waren es von Beginn an nicht einfach Schüler*innenproteste, sondern eine viel breitere Bewegung, die ihre Lebensrealität nicht mehr akzeptieren wollte. Und die Poteste waren von Beginn an militant. Wehe all denen, die Denken, die

Casseurs

 hätten die Bewegung unterwandert. Nein, die

Casseurs

 sind Teil der Bewegung und es gilt, sich uneingeschränkt mit ihnen zu solidarisieren. Ihre Handlungen verstehen wir als revolutionäre Akte der Kollektivierung, Vorboten einer möglichen Welt. Ein kleines bisschen Gerechtigkeit blitzt auf in jeder zerbrochenen Scheibe der sonst für uns unbezahlbaren Innenstädte. Solidarität mit allen

Zerbrecher*innen

 dieser Welt!

Wir haben euch lieb.


Solidarität mit den aktuellen Unruhen in Europa kann dabei nicht nur bedeuten, Soli-Posts zu veröffentlichen. Echte Solidarität muss materiell spürbar sein. Echte Solidarität bedeutet, wenn unsere Geschwister auf die Stasse gehen, dann gehen wir auch. Echte Solidarität bedeutet, wenn

die Anderen

 auf die Fresse bekommen, dann auch wir. Solidarität bedeutet, wir stehen zusammen auf, lassen einander nicht allein und kämpfen Seite an Seite. Auch wenn es ungemütlich wird.

Denn niemand ist frei, sind wir nicht alle frei!


In diesem Sinn:

On en a marre - en Suisse aussi!

 Let's join the fight. 31. Oktober 22Uhr Kreis 4, Zürich. Weitere Daten werden Folgen.

Vive l'insurrection!


Wir möchten mit diesem Aufruf keine avantgardistische Position in der aktuellen Bewegung einnehmen. Wir haben lediglich entschieden, dass wir nicht mehr warten können und die Initative ergriffen. Wir freuen uns über jeden weiteren Aufruf, über jede weitere Aktion. Lasst uns die Schweiz in Aufruhr versetzen. Am 5.11. ist Generalstreik in Frankreich, am 20.11. Aktionstag in ganz Europa. title: Η αντιφασισατική Θεσσαλονίκη έδωσε απάντηση σε φασίστες, Κασιδιάρη, κυβερνητική τρομοκρατία, αστυνομική βία
content:
Οι αντιφασίστες της Θεσσαλονίκης έδωσαν το παρόν στο άγαλμα Βενιζέλου επί της Εγνατίας όπου είχε καλεστεί συγκέντρωση ενάντια στη φασιστοσύναξη του νεοναζί Κασιδιάρη σε ξενοδοχείου του Βαρδαρίου. Όμως τα κυβερνητικά σχέδια προστασίας του προσφάτως αποφυλακισθέντα χρυσαυγίτη, ακολούθησαν η απαγόρευση της συγκέντρωσης από την αστυνομία και τελικά η εκτεταμμένη χρήση βίας από τα ΜΑΤ που είχαν ζώσει την περιοχή.


Οι αντιφασίστες πολίτες ανταποκρίθηκαν στα καλέσματα σωματείων, συλλόγων, οργανώσεων, συλλογικοτήτων και προήλθαν από  ευρύ πολιτικό φάσμα: τον αντιεξουσιαστικό χώρο, τη ριζοσπαστική αριστερά, το ΚΚΕ. Έδειξαν δε μεγάλη αποφασιστικότητα στην πραγματοποίηση της συγκέντρωσης και παρέμειναν στο χώρο παρά τα χημικά, τα δακρυγόνα, τις κρότου λάμψης που έπεσαν σωρηδόν από την ελληνική αστυνομία και τις δύο προσαγωγές.


Χαρακτηριστικά του δυναμισμού και παλμού της αντιφασιστικής συγκέντρωσης ήταν και συνθήματα που καταγράφηκαν: Μπλόκο στους φασίστες, καμιά ανοχή στα τσιράκια των αφεντικών. Είστε η σαπίλα όλου του ντουνιά, μπλόκο στους φασίστες σε κάθε γειτονιά. Φασίστες από το λαό θα τη βρείτε. Το φασισμό τσακίζουν αγώνες λαϊκοί. Έξω οι νεοναζί από τη Θεσσαλονίκη. Στη φυλακή οι νεοναζί. Φασίστες, χίτες, μαυραγορίτες. Ούτε σπιθαμή γής στους φασίστες. Ούτε με φυλακές, ούτε με νόμους, ο φασισμός τσακίζεται στους δρόμους.

author: Julius Gavroche
title: Intifada and fascism. Resisting humans, affirming monsters
content:
by Rodrigo Karmy Bolton


from

Ficción de la razón

, 27/10/2026


It has become fashionable, thanks to sociological bureaucracy, to claim that the danger of any uprising is that it leads to fascism. That fascism can capitalise on it, turn it into an electoral and political enterprise, and triumph by harnessing its power and transforming it into a force. They used to say that revolt expresses “anomie” – that is, a normative mismatch with social dynamics – and that it was “violent” and “senseless” in that it involved burning things, looting shops and disrupting the “normal” flow of events. Now they say it leads to fascism and that, for that reason, it must be avoided at all costs. That if Le Pen wins at the French polls, it will have been due to the undeniable revolt; for if

Kast

 won in Chile, his victory would have been due precisely to that. The revolt would be anomic, violent and, moreover, reactionary. Nothing could be more of a threat to progressivism than the people taking to the streets; nothing could torment its pedagogical mindset more than a crowd on a war footing.


But there are certain things here—too long-standing, too antiquated—which, nevertheless, must be recalled: first and foremost, the argument that revolt leads to fascism (however complex it may be) obscures the question of why fascism exists, why it arose, if not from decades of violent neoliberal reforms which have literally left people on the streets, landless,

with no place in the world

. How are we to interpret the case of 87-year-old

Maricarmen

, who was evicted from the house she was renting because she could not pay the rent? Evicted from their homes and left out in the open, the people today are all Palestinians; they are all Maricarmen: they live landless, homeless, with a longing to return. Neoliberal reforms that have been imposed across the globe and which have now entered a new phase in their process of intensification, where they have had to resort to “so-called primitive accumulation” to escape the stagnation that their own model – their own “civilisation” – has produced.


In its various forms, neo-fascism—steeped in melancholic passions and capitalising on public panic—has been the means by which the model has chosen to realise itself, accelerating its processes of accumulation. To this end, it needs to bury any form of state-legal framework capable of curbing or containing its momentum, thereby hastening the fulfilment of a sort of “

parousia

” of capital in which, at last, capital encounters no restraints whatsoever and is definitively consolidated upon the earth. A new process of plunder, dispossession and conquest of the earth has begun to consolidate the new machine of death: the artificial intelligence corporations that have made war the leap through which they seek to break free from their own stagnation. Led by the super-rich, the violent process of acceleration through which they set out to appropriate new lands is meeting with resistance.


The global intifada—which is nothing other than a field of multiple interdependencies—becomes the disruption of worlds rising up against the levelling imposed by capital. Whilst the latter strips peoples of their lands, their landscapes and their places, the intifadas disrupt this levelling to reweave interdependencies between worlds precisely where capital and its globalisation seek to triumph: without distance, without fissures, without chasms—merely bodies pressed together. Capitalism reveals itself today in a completely transparent manner. There is no need to dream of a “behind-the-scenes” force manipulating history; it is enough to experience what happens every day: psychological disasters, the proliferation of genocides, the frantic efforts to work in the informal sector, widespread precariousness, and the systematic exclusion from our cultural, social and political rights. The repeated discourses of the old fogies who thought they were lecturing us after the October uprising—claiming that the uprising was lawless, violent and, moreover, that it would lead to fascism—believed themselves to be effective, but strictly speaking, they have been nothing but empty words, like all pedagogy today.


Young people have taken to the streets. Uninterrupted, for years now: today in France, Spain and Albania; previously in Chile, Iraq and the United States. The old fogies tell young people that they are “apolitical”, that they admire Spider-Man rather than Lenin, and they resort …

author: Simon Childs
title: Far-Right Loser Flávio Bolsonaro Flees Brazil After Election Defeat
content:
Far-right presidential election loser Flávio Bolsonaro has fled Brazil and is on his way to Florida, allegedly to claim political asylum.


The defeated senator, who lost to leftwing incumbent Luiz Inácio Lula da Silva in a stunning defeat on Sunday, disappeared for 24 hours before Argentinian migration authorities announced he had entered the country on Tuesday night.


There, Bolsonaro boarded a flight to the United States which made a brief stop in Ecuador before heading to Miami,

the Guardian reported

on Wednesday.


The

US State Department confirmed

 it would grant visas to the far-right candidate and his family on Tuesday, while president Donald Trump

said he “approved”

 of Bolsonaro coming to the US..


There was confusion earlier in the week over Bolsonaro’s whereabouts, with conflicting media reports and some sources saying he was already on his way to the US, when in fact he was in Argentina.


On Tuesday night, Argentine migration authorities confirmed that Bolsonaro and his family had crossed the border with Argentina and then boarded a plane to Ecuador.


In a post on X

, Argentina’s migration authorities said: “They did so with valid travel documentation and without any legal impediment to entering the country. Furthermore, the transits were recorded by the competent authority without incident.”


Bolsonaro’s apparent flight from Brazil comes after the Supreme Court ordered him to surrender his passport as part of an investigation into allegations of money laundering.


After he lost the election on Sunday, Bolsonaro insisted he would lead the opposition to the leftwing president. However, after Brazil’s Supreme Court gave him 24 hours to hand over his passport, he missed the deadline and boarded a flight.


Lula condemned Bolsonaro’s apparent decision to flee. “This is what the family Bolsonaro are like,” he said. “Brazil is their second homeland. Their first homeland is licking the boots of the US, as he’s become accustomed to doing.”


“I keep imagining what’s on the conscience of a citizen who just lost the elections and flees his country… He who owes nothing, fears nothing. A citizen who sneaks out of his country owes something. The act of leaving Brazil is shameful.”

author: Sharon Zhang
title: Report: Trump Admin Backing Far Right Viktor Orbán for UN Secretary-General
content:
The former Hungarian prime minister is “the dream MAGA-conservative candidate,” one US official said.

Did you know that Truthout is a nonprofit and independently funded by readers like you? If you value what we do, please support our work with a donation.

The Trump administration has reportedly advocated for far right authoritarian Viktor Orbán, ex-prime minister of Hungary, to serve in the top role at the United Nations amid the administration’s mission to weaken the organization and its role in advancing human rights across the globe.

According to The Wall Street Journal’s editorial board, sources from three countries have said that the U.S. is backing Orbán for UN secretary-general when the new term starts on January 1, 2027, and originally pitched him on the idea, which could be announced after the U.S. midterm elections.

The plan is far-fetched. The far right icon spent his 16 years as prime minister plunging Hungary into fascist authoritarianism, eroding human rights and maintaining power and control through corruption, police violence, surveillance, and censorship. The U.S. State Department has previously recognized “significant human rights issues” in Hungary under Orbán, before his surprise ousting by Péter Magyar earlier this year. Many scholars and commentators warned that Orbán’s rule demonstrated the signs of fascism.

As head of the UN, Orbán would likely seek to advance the far right’s agenda on the world stage, and could “act as an apologist for Vladimir Putin and other dictators,” WSJ’s editorial board wrote.

But the U.S. is willing to set such concerns aside for the rabidly anti-immigrant and anti-LGBTQ figure because he is “the dream MAGA-conservative candidate,” a U.S. official said. Trump administration officials have a favorable view of “his moves against mass migration, liberal NGOs and Hungary’s left-leaning courts and press,” WSJ noted.

Candidates for UN secretary-general have to be approved first by the 15-member Security Council before coming to a vote by the General Assembly.

The Security Council’s five permanent members have sometimes acted as a check on each other with their veto powers. However, a bid by Orbán may also have the support of Russia and China, sources said, and he could even be a joint candidate put forth by the three countries.

It’s unclear how the U.K. and France will react. The U.K. is reportedly leaning toward backing Emirati diplomat Lana Nusseibeh for the role, despite criticisms over the country’s role in funding genocidal forces in Sudan. Right-wing U.K. paper The Times reported that the U.K. and France are opposed to an Orbán bid for secretary-general.

“I cannot overstate the virulent opposition they both have to this idea,” one European diplomat told the paper.

But the U.S., especially under Donald Trump’s second term, has approached global diplomacy with its own authoritarian mindset, wielding the U.S.’s vast power to coerce rather than persuade; Secretary of State Marco Rubio’s punitive campaign to dismantle the International Criminal Court (ICC) has spurred several countries to withdraw from the body.

Several figures have criticized the decision. Republican Rep. Don Bacon (R-Nebraska) said it was a “terrible decision.” Ukraine’s foreign affairs minister, Andrii Sybiha, said that Orbán “would put to good use the masterful veto and blackmail skills he has developed over years of derailing major EU decisions.”

Polish Prime Minister Donald Tusk laughed off the WSJ report. “Just a moment ago, he was a candidate for president of the European Commission. This seems to me just as funny as that first rumor,” a smiling Tusk told Politico on Monday.

title: Αντιφασιστικός συναγερμός στη Θεσσαλονίκη
content:
Αντιφασιστικός συναγερμός στη Θεσσαλονίκη.


Η ανακοίνωση της ομιλίας του, πρόσφατα αποφυλακισθέντα του πρώην μέλους της εγκληματικής οργάνωσης της Χρυσής Αυγής, Ηλία Κασιδιάρη, στη Θεσσαλονίκη ξύπνησε για τα καλά τα αντιφασιστικά αντανακλαστικά της πόλης. Μιας πόλης όπου ο φασισμός δεν κυριάρχησε ποτέ στον δρόμο. Δεν το κατάφερε ούτε το 2012-2013 που η Χρυσή Αυγή αλώνιζε σε πολλές περιοχές της χώρας αλλά ούτε και το 2017-2019 κατά την περίοδο των μακεδονικών συλλαλητηρίων που όλες οι συνθήκες τους ευνοούσαν αλλά το αντιφασιστικό κίνημα της πόλης τους έκοψε τον βήχα. Ο Κασιδιάρης διάλεξε την επέτειο της 28ης Οκτωβρίου για να μιλήσει στο ξενοδοχείο Capsis στον σιδηροδρομικό σταθμό, ιστορικά ένα από τα λιγοστά καταφύγια των φασιστών στη Θεσσαλονίκη. Αναρχικές και αριστερές οργανώσεις αλλά και σωματεία εργαζομένων που πρόσκεινται στο ΠΑΜΕ έχουν βγάλει καλέσματα για αντιφασιστική συγκέντρωση στο άγαλμα Βενιζέλου στις 16:00 και στις 15:30 αντίστοιχα. Ακολουθούν τα καλέσματα:


Αντιφασιστική συγκέντρωση ενάντια στην παρουσία Κασιδιάρη


Ούτε σπιθαμή γης στους εχθρούς του ανθρώπου


Αντιφασιστική συγκέντρωση ενάντια στην παρουσία του νεοναζί Κασιδιάρη στην πόλη μας –


Τετάρτη 28/10 – 16:00 στο Άγαλμα Βενιζέλου


ΑΓΩΝΑΣ ΓΙΑ ΖΩΗ ΚΑΙ ΕΛΕΥΘΕΡΙΑ


Συλλογικότητα για τον Κοινωνικό Αναρχισμό- Μαύρο & Κόκκινο μέλος της Αναρχικής Πολιτικής Οργάνωσης – Ομοσπονδίας Συλλογικοτήτων


Όλοι/όλες/όλα στην αντιφασιστική συγκέντρωση για την προσπάθεια εμφάνισης του καταδικασμένου νεοναζί Κασιδιάρη


Ούτε σπιθαμη γης στους νοσταλγούς των ναζί


Και τώρα και πάντα και όπως το 40,


την φτώχεια και τον φασισμό θα πολεμάμε πάντα!


Φασίστες θα σας θάψουμε, όσα ονόματα κι αν αλλάξετε.


Την Τετάρτη 28/10, στις 5μμ στο πάντα φιλόξενο για τους νεοναζί ξενοδοχείο Capsis στην Θεσσαλονίκη, ο πρόσφατα αποφυλακισθέντας φασίστας και πάλαι ποτέ Νο2 της Χρυσής Αυγής Ηλίας Κασιδιάρης, καλεί σε συγκέντρωση τους οπαδούς του. Αυτό το σκουπίδι τολμάει να βγει από την τρύπα του την ημέρα που μνημονεύεται η έναρξη της αντίστασης του αγωνιζόμενου λαού αυτού του τόπου στις δυνάμεις των ιδεολογικών του προγόνων, των φασιστών του Μουσολίνι και αργότερα των Ναζί του 3ου Ράιχ. Ειναι ο πολιτικός και φυσικός απόγονος εκείνων των εγχώριων καθαρμάτων, δοσίλογων και ταγματασφαλητών, που στην διάρκεια της Κατοχής συνεργάστηκαν με τις δυνάμεις του Άξονα, που κατέδιδαν, βασάνιζαν και δολοφονούσαν αγωνιστές και πλούτιζαν από το λαθρεμπόριο ενώ γύρω τους βασίλευε ο θάνατος.


Υπό την σκέπη ενός νέου κόμματος πλέον, της Συμμαχίας Ελλήνων, η οποία – όπως ανακοίνωσαν και οι ίδιοι- μετράει ήδη κοινοβουλευτική παρουσία μέσα από τις μεταπηδήσεις διαφόρων μπροστινών του από αλλά ακροδεξιά κόμματα, ο Κασιδιάρης φιλοδοξεί να επιστρέψει στην κεντρική πολιτική σκηνή. Σε αυτή του την προσπάθεια δεν είναι μόνος. Στην απόπειρά του να χτίσει το προφίλ του δήθεν “αντισυστημικού”, του έχουν παράσχει πολύτιμες υπηρεσίες τα καθεστωτικά ΜΜΕ, που προσπαθώντας δήθεν να τον στοχοποιήσουν ως επικίνδυνο, ουσιαστικά τον ηρωοποιούν στα μάτια μεγάλης μερίδας της κοινωνίας, η οποία έχει σιχαθεί την καθημερινή προπαγάνδα τους και τα αφεντικά τους και αντιλαμβάνεται έτσι τον Κασιδιάρη ως αντίπαλό τους. Το πόσο πολύ “αντισυστημικός” είναι, τόσο αυτός όσο και ο κάθε φασίστας, αποδεικνύεται περίτρανα από αυτούς που του κάνουν πλάτες: Ένας από τους μεγαλύτερους βιομήχανους της χώρας και αθλητικός παράγοντας, ο Δ. Π. Γιαννακόπουλος, έσπευσε να τον στηρίξει πολιτικά, ανοιχτά και δημόσια. Κάτι βέβαια που δεν πρέπει να μας εκπλήσσει, καθώς είναι γνωστό πως οι φασίστες αποτελούν το μακρύ χέρι του Κεφαλαίου σε περιόδους κρίσης.


Αυτό το τελευταίο είναι άλλωστε που συμβαίνει και σε παγκόσμιο επίπεδο, από τις ΗΠΑ και την Λατινική Αμερική, μέχρι την Κεντρική Ευρώπη, όπου το σύστημα έχει ήδη σχηματίσει την εκλεκτή ακροδεξιά του πτέρυγα (πχ το AfD στην Γερμανία και την Λεπέν στην Γαλλία) και την προετοιμάζει να αναλάβει δράση, σε περίπτωση που οι από-τα-κάτω αποφασίσουν να διεκδικήσουν πίσω τις ζωές τους. Η διαίρεση και η αποδυνάμωση της τάξης μας με βάση την φυλή, την θρησκεία, την γλώσσα είναι το αρχικό σχέδιο. Το βίαιο τσάκισμά της είναι η επόμενη επιλογή, σε περίπτωση που το πρώτο πλάνο αποτύχει. Το πιο ξεκάθαρο πρόσφατο παράδειγμα για όλα τα παραπάνω είναι το ξαμόλημα των φασιστικών συμμοριών απέναντι στους εξεγερμένους στην Γαλλία, σε τουλάχιστον 15 διαφορετικές πόλεις, ενώ στην Ιταλία, όπου η ακροδεξιά είναι επίσημα στην κυβέρνηση, διατάχθηκε απαγόρευση κυκλοφορίας και επιστρατεύεται ο στρατός απέναντι στους …

author: Sara Fayyazi
title: Making Women’s History Part of the Curriculum
content:
Two teachers from Sacred Heart Preparatory School in California, Kristen Kelly and Serene Williams, have proposed an Advanced Placement U.S. Women’s History course in response to the issue of students not learning about women’s history. The courses would allow studying women’s experiences and contributions in greater depth. Establishing this course would create a better understanding of American history as it includes the diverse experiences of women and would help students connect the historical struggles for equality to gender issues today.

Women have contributed to shaping the nation’s politics, economy, and social movements, yet their participation is often overlooked by traditional history classes. From fighting for the right to vote, challenging discrimination, and advocating for female autonomy, women have had a significant role in building the foundation of the United States today.

One of the main arguments for WAPUSH is that women’s experiences are not explored in the classroom. In the article Educational Activism: Creating an AP U.S. Women’s History Course, Serene Williams, Kristen Kelly, and Clara Robinson explain that topics such as women’s suffrage and reproductive rights receive limited attention in the current AP U.S. History curriculum. The women’s suffrage movement involved decades of organizing, political campaigning, and resistance. However, teachers may not introduce this topic to students or have enough time to examine its strategies and leaders in detail. A dedicated course would allow students to study these movements more thoroughly and understand how women helped shape American democracy.

Women’s history is much broader than the fight for voting rights. The proposed WAPUSH curriculum includes women’s labor, politics, religion, culture, war, and violence against women. It also examines how race, class, sexuality, religion, and other identities shaped women’s experiences. This approach is important because women throughout the years have never shared one universal experience. Indigenous women, Black women, Immigrant women, etc., have faced different opportunities and forms of discrimination. Studying these differences would help students develop a greater understanding of American history and that America was not built on just our founding fathers, but by women who paved the path for opportunity and development through blood, sweat, and tears.

An AP course would also help students recognize the connection between historical events and current issues. The debate over reproductive rights and other feminist struggles today cannot be fully understood without examining the laws and political movements that shaped access to contraceptives, abortion, and female economic support. Studying topics from the suffrage movement to the Equal Rights Amendment can help students understand the political equality that has developed through activism and engage in feminist discussion. Learning this history would give students the context needed to evaluate debates instead of viewing them as different events.

Establishing this course would show that women’s history is worthy of advanced academic study. The WAPUSH campaign began in 2022, and according to its website, the campaign gathered more than 4,000 petition signatures and received encouragement from College Board leadership as it worked toward launching this course. Its proposal has also received university support, while the campaign continues seeking letters from high schools willing to offer the course. This continued support brings women closer to bringing light to women’s history and giving women a space in school systems and curricula. This petition is one step closer every day to its goal to educate and inform people all across America of women’s contributions.

An AP U.S. Women’s History course would make education more comprehensive, inform students even more about the history of the U.S., and connect past struggles to present issues. Women have influenced American politics, economics, culture, and social movements, yet their experiences are not always given sufficient attention in existing courses. By offering students an opportunity to examine these experiences, the College Board could help create a more inclusive and accurate understanding of the nation’s past. Women’s history is not separate from American history but instead an essential part of it.

author: Unknown
title: "Women, Justice and Memory" vigil in Amed: “Rojda is not alone”
content:
Women’s organizations have once again protested against patriarchal violence, femicides, and impunity for perpetrators outside the courthouse in Amed (Turkish: Diyarbakır). The “Women, Justice and Memory,” organized by the Network Against Violence, entered its fourth week on Tuesday. Alongside representatives of political parties and civil society organizations, Rojda Odabaşı also took part in today’s demonstration. She had survived an attack in late August when a neighbor shot at her with a shotgun in her apartment.


The participants carried photographs of murdered women and a banner reading “Women hold vigil for justice and memory,” chanting “Jin, Jiyan, Azadî,” “Femicide is political,” and “Long live women’s struggle.”


ÖHD: Rojda’s safety must be ensured immediately


The demonstration focused on demands for protection and justice for Rojda Odabaşı. The suspect had been released late last week following the armed attack on her. Aycan Diril, from the Women’s Commission of the Association of Lawyers for Freedom (ÖHD), criticized the decision and called for a thorough investigation into the case. “We demand that Rojda’s safety be ensured immediately, that the decision to release the suspect be subjected to effective judicial review, and that every aspect of the attack, including possible intent to kill, be investigated. We will continue to follow this case. Rojda is not alone,” Diril declared.


The lawyer emphasized that the vigil was intended not only to commemorate women who had been killed but also to highlight the responsibility of state institutions. This week, the focus was on seven women who were killed or died under unclear circumstances between October 18 and 26. Representatives of the participating organizations shared their stories.


Killed despite protection orders


Criticism of the state’s failure to protect women from violence was particularly evident in the cases of Sevda Dinler and Perihan Akbulut. Both women were killed despite having already obtained protection orders against the suspected or eventual perpetrators. Sevda Dinler, a 22-year-old graduate of a vocational school of health sciences, was shot dead with a hunting rifle on October 21 in the Kozan district of Adana. According to media reports, she had rejected Gamber Fidan’s advances and had subsequently been threatened and stalked by him. A protection order had been issued against the man. Following the killing, he was arrested and placed in pretrial detention.


Perihan Akbulut, a 61-year-old mother of five, was stabbed to death in the street the following day in Yeşilyurt, in Malatya. She sustained eight stab wounds. A protection order had also been issued against her husband, Hasan Akbulut. The perpetrator died in hospital after attempting suicide while being pursued by police.


“Femicide is not an unforeseeable event. Previous violence, threats, persistent stalking, and applications for protection orders are often warning signs. When a woman is killed despite a known risk to her life, it must also be investigated whether state authorities fulfilled their duty to protect her,” the statement said. The activists linked this criticism to the economic conditions that can prevent women from leaving abusive relationships. They opposed political attacks on alimony rights and highlighted the lack of security regarding housing, income, and caregiving responsibilities.


Femicides and unexplained deaths


The vigil also commemorated Melek Altınboğa and Aliye Aker. Melek Altınboğa, a 30-year-old mother of one, was killed with a hunting rifle by her husband, Murat Altınboğa, on October 18 in the Akören district of Konya. The couple had been married for just four months. The perpetrator subsequently injured himself with the same weapon. Women’s organizations criticized media reports that reduced the murder to a domestic dispute, thereby downplaying the patriarchal violence involved.

author: Tam Saavedra
title: The UN CRPD Guidelines on Intersectionality are Here!
content:
Ver versión en español


The UN CRPD Guidelines on Intersectionality Just Changed the Game for Disability Rights—Here’s What You Need to Know 


Big news for women with disabilities and all feminist disabled advocates, allies, and organizations worldwide!

 


During its 35th Session in August 2026, the

UN Committee on the Rights of Persons with Disabilities

 (UN CRPD)

 officially adopted the historic

Guidelines on Identifying and Addressing Intersectional Discrimination Against Girls, Adolescents, Women, and Older Women with Disabilities

.

 


This milestone represents a monumental step forward for disability rights. For the first time, States have explicit, actionable guidance to support their obligations at the intersection of gender and disability.

 


Read the official CRPD Guidelines here

 


What Are the CRPD Guidelines on Intersectional Discrimination?


The Guidelines serve as an authoritative framework developed by the UN


CRPD Committee to help States better prevent, monitor, and address intersectional discrimination.

 


Throughout years of UN CRPD country review processes, the Committee identified a persistent, critical gap:

the specific rights of women with disabilities and the complex, intersectional discrimination they experience are rarely understood or adequately addressed by governments.

 


As the UN CRPD celebrates its 20th anniversary, these Guidelines were issued to bridge that gap—ensuring the convention is implemented to benefit

all

 women, girls, and gender-diverse people with disabilities across their lifespans.

 


Why Are These Guidelines a Game


–

Changer?

 


International documents rarely explicitly focus on the detailed, lived experiences and rights of women with disabilities. These Guidelines clearly name and elaborate on the systemic barriers

 women and gender-diverse people with disabilities face daily across the globe, including:

 


Sexual & Reproductive Health and Rights (SRHR):

 Addressing and preventing enforced sterilization, forced contraception, lack of accessible healthcare, restrictions on abortion, and lack of perinatal, menstrual, and menopause care.

 


Gender-Based & Disability-Based Violence:

 Exposing institutional violence, digital/online abuse, and the widespread lack of support services for victims.

 


Caregiving Recognition:

 Validating women with disabilities as active caregivers and mothers, rather than only recipients of care.

 


Economic & Educational Exclusion:

 Highlighting barriers in the labor market, economic and exclusion from education during puberty.

 


Crisis & Climate Response:

 Tackling compounded exclusion during environmental disasters, climate emergencies, and humanitarian relief efforts.

 


…just to name a few.

 


7 Key Breakthroughs in the Framing of the Guidelines 

 


What makes this document uniquely transformative is its progressive, structural approach:

 


Explicit Inclusion of Gender Diversity:

 The Guidelines explicitly encompass the rights of transgender, intersex, non-binary, and other gender-diverse people with disabilities and ask for gender diversity – inclusive interpretation of all obligations described.

 


Recognition of Historical Root Causes:

 The Committee explicitly addresses the legacy and ongoing impacts of

colonialism and enslavement

, establishing that States benefiting from these historical systems bear a particular responsibility to remedy their ongoing effects.

 


An Open Catalogue of Diversity:

 The text recognizes that women with disabilities belong to multi-marginalized communities—including Indigenous, Black, Dalit, Adivasi, refugee, asylum-seeking, religious minority, and pastoralist groups or people living in informal settings, among others —while leaving space for all intersecting identities.

 


Structural & Preventive Approach:

 Moving beyond a strictly punitive, reactive model, the Guidelines demand the dismantling of systemic oppression (such as ableism, audism, racism, and patriarchy) through early intervention, education, and public policy reform. 

 


Decriminalization

 is also a disability issue:

The guidelines recognize impacts of criminalization of abortion, homosexuality, gender identity and expression as well as

restricting marriage or consensual relationships as an important intersectional disability rights issue.

 


Holding digital platforms accountable:

Call for international and regional cooperation on human rights-based regulation of …

title: New Evidence Allegedly Ties Trump to 11 Sexual Assaults Related to Epstein
content:
A new report notes several patterns of conduct that Trump and Epstein shared in recruiting victims.

Support justice-driven, accurate and transparent news — make a quick donation to Truthout today!

The House Judiciary Committee Democrats have released a trove of evidence regarding allegations of sexual assault, including a new rape allegation, against President Donald Trump in relation to Jeffrey Epstein that the lawmakers say has been deliberately covered up by the Department of Justice.

The 50-page report, released Monday, contains testimony from 11 women who either accuse Trump of rape or sexual assault or say that they had been offered to Trump for sex by Epstein or Ghislaine Maxwell, with most cases happening in the 1990s.

The accounts were pulled together through interviews conducted by the committee, as well as FBI records and the portion of the Epstein files that have been released; the evidence was cross-referenced for timelines and corroboration of testimony between alleged victims. In all, the evidence sharply contrasts Trump’s claims that he was merely an acquaintance of Epstein, and instead paints a picture of Trump as a serial sexual assault perpetrator who collaborated closely with Epstein to find and traffic victims.

“These women have spoken to investigators and, in some cases, testified under oath, yet Trump’s Justice Department has shut down investigations, deliberately withheld evidence and, through Todd Blanche, prevented Ghislaine Maxwell from discussing a survivor whose account implicated Trump,” said the committee’s ranking member, Rep. Jamie Raskin (D-Maryland). “Trump’s Justice Department appears to be covering up these crimes to protect the President.”

Five women said that Trump raped or assaulted them while Epstein was present or was in his company, as detailed in the report. The report also reveals, for the first time, Trump’s alleged rape of Beatrice Keul, who has previously said that Trump groped her.

Keul said that she was recruited to attend the Donald J. Trump American Dream Pageant in November 1993, and was approached by Trump at an event in the Plaza Hotel, which he owned at the time. She says that her passport was taken away when she entered the pageant, and that Trump promised her favors, including saying that then-modelling agent Paolo Zampolli — who was recently fired from a high-level position within the State Department — would “take care” of obtaining a visa for Keul, who is from Switzerland.

The report notes that Trump promised Keul that he could get her admitted to New York University — a promise that Epstein often made “to lure in and then control his victims,” the report says.

After that conversation, Epstein approached her, introducing himself as “Don’s best friend.” As Trump looked on, Epstein also made promises to Keul, including that he would arrange for her to travel to Mar-a-Lago for a party. “You know I can take care of you. We organize many parties with Don,” Epstein allegedly told her. Keul says that Trump raped her later that day, after sending an associate to invite her to a hotel room for a meeting; she described the rape as “brutal.”

The report corroborates Keul and Trump’s meeting with accounts from other women who say that Trump and Epstein used the pageant as a “hunting ground” to prey upon women.

The Democrats also collate other assaults committed by Trump in relation to Epstein, including numerous occasions where Trump allegedly forcibly kissed or groped a girl or woman while Epstein was present, as well as compiled evidence on the alleged assaults of young girls like the case of “Katie Johnson.”

The report establishes several patterns of behavior by Trump and Epstein in relation to victims.

The report notes, for instance, that Trump called Keul several months after the alleged assault to reiterate his offer for favors. Similarly, Trump also sent a postcard to model Stacey Williams, who briefly dated Trump, several months after allegedly assaulting her in Epstein’s presence to invite her to Mar-a-Lago.

The report notes that Epstein had a practice of calling foreign models to visit them in Florida, and that: “Trump and Epstein seemed to share the same playbook for recruiting and abusing women, all the way down to the university they promised admission to and the timing of their follow-up phone calls.”

author: Dominique Gené - Local Journalism Initiative Reporter
title: Nunavik school board to pilot sex-education program
content:
Kativik Ilisarniliriniq, Nunavik’s school board, will test a sexuality education program in Kuujjuaq and Umiujaq in November.


The pilot program was developed with the Nunavik Regional Board of Health and Social Services and is intended to help children understand personal boundaries and how to stay safe in sexual situations, said Sarah Aloupa, president of Kativik Ilisarniliriniq, in an interview.


“It’s important for parents to take this very seriously. This program is for the students’ well being,” she said.


Aloupa said the initiative responds to a need raised by Nunavik residents and parents. The school board’s council of commissioners heard a presentation from the health board about the proposed program in June.


The program will cover students from kindergarten to Grade 11, with information packages for different age groups.


Aloupa declined to share the teaching material.


The pilot is scheduled to run Nov. 2 to 6 at Jaanimmarik School and Pitakallak School in Kuujjuaq and Nov. 16 to 20 at Kiluutaq School in Umiujaq. The schools were chosen in part because they were ready to take part and have staff with relevant experience, said Jade Duchesneau-Bernier, spokesperson for the school board.


During those weeks, staff will participate in training and parents can review material and ask questions at evening information sessions.


Their feedback will help shape the final program. While the board has not yet clarified how parents can do so, they can opt their children out, Aloupa said.


Information about the sessions is being sent to parents through school letters and posted on Facebook.


Aloupa pointed to sexual abuse cases in the region as part of the broader need for education on the subject.


In February 2025, Nicolas Cyr, a physical education teacher at Jaanimmarik School, was

charged

 with sexual assault of a minor, sexual interference of a minor and assault.


The pilot is intended to help the Nunavik school board and the region’s health board assess the program before considering whether to expand it to the other 18 schools Kativik Ilisarniliriniq operates, Aloupa said.


The organizations have not yet set a timeline for a region-wide rollout.

author: Kelly Pavelich
title: Equality Culture Club: Make Equality Reality Bookstore
content:
Equality Culture Club: Make Equality Reality Bookstore


For the second time this year, Equality Now hosted a bookstore at the

Make Equality Reality

 Gala

, an arts-based celebration that brings together visionary leaders, powerful performances, and global changemakers committed to advancing gender equality, to highlight some of our favourite feminist titles. The books – both fiction and non-fiction and for readers of various ages – remind us of the urgency of our work and fill us with hope that a better world is possible. From us to you, enjoy the following recommendations straight from the Equality Now library.


A Hymn to Life

 by Gisèle Pelicot


In

A Hymn to Life

, Gisèle Pelicot tells her story for the first time, tracing a life built over five decades, the hidden abuse of her marriage’s final decade, and the long path to healing. Part memoir, part act of defiance, it is a moving portrait of survival and courage from a woman who broke her silence, reclaimed her voice, and forced a reckoning.


This year, Equality Now honoured Gisèle with the Equality Now Trailblazer Award, which honours individuals whose actions help transform the systems, institutions, and culture that shape the lives of women and girls.


Be Yourself and Other Bad Advice

 by Meredith Walker


Be Yourself and Other Bad Advice

 is part guidebook and part pep talk. The book is infused with humour and packed with practical tools to help teens and young adults figure out who they are, navigate emotions and life’s big questions, and build real confidence. It’s a perfect book for girls learning how to exist in the world. Featuring a foreword by Amy Poehler and stunning illustrations by Nina Cosford, it’s as lovely to look at as it is to read. Meredith attended this year’s Gala and signed copies of her book for guests.


 


For the Sun After Long Nights

 by Fatemeh Jamalpour and Nilo Tabrizy


For the Sun After Long Nights

 documents the rise of the Woman, Life, Freedom movement in Iran, one of Iran’s largest uprisings in decades, which began following the death of Mahsa Jîna Amini. Fatemeh, a local journalist, documented the movement on the ground as a fellow protestor, despite threats to her life, while Nilo reported from afar. The book represents their interwoven stories and sisterhood.


The Freedom Seeker

 by Ruchira Gupta


The Freedom Seeker

 is a young adult novel about an Indian girl whose parents’ interfaith marriage becomes the target of violence. To remain safe, they decide to flee Northern India. Her father leaves first, seeking refuge in the United States, but when her and her mother’s petition is denied, they are left with no choice but to try to reunite their family on their own. Ruchira’s other title,

I Kick and I Fly

, also appeared in our library. This young adult novel follows Heera, who is sold into the sex trade at the age of fourteen. She eventually has the opportunity to learn martial arts, which transforms her life. 


Like Meredith, we were fortunate to have Ruchira in attendance at this year’s

Make Equality Reality

Gala, where she signed books in the Equality Now library. Ruchira also contributed to our

Equality Culture Club interview series

, sharing why storytelling remains important, especially for a young audience; how her experience as a journalist has shaped her writing style; and what she envisions for a gender-equal future.


Nobody’s Girl

 by Virginia Roberts Giuffre


Nobody’s Girl

 is the memoir that Virginia Roberts Giuffre, Jeffrey Epstein and Ghislaine Maxwell’s most outspoken survivor, completed before her passing in April 2025. In it, she gives an unsparing account of her childhood abuse, her years being trafficked by Epstein and Maxwell to prominent men, her escape at nineteen, and the courage it took to hold her abusers to account and fight for other survivors. 


Equality Now was proud to posthumously present the Courage Award to Virginia Roberts Giuffre, an outspoken Epstein survivor, who spoke out when silence would have been easier. Virginia’s brother and sister-in-law, Sky and Amanda Roberts, accepted the award on her behalf.


Anjali Can!

 by Sheetal Sheth


In

Anjali Can!

, the third book in the Anjali picture book series, Anjali works to prevent her local community centre’s closure and shows the power one individual can have in enacting change. Sheetal joined Meredith, Ruchira, and Jackson Katz in the Gala’s library for a book signing after the program.

author: Sue Bolton, Sarah Hathway
title: Socialist Alliance: ‘Stop weaponising shocking attack on Helen Haines MP’
content:
Socialist Alliance condemns the terrible attack on Helen Haines MP and we send our best wishes to her and her family.

This shocking incident had been politically weaponised even before the facts were established; the corporate media and some MPs went looking to find someone to blame.

The Zionists and right-wing commentators were quick to blame the pro-Palestine movement, because the alleged perpetrator — along with the majority of people in Australia — was critical of Israel’s genocide in Gaza. It has become stock in trade for mainstream media to brand critics of Israel as “extremist”.

We now know the alleged perpetrator suffered from poor mental health and that their family was friends with the Haines family.

As pressures mount around housing affordability and the rising cost of living, poorly resourced mental health services, especially in regional and rural Victoria, may contribute to anti-social behaviour.

The 2021 Royal Commission into Victoria’s Mental Health System made 65 recommendations and nine interim recommendations. These largely remain unfunded or not implemented, despite the Victorian Labor government promising to do so.

An independent report earlier this year made 270 sub-recommendations — only 54 have been fully implemented.

Right-wing influencers and the manosphere are also playing a role in influencing a layer of more vulnerable people to take on extreme and conspiracist views.

Data from Women for Election shows that online abuse towards those in elected positions is negatively impacting those in office, those running for office and those considering doing so. Just under 90% of women surveyed reported experiencing online abuse or intimidation connected to their political participation.

No one should be threatened or made to feel fear for themselves or their family members.

This attack on Haines is happening in the context of one woman a week being killed by a current or former partner in Australia. Despite advocacy and mass mobilisations to stop violence against women, misogyny is still pervasive.

Abuse and threats of violence towards women are also on the rise.

Pauline Hanson’s One Nation Party has been aggressively whipping up hate and division. Its scapegoating of vulnerable groups, based on ethnicity, religion, immigration status, gender and ability, as the “cause” of societal problems is part of the political context.

The major parties are contributing to this divisiveness, either through policy or rhetoric. This is being exacerbated by the mainstream media’s clickbait.

As a result, it is not just elected representatives who are being targeted with threats and violence; people are being emboldened by divisive politics to target already marginalised groups with racial, gendered or other violence.

There are solutions, but One Nation doesn’t have them. And while the major parties steal One Nations’ immigration policies, they help fuel the tinderbox atmosphere of fear and hate.

The mainstream parties pander to the extremist right, because it helps them divide and rule.

[Sue Bolton is a Socialist Alliance councillor on Merri-Bek City Council and is the Socialist Alliance candidate for Broadmeadows in the Victorian election. Sarah Hathway is a former City of Greater Geelong Councillor and the Socialist Alliance candidate for Lara in the Victorian election.]

title: I’m fine with anyone using ‘dead naming’ for themselves. People have many reasons to have a painful…
content:
runicdesk

:

Trans sensitivity question!

Is the term ‘dead naming’ reserved for trans people, or can it be used for people who changed their name for other reasons? Thank you in advance.


I’m fine with anyone using 'dead naming’ for themselves. People have many reasons to have a painful association with their past name and if having a term that says ’

do not fucking use this name

’ is convenient for you: go for it.

But also, I may be an outlier, as I am trans and I hate the term 'dead naming’ and would never use it for myself.

I’m not dead. Nothing about me died. My past name isn’t a horrible memory that must never be uttered, it’s just a name I once used. It’s as mundane as my pre-transition pictures, which are still on my wall because my transness is not a dirty secret to be hidden.

Someone who uses my past name for me deliberately is being a transphobic asshole, but they don’t hold any power over me. I will not cry myself to sleep because they used the secret spell of trans pain. I’ll just think they’re a transphobic asshole and I’ll move on.

title: Join the HIV Awareness Week in Berlin to establish the Emergency Support Network
content:
We are organising two free-of-charge parallel training programmes for queer and trans people that will come together on Friday, 20 November, to establish the Emergency Support Network.


This network should help people navigate services, identify realistic pathways to HIV prevention and care, and receive support without having to navigate complex systems alone. We also want to recognise that Ballroom houses, queer and trans collectives, and migrant communities already provide essential care infrastructure. We intend to strengthen these existing relationships, rather than create a parallel system disconnected from the communities themselves.


The initiative is particularly focused on two target audience groups:


Queer and trans people living with HIV who face barriers to accessing healthcare, especially those without health insurance, appropriate documentation, or access to HIV treatment and other essential services.


Queer and trans people on the move, including migrants, refugees, asylum seekers and undocumented people, who face difficulties accessing healthcare, HIV prevention, testing, PrEP, PEP and treatment.


Community HIV Training — 16, 18 and 20 November


This programme is intended for queer and trans adults, particularly queer and trans youth aged 18 and over, migrants, refugees, asylum seekers, undocumented people and other people on the move.


It is especially relevant to queer and trans people who are living with HIV and face difficulties accessing treatment or healthcare, as well as those who need access to HIV prevention, testing, PrEP, PEP and other sexual health services.


The sessions will be interactive and community-led, covering HIV prevention and care, PrEP, PEP, testing, treatment, U=U, sexual health, pleasure, harm reduction and navigating healthcare systems.


An important feature is that registration for this programme is anonymous.

 Participants are not asked to provide their names, email addresses or HIV status. Anyone who wants to receive practical information or reminders can voluntarily register their email address through a separate form, which is not linked to their anonymous demographic responses.


This distinction is particularly important for people who may be reluctant to engage with services or activities because of concerns about confidentiality, stigma or their migration status.


register here


Health Champions Training — 17, 19 and 20 November


This programme is designed for trans and queer community leaders, particularly people involved in Ballroom houses, collectives and grassroots networks.


The training follows a train-the-trainer approach and will cover HIV, STIs and other infectious diseases prevention, treatment and sexual and reproductive health knowledge, and other topics like U=U, harm reduction, structural barriers to healthcare, peer education and safe healthcare navigation.


Participants will work through practical exercises such as community mapping, HIV knowledge games, real-life scenarios, role-play and referral mapping. The objective is to equip them to become trusted points of connection between their communities and healthcare services, while recognising that Health Champions are not expected to act as clinicians, legal experts or crisis responders.


On the final day, Health Champions will meet healthcare professionals, service providers and participants from the other training programme to help establish practical referral pathways and community-based support structures.


register here


Building the Emergency Support Network

—


20 November


On Friday, participants from both programmes will come together with healthcare professionals, community organisations and service providers.


The aim is to establish direct connections between people who need support, trusted community leaders and organisations capable of providing services. Participants will learn what support is available, who can access it, what barriers remain and how to make safe referrals.


The week will culminate in

Under the Jellicle Moon Kiki Ball on Saturday, 21 November

, celebrating Ballroom culture, community leadership and the relationships developed throughout the initiative.


Note:

All workshop participants must be 18 or older and attend all three days of their respective training. Snacks and dinner will be provided each day.

transporte público

 para que as pessoas não chegassem às urnas a uma grande imprensa tacanha jogando contra –

um homem de 81 anos, que tem os olhos do mundo virados para si, mostra publicamente afeto a uma mulher trans. 


Trecho de vídeo publicado por Erika Hilton


Essa cena me emociona por diferentes motivos. Tenho passado os últimos anos me infiltrando em eventos da extrema direita pelo mundo e entrevistando essas figuras. Posso afirmar que não houve um desses congressos sequer, nenhuma dessas conversas, que não passou por discursos ultraviolentos contra pessoas trans. 


Já escrevi bastante sobre isso, inclusive sobre como no governo Trump essa violência levou a resoluções e políticas públicas desde seu primeiro dia de mandato. Não vou me repetir aqui sobre a maneira como essas narrativas são construídas com base no pânico moral e na ideia da destruição da família e de valores sagrados. O que quero ressaltar é que

a demonização de pessoas trans está hoje no epicentro político da extrema direita. É um tema de consenso entre eles, usado para mobilizar o medo, o ressentimento e o ódio e que tem efeitos concretos na vida de milhares de pessoas. 


E a mobilização desses afetos não é exclusiva da extrema direita, também é importante dizer. Não sei dizer quantas vezes eu mesma fui perseguida, ameaçada e exposta por mulheres que se dizem feministas radicais trans excludentes ou quantas vezes o Pauta Pública foi alvo de ódio quando apontamos nosso microfone para pessoas trans. Tudo bem. Como me disse Judith Butler, ser perseguida por essas pessoas é um distintivo de coragem. 


Um outro ponto importante é que

o Brasil é um dos países que mais mata transexuais no mundo

. Quando Lula faz esse gesto, que mensagem ele manda para o povo? E que mensagem ele manda para as pessoas trans?


A cena me lembrou o relato de Suzanne Hommel, uma alemã nascida em 1938 que falou no documentário “Encontro com Lacan” sobre o tempo em que foi paciente do psicanalista francês. Ela carregava traumas profundos de sua vivência durante a Segunda Guerra Mundial, mas, em uma de suas sessões com Lacan, contou de um sonho recorrente que a acordava sob forte angústia todos os dias pontualmente às 5h da manhã. Acrescentou o contexto histórico de sua infância: “Era às 5h da manhã que a Gestapo vinha buscar os judeus em suas casas”. Ao ouvir a palavra “Gestapo” (polícia secreta oficial da Alemanha Nazista) o psicanalista levantou-se rapidamente da poltrona e fez um carinho suave em seu rosto. Quando ela conta isso no documentário, imediatamente leva a mão ao rosto imitando o gesto. 


Através desse ato físico e verbal, Lacan transformou a palavra “Gestapo” em “geste à peau”, que em francês significa “gesto na pele”, e introduziu ternura onde antes habitava apenas o horror e o trauma. No documentário, ela se emociona ao dizer que isso não apagou seu sofrimento mas o modificou de forma definitiva e que mesmo décadas depois, ela ainda sentia aquele toque que mudou a forma como olhava para a própria história e sua própria dor. 


O “geste à peau” de Lula em Erika Hilton neste momento da nossa história, me parece muito poderoso, simbólico, um marco de posição diante do mundo, que pode ressignificar um monte de afetos pra muita gente. E ao mesmo tempo é tão bonito precisamente porque foi um afago espontâneo em um país que está ressignificando sua relação com a política, que ainda sofre com o trauma dos quatro anos sob o governo genocida de Bolsonaro – e que escolheu neste domingo apostar na ternura ao invés do horror.


Aliás, que fique marcado aqui: Erika Hilton foi reeleita como a mulher mais votada da história para a Câmara dos Deputados e, com 1,5 milhão de votos conquistados em São Paulo, é a segunda parlamentar no país a romper a barreira de 1 milhão de votos …
