2.1. The Anarchistic Nature of Buddhism

2.2. Socio-Cultural Critique Emerging from Zen and Anarchism

What can esoteric knowledge and spiritual practices from the East teach us about the deep psychological roots of domination and hierarchy? In what ways have ancient Buddhist sages acted as anarchist exemplars and deep ecologists long before these traditions began in the West? How might these anarchistic spiritual traditions inform our approaches to work in education, expand our notions of community, help us navigate ecological collapse, and contribute to our efforts to sustain living systems and rekindle our connection to the myriad sentient inhabitants of the places we live beyond the reaches of capital and the State? This paper will examine the anti-doctrine doctrine of Zen Buddhism as a concrete and embodied system of thought and practice for seeing through the delusions of the ego and the psychological and cultural conditioning these delusions engender. What will also be acknowledged is the general lack of attention this spiritual tradition has given to the capitalistic, authoritarian, and anti-ecological systems that tap into and flow from these delusions. It will be argued that these experiential approaches to overcoming the tyranny of the ego have significant implications for loosening the grip of hierarchical thinking, capitalist hyper-consumption, centralized systems of obedience and command, and human destruction of the biosphere.

“The mercy of the West has been social revolution; the mercy of the East has been individual insight into the basic self/void. We need both.”

—Gary Snyder, Buddhism and the coming revolution, 1969.

title: Rising from the Ashes : The Yellow Vests Return as France Burns
content:
Helicopter hovering over Place de la République during the curfew implemented in Paris.


Over the past month, France has erupted in a nationwide rebellion that has shaken the ruling order to its core. As politicians of all stripes focus on polishing their brand image for the next

presidential election

 in May 2027, high school students have

organized

 on a grassroots level. Through occupations, blockades, and street protests, they have taken a stand against both the deplorable conditions of their schools today and the

menacing future

 that looms ahead of them. They took France and the entire world by surprise with their determined mass resistance and their courage in confronting the police forces sent to repress them.


After weeks of daily actions and nationwide demonstrations, leading to an unprecedented wave of arrests targeting rebellious youth, the Macron government was reaching a political impasse. It desperately tried to buy time by opening dialogue with some student organizations, in hopes of blunting the force of the movement until the upcoming school break slowed its momentum.


However, the authorities had not anticipated several developments. First, the students multiplied their force by joining the national call to take the streets on Saturday, October 17 to reignite the

Yellow Vests movement

, the popular mobilization against high gas prices and government austerity policies that emerged in 2018. Second, anger over the intense police violence of the previous weeks drew even more people in the streets. Third and most dramatically, the day’s protests snowballed into an insurrectionary situation that

surpassed

 what we experienced eight years ago during the height of the Yellow Vests struggle.


This new wave of collective rage that swept over the cities of France last week has plunged the current government into a deeper crisis. Politicians scrambled to capitalize on the upheavals, while authorities responded by implementing more authoritarian policies on a national scale. In the following article, we describe how the dramatic events around October 17 unfolded, analyzing their significance and reflecting on what is at stake.


Burning barricades blocking a narrow street in the historical part of downtown Bordeaux (October 17.)


Glowing Embers of Discontent


In 2018, the Yellow Vest movement emerged into the French political landscape seemingly out of nowhere. This grassroots wave of protests formed a reaction against rising gas prices and worsening living conditions among the country’s lower and middle classes. After decades of economic crises, inflation, and harsh neoliberal austerity policies, a portion of the population was feeling isolated, disenfranchised, and abandoned. The capitalist dream of ease and opulence that successive governments had promoted was turning into a living nightmare for a growing number of individuals. The politically diverse movement, named after the fluorescent emergency vests drivers were required to carry in their vehicles, made visible the ongoing economic emergency that gripped more and more people across France.


Due to its open-ended form, the Yellow Vests initially attracted populists from the left and the right and autonomous participants with a range of grievances against the ruling order. From the beginning, an internal struggle unfolded within the movement as radical participants

confronted

 far-right and fascist factions and attempted to prevent cooptation by reactionaries. Over time, the Yellow Vest movement gradually shifted to embrace more anti-capitalist and anti-state perspectives.


Since the initial wave of Yellow Vest protests died down in 2020, the economic situation in France has worsened. The gap between rich and poor has continued to

widen

, while the Macron government accelerated its dismantling of public services. International conflicts from Ukraine to Iran have further impacted the French economy, worsening inflation and driving up prices on essential goods, energy, and gas.


It is no surprise that people facing such economic pressure would take to the streets to express their discontent. And what better way to threaten the current ruling order than to bring the Yellow Vest movement back from the dead?

author: labor4pal
title: Motown and the Making of Working-Class Revolutionaries: an Interview with Jerome Scott and Walda Katz-Fishman (UAWD Daily Struggle)
content:
Anthony Stoner October 26, 2026

Jerome Scott and Walda Katz-Fishman, authors of Motown and the Making of Working-Class Revolutionaries: The League of Revolutionary Black Workers, share their reflections on the UAW’s Black radical tradition, the tactic of the wildcat strike, and the importance of unions fighting for the working class as a whole.

In the 1960s, Chrysler—the only Big Three corporation whose operations remained largely in Detroit at the time—began to hire Black workers, many fresh from the U.S. South. They had the worst and most dangerous jobs, and Chrysler frequently fired them before they obtained UAW contract protections after a 90-day probation. In 1968, these conditions and the lack of representation by the white-dominated UAW—at that time led by Walter Reuther, whose “Administration Caucus” dominated the union then and for decades after his death led to a wildcat strike in the Dodge Main plant initiated by the Dodge Revolutionary Union Movement (DRUM) (A wildcat strike is a strike not officially authorized by a union). A number of other RUMs were then created around Detroit, and in 1969 the League of Revolutionary Black Workers (LRBW) was founded by Black militant labor organizers to help unite and aid struggles around the city. Among those organizers was Jerome Scott, who, along with Walda Katz-Fishman, has written an account of the LRBW, based on extensive interviews with surviving members of the League, their families and comrades. Their book, Motown and the Making of Working-Class Revolutionaries: The Story of the League of Revolutionary Black Workers, is available from University of Georgia Press.

—Anthony Stoner, UAW Local 4811

Anthony SToner: Why were wildcat strikes the tactic both DRUM and then the LRBW focused on? What’s the role of a wildcat strike for today?

Jerome scott: The wildcat strike became our principal tactic mainly because it was a two-edged sword. We could attack the company as well as struggle with the union. The company of course was and is the major enemy, but back in the day, and in some unions even today, the collaboration between the union and the corporation is not good for the workers themselves. And so we realized after the first wildcat strike (for us, and the first in the country for about fifty years) at Dodge Main that that wildcat strike really did attack both of our struggles. What we didn’t realize when we started it was that it was also a very offensive tactic. We were making the decisions; and the corporation and the union had to respond and defend against that, rather than the workers always being on the defensive. So the wildcat strike was a hell of a weapon.

AS: How did Doug Fraser [then head of UAW Chrysler Department] and the UAW International use the “flying squadron” during the 1973 wildcat?

JS: A little bit on the history of the flying squadron. It started with the United Mine Workers movement in Appalachia because of the rolling strikes that happened in the organizing of that union. It was an organized group of union members that they would take from strike event to strike event and try to make sure that nobody crossed the picket line. They were an apparatus that actually really backed up the picket lines in the strikes that were held in the heyday of organizing the UAW, the United Mine Workers, and so on. And the purpose was really to let the workers know that the International was part of this strike. So the concept of the flying squadron had a long tradition of respect from the union movement.

In our case, in our strike at Chrysler in 1973, we were able to shut down the entire Chrysler corporation for about a week; and that was because of the strategic nature of the Detroit Forge plant where I worked. There was only one other plant in the world that made the same parts that we made and it was a forging plant in [apartheid-era] South Africa. The corporation had done all it could do to try to break our strike, and try to break the picket line, but the picket line was going on 24/7.

What we learned later is that the corporation had called Solidarity House and said, “you have to do something about this strike.” And it was then that Fraser organized the historic flying squadron to come break our picket line rather than support it. And it was a pitched battle—it wasn’t like we saw them coming and laid down our picket signs—it was a big struggle. But eventually they were able to break our picket line and end our struggle after a week. Now the …

title: Sırbistan | “Rejim devrildi; mücadele daha yeni başladı”
content:
Sırbistan'daki Marks21 sosyalist çevresinin ve Londra merkezli sosyalist yayın ve kampanya ağı Counterfire'ın üyesi olan Marksist yazar, siyasal yorumcu ve sosyalist aktivist Dragan Plavšić'in 26 Ekim 2026'da Counterfire'da yayımlanan Sırbistan seçimlerinde Öğrenci Listesi'nin zaferini değerlendiren “Sırbistan’daki öğrenci hareketi belirleyici bir seçim zaferi kazandı” başlıklı yazısını paylaşıyoruz.

 

2003'te yayımlanan Balkan Sosyalist Geleneği ve Balkan Federasyonu, 1871–1915 (The Balkan Socialist Tradition and the Balkan Federation, 1871–1915) başlıklı kitabın editörlüğünü Andreja Živković ile birlikte üstlenen Plavšić'in çalışmaları ağırlıklı olarak Balkanlar'ın siyasal tarihi, milliyetçilik, sosyalist hareketler ve emperyalizm üzerine. Kosova, Bosna-Hersek ve Sırbistan'ı konu alan yazılarında milliyetçiliği eleştirirken Balkan halkları arasında sosyalist dayanışmayı savunan yazar, Rusya, Çin, NATO ve Avrupa Birliği arasındaki uluslararası güç ilişkilerini de sınıfsal bir perspektiften değerlendiriyor. Makaleleri Counterfire ve LeftEast gibi yayınlarda çıkan Plavšić, Sırbistan'daki öğrenci hareketinin seçim zaferini de neoliberalizme karşı toplumsal mücadele ve demokratik örgütlenme bağlamında değerlendiriyor.


Sırbistan'daki parlamento seçimlerinde Öğrenci Listesi'nin kazandığı zafer muazzam. İlk kez seçimlere katılan liste, 250 sandalyenin tahminen 140'ını kazanarak çoğunluğu elde etti. Başbakanlık makamına sorunsuzca geçip iktidarı da beraberinde taşımayı uman otoriter Cumhurbaşkanı Aleksandar Vučić'in 14 yıllık iktidar hâkimiyeti, öğrencilerin öncülük ettiği kitlesel hareket tarafından kesin biçimde kırıldı. İki yıl önce, yeniden inşa edilmiş bir tren istasyonunun çökmesi ve 16 kişinin ölmesiyle başlayan hareket, 2025'te bir başbakanı istifaya zorlamıştı. Şimdi de cumhurbaşkanını görevinden ayrılmak zorunda bıraktı.


2024'ten bu yana süren kitle hareketleri kararlı ve kesintisizdi. Yalnızca Vučić'e değil, muhalefete de yönelen köklü bir halk hoşnutsuzluğundan güç alan bu hareketler, geleneksel siyasete güvenini kaybetmiş insanlar bağımsız biçimde örgütlendiklerinde kökleşmiş bir siyasal düzenin devrilebileceğini gösterdi.


Ancak zafer ne kadar büyük olursa olsun, hayati bir soruyu gündeme getiriyor: Kolektif eylem ve demokratik katılım üzerine kurulu bir hareket devlet kurumlarına girdiğinde ne olur? Bu sorunun yanıtı, Sırbistan siyasetinde yeni ve ilerici bir dönemin açılması olasılığı ile bir fırsatın daha kaçırılması tehlikesi arasındaki dengede yatıyor. Sonuç, büyük ölçüde hareketin kendisini iktidara taşıyan kitlesel seferberliklerle bağını koruyup koruyamayacağına, aynı zamanda Avrupa'nın dört bir yanında yayılmakta olan neoliberalizme karşı geniş çaplı toplumsal başkaldırıyla birleşip birleşemeyeceğine bağlı olacak.


Trajediden isyana


Kasım 2024'te istasyonun peronu üzerindeki sundurmanın çökmesiyle yaşanan trajedi, Vučić yönetiminin yolsuzluğunu, kayırmacılığını ve hesap verme sorumluluğunun ekonomik ve siyasal bağlantılarla geçiştirilmesini açığa çıkardı. Bunu izleyen öfke dalgasının yükselişine, istasyonun yeniden inşasıyla ilgili belgelerin yayımlanmasını ve sorumluların yargılanmasını talep eden öğrenciler öncülük etti.


Hesap verme sorumluluğu talebiyle başlayan hareket, hızla Vučić'e karşı daha geniş bir isyana dönüştü. Daha da önemlisi, hareket yalnızca tek tek suistimallere değil, sıradan insanların yaşamlarını yöneten kurumlar üzerinde güçten yoksunluğunun kaçınılmazlığına dair temel varsayıma da meydan okudu.


Üniversite işgalleri, gösteriler, yol kesme eylemleri ve mitingler Sırbistan'ın dört bir yanına yayıldı. Öğrenciler kentler ve köyler arasında gidip gelerek, zenginlere ve güç sahiplerine hizmete fazlasıyla alışmış bir siyasal sistem tarafından uzun süredir terk edilmiş insanlarla dayanışma bağları kurdu. Öğretmenler, üniversite çalışanları, işçiler ve diğer yurttaşlar da onlara katıldı.


Öğrenciler mücadelenin harekete geçirici gücü haline geldi. Resmî muhalefetten kararlı bir biçimde bağımsız kalmaları ve üniversite genel kurullarında (plenumlarda) kolektif tartışma ve karar alma ilkesine bağlılıkları, hareketin en belirleyici güç kaynağıydı. 


Mücadelenin sonraki adımı seçimlere katılma kararı oldu. Hareket, üniversitelerden ve toplumun daha geniş kesimlerinden gelen adaylarla kendi seçim listesini oluşturdu. Adaylar üniversite ve fakülte genel kurullarında önerildi; seçilmeden önce öğrenciler tarafından kolektif olarak titizlikle değerlendirildi. Adayların hiçbiri …

title: Brazil’s Lula Wins ‘Historic Victory’ Against Right-Wing Trump Ally Flávio Bolsonaro
content:
Lula’s victory marked an important turning point for the left in

Latin America

, as far-right parties

had


won

 every other national election in the region since the start of Trump’s second term.


 


By

Olivia Rosane


Oct 25, 2026


 


In a historic comeback, Brazilian President Luiz Inácio Lula da Silva triumphed in Sunday’s run-off election over

right-wing

 challenger Flávio Bolsonaro, the son of former Brazilian President and convicted coup-plotter

Jair Bolsonaro

.


 


Lula’s victory comes despite the best efforts of US President

Donald Trump

 and his

Big Tech

 backers, as Trump’s administration openly

intervened

 on behalf of Bolsonaro and Meta


boosted

 pro-Bolsonaro over pro-Lula content on its

social media

 platforms.


 


“Lula won,

Brazil

 won,

democracy

 won, the Americas won,”

said


Pennsylvania

 Democratic House nominee Chris Rabb from Lula’s campaign headquarters in Sao Paulo, Brazil, after the results were announced around 9:15 pm Brasilia time. “They declared victory for Lula da Silva for his fourth term against a raging fascist, rubber-stamped for

Donald Trump

.”


 


“These elections have represented a historic victory for the majority of the Brazilian people, who mobilized to defend democracy against the threat of

fascism

.”


 


Rabb noted that Lula’s victory marked an important turning point for the left in

Latin America

, as far-right parties

had


won

 every other national election in the region since the start of Trump’s second term. “This is the first victory for democracy in this hemisphere since Trump took office,” Rabb said.


 


With 99.99% of the votes counted, Lula

won

 by 51.79% to Bolsonario’s 48.21%, making him the first Brazilian candidate since the restoration of democracy in 1985 to win a second-round election after

coming in second

 in the initial round.


 


“I would like to thank the Brazilian people for the generosity they have shown me for a long time,” Lula

said

 in his victory speech in São Paulo late Sunday. “And, in this second round, I want to thank the generosity of the Brazilian youth, who took to the streets to defend democracy.”


 


After finishing two percentage points behind Bolsonaro in the October 4 poll, Lula re-energized his campaign by finally

shortening

 the Brazilian workweek from six to five days, as his supporters launched

demonstrations

 against the far-right.


 


“These elections have represented a historic victory for the majority of the Brazilian people, who mobilized to defend democracy against the threat of fascism,” Francesca Emanuele, senior international policy associate with the Center for Economic and Policy Research (CEPR), told Common Dreams from Sao Paulo, Brazil, where she was monitoring the elections. “It was the Brazilian people themselves (students, working-class, and middle-class Brazilians) who took to the streets and mobilized tirelessly from the very first day after the first round of voting to overturn the first-round results and secure Lula’s victory.”


 


Reginaldo Lopes, a federal deputy for Lula’s

Workers

’ Party,

told

 The Guardian: “I feel incredible… This is Brazil telling the world that the extreme right is fascist, that the extreme right is against Black people, is against the poor, against the state, against gay people… We are going to reorganize the democratic forces [in this country.]”


 


Sunday’s victory did not come easily, as the Lula campaign

complained

 of bus shortages in the key cities of Salvador and Sao Paulo, requesting that the Brazilian

Supreme Court

 extend the voting by two hours. The court

granted

 the request, so polls closed at 7 pm Brasilia time instead of 5 pm.


 


“Lula’s win is the first good news for the planet in a while!”


 


“Lula has won despite the unfair practices his campaign has faced from Meta, interference from the

Trump administration

, and severe disruptions to public

transportation


on election day in major cities (where up to 50% of bus fleets were reportedly out of service),” Emanuele told Common Dreams. “These disruptions disproportionately affected working-class voters, who rely heavily on public transportation and have historically been a key part of Lula’s electoral base.”

На встрече вы узнаете, кто из наших товарищей сейчас находится в российских тюрьмах за свои убеждения и действия, а также в каких условиях их содержат и каким наказаниям подвергают. Также обсудим, какие инициативы и группы оказывают им поддержку и как можно проявить политическую и материальную солидарность.

После начала войны в Украине все больше и больше анархистов и антифашистов поподают в жернова тюремной системы в России. Люди, участвующие в прямом действии и сопротивляющиеся войне, подвергаются все более жёсткому прессованию.

На конец октября 2026 года в списке политзаключенных АЧК - Москва несколько десятков человек, которым мы в той или иной степени оказываем помощь. Для того, чтобы и дальше их поддерживать, нам регулярно нужно ваше участие.

На встрече в Барселоне будет представлен мерч в пользу политзаключенных: несколько видов футболок и шопперы. Если вы хотите поддержать нашу работу и оказать помощь политзекам, вы можете сделать донат или приобрести понравившийся вам мерч. Все вырученные средства пойдут на поддержку наших товарищей в тюрьмах России.

Когда: воскресенье, 1 ноября, 18:30. Где: CSO La Terminal, Carrer de la Glòria 16, 08902 L'Hospitalet de Llobregat, Barcelona

Если вы в Барселоне или окрестностях, обязательно заглядывайте!

title: Incendie de la mairie de Limoges
content:
point de vue anarchiste


Communiqué anarchiste


Réaction après l'incendie de la mairie de Limoges


À travers ce communiqué, voici un point de vue anarchiste sur l'incendie de la mairie de Limoges.


Mr Guérin est une personne d'extrême droite, proche des réseaux de l'action française.


Le 17 octobre, c'est un mouvement révolutionnaire qui s'est formé.


Cependant il ne s'est pas formé du jour au lendemain, mais à travers des dizaines d'années de luttes.


L'anarchie n'est pas un parti mais un outil de réflexion autour de la société, avec notamment l'absence de pouvoir, de commandement et d'autorité. L'anarchie est un but à atteindre désirable et pratique. L'anarchie refait surface avec notamment un mouvement de jeunesse à l'international acquis à la cause, et souvent réprimé par les forces de l'ordre notamment à travers les Free Party.


Si la droite et ses idées extrêmes accompagnés par les renseignements territoriaux n'ont rien vu venir c'est qu'iels sont ignorantes, idiotes et qu'iels ne pensent qu'à leur confort et carrière au mépris des classes discriminées.


Abus de pouvoir, harcèlement, détournements d'argents publics, favoritisme, pantouflage, etc. sont légions dans les instances des collectivités territoriales.


À Limoges, Mr Guérin a gagné les récentes élections. L'attaque subie par la mairie est aussi une réponse au refus d'une société gouvernée par des personnes autoritaires, bercées par des idées de haines extrémistes envers certains groupes ethniques ou politiques.


Mr Guérin parle de maison commune, mais refuse toutes concertations avec Mr Maudet, élu et députée Haute-Vienne de la France Insoumise qu'il déqualifie sans cesse par mépris de classe.


Drôle d'ambiance pour une maison commune


Cette personne n'est en aucun cas digne de diriger une mairie comme Limoges.


Si cet édifice a brûler ce 17 octobre, c'est aussi le fascisme qui a brûlé.


Face à la volonté de Mr Guérin de démissionner, n'est-il pas temps de profiter de cet instant, pour instaurer une société anarchiste à Limoges et expérimenter cet outil.


Pour terminer, les revendications, les recours administratifs et les actions menées depuis des années par les militant.e.s des droits humains et environnementaux n'ont eu pour réponse que la violence d'un État en faillite de sa propre devise.


La réponse collective à travers la France, (face à l'État totalitaire pour ne pas dire fasciste, du système libéral, mis en place Macron et ses sbires), en ce 17 octobre est une victoire politique. Et un premier avertissement.


La démission de la présidence et de l'ensemble de ce gouvernement est la seule et unique réponse possible et plausible.

title: Федерация Анархо-Коммунистов Болгарии - Платформа Федерации Анархо-Коммунистов Болгарии 1945 года
content:
Автор

: Федерация Анархо-Коммунистов Болгарии

Название

: Платформа Федерации Анархо-Коммунистов Болгарии 1945 года

Дата

: 10 марта 1945

Источник

: https://www.anarchy.bg/articles/platformata-na-fakb-ot-1945-g/


10 марта 1945 года в Княжево под Софией созвана национальная конференция ФАКБ, которая должна была принять проект программы организации. Подготовка и сама конференция проходили нелегально, но её открытие объявлено публично. Прошло ровно шесть месяцев после переворота 9 сентября. Болгарские анархисты — активные участники антифашистского сопротивления — возвращаются из тюрем и концлагерей, из эмиграции, из нелегального положения. Уцелевшие после репрессий разбросаны по городам и сёлам. Ещё к середине сентября они устанавливают связи между собой. В более крупных центрах созываются встречи, а к концу месяца — местные конференции (в Радомире, Казанлыке, Пловдиве, Килифарево и других местах), на которых все участники выражают нетерпение, готовность, волю к активной деятельности. Определена дата общенациональной конференции по восстановлению ФАКБ (Федерации анархо-коммунистов Болгарии), а также по объединению с ФАСБ (анархо-синдикалистами). В Софии начинает выходить газета «Работническа мисъл» («Рабочая мысль»).


Уже на втором выступлении на конференцию врывается вооружённая милиция. Все делегаты под конвоем доставлены в милицейский участок в Княжево. Они остаются там, пока не приезжают тюремные машины, которые выгружают их в Доме слепых, недавно превращённом во временную следственную тюрьму. Это начало большевистских преследований против безвластнического движения в Болгарии, которое продолжится и в последующие десятилетия.


«Партии ясно, что если мы дадим вам свободу агитации и пропаганды, вы станете силой, с которой мы никогда не сможем справиться. Это определяет отношение к вам», — откровенно делится перед лагерниками-анархистами Руси Христозов, крупнейший милицейский начальник в Болгарии того времени.


На партийном пленуме Цола Драгойчева заявляет: «Если мы дадим анархистам свободу организации, пропаганды и печати, все наши революционные кадры уйдут к ним».


Всё же товарищам удаётся опубликовать Платформу ФАКБ в «Работническа мисъл» в 1945 году. Её содержание отнюдь не только исторический документ. Это свидетельство как о времени, так и о нестареющих идеях анархизма. Более того — и поэтому мы её публикуем — она является хорошей основой для дискуссии о том, что изменилось, а что нет за прошедшие 70 лет.


***


ОСНОВЫ


 Мы отвергаем нынешнюю социальную систему государственности, капитализма и централизма, потому что она основана на власти, которая противоречит народным инициативам и свободе. Всякая власть означает политические, экономические или духовные привилегии. В экономическом отношении она представлена частной собственностью, в политическом — государством, а в духовном — религией.


 Эти три формы власти взаимосвязаны — если какая-либо из них сохранится, она восстановит и остальные. Поэтому мы отвергаем сам принцип власти. Мы сторонники упразднения частной собственности, государства и религии и выступаем за полную ликвидацию всех форм и институтов принуждения и насилия.


 Мы отвергаем всякое учение и всякое социальное, политическое и экономическое движение, целью которого является поддержание государства, частной собственности и церкви, принуждения и насилия в общественных отношениях.


 Мы отвергаем фашизм, который является исторической попыткой восстановления абсолютизма, самодержавия и могущества политической формы власти с целью защиты экономического и духовного господства привилегированных классов.


 Мы отвергаем политическую демократию, потому что она не предусматривает упразднения принципа власти, ведёт к дезориентации масс, втягивая их обманом и иллюзиями в битвы против их собственных интересов, и развращает их через осуществление власти и поддержание стремления к господству.


 Кроме того, политическая демократия совершенно неспособна решить великие социальные проблемы. Она поддерживает хаос, противоречия и преступления, проистекающие из социальных основ централизованного государства и капитализма.


 Мы отрицаем государственный социализм, потому что он ведёт к государственному капитализму: к самой чудовищной форме экономической эксплуатации и угнетения и к полному упразднению общественных и индивидуальных свобод.


 Мы за анархо-коммунизм, или свободный коммунизм, который заменит частную собственность полной социализацией земли, фабрик, шахт, всех средств производства и продукции …

title: İsviçre’de aşırı sağa karşı ortak mücadele ve dayanışma çağrısı
content:
Geçtiğimiz hafta sonu İsviçre’nin Basel kentinde BastA! (Basels starke Alternative – Basel’in Güçlü Alternatifi) Tarafından düzenlenen Siyaset Evi etkinliğinde bir araya gelen toplumsal ve politik muhalefet güçleri Avrupa'da yükselen aşırı sağla mücadelede ortak politika imkânlarını harekete geçirmek konusunda görüş birliğine vardılar. 


“Faşizm, Karşı Güç ve Gelecek” başlığıyla gerçekleştirilen etkinlikte, Avrupa’da aşırı sağın yükselişi, otoriter politikaların yaygınlaşması ve bunlara karşı geliştirilebilecek ortak mücadele stratejileri ele alındı.


Konuşmaların, atölyelerin ve grup tartışmalarının gerçekleştirildiği etkinlikte, sol hareketlerin yalnızca mevcut politikalara karşı çıkmakla yetinmemesi, toplumsal sorunlara somut çözümler üreten ve gündelik yaşamda karşılık bulan dayanışma ağları oluşturması gerektiği üzerinde duruldu.


Bolliger: Sol, somut dayanışma yapıları inşa etmeli


Etkinliğin açılış konuşmasını yapan BastA! Başkanı Oliver Bolliger, artan kiralar, yükselen yaşam maliyetleri, ağır çalışma koşulları ve geleceğe ilişkin belirsizliklerin toplumun geniş kesimlerini doğrudan etkilediğine dikkat çekerek, sol hareketlerin bu sorunlar karşısında yalnızca eleştiri üretmesinin yeterli olmadığını söyledi.


Bolliger temel yönelimini çöyle özetledi:


“Kiralardaki artış, yükselen yaşam maliyetleri, stresli çalışma koşulları ve geleceğe yönelik belirsizlik, insanların günlük yaşamlarını doğrudan etkiliyor. Sol, eleştiriyle sınırlı kalmamalı. İnsanların bu sorunlarla başa çıkmalarına yardımcı olacak somut dayanışma yapıları inşa etmelidir.” 


Atölyelerde ortak mücadele yöntemleri tartışıldı


Etkinlik kapsamında düzenlenen beş atölyede feminist mücadele, iklim adaleti, demokratik konfederalizm, antifaşist sosyal politikalar, mahalle örgütlenmesi ve örgüt içi dayanışma konuları ele alındı.


Katılımcılar, farklı toplumsal mücadelelerin birbirleriyle nasıl ilişkilendirilebileceğini, ortak örgütlenme olanaklarını ve dayanışma ağlarının nasıl güçlendirilebileceğini tartıştı.


İsviçre merkezli ilerici kampanya ve dayanışma örgütü Campax’ın Genel Yöneticisi Itziar Marañón, aşırı sağa karşı mücadelenin yalnızca mevcut hak ve kazanımların korunmasıyla sınırlı kalmaması gerektiğini belirtti.


Marañón, alternatiflerin ortaya konulmasını istedi:


“Mücadelemizi mevcut kazanımları savunmakla sınırlamamalı, şiddet içermeyen ve adil bir yaşam için olumlu alternatifleri görünür kılmalıyız."


Faşizme karşı feminist stratejilerin tartışıldığı atölyede, kadın düşmanı erkeklik anlayışlarının gençler üzerindeki etkileri ve sosyal medyada cinsiyetçilikle mücadele yöntemleri değerlendirildi.


Aşırı sağa karşı mücadelede kullanılan dilin de belirleyici olduğunu vurgulayan Marañón, siyasi söylemin toplumun geniş kesimlerinin anlayabileceği ve kendi yaşam deneyimleriyle ilişkilendirebileceği bir biçimde kurulması gerektiğini söyledi.


İklim adaleti mücadelesi ve ekofaşizme karşı direniş


İklim adaleti üzerine gerçekleştirilen atölyenin sonuçlarını paylaşan Kolektif İklim Adaleti temsilcileri Zoë ve Mirjam, iklim krizi ile aşırı sağın yükselişi arasındaki ilişkiye dikkat çekti.


İklim adaleti mücadelesinin ırkçılığa, ayrımcılığa ve otoriter politikalara karşı mücadeleden ayrı düşünülemeyeceğini belirten Zoë ve Mirjam, ekofaşizme karşı örgütlü ve aktif bir direnişin gerekli olduğunu vurguladı.


Atölyede, büyük teknoloji şirketlerinin çevresel ve toplumsal etkileri de tartışıldı. Bu şirketlerin yüksek enerji tüketiminin yanı sıra gözetim ve denetim mekanizmaları aracılığıyla otoriter eğilimleri güçlendirdiği ifade edildi.


Katılımcılar, ekolojik krize karşı mücadelenin yalnızca çevrenin korunmasıyla sınırlı tutulamayacağını, toplumsal eşitsizlikler ve otoriterleşmeyle birlikte ele alınması gerektiğini belirtti.


Demokratik konfederalizm ve mahallelerde öz örgütlenme


Ronahî Kadın Konseyi adına değerlendirme oturumuna katılan Özen Aytaç, yerel örgütlenmenin, toplumsal katılımın ve mahallelerde kurulan dayanışma ilişkilerinin önemine dikkat çekti.


Suriye ve Rojava’daki demokratik konfederalizm deneyimlerinden örnekler veren Aytaç, özellikle kriz dönemlerinde insanların yaşadıkları mahallelerde örgütlenmesinin ve ortak karar alma mekanizmaları oluşturmasının önemini vurguladı.

title: 31.10.2026 – Gathering in memory of Kyriakos Xymitiris and all fallen comrades
content:
[eng,de,ελ]


Remember together – Fight together


Saturday 31 of October 2026, we want to invite people to come together and commemorate. We invite everybody to contribute with speeches and everything that is wanted to be shared. There will be food, music and an open mic.


Saturday 31st of October – 17:00 – Marielle-Franco-Platz in front of New Yorck (Bethanien)


KYRIAKOS XYMITIRIS ALWAYS PRESENT IN THE STREETS OF FIRE


Two years after our beloved friend and comrade Kyriakos Xymitiris lost his life on the 31st of October 2024 while he was handling explosives, we continue to keep the revolutionary memory of him and all our fallen comrades alive. Since the moment we learned the news that broke a lot of hearts, many people in Europe and other places all around the world organized actions and events defending his presence in the struggles and his political ideas. Also in the city of Berlin, Kyriakos was part of the struggle against gentrification patriarchy, borders, fascism and in solidarity with workers and prisoners.


His determination led him to take another step in the fight for a liberated world. A struggle that unites us all despite our differences. We understand that resistance has not a single way, but thousands that can break the chains of an oppressive system: from direct action to mutual aid, from the self-organization of everyday life, to words that ignite consciousness. Every rebellious gesture contributes to the struggles. Nevertheless, we value the courage of those that in a moment of constant retreat, and seeing the risks that the armed struggle carries with it, want to contribute to the fight by other means. For this reason, we also see the responsibility to defend his last decision. A decision that took his life and left the struggle and so many without this wonderful person, comrade and friend.


In the same way that we commemorate Kyriakos, we want to remember all the fallen comrades that we lost in the past years. Even though they died in different circumstances, their history and participation in the struggles fuel our passion for freedom. Sharing personal and political moments is a part of honoring their memory and ideas. And having them in our mind and heart in every action. Because revolutionary memory is more than remembering the past. It is a way not to forget that the fight continues. What they sowed with love are the seeds of rage that permeate every step we take against this system of misery. A capitalist, racist and patriarchal system that one day will be destroyed. And with the same tears in our eyes, we will celebrate that one day we said “we are right, we will win”.


It is us who must preserve their memory, remember their explosive action and their sharp determination. It is us who must transform common grief into anger and militant organisation. It is us who must give something, for those who gave everything.


Marianna Manoura and Dimitra Zarafeta


October 2025 – Month in Memory of Kyriakos Xymitiris

Διήμερη εκδήλωση: Όταν οι αγώνες για ζωή και αξιοπρέπεια νικούν


ΟΤΑΝ ΟΙ ΑΓΩΝΕΣ ΓΙΑ ΖΩΗ ΚΑΙ ΑΞΙΟΠΡΕΠΕΙΑ ΝΙΚΟΥΝ


Ανοιχτό κάλεσμα προς την κοινωνία


Χωρίς τη συλλογική δράση, οι ιδέες κοιμούνται στα κεφάλια και στις βιβλιοθήκες. Η γέννηση της πολιτικής ελευθερίας συμβαδίζει με τον αγώνα για τη συλλογική ιδιοποίηση της θεσμίζουσας αρχής.


Eduardo Colombo


Ως Κοινότητα Κατειλημμένων Προσφυγικών καθ’ όλη τη διάρκεια του πολύμηνου και πολυεπίπεδου αγώνα ενάντια στα τελευταία σχέδια του κράτους και του κεφαλαίου βαδίσαμε και αγωνιστήκαμε πλάι πλάι με τους συντρόφους μας απεργούς πείνας μέχρι θανάτου Αριστοτέλη Χαντζή και Suzon Doppagne και από κοινού με όλους τους ανθρώπους των κινημάτων και της αλληλεγγύης. Ανθρώπους από ευρύτερες κοινωνικές ομάδες που αναγνώρισαν αυτόν τον αγώνα της Κοινότητας ως έναν συλλογικό αγώνα της κοινωνίας που αφορά όλες και όλους, συγκροτώντας ένα ευρύ κοινωνικό μέτωπο.


Και όπως αγωνιστήκαμε συλλογικά, νικήσαμε και συλλογικά!


Έχοντας κλείσει λοιπόν τον πρώτο μεγάλο κύκλο νικηφόρα, είναι ξεκάθαρο πως αυτό που έχουμε να υπερασπιστούμε δεν είναι μόνο αυτή η συγκεκριμένη νίκη ή μια ρωγμή που αποτέλεσε μια στιγμή στον χρόνο ή μια αυτοαναφορική συνθήκη εντός της οποίας βρίσκει τον εαυτό της η Κοινότητα Κατειλημμένων Προσφυγικών. Η παρακαταθήκη αυτού του αγώνα και της νίκης στο παρόν και το μέλλον απλώνεται μπροστά μας αναδεικνύοντας μια τεράστια δυνατότητα: Να ξαναχτίσουμε το συλλογικό φαντασιακό του κόσμου της αλληλεγγύης, της καθημερινής αντίστασης απέναντι στην εξαθλίωση, τον φόβο, την υποταγή, την εξατομίκευση, αντιτάσσοντας την αυτοθέσμιση των κοινωνιών μας και τη συγκρότηση κοινοτήτων, οπουδήποτε οι άνθρωποι αγωνίζονται, στις γειτονιές, σε πόλεις και χωριά, στους χώρους δουλειάς, στα σχολεία και τα πανεπιστήμια, στον δημόσιο χώρο.


Υπό αυτό το πρίσμα καλούμε σε μία διήμερη εκδήλωση στις 24 και 25 Οκτώβρη στις 17.00 στο Πάντειο Πανεπιστήμιο, (Νέο Κτήριο, Αίθουσα Σάκη Καράγιωργα Ι) για να συζητήσουμε πάνω στους κεντρικούς άξονες που δομήθηκε ο αγώνας αυτός, στις διαφορετικές μεθόδους και στα εργαλεία που χρησιμοποιήσαμε, καθώς και να δούμε συλλογικά και συνολικά τα σημεία που οδήγησαν στη νίκη αλλά και τις αδυναμίες, τις αστοχίες και τα λάθη που υπήρξαν. Αλλά κυρίως να εστιάσουμε στη συλλογική δυνατότητα που ανοίχτηκε μέσω αυτού του αγώνα και που πρέπει να διευρύνουμε. Να ενώσουμε τις αντιστάσεις μας για να δημιουργήσουμε τους όρους μιας κοινής δύναμης και να μετατρέψουμε την αλληλεγγύη από αντανακλαστικό σε σταθερή κοινωνική σχέση. author: Gary Chartier
title: Propedeutica al Libertarismo di Sinistra
content:
Di

Gary Chartier

. Originale:

Framing Left Libertarianism: A First Pass

, del 25 ottobre 2012. Tradotto da

Enrico Sanna

.


Questo articolo, scritto da

Gary Chartier

, è stato pubblicato originariamente sul suo blog

Liberalaw

 

il dieci dicembre 2008

.


Qualcuno considera il libertarismo di sinistra un esercizio cosmetico e propagandistico. Ma c’è anche chi ci vede l’espressione forte di questioni che dovrebbero stare al centro dei movimenti per la libertà.


Ci sono cinici libertari e persone di sinistra che nel libertarismo di sinistra vedono una falsa propaganda politica. Nel tentativo, forse, di spacciare a ignare persone di sinistra ideali libertari in contrasto con il programma della sinistra. O forse è il tentativo di infondere un’anima aliena nel corpo del movimento libertario, gravandolo di questioni inesistenti in un vero programma libertario.


Nessuna di queste ipotesi è anche lontanamente persuasiva o interessante.


Il libertarismo di sinistra è profondamente libertario perché è antistatalista (i primi libertari di sinistra che mi vengono in mente sono tutti anarchici: do per scontato che sono tutti anarchici o pressoché tali) e perché conferma il valore del mercato e dei diritti di proprietà. Ma è anche di sinistra perché lotta contro il privilegio, il potere gerarchico, l’esclusione, la privazione e il dominio sia ideologicamente che praticamente, e perché dimostra un sincero attaccamento ai concetti di inclusione, emancipazione e rispetto reciproco.


E lo fa non ridefinendo i termini, così che, ad esempio, la libertà si riduce alla libertà dalla costrizione fisica, ma evidenziando la sintonia tra ideali e principi libertari e concetti di fondo di sinistra.


Ovvero illustrando le conseguenze radicali di un’adesione ai principi libertari.


• Si capirebbe allora che la legittimità della proprietà è viziata da tutta una storia di violenze, collusioni o aiuti da parte dello stato a persone e organizzazioni ricche e potenti, fatto che giustifica l’

appropriazione della loro presunta proprietà da parte di chi ci vive e lavora

.


• Davanti alle ingiustizie e alla sfacciataggine dei monopoli e degli aiuti di stato, l’adozione piena dei principi libertari minerebbe in vari modi il potere delle imprese centralizzate piramidali, facilitandone la sostituzione con cooperative di lavoratori e rafforzando enormemente il potere dei lavoratori.


• Si capirebbe così che i principi libertari portano al rifiuto di quel genere di privilegi che permettono a influenti attività d’affari, professionisti e singoli associati di servirsi del potere statale per sfruttare gli altri (come le società clientelari che ottengono privilegi fiscali sulla concorrenza, o come quelle attività corporative ricche e privilegiate che danneggiano la popolazione e la potenziale concorrenza grazie a licenze e requisiti restrittivi imposti dallo stato).


• Con l’adesione ai principi libertari, infine, diventerebbe evidente che un principio che va contro lo stato offre anche una base forte contro la guerra e soprattutto l’imperialismo.


Gli stessi principi morali che spingono a lottare contro il potere oppressivo dello stato possono offrire una buona ragione per lottare contro tutti quei poteri oppressivi che giustamente attirano l’attenzione della sinistra. Dai principi morali che guidano la lotta contro lo stato possono scaturire le questioni più diverse. Diritto naturale, teoria della virtù, kantismo, pluralismo etico, ma anche (anche se per varie ragioni mi sembra fuori luogo) consequenzialismo: tutto può fare da base dell’anarchismo di mercato o di altre questioni morali. Le ragioni che (ad esempio) nel nome dell’uguaglianza negano il “diritto naturale di governare” e l’insensibilità verso le particolarità individuali, rendono moralmente inammissibile anche il razzismo, il sessismo e l’eterosessismo.


I libertari di destra tendenzialmente rifiutano gli ideali dei libertari di sinistra per ragioni varie. Dicono (I) che non c’è niente di particolarmente libertario in questioni riguardanti il potere sul posto di lavoro o il benessere dei lavoratori, o anche il razzismo. A volte arrivano anche a dire (II) che sono questioni anti-libertarie.


Se la prima obiezione è convincente dipende in parte da come viene concepita la lotta contro il potere dello stato. Finché si basa su un certo principio morale, però, sulla base dello stesso principio si possono dare anche giudizi morali riguardanti questioni diverse dal potere dello …

author: Unknown
title: Münih'ten Paris'e dayanışma mesajı
content:
Bavyera Öğrenci Hareketi’nin (Bayerische Schüler_innen Bewegung) çağrısıyla, GEW (Eğitim ve Bilim Sendikası) başta olmak üzere birçok kurum ve kuruluşun desteklediği yapılan dayanışma mitingi yüzlerce öğrenci ve yurttaşın katılımıyla gerçekleşti.

Münih Ludwig-Maximilians-Üniversitesi ana binasının önündeki Geschwister-Scholl-Platz'da toplanan kalabalık, "Münih'ten Paris'e: Öğrenciler Sokağa!" sloganıyla eylem yaptı.

Fransa'daki öğrenci hareketine güçlü bir destek mesajının verildiği gösterildiği eylemde, hem Almanca hem de Fransızca hazırlanan pankartlar dikkat çekti. Öğrenciler, Fransızca ve Almanca "Eğitimimize yatırım yapın!" yazılı dev pankartın arkasında kenetlendi.

Eylemde, Fransa'dan gelen temsilci öğrenci konuşmacılar da söz alarak ortak mücadele vurgusu yaptı. Mitingde yapılan konuşmalarda, Almanya ve Fransa'daki öğrencilerin karşı karşıya kaldığı eğitim yetersizlikleri, gençliğin sosyal sorunları ve zorunlu askerlik hizmetine (Wehrpflicht) karşı tepkiler dile getirildi.

"Sınır Tanımayan Dayanışma" (Solidarité sans frontières) mottosuyla düzenlenen eyleme WE ACT, GEW Landesverband Bayern, La France Insoumise, Jusos München, Linksjugend ['solid] Bayern, Nein zur Wehrpflicht! München ve Die Linke Landesverband Bayern gibi pek çok örgütsel yapı destek verdi.

31 yıldır emeğin sesi olan Evrensel, gücünü sadece okurlarından alıyor. Emeğin sesinin daha gür çıkması için sen de güç ver.

author: groundxero
title: The Twilight of Trumpism
content:
Contemporary Trumpism is not the conservative attempt to return US society back to the 1950s. It is the attempt to return US society back to the 1850s – an attempt which will fail completely, disastrously and totally.


 


By 

Dionysius


 


Between 2016 and 2026, the political system of the United States has been dominated by Trumpism, a.k.a. the US variant of billionaire fascism or plutofascism. Its domination was so complete that even when non-Trumpist politicians won elections, they did not question Trumpism’s single most compelling argument. This argument, in a nutshell, was that the United States could solve the 21st century problems of a

collapsing middle class

 and

an economy being looted by billionaire monopolists

 by a magical return to 19th century tariff walls, territorial imperialism and settler colonialism.


 


The year 2026 marks the moment when a majority of US citizens have stopped believing in 19th century magic. One of the most telling signs of this shift occurred on October 9, 2026, when Pete Hegseth, the Trumpist official in charge of the US military, announced that the US would broadcast the execution of a former US soldier on live television.


 


Hegseth had fully expected the announcement would create a wave of hurrah-patriotism. After all, the soldier in question, a former US Army major, had shot and killed 13 fellow soldiers and wounded 30 others at a military base in Fort Hood, Texas in 2009. The soldier also happened to be Muslim and the US-born son of Palestinian American immigrants, two groups which have been constantly scapegoated and persecuted by Trumpism.


 


Instead, the announcement triggered a firestorm of condemnation. Numerous former soldiers and Pentagon officials criticized the announcement as tantamount to a lynching, while human rights advocates pointed out that the only two countries which hold public executions are Taliban-ruled Afghanistan and theocrat-ruled Iran. Ten days later, overwhelming political pressure forced the Trump administration to back down and

call off the broadcast

.


 


To understand why Hegseth misread the situation so badly and why this moment is so significant, it is worth pausing for a moment to reflect on the group which forms the electoral core of Trumpism. This group consists of white males who are nostalgic for the settler colonial white masculinity which dominated US politics for almost two hundred years, i.e. between the creation of the US in 1783 and the civil rights and feminist struggles of the 1960s and early 1970s.


 


To understand why this group wants to return to the past, we must first understand that this white masculinity was responsible for 105 years of settler colonial land theft and genocide against the First Nations of North America. This period began with the 1785-1795 Northwest Indian War, and ended in the Wounded Knee Massacre in South Dakota committed by US soldiers against the Lakota people on December 29, 1890. Most of the surviving First Nations were confined to reservations thereafter, and none enjoyed full US citizenship rights until the Snyder Act of 1924.


 


This white masculinity was also crucial to perpetrating the horrors of 82 years of US chattel slavery (1783-1865) on African Americans and citizens kidnapped from Africa by slave traders. After the abolition of slavery in 1865, this white masculinity engineered systems of legal apartheid (commonly called “Jim Crow” laws) which privileged whites at the expense of African Americans. In addition to these laws, many US states had groups of white terrorists who regularly assaulted and murdered African Americans. The most notorious of these terrorists were the Klu Klux Klan, an organization so powerful that as late as August 12, 1925, an estimated 30,000 of their members marched openly through the US capital of Washington, DC without any legal repercussions whatsoever.


 


Official Jim Crow and unofficial racial terror ruled large parts of the US for 87 years (i.e. 1878-1965). They did not disappear until the 1965 Voting Rights Act granted African Americans the right to vote in all US states, and until Federal law enforcement agencies cracked down on white terrorist groups during the 1960s and 1970s.

author: winter oak
title: Calling on our ancestors!
content:
by Paul Cudenec, who reads the article

here


After I published my articles on the Druids and ancient Celtic culture this summer, Franklin O’Kanu wrote on his

Unorthodoxy

 blog about the parallels to his own ancestral culture.


He

said

: “What’s interesting about all of this is how two cultures, across the world, Nigerian and Celtic, have the same spiritual view of the world”. [1]


And he

commented

 on one of my posts: “From the Yoruba and Igbo perspective, what the Celts experience in one continent is what the practitioners of Ifa experienced in another continent: the same honor of the Divine”. [2]


I have now discovered similar echoes from a reverse direction, as it were, through reading

Of Water and the Spirit: Ritual, Magic, and Initiation in the Life of an African Shaman

 by Malidoma Patrice Somé (1956–2021).


Somé belonged to the Dagara, a million-strong people spread across the artificially-created nation-states of Ghana, the Ivory Coast and Burkina Faso – he came from the latter, which was still called French Upper Volta when he was born.


The environment and particular customs of this African people are, of course, very different from those of the ancient Celts – roasted monkey would not have been on the menu at a Beltane feast in Ireland!


But there are similarities as well. In the essay series I

cite

 Jean Markale’s account of how at their celebratory events the Celts drank copious amounts of alcoholic drinks, producing “drunkenness, in other words the trance thanks to which one can go beyond apparent reality and see the supernatural”. [3]


He adds: “For Greek and Roman writers, Celts already had a reputation for being passionate lovers of fermented drinks. Drunkenness is an oft-occurring theme in the epics, especially in Irish accounts.


“Gods and heroes compete in their unquenchable thirst for alcohol, in the form of beer, wine or mead. A religious festival never went by without a serious drinking session”. [4]


In

his

 book, Somé writes: “Millet beer has always been a part of major rituals. Our rituals are long, and one gets thirsty”. [5]


He explains that his tribe was said to have been taught how to make beer by the Kontomboli, mysterious otherwordly beings who introduced a woman to their astonishing brew: “When she drank it, she was delighted. She felt merry and wanted to sing”. [6]


I was also intrigued to learn that the Dagara use a twenty-based counting system, so that eighty-three would be expressed as “four times twenty plus three”. [7]


In France the same number is

quatre-vingt-trois

, “four twenties and three”, after the old Celtic system, and we used to have the same concept in English with a score, meaning twenty, using which eight-three is “four score and three”.


A more important connection between ancient European and African societies has been the effects of colonisation.


From an African perspective it must be strange to hear a white man claim to be the victim of colonialism, but such is the case.


Following the destruction of our indigenous culture by the Roman empire and its religious wing, we were then

colonised

 by the empire of usury and commerce and used as fodder for its insatiable industrial Leviathan. [8]


With our true identities further smothered, our vital energy was hijacked to allow that same empire to enslave and exploit other peoples across the world, including the Dagara.


Somé writes: “My own elders had experienced French colonialism and the culture of the West as a force that used violence as a means to eradicate traditional lifeways.


“They had seen their own youth stolen from them as they vainly struggled against the incursions of these intruders.


“During these years, in which my people were trying to make sense of a people whose every action seemed to go against the natural order of things, creating chaos, death, and destruction, the sense of unified community that sustained their tribal life was profoundly destabilized. These foreigners seemed to have no respect for life, tradition, or the land itself…


“In spite of the best efforts of all my people, the whites kept on coming; kept on doing whatever they pleased; and kept on taking more and more of our land, our beliefs and our lives”. [9]


“It is a sad thing to realize how much my people have lost and how much yet of our reality is to be buried in the pit of oblivion”. [10]


Although Upper Volta officially became independent in 1960 (it became Burkina Faso in 1984), this …

author: Yohannes Woldemariam
title: The New Scramble for Africa
content:
Something important is happening across the Red Sea and the Horn of Africa. Wars that appear local are drawing in actors from increasingly far away. Ports built for commerce acquire military uses. Gold mined in conflict zones travels through international financial centers. Drones purchased abroad alter wars. Governments negotiate with foreign powers while those same powers cultivate armed groups or parallel authorities elsewhere.


Sudan, Libya, Ethiopia, Eritrea, Somalia, Somaliland and Yemen are usually discussed as separate crises. Look more closely and the connections become difficult to ignore. A

 

United Nations investigation

 found that forces aligned with Khalifa Haftar helped move Colombian fighters through Libya to support Sudan’s Rapid Support Forces. Sudanese gold travels toward the Gulf, while


Chatham House has documented

 the importance of the UAE to the regional gold economy. In western Ethiopia, a

 

Reuters investigation

 found a large training camp for fighters intended for the RSF, with reliable sources saying the UAE financed the facility and provided trainers and logistical support. 


These are not isolated developments. They point toward a changing system of power around the Red Sea.


What is emerging is not another Berlin Conference. Foreign governments are not openly dividing Africa into colonies, and African governments are not passive spectators. They bargain, invite investment, seek weapons and sometimes use outside powers against domestic or regional rivals. But something more than ordinary diplomacy is taking place.


One striking change is the growing importance of powers once treated as secondary actors in African geopolitics. The United Arab Emirates, Turkey and Israel do not possess the worldwide reach of the old European empires. Yet wealth, military technology, commercial networks and strategic geography allow these middle powers to exercise influence far beyond their borders.


They are also flexible about how that influence is exercised. A government can be the useful partner in one country, a paramilitary organization in another, a parallel authority somewhere else, and a commercial company across several of them. The relationship need not be ideological, and the partner need not even be a state. Strategic usefulness can be enough.


The UAE provides perhaps the clearest example. In Sudan, it has been supporting the RSF.


In Libya, it became an important external supporter of Khalifa Haftar’s eastern forces.


Reuters has documented

 earlier UN findings that the UAE helped Haftar’s forces build their air power, while Turkey supplied drones and air defenses to the government in Tripoli.


The Sudan and Libya stories have since begun to merge. The


UN Panel of Experts on Libya

 found that Colombian fighters transited through Haftar-controlled territory to support the RSF and described Libya as an operational, logistical and tactical base.


Gold reveals the economic side of the same system.


Chatham House

 describes gold as a major driver of Sudan’s conflict. Between 2012 and 2022, according to

 figures examined by Chatham House

, the UAE imported 2,569 tonnes of African gold that African countries themselves did not record as exports, worth approximately $115 billion.


The connection between gold and armed power is not abstract. The


U.S. Treasury

 sanctioned UAE-based companies connected to the RSF network. It said AZ Gold purchased Sudanese gold apparently for the benefit of the RSF and transported it to Dubai.


Money, weapons and military support can therefore move toward African conflicts while gold and other resources move outward. The old colonial economy required foreign administrators. The contemporary system does not necessarily need them. Governments, armed groups, mining companies, traders, port operators and financial intermediaries can perform different parts of the process.


A recent


Financial Times investigation

 traced a much wider Emirati expansion involving ports, mining, agriculture and infrastructure across Africa. A port can be a commercial asset, logistics hub, source of political leverage and, under different circumstances, military platform.


It is here that the idea of a new scramble for Africa becomes useful.


The old scramble sought possession of territory. The emerging one can operate at a distance. An outside power does not necessarily need to govern the mine, occupy the port or administer the population. It needs …

author: Publicación Abierta
title: La Matriz Ideológica de la Dominación Occidental y el nuevo cerco a los pueblos rebeldes de Nuestra Améfrica Ladina
content:
A 534 años de la Resistencia Indígena Planetaria, en homenaje al maestro Saúl Rivas Rivas: guerra cognitiva, tecno feudalismo y soberanía algorítmica cimarrona frente al cerco electoral, espiritual y epistémico del imperio.


Por Argenis José Delgado Vegas

| @ArgJoDel | 10 de octubre de 2026


Nuestra Améfrica Ladina despierta. En el marco de una resistencia que lleva más de cinco siglos frente a la colonización y la neocolonización, los pueblos de México, Cuba, Haití, Brasil, Colombia, Nicaragua, Bolivia, Venezuela, Ecuador y Argentina —con mayoría de población indígena y afrodescendiente— han impulsado en las últimas décadas procesos de liberación y descolonización estatal. Unos se han aproximado al zapatismo, panafricanismo, socialismo, comunismo, comunitarismo… No importa la etiqueta: importa que se atreven a caminar fuera del guión que Occidente les tenía reservado. Y cuando los pueblos rebeldes se mueven, el imperio afila sus armas. No solo las militares. Las armas más letales son las ideológicas.


La densidad afroindígena de Colombia, Brasil y Venezuela: el corazón demográfico de la rebelión


En Nuestra Améfrica Ladina hay tres países donde la matriz colonial muestra su rostro más descarnado porque allí se concentra una de las mayores densidades de población afrodescendiente e indígena del continente. Brasil, con más de la mitad de su población autoidentificada como negra o parda y cerca de 1,7 millones de indígenas; Colombia, con millones de afrocolombianos, raizales y palenqueros y más de un centenar de pueblos originarios; y Venezuela, con una presencia afrodescendiente que atraviesa la región norte costera frente al Caribe, los llanos y los Andes, el Sur y con 2,8 % de población indígena reconocida. No son datos menores: son la prueba viviente de que la colonialidad no terminó. Son también el sujeto histórico que el imperio teme, porque su memoria colectiva guarda el cimarronaje, el Cumbe, el resguardo, el conuco, el territorio y la espiritualidad como formas de libertad.


Esa densidad afroindígena explica por qué estos países son blanco prioritario de la Matriz Ideológica de la Dominación Occidental. En Brasil, el bolsonarismo no solo disputa el Estado: disputa el relato sobre la esclavitud, los quilombos y los pueblos indígenas. La bancada evangélica ultraconservadora, el agronegocio y la minería ilegal avanzan sobre tierras indígenas y quilombolas mientras se boicotea Durban y se criminaliza el racismo estructural. En Colombia, el giro a la derecha de Abelardo de la Espriella se monta sobre el miedo, el extractivismo y la guerra cognitiva contra el Acuerdo de Paz, justo en el país con mayor población afrodescendiente del mundo después de Brasil y con pueblos indígenas que han sido víctimas del conflicto armado. En Venezuela, el cerco financiero, el secuestro del presidente legítimo Nicolás Maduro y su esposa la diputada Cilia Flores, la ofensiva contra los cultos populares apuntan al corazón afroindígena del proyecto bolivariano.


 Estos tres países son, además, la demostración de que las Causas Comunes de la Humanidad no son abstracciones: la causa indígena, la causa de la diáspora africana, la causa del planeta, la de la mujer, la del trabajo y la intergeneracional se intersectan en la Amazonía, el Pacífico colombiano, el Cerrado brasileño, Barlovento y la Guayana venezolanaa ( incluye el Esequibo). Allí la colonialidad de los datos se vuelve concreta: los algoritmos de Silicon Valley clasifican, vigilan y expropian los saberes de pueblos que han cuidado la vida durante milenios. Por eso la soberanía algorítmica cimarrona no es un lujo teórico: es la continuación digital del palenque y del resguardo. Sin ella, la gran población afro e indígena de Colombia, Brasil y Venezuela seguirá siendo materia prima de la guerra cognitiva, del tecno feudalismo y del viejo Dios blanco que no tolera la pluriversalidad.


Marco Teórico:

«Saúl Rivas Rivas lo advirtió con claridad: existe una Matriz Ideológica de la Dominación Occidental, un entramado histórico, cultural, social y espiritual cuyo fin es ‘dar continuidad a toda una opresión capitalista occidental’. Esa matriz no es un invento reciente. Es la misma que construyó un ‘Dios blanco y europeo’ frente a un ‘Diablo negro, indio o árabe’, justificando la dominación como un acto de perfeccionamiento racial.»
