title: Ulus: Healthcare must be free and accessible to all
content:
Structural problems in public hospitals and shortcomings in healthcare services are making it increasingly difficult for citizens to access medical care. People struggling to secure appointments through the Central Physician Appointment System (MHRS) sometimes have to wait at least 15 days just to submit an appointment request. Patients who eventually manage to obtain appointments after considerable effort must then try to explain their health problems within limited consultation times due to overcrowding in hospitals.


Difficulties in securing appointments and restrictions on consultation times are further deepening problems concerning the quality and accessibility of healthcare services.


Mehmet Nuri Ulus, Co-Chair of the Diyarbakır (Amed) Branch of the Health and Social Service Workers’ Union (SES), spoke to ANF about the problems facing public hospitals.


‘Healthcare is not being transformed, it is going backwards’


Ulus recalled that the Justice and Development Party (AKP) government has introduced healthcare reform and transformation programmes since 2002. He said that the policies implemented in recent years have caused serious problems in healthcare services and continued: “The AKP government has announced numerous programmes under the names of healthcare reform and healthcare transformation. However, particularly over the past 10 to 15 years, what has been called healthcare transformation has, from our perspective, meant collapse and regression. We have experienced both the COVID-19 pandemic and the earthquake during this period. These major crises showed us just how inadequate the healthcare system was in responding to the problems that arose.


The healthcare system should have been prepared for these crises and should have had the capacity to meet society's healthcare needs. Healthcare is a service that must be provided within the framework of the social welfare state. Everyone must be able to receive healthcare services equally, accessibly and in their mother tongue.


However, in recent years, we have seen healthcare services increasingly turn into a system in which those who have money can access care more easily. The proliferation of private hospitals is one aspect of this. Another is the emergence of an approach in which even public hospitals link faster access to certain tests, radiological examinations, medical reports and surgical procedures to payment. This undermines the principle that healthcare services should be equal for everyone.”


‘Physical queues have been replaced by virtual queues’


Ulus addressed the appointment crisis in the healthcare system, pointing out that the queues once seen outside hospitals now continue through the Central Physician Appointment System. He said appointment systems should make healthcare more accessible, but many citizens are currently unable to secure appointments.


Ulus said: “The AKP government used to say that people had to go to hospitals early in the morning and wait in queues to see a doctor. Today, physical queues have been replaced by virtual queues. Instead of waiting for hours outside hospitals, people now try to book appointments on their phones or online. However, when you access the system, you cannot find an available appointment. The queues have therefore not disappeared; they have simply changed form. Citizens now find themselves waiting in front of digital systems to access healthcare.


People face serious difficulties securing appointments, particularly in departments such as ear, nose and throat, ophthalmology and dermatology. Citizens who cannot obtain appointments are then forced to turn to private hospitals. However, considering the economic crisis, the struggle to make ends meet and the housing problems in Turkey, not everyone has the financial means to seek treatment at private hospitals.


As a result, the inability to access healthcare has become another dimension of economic hardship. Healthcare should be free and accessible, yet citizens are forced to stretch their financial resources to obtain the medical care they need.”


‘The budget is not allocated to preventive healthcare services’


Ulus said that the problems facing the healthcare system are not limited to difficulties in securing appointments. He drew attention to the following issues: “When we look at the Ministry of Health's budget and healthcare policies, we see that preventive healthcare services are consistently pushed into the background. title: Söke Ekmek ve Gül açıklaması: Her çocuğa okullarda bir öğün ücretsiz, sağlıklı yemek istiyoruz
content:
Aydın - Söke'de Belediye Meydanı’nda Söke Ekmek ve Gül "Bir Öğün Ücretsiz Sağlıklı Yemek Güvenli Okul Güvenli Ulaşım İstiyoruz” diyerek basın açıklaması yaptı.

Söke Ekmek ve Gül’ün çağrısıyla yapılan açıklamaya veliler, Söke Kadın Dayanışma Derneği ve Söke Emek ve Demokrasi Güçleri de destek verdi. "Bir öğün ücretsiz sağlıklı yemek güvenli okul güvenli ulaşım istiyoruz” pankartının açıldığı basın açıklamasıni Söke Ekmek ve Gül adına öğrenci velisi Huri Abrinç okudu.

Çocukların okullarda bir öğün ücretsiz, sağlıklı ve dengeli yemek yiyebilmesi için yıllardır ülkenin dört bir yanında ve Söke’de aralıksız mücadele ettiklerini belirten Abrinç; “Söke Ekmek ve Gül olarak imza kampanyaları düzenledik, stantlar açtık, çocukların beslenme hakkını kararlılıkla savunduk. 2022 yılında Ekmek ve Gül tarafından başlatılan, 2023’te Kocaeli Ekmek ve Gül Kadın Dayanışma Derneği’nin çalışmalarıyla büyüyen, Esenyalı Kadın Dayanışma Derneği üyesi bir kadının hukuki mücadelesine kadar uzanan bu talep; bugün Türkiye’nin her köşesindeki kadınların, velilerin, öğretmenlerin ve eğitim emekçilerinin ortak talebidir. Toplanan binlerce imza, yapılan basın açıklamaları ve dayanışma ağları bu ihtiyacın ne kadar hayati, acil ve vazgeçilmez olduğunu defalarca kanıtlamıştır.

Çünkü biliyoruz ki derinleşen ekonomik kriz ortamında çocukların okula aç gittiği, ailelerin beslenme çantalarını doldurmakta zorlandığı, temel gıda ürünlerinin dahi lüks hâline geldiği bir ülkede; sağlıklı beslenme bir lütuf veya yardım değil, en temel insan hakkıdır. Çocuklar açken eğitimde fırsat eşitliğinden ya da nitelikli bir eğitimden söz edilemez” dedi.

Yürütülen bu haklı mücadeleler ve yükselen kamuoyu baskısı sonucunda Millî Eğitim Bakanlığının 5-19 Ekim tarihleri arasında ücretsiz okul yemeğine ilişkin velilerin görüşlerini almak amacıyla bir anket süreci yürüttüğünü hatırlatan Abrinç: “Yıllardır dile getirilen bu yakıcı ihtiyacı anlamak için çocukların açlığının bu kadar derinleşmesini bekleyen Bakanlığa soruyoruz: Velilerin ve kadınların sesi neden bugüne kadar duyulmadı” sorusunu sordu.

Bakanlığın adım atması önemli olsa da, yürütülen anketin kapsamı, erişilebilirliği ve yöntemi ciddi soru işaretleri doğurduğunu vurgulayan Abrinç anketle ilgili eksiklikleri sıraladı:

İnternet üzerinden yürütülen ankete pek çok veli eşit biçimde katılamamıştır. Veliler ankete ulaşmaya çalıştıklarında "yetkiniz yok" uyarılarıyla, sistemde yaşanan teknik sorunlarla karşılaşmış; internet ve telefon imkânı bulunmayan ya da dijital araçları kullanmakta zorlanan aileler süreçten tamamen izole edilmiştir. Ayrıca anket hakkında velilere yeterli bilgilendirme yapılmamıştır.

Edindiğimiz bilgilere göre ilkokul öğrencileri anket kapsamı dışında tutulmuş, süreç yalnızca ortaokul ve lise düzeyine sıkıştırılmıştır. Oysa en temel gelişim çağındaki ilkokul ve okul öncesi çocukların beslenme hakkı nasıl göz ardı edilebilir?

Servis imkânlarının kaldırılması veya kısıtlanmasıyla mağdur edilen taşımalı eğitim kapsamındaki aileler, bu anket hakkında da yeterince bilgilendirilmemiştir. Çocukların ulaşım ve beslenme ihtiyaçları birlikte değerlendirilmelidir.”

“İnternete erişemeyen, yetki engeline takılan ya da anket kapsamına alınmayan çocukların sağlıklı beslenmeye ihtiyacı yok mu? Çocukların en temel hakkı, teknik aksaklıklarla dolu bir anketin sonucuna ya da hangi eğitim kademesinde olduğuna indirgenebilir mi?” sorularını soran Abrinç, “Bir ankete katılamamış olmak, ücretsiz yemek ihtiyacının olmadığı anlamına gelmez! Çocukların açlığı anket sorularıyla giderilemez; beslenme sorumluluğu yalnızca ailelerin ve kadınların omuzlarına yıkılamaz” ifadelerini kullandı

Mıllî Eğitim Bakanlığına ve yetkililere çağrı yapan Abrinç şu talepleri sıraladı

Eşit ve Koşulsuz Hak: Okul öncesinden liseye kadar, kamu okullarındaki tüm öğrencilere ayrım yapılmaksızın her gün bir öğün ücretsiz, sağlıklı ve dengeli yemek derhal sağlanmalıdır.

Anket Sonucu Beklenmemelidir: Ücretsiz okul yemeği bir anketin sonucuna bağlanmadan, bütçe bahanelerinin arkasına sığınmadan kalıcı bir kamu hizmeti olarak uygulamaya konulmalıdır.

Şeffaflık ve Hesap Verilebilirlik: Yapılan anketin kaç veliye ulaştığı, hangi kademeleri kapsadığı ve sonuçların nasıl değerlendirildiği kamuoyuyla açık ve şeffaf bir şekilde paylaşılmalıdır.

Erişilebilir Katılım Yöntemleri: Dijital araçları kullanamayan veya erişim sorunu yaşayan veliler için yüz yüze görüşmeler, basılı formlar ve okullar aracılığıyla katılım kanalları oluşturulmalıdır.

author: Mag
title: Immer nur Behindertenwerkstätten: Warum verdienen Menschen mit Behinderung so wenig? Und wo bleibt die Inklusion?
content:
Dossier


„

In der Pandemie sind beinahe unbemerkt Löhne in Behindertenwerkstätten gekürzt worden. Schon vorher ließ sich von den Geld kaum leben. (…) Der Lohn der Beschäftigten in Behinderten-Werkstätten setzt sich in Deutschland aus mehreren Teilen zusammen: Ein sogenanntes Arbeitsförderungsgeld von 52 Euro wird aus Töpfen des Landes gezahlt. Dazu kommt ein Grundlohn von 89 Euro und ein individuell festgelegter Steigerungsbetrag. Diese beiden Posten müssen die Werkstätten selbst erwirtschaften. Als die Corona-Pandemie Deutschland erreichte, schlossen die Betreiber ihre Werkstätten für Menschen mit Behinderung. In der Folge konnten viele Aufträge nicht mehr erfüllt werden. Der Steigerungslohn entfiel. (…) 19 Prozent der Werkstätten, die an der Umfrage teil nahmen, gaben an, Löhne gekürzt zu haben. Weitere 18 Prozent gaben an, dass Kürzungen absehbar sind. Insgesamt hat sich in der Umfrage gezeigt, dass die Auswirkungen der Krise verzögert in den Werkstätten ankommen

…“

Artikel von Fabian Hillebrand vom 14.11.2020 im ND online

 

 und auch dazu:


Gerechtigkeit statt Almosen: Die GFF geht mit Jürgen Linnemann gegen das diskriminierende Entgeltsystem in „Werkstätten für behinderte Menschen“ (WfbM) vor Gericht


Mindestlohn in Werkstätten: Der sitzende Leistungsträger


„

Jürgen Linnemann hat 40 Jahre in Werkstätten für Menschen mit Behinderung gearbeitet. Jetzt zieht er für den Mindestlohn vor Gericht. (…) Sie klagen vor dem Arbeitsgericht Münster darauf, dass die Werkstatt ihm die Differenz zwischen seinem bisherigen Arbeitsentgelt und dem Mindestlohn zahlt. Linnemann sei Arbeitnehmer und habe dementsprechend Anrecht auf den Mindestlohn, so die Begründung. Der gesetzliche Mindestlohn müsse zudem auch in Werkstätten gelten. Anfang September soll das Arbeitsgericht eine Entscheidung treffen. Falls es beides verneint, will die GFF das derzeitige Entgeltsystem auf Vereinbarkeit mit Verfassungs-, Unions- und Völkerrecht überprüfen lassen. Bislang fehlen entsprechende Gerichtsentscheidungen. Das könnte sieben bis zehn Jahre dauern, wie Linnemanns Anwältin schätzt. Bis dahin ist er bereits in Rente. (…)


Das Sondersystem der Werkstätten hat der Bundesrepublik bereits zwei Rügen durch den UN-Fachausschuss für die Rechte von Menschen mit Behinderungen beschert. Reformpläne gibt es zahlreiche. Erst 2023 kam eine Studie im Auftrag der damaligen Ampel-Regierung zu dem Ergebnis, dass ein steuersubventioniertes Mindestlohnmodell besser funktionieren und zu mehr Gerechtigkeit führen würde. Andere fordern für einen inklusiven Arbeitsmarkt die Abschaffung der Werkstätten

author: Alan Robinson
title: Overcoming Schizophrenia and Transforming Psychiatry: An Interview with Dr. Daniel Fisher
content:
Editor’s Note: This Mad in the World report features an interview with eCPR founder Dr. Daniel Fisher, interviewed by Locura en Argentina founder Alan Robinson.


D

r. Daniel Fisher is an international pioneer in the mental health recovery movement who helped transform psychiatric care by demonstrating that full recovery from severe mental health conditions is possible. After personally overcoming a diagnosis of schizophrenia, he earned his medical degree from Harvard Medical School to reform the mental health system from within as a psychiatrist. A former member of the White House Commission on Mental Health and co-developer of Emotional CPR (eCPR), Dr. Fisher’s work has shifted international policy toward human connection and peer-led empowerment rather than forced treatment and lifelong institutionalization. He is also the author of

Heartbeats of Hope: The Empowerment Way to Recover Your Life

, which is being translated into Spanish.


Alan Robinson: Welcome, Dr. Daniel Fisher. In the early 1970s and 1980s, the Mental Patients Liberation Front (MPLF) was rooted in radical resistance. What was your first interaction with them like, and how did working with them shape your vision for peer-run alternatives?


Daniel Fisher:

 I first learned about the Mental Patients Liberation Front by reading a radical mental health newsletter called

Madness Network News

, which was published by a group in San Francisco starting in the early 1970s. At the time, I was completing my medical school training and discovered that the MPLF was located in Boston. When choosing where to do my psychiatric residency, I specifically sought a Harvard teaching hospital in Boston because the MPLF was there—not primarily because of Harvard itself. I instinctively felt that my best education would come from people with lived experience in the mental health system.


Prior to that, I had been hospitalized three times—twice before medical school and once during. Those experiences taught me that the mental health system desperately needed major reform, as the treatment was barbaric. I believed I could change the system from within by becoming a psychiatrist.


Daniel Fisher. Photo by Kermit Cole.


In 1976, I wrote to the MPLF asking to join. They sent back a postcard stating I could join as an ex-patient, but not as a psychiatrist. When I arrived in Boston and began my residency on an inpatient unit, a couple of hospitalized clients whispered to me that they knew who I was, as I had to keep my history quiet due to the severe stigma attached to a schizophrenia diagnosis. Eventually, they formed a group called “Friends of MPLF” for professionals with lived experience. Through that group, I met Judy Chamberlin, author of

On Our Own

, who became my lifelong mentor starting in 1976.


Later, another member blurted out to her psychiatrist—who happened to be Dr. Lee Mock, the head of my psychiatry department—that I was in the group. When I approached Dr. Mock, he called my lived experience a “great asset,” though he advised keeping it secret from other psychiatrists who would not understand.


Robinson:

 How did you handle the potential confusion or conflict of being both a former patient on one hand and a practicing doctor on the other?


Fisher:

 Bridging those two worlds has been a lifelong task. Initially, I coped by leading two separate lives and keeping my lived experience secret for three years, sharing it only with the head of the department. Over time, I earned the trust of survivor advocates. Judy Chamberlin used to joke that I was one of only three psychiatrists in the U.S. whom advocates accepted—the other two being Peter Breggin, author of

Toxic Psychiatry

, and Peter Stastny.


I waited until I finished my three-year residency before publicly disclosing my history. At the end of my residency, I was invited onto a television talk show,

People Are Talking

, to debate forced treatment. I invited my former supervisor to debate me. Right before we walked onto the stage, I told him I was going to reveal my past hospitalization. He sarcastically responded, “It’s very fashionable these days to have been hospitalized”.


Robinson:


Both you and Dr. Pat Deegan received diagnoses of schizophrenia, were told you would never recover, and went on to earn doctorates. Did you feel living proof that the system’s prognosis was completely wrong?

author: Tam Saavedra
title: ¡Las Directrices de la CDPD de la ONU sobre Interseccionalidad están aquí!
content:
Read in English


Las Directrices de la CDPD de la ONU sobre Interseccionalidad acaban de cambiar las reglas del juego para los derechos de las personas con discapacidad: Esto es lo que necesitas saber

 


¡Grandes noticias para las mujeres con discapacidad y para todas las personas defensoras, aliadas y organizaciones feministas y con discapacidad en todo el mundo!

 


Durante su 35º Período de Sesiones en agosto de 2026, el

Comité de las Naciones Unidas sobre los Derechos de las Personas con Discapacidad

 (CDPD de la ONU)

 adoptó oficialmente las

Directrices sobre la Identificación y Abordaje de la Discriminación Interseccional Contra las Niñas, Adolescentes, Mujeres y Mujeres Mayores con Discapacidad

.

 


Este hito representa un paso gigante para los derechos de las personas con discapacidad. Por primera vez, los Estados Partes cuentan con orientación explícita y accionable para respaldar sus obligaciones en la intersección entre género y discapacidad.

 


Lee las Directrices oficiales de la CDPD de la ONU aquí

 


¿Qué son las Directrices de la CDPD sobre Discriminación Interseccional?

 


Las Directrices constituyen un marco internacional autorizado, desarrollado por la CDPD de la ONU, para ayudar a los Estados a prevenir, supervisar y abordar de mejor manera la discriminación interseccional.

 


A lo largo de años de procesos de revisión de países por parte de la CDPD de la ONU, el Comité identificó una brecha persistente y crítica:

los derechos humanos específicos de las mujeres con discapacidad y la discriminación interseccional y compleja que experimentan, rara vez son comprendidas o abordadas por los gobiernos.

 


Al celebrar el 20º aniversario de la CDPD de la ONU

, e

stas Directrices fueron emitidas para cerrar esa brecha, garantizando que la convención se aplique a favor de

todas

las mujeres y niñas con discapacidad, y las personas de género diverso con discapacidad a lo largo de sus vidas.

 


¿Por qué estas Directrices cambian las reglas del juego?

 


Los documentos internacionales rara vez se centran de forma explícita en las experiencias de vida y los derechos de las mujeres con discapacidad. Estas Directrices nombran y explican las barreras sistémicas que las mujeres y personas de género diverso con discapacidad enfrentan a diario en todo el mundo, incluyendo:

 


Salud y Derechos Sexuales y Reproductivos (SDSR):

 Abordar y prevenir la esterilización forzada, la anticoncepción forzada, la falta de atención médica accesible, las restricciones al aborto y la falta de atención perinatal, menstrual y menopáusica.

 


Violencia de Género y Basada en la Discapacidad:

 Exponer la violencia institucional, el abuso digital/en línea y la falta generalizada de servicios de apoyo para las víctimas.

 


Reconocimiento de las labores de cuidado:

 Validar a las mujeres con discapacidad como cuidadoras activas y madres, en lugar de tratarlas únicamente como receptoras de cuidados.

 


Exclusión económica y educativa:

 Destacar las barreras en el mercado laboral y la exclusión de la educación durante la pubertad.

 


Respuesta a crisis y cambio climático:

 Combatir la exclusión agravada durante desastres ambientales, emergencias climáticas y esfuerzos de ayuda humanitaria.

 


Por nombrar sólo algunas.

 


7 avances clave en el enfoque de las Directrices

 


Lo que hace que este documento sea un instrumento transformador único es su enfoque estructural y progresista:

 


Inclusión explícita de la diversidad de género:

 Las Directrices abarcan explícitamente los derechos de las personas transgénero, intersexuales, no binarias y de otras diversidades de género con discapacidad, y solicitan una interpretación inclusiva de la diversidad de género de todas las obligaciones descritas.

 


Reconocimiento de las raíces históricas:

 El Comité aborda explícitamente el legado y los impactos continuos del colonialismo y la esclavización, estableciendo que los Estados que se benefician de estos sistemas históricos tienen la responsabilidad particular de reparar sus efectos actuales.

 


Un catálogo abierto de diversidad:

 El texto reconoce que las mujeres con discapacidad pertenecen a comunidades multimarginalizadas —incluidos grupos indígenas, afrodescendientes/negros, dalit, adivasi, refugiados, solicitantes de asilo, minorías religiosas, pastoriles o personas que viven en asentamientos informales, entre otros— dejando espacio para todas las identidades interseccionales.

title: Эррико Малатеста - Наконец-то! Что такое "диктатура пролетариата"
content:
Автор

: Эррико Малатеста

Название

: Наконец-то! Что такое "диктатура пролетариата"

Дата

: 28 сентября 1920

Источник

: Umanità Nova, год 1-й, №187


НАКОНЕЦ-ТО!

Что такое "диктатура пролетариата"


 Наконец-то появился тот, кто говорит ясно!


 До сих пор, когда мы говорили, что то, что социалисты называют

диктатурой пролетариата

, на самом деле есть не что иное, как диктатура некоторых людей, которые с поддержкой партии становятся над пролетариатом и навязывают себя ему, нас за это называли чуть ли не клеветниками.


 Вопреки всякой вероятности и всем установленным фактам утверждалось, что в России разрешена та квадратура круга, которой было бы правительство, действительно представляющее интересы и волю управляемых.


 Соответственно, Москва стала Меккой пролетариата: оттуда исходил свет, а вместе со светом – и категорические приказы относительно идей, которых должны придерживаться, и линии поведения, которой должны держаться те, кто с разрешения вышестоящих хотел называть себя коммунистами.


 Вследствие этого изумительного открытия, сделанного в России, – правительства, созданного по образу народа и для блага народа (или пролетариата, как угодно называть), – всё, что приходило из России, казалось обладающим чудотворной силой; и достаточно было назвать по-русски

советом

 любое собрание или комитет, чтобы он был возведён в верховный фактор революции.


 Но вот очарование разрушено.


 На этот раз не мы раскрываем секрет: мы, анархисты, злоязычные и непочтительные по убеждению. На этот раз это официальная газета Итальянской социалистической партии, до сих пор наиболее авторитетный орган московского слова.


 Это

Avanti!

 от 20-го числа текущего месяца, которая говорит:


 «....

В России при советском режиме Партия действительно направляет всю политику Государства, и вся общественная деятельность как отдельных лиц, так и коллективов подчинена решениям Партии, так что

 В САМОМ ДЕЛЕ ДИКТАТУРА ПРОЛЕТАРИАТА ЕСТЬ ДИКТАТУРА ПАРТИИ И, СЛЕДОВАТЕЛЬНО, САМОГО ЦЕНТРАЛЬНОГО КОМИТЕТА».


 Итак, теперь мы знаем, чего нам следует ожидать: диктатуры Руководящего органа Социалистической партии, или диктатуры нарождающейся Коммунистической партии, или даже диктатуры Д'Арагона и компании!


 Но руководители Социалистической партии, претендующие ввести Диктатуру, должны понять, что это, по крайней мере в Италии, невозможно: невозможно, потому что есть мы, анархисты и синдикалисты.


 Если бы мы находились в том же соотношении сил с социалистами, в каком, возможно, оказались наши товарищи в России, дело было бы простым: диктаторы избавились бы от нас средствами, дорогими всем диктатурам, – виселицами и тюрьмами, – и шли бы вперёд, пока не были бы свергнуты революцией или реакцией.


 Но мы уже сила, с которой необходимо считаться, и мы быстро развиваемся, чему благоприятствуют обстоятельства и то, что

Avanti!

 называет

необузданным темпераментом трудящихся масс

. И мы твёрдо решили не подчиняться.


 Не то чтобы мы верили, что массы всегда правы и что мы хотим всегда следовать за массами в их изменчивых настроениях. У нас есть программа, идеал, который мы хотим привести к победе, и поэтому мы отличаемся от массы, – мы люди определенного направления. Мы хотим воздействовать на массу, подталкивать её по пути, который считаем лучшим; но поскольку наша цель – освобождение, а не господство, мы хотим приучать массы к свободной инициативе и свободному действию.


 Мы верим, что свобода учит свободе и солидарности, и поэтому питаем отвращение к любому авторитарному устройству – как в обществе в целом, так и в любой отдельной партии или объединении.


 Социалисты хотели бы подготовить народ к свободе посредством власти.


 Но если бы, по предположению, которое мы отвергаем, было верно, что для торжества революции и устройства нового общества необходимо сосредоточить в немногих руках государственную власть, если бы было верно, что кто-то обязательно должен командовать, – тогда, пусть социалисты хорошенько поймут, – командовать хотели бы мы и не подчинились бы, разве что силой, командованию того, кто, по нашему мнению, заблуждается.


 Следствием чего было бы то, что революция, совершённая по авторитарным меркам и с диктаторскими целями, неизбежно привела бы в Италии к войне между одними революционерами и другими.


 Этого не хотели бы мы; этого не должны хотеть социалисты.


 Поэтому, оставив в стороне теории и судя о вещах реалистично, социалистам следовало бы отказаться от всяких диктаторских притязаний и принять либертарную …

author: 张皓翔
title: The Dislocation of Vendémiaire (II): The Illusion of National Economics and the Polarization of Political Economy【葡⽉的错位 （⼆）国⺠经济学的幻象与政治经济学的极化】【A commentary on the French riots between September and October】
content: This essay is the second part of The Dislocation of Vendémiaire, following Part I, “The Disruptors of the 21st Century and the Ideological Collusion.” While Part I interprets the 2026 France-centered student-led protest wave as a politically dislocated movement—one misread by mainstream discourse as a multi-class coalition when it is in fact an expression of fragmentation within the proletariat—Part II develops the theoretical argument behind that claim. Drawing on Marx’s thesis of society’s polarization into two hostile camps, it distinguishes between “property” and “proletarianization” in the sense of national economics and in the sense of political economy. The essay argues that class should be analyzed through the actual control over the production of labor-power, and that digital capitalism increasingly enables capital to dominate labor-power directly, beyond the mediation of formal ownership of physical means of production. On this basis, it explains why many who appear as middle-class or petty-producer subjects in national-economic terms—scholars, franchise shopkeepers, senior programmers, platform creators—are in political-economic terms being proletarianized, while carrying petty-bourgeois habits of political compromise, individualism, hostility to centralized discipline, and identity- or interest-based linkage. The result is a form of struggle that is radical in appearance but conservative and spontaneous in its core: it completes the first step of linkage through identity and affinity, but fails to return to the common ground of class interests and to connect with the broader industrial working class.

¿QUÉ es el patriotismo? ¿Es el amor por el lugar donde uno nació, el lugar de los recuerdos y las esperanzas de la infancia, de los sueños y las aspiraciones? ¿Es el lugar donde, con ingenuidad infantil, contemplábamos las nubes fugaces y nos preguntábamos por qué nosotros tampoco podíamos correr tan rápido? ¿El lugar donde contábamos los miles de millones de estrellas centelleantes, aterrorizados ante la idea de que cada una de ellas fuera «un ojo» que traspasara lo más profundo de nuestras pequeñas almas? ¿Es el lugar donde escuchábamos el canto de los pájaros y anhelábamos tener alas para volar, como ellos, hacia tierras lejanas? ¿O el lugar donde nos sentábamos a los pies de nuestra madre, embelesados por maravillosos relatos de grandes hazañas y conquistas? En resumen, ¿es el amor por ese lugar, donde cada pulgada representa recuerdos queridos y preciosos de una infancia feliz, alegre y juguetona?

Si eso fuera patriotismo, pocos hombres estadounidenses de hoy en día podrían considerarse patriotas, ya que el lugar de juego se ha convertido en fábrica, molino y mina, mientras que los sonidos ensordecedores de la maquinaria han sustituido a la música de los pájaros. Tampoco podemos ya escuchar las historias de grandes hazañas, pues las que cuentan hoy nuestras madres no son más que historias de dolor, lágrimas y aflicción.

¿Qué es, entonces, el patriotismo? «El patriotismo, señor, es el último recurso de los sinvergüenzas», dijo el Dr. Johnson. León Tolstói, el mayor antipatriota de nuestro tiempo, define el patriotismo como el principio que justifica la formación de asesinos en masa; un oficio que requiere mejor equipamiento para el ejercicio del asesinato que para la fabricación de artículos de primera necesidad como zapatos, ropa y viviendas; un oficio que garantiza mejores beneficios y mayor gloria que el del trabajador medio.

Gustave Hervé [1], otro gran antipatriota, califica acertadamente el patriotismo de superstición —una mucho más perjudicial, brutal e inhumana que la religión—. La superstición de la religión tuvo su origen en la incapacidad del hombre para explicar los fenómenos naturales. Es decir, cuando el hombre primitivo oía un trueno o veía un relámpago, no podía dar una explicación a ninguno de ellos y, por lo tanto, concluía que detrás de ellos debía de haber una fuerza mayor que él mismo. Del mismo modo, veía una fuerza sobrenatural en la lluvia y en los diversos cambios que se producen en la naturaleza. El patriotismo, por el contrario, es una superstición creada artificialmente y mantenida a través de una red de mentiras y falsedades; una superstición que despoja al hombre de su autoestima y dignidad, y aumenta su arrogancia y vanidad.

De hecho, la vanidad, la arrogancia y el egoísmo son los elementos esenciales del patriotismo. Permítanme ilustrarlo. El patriotismo parte de la base de que nuestro planeta está dividido en pequeños rincones, cada uno rodeado por una verja de hierro. Quienes han tenido la suerte de nacer en un rincón concreto se consideran mejores, más nobles, más grandiosos y más inteligentes que los seres vivos que habitan en cualquier otro rincón. Por lo tanto, es deber de todo aquel que vive en ese rincón elegido luchar, matar y morir en el intento de imponer su superioridad sobre todos los demás.

I den ungsocialistiska pressen hade så tidigt som år 1907 agitation förts för syndikalismen. I majnumret år 1910 av den fackliga tidningen Bageriarbetaren gjorde bagarnas förtroendeman, Anders Sjöstedt, som var redaktör för nämnda tidning, ett försök att hindra syndikalismens spridning bland bagarna, vilka i stort antal gripits av den syndikalistiska agitationen. Då skrev undertecknad ett genmäle mot den mäktiga förbundschefens angrepp under rubriken: **.."Man säger... Genmäle på artikeln i majnumret."*

"Man säger, att bagarna skola vara med då det gäller att upplösa förbunden och bilda Lokala Samorganisationer", inledde vår förtroendeman Anders Sjöstedt, och tillade sedan: "Tack för erbjudandet, men skall man då behandla bagarna på samma sätt som man vill göra nu, tycker vi synd om bagarna." På detta sätt vill jag svara att aggressiva kommer arbetsgivarna alltid att vara oavsett vilken organisationsform arbetarna har, tills dess de får så kraftigt mothugg så de lugnar sina rovdjurskänslor. Och då behövs det sannerligen syndikalistiskt försvarskraft. Därför kan inte en förtroendeman, om än med stor vilja, uträtta något ensamt - utan en vaken, handlingsfull och slagkraftig organisation.

Lusten att krossa arbetarnas organisationer har icke saknats av de privata arbetsgivarna - ej ens från styrelser och föreståndare för kooperativa bagerier i södra Sverge. Närmare angivet Skåne. Där har till och med öppna strider utbrutit.

Alla arbetsgivare vill ha utgifterna så små som möjligt. Men inkomsterna så stora som möjligt. Detta får ju främst arbetarna, producenterna, lida för.

Vidare hade Sjöstedt skrivit: "Lyssna på styrelserna för 'Föreningsbagerierna' och och för en del kooperativa bagerier vilka diskutera om bagarna på ett utmanande sätt, när det gäller deras avtal."

För min del tyckte jag att bagarna icke skulle bry sig om vad dessa konservativa styrelsemedlemmar pladdrar om. Och är det någon underhandling de ej vill bry sig om och önskar de icke vara med om någon överenskommelse som vi vet att de kan gå med på, behöver vi icke kompromissa och springa och berusa dessa herrar i all evighet, och tigga om rätt till mänsklig existens. Vi ha förmåga att slå till! Vi äro de starka! Gör slut på fegheten! Det är vi som är producenter!

Därför behöva att omändra organisationerna till kampduglighet och smidig anpassningsförmåga efter de förhållanden som kan uppstå. Vad de Lokala Samorganisationerna angår så äro de mest praktiska, och kan med heder avlösa de gamla tungrodda byråkratiska fackföreningarna, som äro i majoritet i detta land.

Att inte organisationsfrågan är ett aktuellt spörsmål just nu, bland bagarna, är en lögn av stort mått. Den är aktuell och skall bliva det ännu mer när tiden är mogen. Trots vad Sjöstedt skriver! Och hans ångest som så tydligt märks!

Allt sedan de reformistiska organisationernas början har i regel "förts de korslagda armarnas strid", som de gamla ledana är så förtjusta i - till borgardömets fromma!

Detta har visat sig odugligt. Vi har ju bagerier, som är bojkottade ända sedan den tid som "Svenska Bageri- och Konditoriarbetareförbundet" startades. Och det var inte i går!

Vi har exempel på detta i Göteborg och i Uddevalla, ja lite varstans i detta land.

Det skulle taga allt för stort utrymme i anspråk att räkna upp alla. Och när uppgörelse kommer att träffas vet ingen! Och ingen gör något för att ändring skall ske. Ingen delar ut så mycket som en bojkottslapp för att upplysa allmänheten om förhållandet, att konflikt råder. Därför behövs det pigga organisationer i vilka medlemmarna äro socialistiskt skolade och nyktra. Då kan vi marschera framåt och vinna något, trots det att arbetsgivarna göra allt för att slå ned vår frammarsch. Detta få ingen glömma!

Man skriver så ofta och påstår att folk är så egoistiska, att de ej vill betala avgifterna till föreningarna …

title: Sara Blum - Martyr Culture
content:
Author

: Sara Blum

Title

: Martyr Culture

Subtitle

: Revolutionary Culture in Rojava

Date

: June 2025

Notes

: This essay was written by Sara Blum, and internationalist who spent several years with the YPJ in Rojava, to accompany and contextualize

Orso: Wartime Journals of an Anarchist

,

 published in July 2025.

Source

: retrieved on 10/27/2026 from https://www.tangledwilderness.org/features/martyr-culture


I remain committed, until the end, to the struggle for liberation

and to the beauty and love it creates.


Abdullah Öcalan


 Kurdish friends, upon meeting an internationalist, often ask about our decision to come to their homeland in Rojava, Kurdistan. When they’d ask how I first came into contact with the friends, I felt a bit embarrassed to say that, honestly, the first friends of the movement I met were those who helped me after I actually arrived in Mesopotamia. (Editor’s note: “The friends” is a colloquialism stemming from the literal translation of the word “heval” which has historically been used by members of the Kurdish liberation movement to refer to each other.) I told them I learned about the movement by reading articles on a few different anarchist websites and contacted the friends by email. In fact, I knew so little about the movement that I first emailed YPG (People’s Protection Units) instead of YPJ (Women’s Protection Units). The friends were often amazed at this, and in their generosity considered it some kind of bravery or indication of the depth of my belief in the revolution and the people, rather than of naivety or impulsivity. It’s a common story among internationalists from the so-called USA, because the Kurdish Freedom Movement doesn’t have a presence here like it does in many parts of Europe, where there is a bigger Kurdish diaspora. When I initially went, I planned to stay for six months or a year. I ended up staying for several years, and for most of that time I was with the autonomous women’s military defense forces, YPJ.


 I decided to go in late 2018, and at that time it was hard to find much information about what to expect. Not much has changed in that regard. My dad told me to bring extra socks, and that before going I must read Che Guevara’s

On Guerrilla Warfare

. Other than that, most of the practical information about what to bring I received from an internationalist fighter whom I reached through an online message board. He said to bring all sorts of supplies, sent a packing list, and told me to bring a bunch of US dollars. He emphasized that I should bring water for border crossing across the mountains, which he said would be long and difficult, but to not share my water because the Kurdish comrades would pass it down the line until there was none left, and then I wouldn’t have water. The YPJ friend I was corresponding with told me I didn’t need much, and if it came to be that I needed something when I got there or along the way, comrades would sort it out then. This seemed to me rather casual at the time. I felt frustrated at the vagueness.


 Packing and repacking my bag, researching the weather conditions, trying to prepare as much as possible for what could be the rest of my short little life, I wanted all the information I could find and there wasn’t much. I didn’t realize then that I was encountering the first contrast of revolutionary and capitalist culture: different modes of being. The internationalist from the message board, with his best intentions, showed me one way to go about struggle, while the YPJ comrade showed me another way of joining the revolution. Preparing myself as an individual by making sure I had all the right specific things on the one hand, and on the other, preparing myself to take on the same circumstances as whomever I end up with and to sort all my needs within the context of our collective needs. As an internationalist from the West, the tension between these tendencies has long lived in me. I find that it still does, but I have also found that being out of water together always seems to be better than having water while the person next to me doesn’t.


 Before I left, I tried many times to write letters to my family, close friends, and comrades, which I would leave in the hands of a trusted friend so that, in the event of my death, they could be sent. I was determined to leave loved ones with some words of strength—I didn’t want to die, but since it was a distinct possibility, it was important to ensure that my death …

title: Рикардо Флорес Магон - Революция
content:
Автор

: Рикардо Флорес Магон

Название

: Революция

Дата

: 19 ноября 1910

Источник

: Regeneración


 Вот-вот упадёт вполне созревший плод внутреннего мятежа; плод горький для всех, кто возгордился положением, которое приносит почести, богатства и награды тем, кто основывает свои наслаждения на страдании и рабстве человечества; но плод сладкий и отрадный для всех, кто так или иначе ощутил на своём достоинстве копыта тех зверей, которые в одну ночь, длившуюся тридцать четыре года, крали, насиловали, убивали, обманывали, предавали, скрывая свои преступления под покровом закона и уклоняясь от кары под сенью официальной власти.


 Кто боится Революции? Те же самые, кто её вызвал; те, кто своим гнётом или своей эксплуатацией народных масс довёл до того, что отчаяние овладело жертвами их подлостей; те, кто несправедливостью и грабежом возмутил совесть и заставил бледнеть от негодования честных людей земли.


 Революция вот-вот разразится. Мы, столько лет следившие за всеми событиями общественной и политической жизни мексиканского народа, не можем обманываться. Симптомы грозного катаклизма не оставляют места сомнению в том, что нечто вот-вот возникнет и нечто вот-вот рухнет, что нечто воспрянет и нечто вот-вот падёт. Наконец, после тридцати четырёх лет позора, поднимет голову мексиканский народ, и наконец, после этой долгой ночи, обратится в развалины чёрное здание, чья тяжесть нас душила.


 Сейчас уместно снова сказать то, что мы говорили так часто: нужно сделать так, чтобы это движение, вызванное отчаянием, не стало слепым движением того, кто делает усилие, чтобы сбросить с себя вес огромной ноши, – движением, в котором инстинкт почти полностью господствует над разумом. Мы, либертарии, должны позаботиться о том, чтобы это движение приняло направление, которое указывает Наука. Если этого не сделать, поднимающаяся Революция послужит лишь тому, чтобы заменить одного Президента другим Президентом, или, что то же самое, одного хозяина другим хозяином. Мы должны помнить, что нужно, чтобы у народа был хлеб, было жильё, была земля для обработки; мы должны помнить, что никакое Правительство, сколь бы честным оно ни было, не может декретировать отмену нищеты. Именно сам народ, именно голодные, именно обездоленные должны отменить нищету, в первую очередь вступив во владение землёй, которая по естественному праву не может быть прибрана к рукам несколькими, но является собственностью всякого человеческого существа. Невозможно предсказать, до какого предела дойдёт дело восстановления прав в грядущей Революции; но если мы, борцы доброй воли, несём намерение продвинуться по этому пути как можно дальше; если, берясь за винчестер, мы идём решительно не к возвышению очередного хозяина, но к восстановлению прав пролетариата; если мы несём на поле вооружённой борьбы стремление завоевать экономическую свободу, которая есть основа всех свобод, которая есть условие, без которого нет никакой свободы; если мы несём это намерение, мы направим грядущее народное движение по пути, достойному этой эпохи; но если из желания легко победить; если из стремления поскорее закончить борьбу мы уберём из наших устремлений тот радикализм, который делает их несовместимыми с устремлениями чисто буржуазных и консервативных партий, тогда мы совершим дело разбойников и убийц, ибо пролитая кровь послужит лишь тому, чтобы придать больше силы буржуазии, то есть касте, владеющей богатством, которая после победы снова наденет цепь на пролетариат, чьей кровью, чьей жертвой, чьим мученичеством она завоевала власть.


 Итак, необходимо, пролетарии; необходимо, обездоленные, чтобы вы не обманывались. Консервативные и буржуазные партии говорят вам о свободе, о справедливости, о законе, о честном правительстве и говорят вам, что, если народ сменит людей, стоящих у Власти, на других, у вас будет свобода, будет справедливость, будет закон, будет честное правительство. Не давайте себя обмануть. Вам нужно, чтобы вам обеспечили довольство ваших семей и хлеб насущный; довольство семей не сможет дать вам никакое Правительство. Это вы сами должны завоевать эти блага, с самого начала вступив во владение землёй, которая есть первоисточник богатства, а землю не сможет дать вам никакое Правительство, – поймите это хорошо! – потому что закон защищает

право

author: 张皓翔
title: The Dislocation of Vendémiaire (Part I): The 21st-Century Breakthrough Actors and Ideological Collusion【A commentary on the French riots between September and October】
content: This article takes the French student-led protests and unrest between September and October 2026 as its point of departure. It rejects the mainstream interpretation of the movement as a broad multi-class alliance of diverse demands, and instead argues that it reflects a deep internal differentiation and fragmentation of the proletariat under digital capitalism. While affirming the student group’s role as a “quasi-proletariat” and an early outpost of struggle, the article contends that the movement remained at a pre-Marxist spontaneous stage because it lacked a scientific program and the integration of an advanced party. It proposes “actual control over the production of labor power” as the core criterion for class analysis and describes the movement as a “dislocated” struggle shaped by an ideological collusion between bourgeois narratives and the movement’s own political weaknesses.

Title

Subtitle

Date

Notes

ideas & action

 on whether or not anarcho-syndicalists and libertarian socialists should participate in the Democratic Socialists of America (DSA).

Source

Editors’ Note/Introduction:

Bureaucratic Utopianism?

,

by Tom Wetzel


The last few years have been a discouraging period for those in the U. S. who want fundamental change in the direction of freedom and equality. Though struggle against the powers-that-be goes on, as always, struggles in the last few years have tended to be episodic and isolated. It’s hard to find signs of a widespread willingness to fight the bosses and the government. This lack of movement among the mainstream of the population is, in all likelihood, the root cause of the general political drift to the right and, as well, the evolution towards social-democracy among so many leftists whose radicalism had been spawned by the movements of the late 60s and early

 ’70s.

One evidence of this latter trend was the evolution of the New American Movement (NAM) away from the revolutionary New Left politics of its origin, culminating in its merger last year with Michael Harrington’s Democratic Socialist Organizing Committee

 (

DSOC) — a tiny social-democratic sect that had emerged from the break-up of the old Socialist Party in 1972. That split-up had been itself a reflection of the Vietnam War, since the Socialist Party of the 1960s had been firmly in the hands of the “State Department socialists” who thought the Communists were such a threat that it merited allying themselves with U.S. bosses, by supporting the U.S. government’s imperialist foreign policy. This fit in with the practice of cooperation with the bosses which characterized the union chiefs who controlled the Socialist Party in those days. The split in the SP created three groups

 —

the majority formed the Social Democrats USA, made up of such class-collaborationist union leaders as Lloyd McBride of the United Steelworkers and Albert Shanker of the American Federation of Teachers. They had no compunction about supporting U.S. imperialism in Indo-China (and anywhere else) right to the bitter end. In 1981, for example, Shanker’s AFT ran a major spread in the “American Teacher” supporting U.S. policy in El Salvador as a struggle for “democracy” (even while members of the Salvadoran teachers union were being tortured or hunted down by forces of the local dictatorship). Another outfit that came out of the break-up of the old SP was the group headed by ex-Milwaukee mayor Frank Zeidler which resurrected the name “Socialist Party “ for itself. This group opposed the Vietnam war but more on the basis of liberal pacifist than class-struggle grounds. And finally, the third fragment from the old SP was Harrington’s liberal group who had no consistently anti-militarist or anti-imperialist position (for example, they have supported U.S. military aid to Israel until just recently) but who simply followed the evolution of the liberal mainstream in its belated opposition to the Vietnam War. Democratic Socialists of America (DSA) is the organization which resulted from the absorption of NAM by Harrington’s DSOC. Chris Nielsen, whose piece on “DSA and Libertarian Socialists” we are printing here, recommends the “democratic socialist” milieu — and specifically DSA — as an appropriate area for participation by anti-authoritarian socialists or anarchists. Though we disagree with Chris’ conclusion, we think he raises a number of issues worth discussing. Social democratic ideas are on the rise, and the sort of position Chris argues for is one that needs to be answered by libertarian socialists.


What is “social-democracy’’? Social-democracy is not unique in pursuing or supporting short-range changes to benefit working people — the revolutionary libertarian unions of the early decades of this century, such as the IWW in this country, used militant tactics for goals short of class emancipation. Social-democratic politics is typified by a reliance on electoral politics with the union bureaucracy providing the major base of support. Social-democratic tactics have traditionally led to a statist conception of what socialism is all about — …

Мак-Кинли, глава североамериканской олигархии, орудие и защитник крупных капиталистов, предатель кубинцев и филиппинцев, человек, санкционировавший расправу над бастующими в Хэзлтоне, пытки шахтёров Айдахо и тысячу гнусностей, ежедневно совершаемых против рабочих в «образцовой республике», тот, кто воплощал милитаристскую, завоевательную, империалистическую политику, в которую ринулась американская буржуазия, пал жертвой револьвера анархиста.

О чём вы хотите, чтобы мы скорбели, если не о судьбе, уготованной великодушному человеку, который – уместно или неуместно, с хорошей или плохой тактикой – принёс себя в жертву делу равенства и свободы?

Повторим это и в данном случае, как и во всех аналогичных: поскольку мы находимся в обществе волков, где насилие окружает нас и разит со всех сторон, мы, продолжая спокойно бороться за то, чтобы прекратилась эта ужасная необходимость отвечать на насилие насилием, – хотя и желая, чтобы скорее наступил день, когда антагонизмы интересов и страстей между людьми можно будет разрешать человеческими и цивилизованными средствами, – бережём свои слёзы и свои цветы для других жертв, а не для этих людей, которые, становясь во главе эксплуататорских и угнетательских классов, берут на себя ответственность и идут на риск, связанный с их положением.

И всё же нашлись анархисты, которые сочли полезным и прекрасным оскорблять угнетённого, который восстаёт, не имея ни слова осуждения для угнетателя, понёсшего кару за преступления, которые он совершил или позволил совершить!

Это извращение, это нездоровое желание получить одобрение противников, или же неосмотрительная ловкость, которая хотела бы завоевать свободу пропаганды своих идей, добровольно отказываясь от права выражать истинное и глубокое чувство души, – более того, искажая это чувство, притворяясь не тем, что есть?

Я делаю это с сожалением, но не могу не выразить боль и возмущение, которые вызвали во мне и во всех товарищах, каких мне довелось видеть в эти дни, необдуманные слова, посвящённые Agitazione покушению в Буффало.

Чолгош – несознательный человек! Но знают ли они его? Его поступок – обычное преступление, не имеющее ни одного из признаков, необходимых для того, чтобы подобный акт мог считаться политическим!

Полагаю, что ни один государственный обвинитель – королевский или республиканский – не осмелился бы утверждать нечто подобное. В самом деле, есть ли хоть какой-нибудь повод судить о Чолгоше как о человеке, движимом личными интересами или личной злобой? Разве не ясно, что он действовал по мотивам общественного порядка и намеревался – с основанием или без основания, но, несомненно, искренне и самоотверженно – принести себя в жертву ради дела? И разве не эти элементы придают факту наиболее яркий характер политико-социального покушения?

Впрочем, неправильно говорить о преступлении в подобных случаях. Кодекс это делает, но кодекс создан против нас, против угнетённых, и не может служить критерием для наших суждений.

Эти факты – акты войны; и если война есть преступление, то она преступление для тех, кто в ней стоит на стороне несправедливости и угнетения. Преступниками могут быть, являются английские захватчики Трансвааля; ими не являются буры, когда защищают свою свободу, даже если защита была бы безнадёжной.

Поступок Чолгоша (могла бы ответить Agitazione) нисколько не продвинул дело пролетариата и революции: Вместо Мак-Кинли придет Рузвельт, такой же, как и он, и всё останется как прежде, разве что положение анархистов станет немного труднее. И, возможно, Agitazione была бы права; более того, в американской среде, насколько я её знаю, мне это кажется вероятным.

Это значит, что на войне есть ходы удачные и ошибочные, есть бойцы осмотрительные и есть те, кто …

author: Guerre de Classe
title: Towards the Hot Autumn 2026!
content:
Occupations of schools and squares, confrontations with police, strikes, blockades of roads and ports, burning State buildings, lootings… In France, in Belgium, in Spain, in Albania, in Argentina… in Italy…

Occupations of schools and squares, confrontations with police, strikes, blockades of roads and ports, burning State buildings, lootings… In France, in Belgium, in Spain, in Albania, in Argentina… in Italy…

High school students, university students, teachers, steel workers, dockers, farm workers, inhabitants of suburbs and “popular housing” – in short the working class – are revolting against this shitty capitalist reality!

The global Capital and its State can’t bring us anything else than always accelerating misery, life of exploitation and alienation or death.

A perspective it has for us is to be a cannon fodder in the capitalist war or to drain our life force “on the home front”. And if we are lucky not to live in the war zone and our limbs are not teared off by the killer drones, there is still a climate catastrophe, pollution and toxic food, poverty, prisons, state control, militarization, digital slavery…

Now the ruling class is starting to panic – they are afraid that we will overcome the categories to which they locked us in – students, workers, pensioners, unemployed, men or women, “Italians”, “French” or “Albanians”, white or black, local or immigrants, “Western” or “Eastern”… they are afraid that we realize that we have common class interests as proletarians across all the borders and categories. And on the contrary, we have opposing class interests to them, even if they happen to look the same or speak the same language.

They are afraid of ghosts of May 1968, the Hot Autumn in Italy of 1969-70, the Movement of ‘77, uprising in Albania in 97, the “Arab Spring”, the “Yellow Vests”, the “One Piece uprising” of 2025…

Their cops and thugs attack us and to repress our movement, but we are not afraid! On the contrary we pass into a counter-attack!

Their trade unions try to pacify our struggle, pretending that they can order us back to work, but we do not obey!

Their political parties try to fool us to give up our own class emancipation and let them “represent us”, but we spit on democracy! We do not trust these snake-oil merchants regardless if they are “right-wing”, “left-wing” or even pretending to be “communists” (by which they mean red painted capitalism in the style of Lenin, Mao or Hoxha)!

Their propagandists on social media or in TV try to misrepresent our interests and pit us against each other, but we laugh into their faces!

We inspire each other despite the national borders imposed on us by our class enemies. Let’s take it a step further and let’s organize ourselves internationally against all nation states! Against the State!!!

Let’s turn the schools, factories, offices, barracks, prisons, streets, squares and neighborhoods of every city into a battleground between us who struggle for a revolutionary change and them who want to preserve the World of exploitation!

Against the capitalist war and the capitalist peace – towards the global uprising for communism!

A contemporary study of Proudhonian ideas might have one of two objectives. Either we will strive to retrace Proudhon’s historical physiognomy,{1} discover the guiding principles of his thought, and explain them by his heredity and temperament, the social circles he lived in, and the events he witnessed. Or else, concerned more with utility than with reconstruction, we will retain from Proudhonism only what may be used by scholars to understand today’s world and foresee tomorrow’s, and by reformers to build an effective, fruitful doctrine for action. Both methods are equally legitimate. The first is necessary for historians of ideas, for whoever wishes to restore Proudhon to us as he was. The second should be preferred if we seek less to describe the past than to shed light on the present and prepare for the future.

Depending on which of these two angles we approach it from, the relationship between Proudhonism and Marxism appears very different.

Historically, Proudhon and Marx are adversaries and constitute an antithesis.[1] After having maintained friendly and sustained relations in 1844 during Marx’s stay in France, and having spent whole nights discussing philosophy and political economy, they fell out irremediably when Marx replied to Economic Contradictions with The Poverty of Philosophy and disdainfully dismissed Proudhon as petty-bourgeois. The years passed without softening this animosity. In 1865, in his famous letter to the Sozial-Demokrat, Marx did not hesitate to judge Proudhon’s memoir in these terms, forgetting his past praise: ‘What Is Property? In a rigorously scientific history of political economy this work would scarcely be worthy of mention’, and he protested against Proudhon’s ‘scientific charlatanism’, ‘unbearable chatter’, and ‘imbecile cynicism’.[2]

In fact, between Proudhon and Marx the contrast of spirit and tendency is obvious. Whereas Marxist thought arose from the development of industrial life, from large-scale production concentrated and socialised in its technical forms if not in its legal regime, Proudhonian thought is fundamentally rural in origin and orientation: the social cell of the future society that Proudhon envisages is neither the factory nor the workers’ group, but the peasant family with austere morals and an individualistic life, whose property, founded on possession, takes on an absolute and sacred character. If Marx holds that the fundamental explanation of world history lies in variations of economic technique, according to Proudhon the guiding thread that enables us to find our way in the chaos of historical events is philosophical in nature: history is a long process of reasoning and society a metaphysics in action. And while for Marx only a change in the mode of production is capable of putting an end to economic instability and class struggle, Proudhon seeks the solution of the social problem in a reform of circulation and exchange, leading gradually to the disappearance of all usurious levies.

title: DEM Party: The Republic must be updated
content:
The Turkish Republic was officially proclaimed on 29 October 1923 in Ankara, the country's new capital. In a statement titled “May the Republic endure, democracy prevail, and the brotherhood of peoples remain eternal in the second century,” the co-chairs of the DEM Party, Tülay Hatimoğulları and Tuncer Bakırhan marked the 103rd anniversary saying that citizenship could only be fully realised through an understanding that guarantees equal protection for everyone’s language, identity, culture, beliefs and opinions. The statement emphasised that Turks, Kurds and other peoples, together with all religious communities, are equal owners of the country.


The message added: “A democratic future can only be built through a shared life in which we all have an equal voice and an equal say in decision-making. A Türkiye in which women live as equals, workers enjoy security, young people have hope, and the law applies equally to everyone is possible. A Democratic Republic is one in which no one is required to be like anyone else and the will of the people is respected. This is also a vision of a country where people can live together in greater peace and harmony. An independent judiciary, the rule of law, universal human rights, a free press, the separation of powers and strong local democracy are essential to achieving this.”


The statement said that the Republic’s embrace of multiple identities would not weaken shared citizenship but would instead strengthen it. It also called for a new beginning without denying the painful experiences of the past.


The message continued: “The founding idea of the Republic is valuable, and it needs to be updated so that it meets the needs of today. If we place democratic principles at the centre of every area, from legislation to institutional structures, the Republic will provide the foundation for a country associated with peace and harmony. The Republic’s embrace of multiple identities does not weaken shared citizenship or common values; it strengthens them. We have the opportunity to turn a new page by standing side by side, without denying the pain of the past but without remaining imprisoned by it.”


Tülay Hatimoğulları and Bakırhan said that freedom, equality and justice must be guaranteed for everyone. They added that creating the conditions for peace, democratic politics and social reconciliation to flourish was a shared responsibility.

title: Journalist Mavioğlu: Corruption in Turkey has become institutionalised plunder - Part One
content:
As the Peace and Democratic Society Process continues in Turkey, investigations into financial scandals, match-fixing and betting operations in football, allegations of corruption in public tenders and links to the criminal underworld have once again brought relations between politics, capital and criminal networks into focus.


Journalist Ertuğrul Mavioğlu spoke to ANF about how corruption has developed into a systematic structure over the years, the mechanisms through which public resources are transferred to capital and how this system is sustained through impunity.


Mavioğlu also discussed the current stage of the Peace and Democratic Society Process, saying that the state had failed to take concrete steps towards democratisation despite the measures taken by the Kurdish Freedom Movement. He argued that the struggle against corruption could not be separated from the struggle for democracy, as the weakening of oversight mechanisms and the suppression of public dissent had facilitated the plundering of public resources.


‘The state aims to dismantle the Freedom Movement’


Mavioğlu assessed the current stage of the Peace and Democratic Society Process in light of the steps taken by the Kurdish Freedom Movement and the state's response, saying that the process was still in its early stages.


He criticised the framework law passed by parliament for being limited to disarmament and for making its implementation dependent on verification by the security bureaucracy.


Mavioğlu said: “We are still at the very beginning of the Peace and Democratic Society Process. The main reason is that, despite a series of important steps taken by the Kurdish Freedom Movement, the state has yet to take any clear and concrete action. Parliament passed an extremely inadequate framework law and, at the same time, handed over its authority to the security bureaucracy. In other words, for the law to come into force, disarmament must first be established and verified. It is not yet clear how long this will take.


Another issue is that the law is limited solely to disarmament and contains nothing concerning democratisation or the collective rights of the Kurds. Although the Kurdish side has accepted this as the first step on a thousand-kilometre journey, statements from the state offer no glimmer of hope regarding democratisation. Meanwhile, anti-democratic practices continue with undiminished intensity and severity.


Yet the government does not need any new legislation to abandon the appointment of trustees, which amounts to the usurpation of the people's will, or to stop effectively condemning sick prisoners to death. Nor does it need legislation to end the repression and intimidation of journalists, attempts to reshape the opposition through bribery and pressure, or the violent suppression of protests demanding rights. Nevertheless, everything continues as before.”


Mavioğlu argued that the state's decision to call the process a “Terror-free Turkey” process was not merely a matter of terminology, claiming that the state aimed to dismantle the organised structure of the Kurdish Freedom Movement.


Mavioğlu continued: “In other words, the state's description of this process as a ‘Terror-free Turkey’ process is not a mistake in terminology. The state's real objective is not simply to disarm the Kurdish Freedom Movement. Various statements make it clear that there is an attempt to impose surrender by demanding that the movement dismantle its organised structure. It is therefore possible to say that, from the state's perspective, this process has nothing to do with democracy.


On the other hand, the Kurdish Freedom Movement has not left the Peace and Democratic Society Process entirely at the mercy of the state from the outset. In fact, because they know that the Turkish state will not take democratic steps of its own accord, they regard the transition to democracy as a process of struggle.


Seen from this perspective, it is possible to answer your question with both yes and no. If you simply wait for the state to act, you will continue to live under repression and coercion. But the more you struggle, the greater your chances of securing democratic rights.”

title: YJA Star guerrillas: We gained our identity as resisting women through Bêrîtan
content:
Commander Bêrîtan (Gülnaz Karataş) was commemorated by her comrades in the guerrilla areas on the 34th anniversary of her martyrdom. Commander Bêrîtan was martyred in 1992 after carrying out a self-sacrificial action in Xakurkê during the war against the Turkish state and its collaborators. Bêrîtan, who became a symbol of women who refused to submit in the face of calls for surrender, established a new path of struggle. Guerrillas of the Free Women's Units (YJA Star) shared their feelings and thoughts on the anniversary of Martyr Bêrîtan's death.


YJA Star guerrilla Avaşîn Efrîn

 


 


"First of all, on the anniversary of Comrade Bêrîtan's martyrdom, we respectfully commemorate all the martyrs of freedom. We have reached this stage thanks to the efforts and truth of our pioneering martyrs. We will never forget the efforts of these heroes. Through her stance, Comrade Bêrîtan showed us the path of self-sacrifice. Bêrîtan's path is the path of freedom, and it is also the path of all martyrs. We unite around this path and educate ourselves on this basis. Particularly in this period, establishing genuine comradeship with Abdullah Öcalan is possible through a proper understanding of the martyrs. Thanks to Comrade Bêrîtan, we learned how to struggle as YJA Star guerrillas, came to know ourselves and developed an identity. On this basis, we renew our promise to uphold the legacy of the martyrs."


YJA Star guerrilla Azê Azad 


 


"On the anniversary of Comrade Bêrîtan's martyrdom, I respectfully commemorate all our martyred comrades. Upholding the dreams of our martyred comrades is a fundamental duty for us. Words may be inadequate to express our feelings about Martyr Bêrîtan. However, today we follow in Comrade Bêrîtan's footsteps and want to wage a genuine struggle worthy of the martyrs of freedom. Through her efforts and knowledge, Bêrîtan reached the highest level of self-sacrifice, and the women's army was established through her example. We have reached this point today thanks to Comrade Bêrîtan's sacrifice. As YJA Star guerrillas, we will uphold the dreams of our martyred comrades who sought to secure Abdullah Öcalan's freedom and strengthen our struggle."


YJA Star guerrilla Bêrîtan Zagros 


 


"As YJA Star guerrillas, we commemorate all our comrades who were martyred in October through the example of Comrade Bêrîtan, and we promise to fulfil their dreams. As YJA Star, we are carrying out such a strong struggle today particularly thanks to the legacy of the martyrs. Through Bêrîtan, we gained our identity as women of resistance. Martyr Bêrîtan's stance did not remain confined to the past; it is kept alive at every moment.


Just as Comrade Bêrîtan took the path of Besê and Zarîfe as her guiding principle and resisted, we also uphold the path of free women on the basis of the truth of those martyrs. Comrade Bêrîtan constantly strove to understand the reality of Abdullah Öcalan's leadership. She had developed a clear commitment to this path and therefore adopted radical and organised positions. This stance formed the foundation of our freedom struggle. Our aim is to secure the physical freedom of Abdullah Öcalan and uphold the struggle and dreams of the martyrs."

title: Shengal is at a historic turning point
content:
Shengal is now at a historic turning point. Shengal’s existence and integration bring with them a comprehensive unity with Iraq. The integration of the collective will and the genuine integration of people’s everyday lives represent the first concrete step towards bringing the two communities together in a shared life, while preserving their mother tongues and native cultures. The political reality and future represent a historic stage in which this social unity is translated into a political reality.


The coming together of the two communities through their respective cultural values and their ability to live in their mother tongues forms the cornerstone of this process. This political and cultural integration carries a force that connects with the reality of Abdullah Öcalan’s life and unites the entire society around this collective will.


This historic process expresses the will of the people of Shengal to determine their own future and live on an equal footing with Iraqi society, while also laying the foundations for building a shared future, peace and stability.


A shared political future aims to strengthen the political and social status of the Shengal region within Iraq as a whole and to permanently enshrine the people’s right to self-determination on a constitutional basis.


The integration process enables people of different faiths and identities to develop practices of coexistence based on social peace and tolerance. It is clear that the harmony fostered by integration will contribute to preserving regional stability and establishing lasting peace in Shengal and the surrounding areas.


The integration of security and administrative structures also involves reorganising the region’s security and administrative mechanisms so that they are aligned with the collective will of the people.


Socio-economic development and the integration of services will also improve people’s living standards by strengthening the region’s infrastructure, healthcare and education services.


Historical memory and recognition of identity


This process also entails preserving historical memory and acknowledging the truth, demonstrating respect for the region’s past and enabling its people to look towards the future with confidence in their own identity.


Shengal’s legal status and administrative structure within Iraq as a whole are being balanced within a framework of mutual respect and shared interests with other communities in the region. The key to the success of this process lies in the people’s will and their ability to shape their own future through their own collective decisions, across every area, from infrastructure to education.


Democratic Participation and Representation:

 The process is based on a participatory model of democracy that ensures different segments of society are represented equally and effectively within governing institutions.


Pluralistic Representation and Participatory Politics:

 The integration process has been designed to ensure that the will of all social groups, religious communities and women’s councils living throughout Shengal is reflected at the highest level in governing institutions. Rather than a narrow structure of power, this approach demonstrates a commitment to implementing an egalitarian, participatory political model that develops from the grassroots upwards. In this way, every individual’s voice can be represented in the process of governance.


The Principles of Justice and Equal Citizenship:

 The integration process is based on establishing justice in the region and fully safeguarding the constitutional rights of all ethnic and religious groups. This is intended to guarantee equality before the law for every segment of society and peaceful coexistence within a democratic legal order.


Distinctive Education and Cultural Preservation:

 The integration process guarantees the restructuring of the region’s education system in accordance with the principle of education in the mother tongue, as well as the transmission of cultural heritage to future generations. This is a critical step towards protecting and strengthening local identity.

title: Iran sentences three protest detainees to death, whereabouts unknown
content:
Branch 23 of the Islamic Revolutionary Court in Tehran has sentenced three men arrested during the December 2025–January 2026 protests to death on charges of “espionage.”


An informed source who spoke to the Kurdistan Human Rights Network (KHRN) said that the men, named Mehdi, Amir-Reza and Vahid, were notified of their sentences in Greater Tehran Central Penitentiary on 26 October.


The source added that on 28 October, the three political prisoners were summoned to the prison’s guard office on the pretext of being transferred to Ghezel Hesar Prison in Karaj, but were taken to an undisclosed location.


Security forces arrested the three men during the protests in Tehran and transferred them to the Greater Tehran Central Penitentiary after a period in detention. Their case was referred to Branch 23 following their indictment on charges of “espionage”, the source said.


At the time of the report, their transfer to Ghezel Hesar Prison remained unconfirmed, with no precise information available about the trial proceedings or the latest status of their cases.

title: Kurdish Peace Mothers to launch a vigil in Ankara
content:
The Peace Mothers Initiative aims to increase pressure for concrete steps in the peace and democratic society process through a multi-day vigil in the Turkish capital, Ankara. Representatives of the Peace Mothers’ Councils from 24 cities will gather on November 1, hold talks with political parties, and set up a protest tent. Their central demands include freedom for Abdullah Öcalan, action to address the situation of political prisoners, and accountability from the Turkish state for advancing the peace process.


At a press conference held at the branch of the Human Rights Association (IHD) in the province of Amed (Turkish: Diyarbakır), Nezahat Teke recalled that Öcalan’s call on February 27, 2025, had raised great hopes. “However, for these hopes to develop into a genuine peace process, the state must also take action. If Öcalan is not free, any laws that are passed will be meaningless,” Teke said.


Demands for Öcalan’s freedom and improved prison conditions


The Peace Mothers are demanding that Öcalan be granted a legally and politically recognized status that would enable him to participate actively in the peace process. According to Teke, his inclusion in existing or planned commissions could make a significant contribution to advancing the process. “Our most important demand is the freedom and recognition of our leader’s status. Talks are held only once every two months, and that is not enough. The person who can bring about a solution is Abdullah Öcalan,” Teke said.


She also drew attention to conditions in Turkish prisons, saying: “Numerous prisoners are seriously ill, while others are being denied release despite having served their sentences. The Peace Mothers no longer want to see prisoners returning from detention facilities only after their deaths.”


Talks with political parties planned through Tuesday


The delegations plan to present their demands in Ankara. In addition to meetings with political parties, they intend to hold a vigil and submit documents outlining the Peace Mothers’ concerns. “We will go to Ankara and convey our demands to the political parties. We will stay there until Tuesday,” Teke stated. She also called on civil society organizations in the capital to show solidarity: “Today, everyone has something to say about peace. They should support the mothers as well.”


The Peace Mothers hope that political leaders will respond to their demands. “We will present our documents, demands, and concerns in Ankara. We hope they will receive us and not send us back empty-handed,” Teke said. In closing, she appealed to the media to refrain from using language that fuels hostility and obstructs peace.
