content:
Hrant Dink cinayetinin ardından oluşan ortak hafızayı konu edinen “Özgürlüğü Kanadında: Hrant Dink İçin Öyküler” kitabı 31 Ekim’de yayımlanacak.


İletişim Yayınları etiketli ile okurla buluşacak kitabın kapak çizimini Kemal Gökhan Gürses’in hazırladı. Esere aralarında Selahattin Demirtaş’ın da bulunduğu 20 yazar öyküleriyle katkı sundu.


20 edebiyatçı aynı vicdan atlasında buluştu


Agos'un haberne göre, kitapta; Karin Karakaşlı, Murathan Mungan, Rıdvan Hatun, Sema Kaygusuz, Sevim Çiçek, Ayfer Tunç, Irmak Zileli,Murat Gülsoy, Melisa Kesmez, Murat Uyurkulak, Selahattin Demirtaş, Behçet Çelik, Kerem Bakıcı, Polat Özlüoğlu,Kâmil Erdem, Fethiye Çetin, Şebnem İşigüzel, Figen Alkaç, Ayşegül Devecioğlu ve Eylem Ata’nın özel olarak kaleme aldığı öyküler bulunuyor.


“Buradayız Ahparig”


Gaye Boralıoğlu, kitabın

“İnattan Umuda, Umuttan Hakikate”

 başlıklı sunuş yazısında, cinayetin ardından oluşan toplumsal acının kişisel hikâyelerle nasıl birleştiğine dikkat çekiyor. Oluşan bu ortak hafızanın, farklılıkların bir arada kardeşçe yaşayabildiği adil bir geleceğin temelini oluşturduğunu belirten Boralıoğlu, edebiyatçıların bu derlemeyle Hrant’a yeniden seslendiğini ifade ediyor:


"Şimdi bu kitapta bu kez edebiyatçılar ‘Buradayız Ahparig’ diye sesleniyorlar. Onun sözünden, sesinden, yok edilememiş varlığından ilham alarak kendi edebî dünyalarını yeniden kuruyorlar. Yazdıkları öykülerle Hrant’ın sözünü genişletirken, bir yandan da o büyük vicdan atlasının parçası oluyorlar."


Sunuş yazısında Hrant Dink’in yüz binlerin katıldığı cenaze törenindeki o unutulmaz simgeye değinen Boralıoğlu; siyahlar içindeki Ermeni gençlerin taşıdığı tabuta cenaze boyunca eşlik eden beyaz güvercinleri hatırlatıyor. Boralıoğlu,kaleme alınan öyküler ile bu simge arasındaki bağı şu dokunaklı sözlerle özetliyor:


"Bugün o güvercinler bu öykülerin arasında dolaşıyor; Hrant’ın ruhuna, o güzel ruha bizden de bir selam götürmek için."

title: Bir ayda ikinci emekli polis intiharı: Ekonomik koşullar karşısında hayatlar sönüyor
content:
Zonguldak'ta 2023 yılında emekliye ayrılan 51 yaşındaki polis memuru Baskın Pekmen, 21 Ekim'de babasının mezarı başında ölü bulundu. Üç çocuk babası Pekmen'in, yaşamını yitirmeden önce evinden ayrılırken bir not bıraktığı, borçlarının bulunduğu ve ailesine "Size iyi bakamadım" yazılı bir mektup yazdığı öğrenildi.

Sözcü'den Cengiz Karagöz'ün haberine göre, Yeni Parti Zonguldak Milletvekili Deniz Yavuzyılmaz, Baskın Pekmen'in ölümüne ilişkin yaptığı açıklamada, emeklilerin yaşadığı ekonomik sorunlara dikkat çekti. Yavuzyılmaz, "Emeklileri yoksulluğa, aileleri çaresizliğe mahkum eden ekonomik koşullar karşısında hayatlar sönmeye devam ediyor. Çok üzgünüm" dedi.

Birleşik Emekliler Sendikası da yaptığı açıklamada, emeklilerin yaşadığı geçim sıkıntısına tepki gösterdi. İktidarın seçim dönemlerinde emeklilere yönelik sınırlı düzenlemelerle oy desteği sağlamaya çalıştığı ifade edilen açıklamada, "Ama biz emekliler yapılanı unutmayacağız, sandıkta hesabını soracağız. Bizler oy deposu değiliz" denildi.

Emekli dernekleri ve sendikaların zam talebiyle Ankara'da AYM önünde yaptığı eylem sırasında "Geçinemiyorum" diyerek kendisini vuran emekli polis Ali Şekeroğlu hayatını kaybetmişti.

author: Publicación Abierta
title: La impunidad de Machado
content:
Diez meses fuera y vuelve en caravana


El 25 de octubre, María Corina Machado regresó a Venezuela. Recorrió el país, de Barquisimeto a Caracas, entre banderas y vítores, como quien vuelve de unas vacaciones. Y, sin embargo, desde el propio Gobierno venezolano se la había calificado de prófuga de la justicia y se había advertido de que «tendrá que rendir cuentas» si pisaba el país. No ha rendido ninguna. Se pasea libremente, aclamada y sin que nadie le pida explicaciones.


El historial de la que vuelve


Conviene recordar quién es. La que llamó a las guarimbas. La que incitó a la violencia y al enfrentamiento entre venezolanos. La que pidió, una y otra vez, la intervención militar de los Estados Unidos de Trump y del Israel de Netanyahu contra su propio país. La que reclamó sanciones contra su pueblo y apoyó el sabotaje para rendir a Venezuela por hambre, sin medicinas, sin comida, sin lo más básico para la vida. Una venepatria de manual, que nunca dudó en poner su tierra en bandeja a las potencias extranjeras.


Su amo la despacha con un «muy agradable»


Y mírese cómo recibe su amo el regreso de su sierva. Preguntado por los periodistas, Trump respondió: «Es una mujer muy agradable. Me dio su Premio Nobel, así que ¿cómo puedo decir otra cosa? Y espero que esté a salvo». Ni una palabra más. Enseguida, a lo suyo: a Estados Unidos, dijo, le va «realmente bien en Venezuela». Ese es todo el pago por años de servicio y por regalarle hasta el Nobel. El 3 de enero, el día de la captura de Maduro, ya la había descartado para dirigir el país con la misma fórmula: muy agradable, pero sin el respeto necesario. Así pagan los imperios a quienes les sirven: los usan mientras son útiles y les dan una palmadita cuando estorban.


Una justicia para cada clase


Que nadie se engañe: esta impunidad no es un accidente; es justicia de clase. A quien se juega el sueldo defendiendo a sus compañeros en un centro de trabajo le piden cuentas por mucho menos. A quien trabajó para que el sufrimiento llegase a miles de familias venezolanas la recibe una multitud, con las cámaras de medio mundo apuntando hacia ella. Hay una vara de medir para el pueblo trabajador y otra muy distinta para quienes sirven a los poderosos.


No hay redención para quien traiciona a su pueblo


No hay perdón para quien ayudó a traer tanto dolor a Venezuela. Nunca pensé que llegaría a ver cómo quienes empujaron a la guerra, a la necesidad y a la muerte caminan tranquilos por la calle, sin pagar por sus actos. Con el Nobel de la Paz colgado, además: un premio concedido a quien se ha pasado la vida pidiendo la invasión de su propio país, convertido así en el Nobel de la vergüenza. Pero esa vergüenza palidece ante lo que hoy vemos en Venezuela. El pueblo venezolano sabe quién le hizo daño, y la historia no suele ser tan indulgente como un presidente con quien le hace un regalo.


¡Até á vitoria sempre!


André Abeledo Fernández

La impunidad de Machado

title: Ephéméride des luttes : 28 octobre
content:
L'éphéméride des luttes du 28 octobre abhorre les fascistes, comme toujours, ainsi que les armées et les patrons. Elle se méfie toujours autant des faux alliés autoritaires et pose de nouvelles bases pour un mouvement féministe, tout en ne reniant pas sa culture émeutière.


1791 :

 Olympe de Gouges, militante "proto-féministe", présente la

Déclaration des Droits de la Femme et de la Citoyenne

 à l'Assemblée nationale.


1893 :

 A Chicago (Etats-Unis), "

un individu qu'on dit être un anarchiste pénétra dans la résidence du maire de Chicago Mr. Carter Harrison et le tua de plusieurs coups de révolver. Mr. Harrison avait été plusieurs fois menacé par les anarchistes et un attentat avait été commis contre lui, sans succès, quelques semaines auparavant

".


Repris de l'éphéméride anarchiste.


1904 :

 La police apprend à utiliser les dépôts gras laissés par les doigts : c'est le début de l'utilisation des empreintes digitales à des fins policières.


1919 :

 Au Japon, sortie du premier numéro du journal "Rôdô Undô - The Labor Movement" (Le Mouvement Ouvrier), d'inspiration anarchiste.


1922 :

 En Italie, les fasciste commencent leur marche sur Rome. C'est de lébut de 22 ans de dictature.


1937 :

 Au cours de la guerre d'Espagne, le gouvernement républicain est transféré à Barcelone.


1938 :

 En Espagne, les Brigades Internationales sont démobilisées du front.


1938 :

 A Marseille, pendant un congrès radical-socialiste, un incendie accidentel ravage les Nouvelles Galeries sur la Canebière, gagnant l'hôtel de Noailles, le Grand-Hôtel et l'hôtel Astoria. Plusieurs dizaines de personnes y ont trouvé la mort. Le Grand-Hôtel abrite aujourd'hui le commissariat de Noailles.


1956 :

 A Budapest, on est toujours en plein dans l'insurrection Hongroise.


1968 :

 A Paris, des militants maoïstes et anarchistes attaquent au molotov le bar Relais-Odéon, qui accueille les meetings de l'organisation néofasciste Occident.


1974 :

 A Ballynkilar en Irlande du Nord, l'IRA fait sauter des explosifs contre une caserne de l'armée Britannique. Deux soldats trouvent la mort dans l'explosion.


1979 :

 - En Irlande du Nord, deux soldats sont abattus par l'IRA près de Belfast.


 Aux Etats-Unis, les Hopis et Big Mountain Dine déclarent leur indépendance vis-à-vis des gouvernements tribaux et du pays.


1986 :

 A Berlin, les Cellules Révolutionnaires (RZ) tirent dans les jambes du chef de la police des étrangers.


1988 :

 A Las Queñes, dans la cordillère chilienne, deux commandants du FPMR-Autonome, Cecilia Magni ("comandante Tamara") et Raúl Pellegrín ("comandante Rodrigo") sont abattus par les carabiniers de Pinochet après une attaque à l'explosif et à la mitrailleuse contre la caserne du village. Rodrigo et Tamara faisaient partie des principaux responsables de cette organisation de lutte armée contre la dictature.


1998 :

 A Vitrolles, destruction à l'explosif du transformateur du stade qui devait accueillir un concert de Rock Identitaire organisé par la mairie FN.


2001 :

 De grosses émeutes ont lieu à Belfast, des bombes artisanales sont lancées sur les officers du Royal Ulster Constabulary par les émeutiers. De nombreuses voitures sont incendiées et deux autres charges explosifs dans d'autres zones de la ville.


2011 :

 A Thessalonique, des manifestant-e-s parviennent à faire annuler un défilé militaire en bloquant les voies de chemin de fer et en attaquant la tribune officielle.


2013 :

 A Berlin, un véhicule de l'entreprise Sodexo est incendié pour protester contre la cogestion des prisons et des centres de rétention par l'entreprise d'alimentation de masse.

author: none
title: Censorship in the Education Department at FCI Allenwood Medium
content:
Casey Goonan

10/26/26


Casey offers here their reflections on the recent book drive they organized for the prison library, its popularity with everyone locked up, as well as how it has since been blocked and how Casey subsequently was fired from their library job.

Please share and repost.

– Casey Support Committee


AFFIRMATION

Thank you to everyone out in the so-called “free world” for contributing to our Summer Book Drive. On behalf of the Support Committee and every convict at FCI Allenwood Medium involved in this autonomous initiative, we send our revolutionary love and profound gratitude. From this self-organized prisoner initiative, we introduced a wide range of new, interesting, and relevant books into the prison’s official library collection. During my time as a library worker, many significant changes were made to the form and content of the library here at Allenwood Medium. Unfortunately, because of the Book Drive’s budding success and overwhelming popularity among the captives, i was fired from my job as librarian last week.

TERMINATION

On Thursday, October 1, i was fired as a library worker at FCI Allenwood Medium prison for no reason other than “ordering too many books” and “donating them directly into the library catalog” without the approval of the Education Department Supervisor, Mr. Williams. Although my boss, Ms. Ashton, knew about the plans for a mass donation and granted permission to do so, i was thrown under the bus once she learned her boss found out, and especially once she learned i was adding certain books into the catalog without her approval. There is nothing against policy within the books that were donated, even the ones i donated without Ms. Ashton’s knowledge. The Book Drive was successful in adding around one hundred brand new books to the library catalog, which transformed the library space from a realm of entertainment and distraction into one of pedagogy and critical study. By the first week of September, around seventy more books were delivered to the mailroom, yet staff deliberately let them pile up, before complaining to admin about the quantity of donations and returning them all back to sender. A few days later i learned of my termination.

It’s the overwhelming pettiness of the reaction that bothers me. There is no BOP policy that states we as prisoners cannot donate books into the library collection. There is an official process to do so however and i bypassed some of the red tape. Yet the only violation of policy i am “guilty” of is not showing my boss, Ms. Ashton, every single book that i was donating. My decision to not report donations wasn’t at all due to any intentional plot of deception. It was simply because whenever i gave my donations to Ms. Ashton, she would “never get around” to adding them into the catalog. They would just sit around and often disappear. I was frustrated by Ashton’s lack of enthusiasm regarding this rare opportunity to enhance the library collection, so i decided to just start marking, labeling, and cataloging the books myself. Basic direct action.

ACTION/REACTION

All who were involved in the Summer Book Drive (not only me as an individual) took direct action both to remedy the negligence of the correctional officers who oversee “education” operations at Allenwood Medium and to counter fascist anti-intellectualism, of which the official indifference to our depraved learning conditions is symptomatic. I am not exactly sure how the process occurred behind the scenes, but apparently a mailroom officer (who does not like me) contacted S.I.S. (the surveillance and investigative wing of the prison administration), who then contacted Mr. Williams, who in turn emailed Ms. Ashton ordering my termination as a library employee. I believe that the primary reason i was fired was politically motivated censorship, coupled with the fact that some of the COs already had an issue with me working in the library.

My termination as a library worker demonstrates how the administration at FCI Allenwood Medium will attempt to stifle any act of autonomous sufficiency and self-organization among us convicts, especially if activities aim to improve the conditions of life. The Summer Book Drive initiative was not only an attempt to counter the dehumanizing conditions of a neglectful Education Department but a demonstration of collective action to provide and (re)distribute resources in the face of (or rather in spite of) organized abandonment. author: Maria Martha Bruno
title: Bolsonaristas fogem da Justiça e se espalham por ao menos quatro países
content:
Flávio Bolsonaro (PL) pode ser o mais novo integrante da lista de bolsonaristas que deixaram o Brasil. Caso confirmada a chegada aos Estados Unidos, o candidato derrotado nas eleições de 2026 se somará a parentes, influenciadores e ex-membros do governo de Jair Bolsonaro, que deixaram o país por condenações ou investigações. Sempre sob o argumento de perseguição política. 


A denúncia partiu do veículo argentino

Infobae

, que publicou hoje, 27 de outubro, que Flávio estaria na cidade de Puerto Iguazú, que faz fronteira com o Brasil, pronto para tomar um voo rumo aos EUA. Ainda não se sabe como o senador teria saído do Brasil para o país vizinho. Em 26 de outubro, dia seguinte à derrota nas urnas, o ministro Alexandre de Moraes determinou que Flávio entregasse o passaporte à Justiça.


Um dos fundamentos da decisão de Moraes foi uma entrevista do irmão de Flávio, Eduardo Bolsonaro, dada dois dias antes do segundo turno, afirmando que o então candidato deveria deixar o país se perdesse o pleito. Também nesta terça, o blogueiro Paulo Figueiredo disse em sua live que, na noite de domingo, após confirmada a derrota, havia aconselhado o senador a ir para os EUA.


Flávio Bolsonaro é investigado em duas frentes pelo Supremo Tribunal Federal, mas, terminado seu mandato como senador, em 31 de janeiro de 2027, perderá o foro privilegiado. Sob relatoria do ministro André Mendonça, ele é investigado pela suspeita de evasão de divisas e de lavagem de dinheiro por conta do financiamento da produção do filme “Dark Horse”, sobre a trajetória de Jair Bolsonaro. A investigação mira repasses de Daniel Vorcaro, ex-dono do Banco Master, à produção do longa. 


Em outra frente, sob relatoria do ministro Alexandre de Moraes, Flávio é investigado pela suspeita de lavagem de dinheiro por meio de uma casa de apostas. A Polícia Federal (PF) quebrou o sigilo telemático do

advogado Willer Tomaz

, amigo de Flávio, e encontrou e-mails que apontariam que o senador foi cadastrado como “usuário master” de uma conta bancária da empresa Alcazar Holdings, de propriedade de Tomaz.


Segundo a PF, há indícios de “vínculo de controle ou propriedade de fato de Willer Tomaz sobre a Rede Loto”, a primeira a obter autorização estadual da Loterj, no Rio de Janeiro, para explorar bets no estado.


O senador Flávio Bolsonaro afirmou em seu Instagram ter sido intimado pela Polícia Federal (PF), nesta segunda-feira (26), a entregar seus passaportes.


Bolsonaristas nos EUA de Trump


Eduardo Bolsonaro mora no Texas (EUA) desde março de 2025. Ele foi condenado pelo STF em junho de 2026 por sua atuação para obter sanções americanas contra autoridades brasileiras. O ex-deputado teve a prisão decretada em outubro, entre o primeiro e o segundo turno das eleições.


Eduardo tem passaporte italiano e também

conseguiu

 o

green card

, documento que garante a residência permanente nos EUA. Desde que fugiu do Brasil, ele fez diversas viagens ao Oriente Médio e chegou a

abrir uma empresa

 no Bahrein, conforme a

Pública

 revelou.


Seu braço direito nos EUA, Paulo Figueiredo, mora na Flórida há dez anos.

Ele

 é investigado no Inquérito das

fake news

 e foi denunciado pela Procuradoria-Geral da República pela tentativa de golpe em 8 de janeiro de 2023. Seu caso nunca foi julgado porque o neto do ex-ditador João Figueiredo

nunca foi intimado

, mas ele é considerado

foragido

.


Eduardo, Allan dos Santos e Alexandre Ramagem juntos, em 2026, em encontro nos EUA


Outro foragido que vive na Flórida é o blogueiro Allan dos Santos. Ele teve mandado de prisão preventiva decretado pelo STF em outubro de 2021 e

reforçado

 em 2024, bem como o bloqueio de suas contas bancárias e perfis digitais no Brasil. O criador do extinto “Terça Livre” também é investigado no Inquérito das

fake news

 e das milícias digitais por disseminação de conteúdo falso e ataques a autoridades.


Ainda na Flórida mora Alexandre Ramagem, ex-diretor da Agência Brasileira de Inteligência (Abin) e ex-deputado federal pelo PL. Ele foi alvo de pedido de extradição após ser condenado pelo STF a 16 anos de prisão pela trama golpista.


A fuga, em setembro de 2025, contou com a ajuda de Rodrigo Cataratas, condenado por liderar o garimpo ilegal na Terra Yanomami, conforme

revelou

 a

Pública

. O empresário do garimpo

também está foragido

 por ter ajudado na fuga de Ramagem.


Em abril de 2026, Ramagem chegou a ser detido pelo serviço de imigração dos EUA (ICE), mas foi liberado dois dias …

author: Unknown
title: İranlı yönetmen Cafer Penahi'ye 5 yıl 1 ay hapis kararı
content:
Fotoğraf: Kacy Bao/Wikimedia Commons CC BY-SA 4.0

İranlı yönetmen ve senarist Cafer Penahi, Tahran Devrim Mahkemesi’nin 26. Şubesi tarafından görülen davada 5 yıl 1 ay hapis cezasına çarptırıldı. Mahkeme, Penahi’nin taşınır ve taşınmaz tüm mal varlığına el konulmasına, 2 yıl sanal medya faaliyetlerinden men edilmesine ve yurt dışına çıkışının yasaklanmasına karar verdi.

HRANA’nın Emtedad’a dayandırdığı habere göre, Penahi’nin avukatı Mostafa Nili, kararın müvekkilinin yokluğunda verildiğini açıkladı. Nili, Penahi’nin banka hesaplarının dondurulmasının ardından karardan haberdar olduğunu belirtti. Avukat Nili, müvekkilinin 30 Mart 2026’da İran’a dönmesine rağmen dava dosyasında ülke dışında olduğunun belirtildiğini ve duruşma tarihinin kendisine bildirilmediğini söyledi. Penahi hakkında 20 Mayıs 2026’da yakalama kararı çıkarıldığını da aktaran Nili, yönetmenin şu anda üç ayrı hukuki dosyasının bulunduğunu ifade etti.

Penahi, daha önce “rejime karşı propaganda” suçlamasıyla ayrı bir davada 1 yıl hapis cezasına çarptırılmış, 2 yıl yurt dışına çıkış ve siyasi ve toplumsal örgütlere üyelik yasağı almıştı. Yönetmenin yeniden yargılanma talebi Haziran 2026’da reddedilmişti.

author: Karyn Pugliese
title: Nearly 200 First Nations leaders, the prime minister and premiers gathered for a historic meeting about almost everything. Now what?
content:
The John G. Diefenbaker Building on Sussex Drive was perhaps, in its own imperfect way, a fitting place for nearly 200 First Nations leaders, most of the country’s premiers and a prime minister to hold a meeting First Nations have wanted for more than a century.


It’s actually two buildings mashed together: a modern glass construction, like a church nave, that lets light pour in from above and gives the hallways a sense of something sacred, while behind it, the old city hall rises as a plain grey slab, a maze of stairs leading to small, dark meeting rooms. 


Outside, the chief set up teepees that strangely echo the building’s peaks.


Three very different structures, sharing the same address.


“This is the first time in 119 years of Crown-First Nations relations that a first ministers meeting has focused solely on First Nations,” Cindy Woodhouse-Nepinak, the national chief of the Assembly of First Nations, has said many times leading up to the meeting and it’s a line she would repeat at the gathering.


Of course, a hundred-year wait puts a lot of pressure on a meeting.


After an opening prayer by Algonquin Elder Claudette Commanda, the mic went to Algonquin Grand Chief Verna Polson, who reminded everyone that Ottawa sits on unceded Algonquin territory, that the Algonquin have shared the land, been welcoming and “expect respect in return.”


 ”We are ready to work with you. That work must begin with respect for our land, our rights, and our responsibilities. Today, I welcome you as our people had welcomed others before you. Respect our land you’re on, listen to the people who have cared for it for generations, and carry the respect into the decision you make today and the years that go by,” said Polson.


The national chief’s opening statement covered the hundred-year list of asks: sovereignty, treaty rights, the environment, land, water, natural resource rights, closing the gaps in health, racism in the health system, Jordan’s Principle, Joyce’s Principle, infrastructure, education, jobs, and income.


Ultimately, the meeting seemed to be about everything, which made it hard even for those who had spent months preparing position papers, trying to compress a philosophy of survival worked out over generations, into the three minutes most were allotted to speak.


“ Of course, three minutes is not nearly enough time,” said Assembly of Manitoba Chiefs Grand Chief Kyra Wilson. “And having one representative speak on a number of different issues, it’s very difficult to ensure that we’re getting everything forward in terms of what our needs are as First Nations and our respective regions.”


Space was also limited, she added, “I’m somewhat disappointed that some of our leadership who should have definitely been in the room were not able to be in the room.”


Chiefs crammed so much into each three-minute burst.


In his opening remarks, Chief Sheldon  Sunshine of the Sturgeon Lake Cree Nation, speaking on behalf of Treaty No. 6, Treaty Number 7, Treaty Number 8, and the Blackfoot Confederacy delegation, said the meeting must be about changing the relationship.


“ I’ve heard people describe this meeting as historic. It certainly has the potential to be. But history will not remember us for gathering in a room, taking photographs, making speeches,” said Sunshine. “History will judge us by what we change. 


“Prime Minister, premiers, we need your commitment for a different way forward, one that is grounded in treaty, demonstrates the respect for treaty nations, and a shared responsibility and results.”


Inside the room at the First Ministers Meeting Photo: Raven Brascoupe/APTN.


Matthew Coon Come was back in the room, this time as a consultant on natural resource rights. He is a former AFN national chief who served from 2000 to 2003, and a former grand chief of the Cree in Quebec, credited with helping stop Hydro-Québec’s Great Whale project, which threatened to flood Cree and Inuit lands. 


“You’re right, I’ve been in a few meetings,” Coon Come joked when reporters asked for his insights on what would make this meeting a success. “One of the challenges of meetings of this nature is that you’re tempted to rehash history, repeat injustices, talk about unfulfilled obligations of the federal government. 


“If this First Ministers’ meeting is to succeed, it must come up with concrete measures for next steps. If they don’t do that, this is another meeting of just talks — ‘we’re going to do this, we’re going to do that’ — …

title: İsrail ordusunun Gazze'ye düzenlediği saldırılarda 4 Filistinli hayatını kaybetti
content:
Filistin sağlık kaynaklarından alınan bilgiye göre, Gazze Şeridi'nin kuzeyindeki Cibaliya Mülteci Kampı'nda bulunan El-Hoca Caddesi'nde İsrail askerlerinin açtığı ateş sonucu 28 yaşındaki Filistinli Mahmud Semih el-Herş hayatını kaybetti.

Refah kentinin batısında yer alan Mevasi bölgesindeki El-Alem Kavşağı'nı hedef alan İsrail saldırısında kimliği belirlenemeyen bir Filistinlinin de cenazesine ulaşıldığı aktarıldı.

Önceki saldırılarda yaralanan 2 Filistinli öldü

İsrail ordusunun açtığı ateş sonucu Mevasi bölgesinde yaralanan 6 yaşındaki Tehani Muhammed Said Şelalife, müdahaleye rağmen kurtarılamadı.

Gazze kent merkezindeki Es-Sevra Caddesi'ne birkaç gün önce düzenlenen İsrail saldırısında yaralanan Ahmed Yasin Buseyso da tedavi gördüğü hastanede hayatını kaybetti.

Gazze'nin çeşitli bölgelerinde birisi çocuk yaşta olmak üzere 5 Filistinlinin de İsrail saldırılarında yaralandığı aktarıldı.

İsrail'in Ekim 2023'ten bu yana Gazze Şeridi'ne düzenlediği saldırılarda en az 74 bin 561 Filistinli hayatını kaybederken, yaralı sayısı 175 bin 759'a ulaştı.

31 yıldır emeğin sesi olan Evrensel, gücünü sadece okurlarından alıyor. Emeğin sesinin daha gür çıkması için sen de güç ver.

title: Eğitim-İş'ten beslenme çantası tepkisi: "Bir ayda yüzde 6,20 zamlandı, maliyeti 2 bin 147 liraya çıktı"
content:
Eğitim-İş, beslenme çantasının maliyetinin yüzde 6,20 artarak 2 bin 147 liraya yükseldiğini açıkladı.

Eğitim-İş'in sosyal medya hesabından yapılan açıklamada, şu ifadelere yer verildi:

"Okulların açılmasından yalnızca bir ay sonra beslenme çantasının maliyeti yüzde 6,20 artarak 2 bin 147 TL’ye yükseldi. Bu tutar, asgari ücretin yüzde 7,65’ine, emekli gelirinin yüzde 9,12’sine, yeni başlayan öğretmenin maaşının ise yüzde 3’üne karşılık geliyor. Emekçilerin gelirleri temel ihtiyaçları karşılamaya yetmezken çocuklar okula boş beslenme çantalarıyla gidiyor. Aileleri yoksullaştıran ekonomik politikaların sorumlusu siyasi iktidar, çocukların beslenme sorununu görmezden gelerek kamusal sorumluluğu ailelerin omuzlarına yüklüyor. 15 Ekim 2026’da açıklanan bütçe gerçekleşmelerine göre Türkiye Maarif Vakfı’na yalnızca eylülde 2 milyar TL, yılın ilk dokuz ayında ise 4 milyar 58 milyon TL aktarıldı. Eylül ayında vakfa aktarılan kaynakla 931 bin 150 öğrencinin bir aylık beslenme ihtiyacı karşılanabilirdi. Çocukların beslenmesi kamusal bir sorumluluktur. Ücretsiz bir öğün yemek haktır."

31 yıldır emeğin sesi olan Evrensel, gücünü sadece okurlarından alıyor. Emeğin sesinin daha gür çıkması için sen de güç ver.

title: İsrail'de çıkış anketleri: Netanyahu çoğunluğu sağlayamıyor
content:
İsrail'de 26. Knesset'i belirlemek üzere yapılan seçimlerde sandıkların yerel saatle 22.00'de  kapanmasının ardından yayımlanan çıkış anketleri, hükümet kurma müzakerelerinde Filistinli Arap yurttaşların partilerinin belirleyici konuma gelebileceğini gösterdi.


Netanyahu'nun bloku 61 sandalyeye ulaşamıyor


120 üyeli Knesset'te parlamenter çoğunluk için 61 sandalye gerekiyor. Üç büyük televizyonun güncellenen çıkış anketleri Netanyahu'nun Likud, Şas, Birleşik Tevrat Yahudiliği ve aşırı sağ partilerden oluşan blokuna 50 sandalye öngörüyor.


Eisenkot öncülüğündeki Netanyahu karşıtı partiler ise 52 sandalyede kalıyor. Böylece iki blok da tek başına çoğunluğun altında kalıyor.


Bununla birlikte, Netanyahu'ya yakın yayın çizgisiyle bilinen Kanal 14'ün çıkış anketi iktidar blokuna 60 sandalye veriyor. Bu projeksiyonda Likud 30 sandalyeye ulaşıyor. Ancak Kanal 14'ün tahmininde de Netanyahu bloku çoğunluk sınırının bir sandalye gerisinde.


Çıkış anketleri ile kesin sonuçlar geleneksel olarak çok yakın


İsrail’de çıkış anketleri genellikle kesin sonuçlara birkaç sandalyelik farkla yaklaşırken, 2022 seçimlerinde Netanyahu blokuna 61–62 sandalye öngörülmesine karşılık blok 64 sandalye kazanmıştı; dolayısıyla bu kez üç büyük kanalın ortak 50 sandalye tahmini, Netanyahu’nun çoğunluğu sağlayamayacağına ilişkin güçlü bir gösterge olmakla birlikte kesin sonuç sayılmaz.


Kamu yayıncısı Kan 11 ile Kanal 12 ve Kanal 13'ün ilk projeksiyonlarında Likud 24–25 sandalyeyle birinci, eski Genelkurmay Başkanı Gadi Eisenkot'un Yashar partisi 21–23 sandalyeyle ikinci sırada yer aldı.


Eski Başbakan Naftali Bennett'in B'Yachad (Birlikte) ittifakı 12–14, Yair Golan'ın Demokratlar Partisi 9–10 sandalye düzeyinde görünüyor.


Arap partileri 18 sandalyeye yükseliyor


Çıkış anketlerinin en dikkat çekici sonuçlarından biri, Filistinli Arap yurttaşların partilerinin parlamentodaki temsilinde öngörülen artış.


Hadash, Ta'al ve Balad'ın oluşturduğu Birleşik Liste'ye 11, Mansur Abbas'ın Ra'am partisine ise 7 sandalye öngörülüyor. Böylece Arap partilerinin toplam sandalye sayısı 18'e ulaşabilecek.


Bu sonuç, 2022 seçimlerinde toplam 10 sandalye elde eden Arap partilerin temsili açısından önemli bir artışı demek.


İsrail Komünist Partisi'nin de yer aldığı Hadash'ın Birleşik Liste içindeki temsili sürecek gibi görünüyor. Ancak Ofer Cassif dahil komünist adayların milletvekilliklerinin kesinleşmesi için resmî oy sayımının tamamlanması gerekiyor.


Koalisyonun anahtarı Arap partilerinde


Çıkış anketlerindeki dağılım, Netanyahu karşıtı muhalefetin parlamenter çoğunluğu sağlayabilmek için Arap partilerinin desteğine ihtiyaç duyacağını gösteriyor.


Eisenkot çevresindeki muhalefet partilerinin 52 sandalyesine Ra'am'ın yedi sandalyesi eklendiğinde toplam 59'a ulaşılıyor. Bu durumda Birleşik Liste'den en az iki milletvekilinin daha desteği gerekiyor.


Ancak Eisenkot ve diğer merkez sağ muhalefet liderlerinin Arap partileriyle resmî koalisyon kurmaya karşı tutumları, parlamenter aritmetiğin siyasal bir hükümet anlaşmasına dönüşmesini güçleştiriyor.


Bu koşullarda, Arap partilerinin dışarıdan desteklediği bir azınlık hükümeti kurulamazsa veya partiler arasında yeni bir koalisyon düzenlemesi yapılamazsa, yeniden seçim seçenekleri gündemde.


Katılımda büyük artış


Seçim gecesi açıklanan verilere göre katılım yüzde 77,7'ye ulaştı. Bu oran son yılların en yüksek katılım düzeylerinden biri olarak bildirildi.


Filistinli Arap seçmenlerin katılımına ilişkin ülke çapında kesinleşmiş ayrı bir oran henüz açıklanmadı. Arap partilerinin sandalye projeksiyonlarındaki artış ise bu seçmenlerin hükümet aritmetiğindeki ağırlığını ortaya koyuyor.


Resmî sayım bekleniyor


İsrail Merkez Seçim Komitesinin oy sayımı sürüyor. Çıkış anketleri kesin seçim sonuçlarını yansıtmıyor ve sandalye dağılımı resmî sayımla değişebilir.


Reuters'a göre sayımın 30 Ekim'e kadar tamamlanması, sonuçların ise 4 Kasım'da resmen yayımlanması bekleniyor.


Çıkış anketlerinin doğrulanması hâlinde seçim, Netanyahu'nun parlamenter çoğunluğunu yeniden elde edemediği, ancak muhalefetin de Arap partilerinin desteği olmaksızın hükümet kuramadığı bir tablo ortaya çıkaracak.

author: The Canadian Press
title: Cowichan Tribes to propose solution protecting private property in January: lawyer
content:
The lawyer for the Cowichan Tribes said they will make a proposal in January that protects private property rights in the landmark Aboriginal title case that the B.C. Conservatives have said calls into question who controls British Columbia.


Lawyer David Rosenberg said that if it has “the right attitude,” the incoming Conservative government will find it easier to resolve the Cowichan case than to repeal the Declaration on the Rights of Indigenous Peoples Act, known as

DRIPA

.


The 2025 Cowichan ruling on a portion of Crown, city and private land in Richmond, B.C., found that Aboriginal title is a “senior interest” compared with fee-simple title, and sections of B.C.’s Land Title Act that establish fee-simple title as “indefeasible” do not apply to Aboriginal title.


It has triggered concerns about the impact on private property rights and values, but Rosenberg said the tribes will go to court in the new year with a solution to respect and protect private property and its value, as well as Cowichan Aboriginal title.


“That is what negotiations are supposed to be leading to,” he said.


He said the case has nothing to do with the repeal of DRIPA, which premier-designate Lorne Doerkson has said is his top priority after Saturday’s election victory.


Rosenberg said Doerkson’s election could be seen as a fresh start in resolving the Cowichan case.


“That a new government could come to the issue with a positive attitude, and show some leadership, and take the high road, and say, ‘We’re going to recognize Aboriginal title and we’re going to protect property interests,'” he said.


While Rosenberg said it could be easier to resolve the Cowichan case, former B.C. Conservative leader John Rustad said DRIPA can be repealed quickly, while the Cowichan Tribes case could drag on for years.


Rustad, who didn’t seek re-election, said last year that “Indigenous rights and private property cannot coexist,” and called on the Supreme Court of Canada to resolve the conflict as soon as possible.


He said in an interview on Monday that the case cannot be allowed to drag on because of the uncertainty it has created around private property rights.


Rustad said the incoming government must argue in its appeal for the extinguishment of Aboriginal title, something the previous government did not do in the original case.


“Private property is the foundation of society,” he said. “If you are going to take private property rights, which the court is now in the process of doing, you completely undermine society,” he said.


Extinguishment, however, does not rule out some agreement that would compensate First Nations, said Rustad, who was the Aboriginal relations minister under the former B.C. Liberal government.


But Rosenberg said neither British Columbia nor the federal government could extinguish existing Aboriginal title, unless the Constitution were amended, and he warned against conflating DRIPA with the Cowichan Tribes case. He added that the City of Richmond had argued for extinguishment, and was unsuccessful.


“I don’t believe the repeal of DRIPA would in substance affect what the court ordered,” he said, referring to the ruling that British Columbia must negotiate in good faith how to reconcile fee-simple interests with Cowichan Aboriginal title.


Watch APTN News Answers for information on the Cowichan Decision:


Rosenberg said the tribes’ proposal on private property will be filed when the court hears requests for the Cowichan judgment to be stayed pending appeal.


The Conservatives’ resounding election win, in which they secured a two-thirds majority, has raised concern among First Nations leaders.


The First Nations Leadership Council said Monday that B.C. is at a crossroads with the incoming government that could result in either a “battleground” or reconciliation.


Doerkson said at a postelection news conference on Sunday that he is “completely committed to working with First Nations” but would stick with his election promise to repeal DRIPA.


He said the declaration act brought in by the New Democrat government had caused more problems.


“So, I am committed with working on a great path forward of respect, partnership, friendship and conversation.”


Rustad said the situation facing the new government is how to reconcile private property rights with outstanding Indigenous rights.


“The Indigenous question is the elephant in the room,” Rustad said. “You cannot get your economy going without finding a path …

title: Comunicado de CNT sobre los incidentes en Bilbao
content:
Leer en

Castellano

Euskera


Castellano

Comunicado de CNT sobre los incidentes en Bilbao


Desde CNT queremos desmarcarnos y mostrar nuestra preocupación ante los incidentes registrados la noche del 26 al 27 de octubre en Bilbao tras la finalización del acto de protesta contra la presencia de un provocador de extrema derecha en nuestra ciudad. Diversas organizaciones, asociaciones y colectivos antifascistas secundamos la convocatoria, que en todo momento transcurrió de manera tan multitudinaria como pacífica.


La movilización se dio por terminada y quedó disuelta tras conocer la cancelación del acto ultraderechista.


Fue en ese momento cuando elementos desconocidos, que nada tenían que ver con los convocantes, comenzaron a provocar incidentes, con el resultado conocido.


Aún desconocemos con certeza quiénes fueron los instigadores e iniciadores de los disturbios, pero nos resulta llamativa la juventud, inexperiencia y actitud caótica de los participantes en los mismos. Nos preocupa la utilización política que se está haciendo de estos hechos, con la intención de criminalizar las legítimas y necesarias movilizaciones populares de la izquierda contra el fascismo y a favor de los derechos laborales y sociales. Observamos una clara intención por parte de la derecha mediática y política de trasladar la imagen de un clima de caos y violencia en las calles, con el objetivo de influir electoralmente para beneficiar a partidos defensores de planteamientos autoritarios.


Desde CNT, queremos alertar a la sociedad en general, a la juventud en particular y a las personas más oprimidas, del riesgo de ser manipuladas, instrumentalizadas y utilizadas por sectores de la derecha y la ultraderecha para favorecer sus intereses en contra de las libertades y derechos de la clase trabajadora.


La mejor manera de evitar este riesgo es la organización y militancia política, social, sindical y vecinal.


Unidad, organización, cabezas frías y claridad de ideas.


Euskera

CNTren komunikatua Bilboko istiluen inguruan.


CNT sindikatutik gure kezka adierazi nahi dugu urriaren 26ko gauean Bilbon izandako istiluengatik, gure hirian eskuin muturreko probokatzaile baten presentziaren aurkako protesta-ekitaldia amaitu ondoren. Hainbat erakunde, elkarte eta kolektibo antifaxistek bat egin genuen deialdiarekin, manifestazio jendetsu eta baketsua izan zen.


Ultraeskuindarrak bere ekitaldia bertan behera utziko zuela jakinarazi zuenean, mobilizazioa amaitutzat eman eta manifestazioa desegin zen.


Une horretan, deitzaileekin zerikusirik ez zuten pertsona ezezagunak istiluak sortzen hasi ziren, denok ezagutzen ditugun gertaerak sortuz.


Oraindik ez dakigu nortzuk piztu eta bultzatu zituzten istiluak, baina deigarria egiten zaigu parte-hartzaileen gaztetasuna, esperientziarik eza eta jarrera kaotikoa. Kezkatzen gaitu gertatutakoari buruz egiten ari den erabilera politikoak, faxismoaren aurka eta lan eta gizarte eskubideen alde beharrezkoak eta legitimoak diren ezkerreko herri-mobilizazioak kriminalizatzeko. Ikusten dugu eskuin mediatiko eta politikoak asmo argia duela kaleetan kaos eta indarkeria giroa dagoela erakusteko, hauteskundeetan eragina izateko eta planteamendu autoritarioak defendatzen dituzten alderdiei mesede egiteko.


CNTtik, gizarteari oro har, zapalduenei eta gazteei bereziki ohartarazi nahi diegu eskuinaren eta ultraeskuinaren sektoreek manipulatuak, instrumentalizatuak eta erabiliak izateko arriskuaz, langileen askatasun eta eskubideen aurka beren interesak bultzatzeko.


Arrisku hori saihesteko modurik onena antolakuntza eta militantzia politiko, soziala, sindikala eta auzotarra da.

Batasuna, antolakuntza, buru hotzak eta ideia argiak.

author: Emma Honeybun
title: Treaty One opens campus to the first national First Nations business training centre
content:
The CEO of a First Nations-led centre for business education and mentorship says that her goal is to shift the narrative so that Indigenous Peoples are not seen as “recipients,” but “creators and innovators” of wealth and services.

Kathleen Bluesky leads the Wiitahnookiinitaw Tahshkayzing Entrepreneurship Centre (WTEC), which is, according to its website, “Canada’s first fully First Nations-led Business Incubator.”

WTEC was founded in May 2025, but did not have a physical location until Tuesday.

“When we talk about First Nations economic development, it usually starts with what we lack,” Bluesky said at the grand opening event. “We lack capital, we lack capacity, we lack opportunities. And those barriers are real, I’m not trying to deny that, and we do have to address them, but I believe the conversation has to start with, what do our people already bring?

“We bring knowledge, we bring our relationships, and we bring our determination, and we show up,” she continued. “And we’ve been providing for our people, our families, our communities, for generations, and we will continue to do so.”

She said, “aside from the paint on the walls,” the space, located on the third floor of 191 Broadway St. in downtown Winnipeg, was funded entirely by First Nations startups who have benefited from services at WTEC since its inception.

“So I’m very proud of that,” she said.

The centre was developed by Treaty One Development Corporation (T1DC) “in collaboration with Treaty One Nations and key development partners,” according to its website, which includes a partnership with the province of Manitoba.

Treaty One is composed of seven First Nations in Manitoba, and T1DC is the economic and business stream that retains control from leadership.

WTEC to support planned business district through training youth, says CEO

Under Treaty One leadership, WTEC will also play a part in what the National Indigenous Economic Development Board has labeled “the largest urban reserve in Canada” — Naawi-Oodena, which is 108 acres and located within Winnipeg.

The 2021 Naawi-Oodena Master Plan, developed by T1DC, proposed a mixed-use village, high-and-low density residential neighbourhoods, a business district, schools and community spaces, and more, to be slowly built over several years.

The first completed project was the Oodena Gas and Convenience Store, which opened to the public in June 2025.

Additionally, on March 18, the federal government announced that its Housing Accelerator Fund would support a $91 million apartment block project, with additional funds from the province.

With a predicted completion in January 2028, the project — which “requires a minimum 30 per cent Indigenous workforce, with 20 per cent consisting of Treaty One First Nation members,” according to the government release — would allow for Naawi-Oodena’s first 260 housing units on-site.

With housing underway, WTEC will contribute to the business district, Bluesky said.

“What I want to see is more First Nation businesses winning major contracts, more First Nations women building enterprises, more young people being on the entrepreneurial path, and more of our businesses growing from community operations into regional, national and international companies with wealth staying in communities,” she said. “That’s what I want to see.”

Alongside its mentorship program, WTEC offers a “three-month boot camp and business feasibility analysis certificate” called Roots to Rise, as well as a certificate program in partnership with the Western British Columbia Polytechnic College (WBCPC), according to its website.

Bluesky said that currently, there are about 30 entrepreneurs enrolled in WTEC programs, and she’s happy they now have a space to study and speak with mentors.

“We’re not starting from nothing, we’re building on everything that came before us,” Bluesky said, “and I want our entrepreneurs to know that you belong here. Your ideals, and your language and your culture belong here.”

Premier Wab Kinew, who was present at the location’s grand opening, said his provincial government was “very, very happy to support this.

“I just think it’s really important to have entrepreneurship,” he said. “There’s so much uncertainty in the world today …The best way to have certainty in a time of uncertainty is to make your own destiny. And that includes making your own destiny when it comes to what you do for a living.

author: CMI Argentina
title: Impunidad para Macri, Caputo y Sturzenegger: “Poder Judicial al servicio de la Dependencia y la Corrupción”
content:
La Autoconvocatoria por la Suspensión del Pago e Investigación de la Deuda se pronunció respecto a la confirmación realizada por la Sala I de la Cámara Federal de la absolución de Mauricio Macri, Luis Caputo y Federico Sturzenegger por haber tomado 45.000 millones de dólares de deuda externa violando todos los procedimientos establecidos. “Los responsables de ese endeudamiento fraudulento, que empobrece cada día más al pueblo trabajador y atenta contra la naturaleza y nuestra soberanía, tienen que ser juzgados e ir presos”.


Compartimos el comunicado:


Otra vez el Poder Judicial al servicio de la Dependencia y la Corrupción


La “justicia” que opera impunemente desde Comodoro Py, en sintonía con la Corte Suprema de Injusticia alojada en Talcahuano, cerró el lunes 19 de octubre una causa originada en el préstamo otorgado por el FMI al gobierno de Mauricio Macri en 2018. Mientras crece la resistencia y la incertidumbre frente al plan económico y financiero del gobierno, se busca blindar a quienes ahora reinciden. Los apellidos involucrados en esa estafa, que aumentó en 45.000 millones de dólares la deuda externa de nuestro país y determinó la profundización de las políticas de miseria y saqueo fueron, además del multiprocesado Macri, su ministro de Hacienda Nicolás Dujovne y otros funcionarios que hoy también son ministros de Javier Milei, tales como Luis Caputo y Federico Sturzenegger, entonces titulares del Ministerio de Finanzas y del Banco Central, y Santiago Bausili, actual presidente del Banco.


Son numerosas las denuncias contra ese empréstito, pues el objetivo del FMI y su mandamás, EEUU, era asegurar la reelección de Macri, tal como lo admitió el entonces representante de EEUU en el FMI y futuro titular del BID, Claver Carone. Desde esta Autoconvocatoria, nos presentamos en otra causa que aún espera dictamen en el Juzgado de Martín Cormick. Esas causas se abrieron bajo la acusación de delitos graves como administración fraudulenta y defraudación contra la administración pública, ya que esos 45.000 millones de dólares no tuvieron ningún destino productivo ni social sino que sirvieron para la fuga de capitales al exterior, no sin antes haber servido para comprar Lebacs, venderlas percibiendo un interés del 10 por ciento en dólares y salir otra vez a cuentas del exterior de una minoría de inversores, entre los que se presume hay familiares y empresarios amigos de los funcionarios acusados.


Es sabido además que la tramitación del crédito violó todos los procedimientos al respecto, sin pasar por el Congreso como ordena la Constitución Nacional, artículo 75, inc 4, ni basarse en informes y dictámenes previos. La acusación del fiscal Franco Picardi se basaba también en informes de la Sindicatura General de la Nación y la Auditoría General de la Nación, que había cuestionado que la deuda con el FMI se contrajo sin que existiera un expediente previo que avalara la operación.


Crónica de una impunidad anunciada


Aunque la investigación fiscal fue correcta, la jueza federal María Eugenia Capuchetti, nombrada por Macri en 2019, absolvió en febrero de este año a él y demás acusados de semejantes hechos de dependencia y corrupción. Previo a eso, el gobierno de Javier Milei había retirado a la Procuración del Tesoro como impulsora de la causa. Según lo denunciamos entonces, fue un gesto que además buscaba respaldar la legitimidad del Fondo, en circunstancias que ahora se repiten, cuando el gobierno de Milei intentaba destrabar un nuevo desembolso del FMI.


En septiembre, la Sala I de la Cámara Federal confirmó la resolución de Capuchetti, con las firmas de Pablo Bertuzzi y Mariano Llorens, aunque el fiscal de Cámara Agüero Iturbe había respaldado el dictamen de Picardi y pedido la anulación de lo resuelto. Y seguidamente la maquinaria judicial macrista y mileísta actuó bajo el dictamen de otro fiscal, Raúl Pleé, que falló a favor de cerrar la causa y salvar a los endeudadores y corruptos según fue confirmado el 19 de octubre por Gustavo Hornos, Mariano Borinsky y Javier Carbajo de la Sala IV de la Cámara de Casación.


Desde Capuchetti hasta los jueces de Casación arriba mencionados, pasando por la Cámara y el fiscal Pleé, todos mintieron al afirmar que “no existían pruebas de un delito penal y que se trataba de una decisión de política económica ajena al control judicial”. author: Corynne McSherry
title: Social Media When Elections Are Close: Doing the Impossible Better
content:
Everyone knows, or should, that perfect (balanced, targeted, transparent, swift and swiftly appealable) content moderation at scale is impossible. That doesn’t mean powerful social platforms don’t have to try to get at least reasonably close, especially when access to good information can have a profound effect on political participation and speech.

That’s why so many people, including the Meta Oversight Board, criticized Meta for suspending a major political Instagram account for hours during a huge early voting push on October 17; and for allegedly boosting one candidate in Brazil’s recent presidential election. Meta denies deliberate interference in either instance, blaming “mistakes” in its automated content moderation systems (including AI tools that can’t tell the difference between enthusiastic follower engagement and a bot attack).

Mistakes or not, with early voting in the U.S. midterms already underway, these events serve as a stark reminder that all major social media platforms need to have stronger systems in place to ensure that they serve, rather than impede, democratic communication.

Access to good information can have a profound effect on political participation and speech.

This is not inherently an “AI” problem: automated systems can process content at a scale that humans never could, potentially enabling better moderation at scale and alleviating the psychological load on ill-paid moderators whose jobs require them to view incredibly disturbing content. But automated systems also reproduce existing biases, struggle to understand context, and often make mistakes that disproportionately affect journalists, activists, artists, and other vulnerable and marginalized communities. And moderation errors are even more likely when the language is spoken principally by the global majority. In 2020, leaked document showed that Meta’s algorithms incorrectly deleted nonviolent Arabic-language content 77 percent of the time, while failing to detect hate speech under the company’s own policies in many instances. Where these systems are faltering in Arabic, they’re positively failing in less-resourced languages. As a 2025 report from the Center for Democracy and Technology found, labeled datasets in certain languages and dialects such as Maghrebi Arabic and Kiswahili contain inconsistencies, bias, and inaccuracies due to the limited hiring of annotators who actually speak the languages as well as shifts in the languages themselves. An investigation into ChatGPT’s outputs in several low-resource languages demonstrates the depth of problem.

But language disparities are just one of several concerns as automated moderation becomes more widespread. From the systemic suppression of content from Palestine to the repeated misclassification of LGBTQ+ content as adult or explicit material, these varied examples demonstrate the risks of overreliance on automated moderation—and the need for stronger safeguards.

Fortunately, there is a great deal companies, policymakers, and civil society can do to help ensure that highly automated systems operate in ways that respect human rights, minimize predictable harms, and provide meaningful accountability when they fail. If companies are going to continue relying on automation to moderate users’ speech—and there is little reason to believe they won’t—then accountability must evolve alongside these technologies.

That work should start with publicly committing to the Santa Clara Principles 2.0. Specifically:

Automated technologies should help, not replace, human moderators. For example, automated systems can help flag and prioritize content for review, while humans can interpret context, handle sensitive cases, and refine system performance. This investment is particularly important during the weeks immediately before and after an election.

Companies must be transparent about when and how automation is used in content decisions.

Companies must regularly audit their automated systems for bias, with particular attention to low-resource languages, vulnerable and marginalized communities, and conflict zones.

Companies should strengthen personal data protection guarantees and policies. Automated content moderation often relies on personal data and profiling, so companies should think carefully about what data these systems use, what's necessary and proportionate and how their systems shape moderation outcomes.

Users must have the ability to appeal, and to provide context when they …

author: Sharon Zhang
title: Supreme Court Bars Judges From Pausing Deportations While Appeals Are Decided
content:
The agreement between the DOJ and Texas at the center of the case was labelled as “egregious collusion” by opponents.

Honest, paywall-free news is rare. Please support our boldly independent journalism with a donation of any size.

The Supreme Court stripped immigration judges of the ability to pause certain deportation proceedings on Tuesday, declining to block a deal slammed as “egregious collusion” between the Justice Department and the state of Texas.

The unsigned order on Tuesday halts the practice known as “administrative closure,” which allows judges to pause deportation cases. The practice affects thousands of cases a year, and has been granted 360,000 times since 1990, according to statistics by the Executive Office for Immigration Review.

The procedure clears a judge’s dockets while other circumstances surrounding the migrant are resolved, including appeals of criminal cases or if they are seeking humanitarian protections or other legal status. It can also give some people relief in difficult circumstances, such as those who were the victims of certain crimes or children who were abused or abandoned.

Data has previously shown that most immigrants whose cases return to court after administrative closure are ultimately allowed to stay in the U.S.

The first Trump administration had said that judges lacked the authority to perform the practice, but the Biden administration restored it through a rule issued in 2024.

There were no noted dissents to the Supreme Court’s decision, and the Court provided no explanation for its reasoning. The decision hands the Trump administration another tool in its mass deportation campaign as immigration officials wantonly violate court orders and pressure judges to issue more deportation orders.

The ruling upholds an extraordinary judiciary maneuver by the state of Texas and the Trump administration, as critics said.

Texas Attorney General Ken Paxton had originally sued the government over the Biden administration rule in 2024. The case was brought to federal court this June, where Texas officials argued that the rule was “one part of the Biden-Harris Administration’s campaign to undermine our immigration laws,” and said it exceeds the government’s authority.

Hours after Texas officials filed that case, Texas and the Trump Department of Justice — which oversees immigration judges — jointly filed in the same court asking for the Biden rule to be thrown out. The judge promptly granted that order.

Three cities challenged that order, with their lawyers saying in a filing to the Supreme Court that the Texas-DOJ deal amounted to “egregious collusion.”

“The government … announced in advance that it would not defend a disfavored regulation and then colluded with the challenger from the moment that suit was filed,” the lawyers challenging the deal said.

author: Unknown
title: Trial begins in Leipzig over knife attack on Kurdish woman
content:
Proceedings began today, 27 October, at the Leipzig Regional Court in a case concerning the stabbing and serious injury of a 31-year-old Kurdish woman on a tram on 26 January 2026. The 21-year-old Syrian defendant, Ahmed A., faces charges including aggravated assault, threats, robbery and insult.


According to the indictment, the defendant, Ahmad A., and another person who is being investigated separately insulted and attacked the Kurdish woman aboard tram line 16. The attackers reportedly threatened Kurds, saying, “We will kill all Kurds.”


During the incident, the woman was injured by knife blows and her thumb was severed. It was later surgically reattached at a hospital. She reportedly sustained permanent restrictions in movement and loss of sensation in her hands and fingers, and continues to receive psychological treatment.


Defendant denies anti-Kurdish motive


Speaking in court, the defendant, Ahmed A., admitted to attacking and robbing the victim but claimed that he had no personal issue with Kurds or with the woman he attacked. He said he had consumed alcohol on the night of the incident and had become involved in a knife fight on the tram.


The victim previously told the German newspaper

Taz

 that she believed she had been attacked because of her Kurdish identity. “Their problem was that I was Kurdish. They didn’t need my money,” she said.


Defendant faces up to eight years in prison


Ahmed A. has been held in pretrial detention since May. He is also facing charges relating to another robbery that took place in Leipzig in February and resisting police officers.


The presiding judge stated that, under certain circumstances, the defendant could face up to eight years in prison for the attack on the tram. The trial is scheduled to continue with four further hearings through 24 November.

author: Breza Race Maksimovic
title: How Serbian students toppled a dictator
content:
This article

How Serbian students toppled a dictator

 was originally published by

Waging Nonviolence

.


On Oct. 25, Serbia voted and the Student List won. Late that evening, President Aleksandar Vučić — the man who has dominated the country’s politics since 2012, steadily hollowing out its courts, media and elections along the way — went on television and admitted that his Serbian Progressive Party and its allies had lost. The final count isn’t in yet, but the result is not in doubt. Candidates selected by the Students List protest movement have more than half the vote and a majority in the 250-seat parliament.


For more than 20 years, our team at the Belgrade-based Center for Applied NonViolent Actions and Strategies, or CANVAS, has worked with activists from dozens of countries on one question: How do ordinary people defeat a government that looks unbeatable? This time the answer came from our own streets, again. We want to explain what happened, because movements elsewhere will try to learn from it, and we’d like them to learn the right lessons.


Sign Up for our Newsletter


We’ll send you a weekly email with the latest articles.


You can’t understand Sunday without understanding the 14 years before it, since Vučić first came to power.


Most people in Serbia learned to live with a low, constant fear. You assumed your phone wasn’t really yours. Amnesty International later

confirmed

 what many suspected: Spyware was being installed on the phones of activists and journalists, sometimes while they sat in a police station. If you spoke up, a tabloid might put your face on the front page the next morning with a story about who was

supposedly

 bankrolling you. People lost jobs and contracts for being on the wrong side. Plenty stopped saying what they thought, even at the kitchen table.


We see this pattern in almost every country we work in. That kind of power doesn’t have to arrest everyone. It only needs everyone to believe they could be next.


How it started


On Nov. 1, 2024, the concrete canopy at the Novi Sad railway station fell and killed 16 people. The station had just been renovated. Everyone understood immediately what that meant: The money meant to keep people safe had gone into someone’s pocket. Within days, “Corruption kills” was written on walls across the country.


Students shut down their colleges and refused to go back to class. Many observers abroad missed how important this was. A march lasts an afternoon. The blockade of the universities lasted for months and took a whole part of society out of normal life. In our field we call that noncooperation, and it is far more powerful than protest alone. Every regime depends on people showing up and doing what is expected of them. The students stopped.


For two years the students were arrested, followed, slandered and called foreign agents. Cars drove into crowds. People were beaten. The government gave them every excuse to respond with violence, and they didn’t.


A protest marshal at the front of a crowd during the largest march in Serbia’s history on March 15, 2025 in Belgrade. (Gavrilo Andrić / protesti.pics)


At the largest protest in Serbia’s history, in Belgrade on March 15, 2025 — with between 275,000 and 325,000 people, according to the independent Archive of Public Gatherings — student marshals in yellow vests kept the crowd calm and blue flares showed people the way out if things went wrong. None of that was improvised. The students organized themselves. The assembly of each fakultet (a specialized college within a university) chose its marshals. Before every big action they went over the same things again and again: how to spot provocateurs, how to calm a tense moment, how to move a crowd out safely. At CANVAS, we teach this in every training we run: Nonviolent discipline doesn’t happen by itself. It is planned, practiced and repeated until it’s second nature. The students did exactly that.


Here is why it mattered so much. Violence was the one thing the regime wanted from them. A single burning car would have given the government its “terrorists” and sent the cautious middle class back indoors. 


Because the students stayed nonviolent, everyone could join. Grandmothers did. Farmers did. People who had never been to a protest in their lives did.


What it cost


People sometimes talk about nonviolent action as if it were the soft option. Anyone who watched these students over the past two years knows better.


They walked …

author: David Swanson
title: The Coup This Time
content:
Asia, East and Southeast Asia, Nonviolent Activism, North America, World

By David Swanson, World BEYOND War, October 27, 2026

When the South Korean President declared martial law in December 2024, protesters immediately assembled, the National Assembly voted down the decree, and the protests grew to include a million people following through until impeachment, arrest, and a change of power were achieved. The Nation had an article last week called How to Stop Trump’s Coup. It brought lessons to the United States from South Korea and was written by Jungmin Choi and by Paul Loeb who had made Choi’s earlier article into the first chapter of his book.

The lessons are key, but I think we should be careful to apply them fully. The version in The Nation has been made timely by claiming to offer “lessons for how Americans can counter Donald Trump and his allies if they disrupt or defy the results of November’s midterms,” while the version in the book has been made timeless by being stripped of explicit reference to any application. But the original article in Waging Nonviolence got it right, I think, in suggesting that the emergency was already upon us, that in fact there was no need to wait for a moment of even worse government malfeasance.

A man who campaigned for the presidency the first time instigating violence at his rallies and promising to strip the public treasury for his personal profit while disregarding laws as he saw fit has been put into office twice, has scorned the rule of law, has used wars and all variety of lesser crimes to fill his own bank account, and has intentionally damaged our health and environment, all while promoting fascistic hatred. Every day has been an appropriate moment for an impeachment, a prosecution, and a nonviolent public uprising — but the U.S. Congress and public have mostly been otherwise occupied. And the attempted coup of January 2021 was halted by the Capitol Police of all things without most members of the public needing to trouble themselves to leave their homes. One might draw the lesson that, while the rest of the world needs to rise up against its tyrannical threats, we in the United States are all right sticking with football and shopping. This would be a dangerously erroneous lesson.

A particularly outrageous moment can be used as a catalyst for action, but there is no reason to wait to plan actions until a worse moment than the current one arrives. In recent months, the people of Bolivia have shut down their capital, not because of a military coup but because of an elected government not keeping its promises. I don’t know which is harder to imagine, the people of the United States nonviolently shutting down Washington or a U.S. government keeping its promises. Last year in Peru, protesters forced out a brutal and illegitimate president as part of an ongoing years-long struggle. Two years ago, in Bangladesh, a student-led movement replaced an oppressive government without “resorting to war.” Equally useful, perhaps, for our learning, in recent years in Colombia, a community has claimed its land and largely removed itself from war. (See here, here, and here.) In Mexico, a community has done the same. (See here, here, and here.) In Canada, indigenous people have used nonviolent action to prevent the armed installation of pipelines on their lands. These are nonviolent actions taken against heavily armed powers because the corruption and cruelty have grown too horrible to any longer withstand. Just like real-world frogs, and unlike the libel we tell about them, humans can jump out of a heating pot.

It’s tempting to lament how enormous and spread-out the land of the United States is, as if demographics completely prevent behaving like Koreans or Bolivians (or as if the much larger Russia has never had a revolution). Bolivia has only 12.7 million people, of whom 2 million are in or very near a capital of only 182 square miles, and the rest of whom are within 700 miles of there. South Korea has only 51 million people of whom 26 million are in or very near a capital of only 234 square miles, and the rest of whom, on the mainland, are within 230 miles of there, with lots of trains available. The United States has 342 million people of whom only 5 million are in or very near a capital of 68 square miles, the rest of whom are within 2,400 miles of there, not counting Alaska, Hawaii, or other territories. author: Sharon Zhang
title: Rogers Solicits Funds to “Protect Elon” — the Biggest Political Donor in History
content:
The Republican’s campaign made the plea to help Musk avoid congressional inquiry into his DOGE work.

Did you know that Truthout is a nonprofit and independently funded by readers like you? If you value what we do, please support our work with a donation.

The world’s first trillionaire, Elon Musk, recently took another record: He is now the largest single political donor in modern American history, according to an analysis by The Washington Post, after pouring nearly half a billion dollars into backing Republicans in this year’s midterm elections.

This has contributed to an enormous gap between Republican and Democratic political spending this cycle, with Republicans outspending Democrats by over $300 million as of last week. Musk’s spending in particular could be the edge in several tight races across the nation, like the race for Senate in Texas.

And at least one Republican candidate is seeking to return the favor. Michigan’s Democratic Party posted a leaked fundraising email on Monday from U.S. Senate candidate Mike Rogers that calls on supporters to back his campaign in order to “protect Elon.”

“When you stand with my Senate campaign today, you are directly shielding Elon Musk, protecting the movement to audit the federal government, and stopping this socialist retaliation plot dead in its tracks,” the email reportedly says.

“Please, make an immediate, urgent contribution right now to protect Elon and save America,” concludes the message, signed by Rogers.

The Democrats did not specify when this email was sent, but the Detroit Metro Times reported on an appeal with the same wording sent in July.

According to that report, the email is referring to a call by Rep. Ro Khanna (D-California) for Musk to be subpoenaed and for there to be “accountability” for his sweeping “Department of Government Efficiency” (DOGE) actions that he took as a “special” government official early in Donald Trump’s second term. Khanna said that, among other things, Musk must answer for “the 4.5 million children around the world who he possibly sentenced to death by dismantling” the U.S. Agency for International Development.

Numerous court cases have found that Musk and DOGE’s gutting of the federal government broke the law, but Musk has faced little consequence or even congressional oversight of his actions, despite the vast impacts on the American public and the 14 million people abroad that his cuts are projected to kill by 2030. Though the sweeping cuts spurred by DOGE affected everything from Social Security to veterans’ care to cancer treatments, little is known by the public about Musk’s role in leading the illegal purge.

Still, Rogers’s fundraising email paints the call for accountability as a “socialist retaliation plot” in the style of “Soviet Russia and communist Cuba” that seeks to “destroy him.”

Rogers’s pledge to protect Musk comes as his campaign has benefited from Musk’s massive spending spree this election cycle.

Musk’s America PAC, of which he is the primary donor, has contributed $8.6 million to the Michigan Senate race. Roughly $5.2 million of that has been spent opposing Abdul El-Sayed, while $3.4 million has gone toward backing Rogers.

Musk also gave $158 million to the Senate Leadership Fund, Republicans’ super PAC for Senate races, this summer, representing one of the largest political donations in U.S. history. That PAC has been the biggest outside contributor in the Michigan Senate race, according to Detroit News, pouring $43.3 million into the race, the vast majority of which has been put toward opposing El-Sayed.

author: Chris Walker
title: Trump Says He’ll Accept Midterm Results If He Deems Them “Honest”
content:
Trump has repeatedly — and baselessly — suggested that widespread voter fraud may play a role in this year’s races.

Did you know that Truthout is a nonprofit and independently funded by readers like you? If you value what we do, please support our work with a donation.

On Tuesday, President Donald Trump told reporters that he would only accept the results of the 2026 midterm elections if he felt they were “honest” — echoing statements he’s made in the past while peddling baseless claims of widespread voter fraud.

When asked by journalists if he would “respect” the results of the midterms, Trump indicated his response may depend on the elections’ outcome.

“I will, if they’re honest elections, yeah,” Trump said. He then walked away, seemingly to avoid follow-up questions.

Q: You'll respect the election results whatever happens?TRUMP: If they're honest elections(That's a no!)

Trump’s recent remarks echo other statements he’s made regarding election integrity.

In February, for example, he said that he would only accept the results of the midterms if he deemed them “honest.” If not, Trump added, then “something else has to happen.” The president didn’t elaborate on what he meant.

In the spring of 2024, Trump similarly said he’d only accept the 2024 election results “if everything’s honest,” saying that, if it wasn’t, he would “have to fight for the right of the country.” Trump ended up winning that race, but afterward made grandiose claims that he had won with a mandate, despite not winning a majority of the vote and having one of the narrowest Electoral College victories in U.S. history.

Trump has peddled baseless claims that widespread fraud has affected election results over the past decade, particularly in the 2020 election, which he lost to Joe Biden. In that year’s race, Trump repeatedly indicated a reluctance to accept the pending results, stating in July of that year that he would “have to see” the results before accepting them.

Months later, when Biden won over Trump, the latter refused to accept the outcome, filing dozens of lawsuits and ranting online about supposed fraud he could never prove. He eventually invited his loyalists to Washington, D.C. on January 6, 2021, the day the Electoral College was set to be certified. Following Trump’s incendiary speech that morning, a mob of his followers attacked the Capitol building with Congress inside, delaying the certification of the election.

Trump has continued to sow doubts about elections, including the upcoming 2026 midterms, with his administration publishing questionable reports suggesting that tens of thousands of voters are registered illegally. He has pressured states to remove these residents from voter rolls, and has called for Republicans to “nationalize” elections based on his claims, despite constitutional restraints that place control of elections in the hands of states.

Trump’s most brazen attempt to interfere with this year’s elections took place in Alaska last week, when he ordered the Department of Justice (DOJ) to preemptively sue to block the state from certifying a U.S. Senate election if the incumbent Republican, a loyalist to the president, lost the race.

These and other actions and statements from Trump have sparked doubt among voters that he will accept the midterm results, especially if Democrats win one or both houses of Congress, which they are currently favored to do. A recent Washington Post/ABC News/Ipsos poll found that 7 in 10 voters are not confident that Trump will respect the election outcomes.

Some observers have posited that Trump could be attempting to create just enough distrust among his base for Republicans to justify refusing to certify the midterm results. In one such scenario, GOP Speaker of the House Mike Johnson could replace the House Clerk, or pressure the current one, telling whoever is in that position that they must refuse to seat election winners due to supposed voter irregularities.

Election experts say that such a move would likely be illegal and blocked by the courts. But given Trump’s history — and Johnson’s willingness to block election winners from assuming office before — many are worried that partisan maneuvers by Republicans are within the realm of possibility.
