title: NTI commits $40.8M in federal funding toward health initiatives
content:
Over the next five years, Nunavut Tunngavik Inc. is committing $40.8 million in federal funding to support health and wellness programs.


The organization made the announcement Oct. 21 in a news release.


The funding covers April 1, 2027 to March 31, 2032, and is intended to close the “gap in health outcomes between Inuit and other Canadians,” according to the release.


Nunatsiaq News has requested a copy of the full five-year spending plan from NTI but has not received a response.


In Iqaluit, the Umingmak child and youth advocacy centre and the Piruqatigiit Resource Centre, which provides support to those with fetal alcohol spectrum disorders and other conditions, are among those that will receive an unspecified amount of money.


As well, an unspecified portion of money is earmarked for Qaujigiartiit Health Research Centre’s Inunnguiniq childrearing and parenting training program, as well as its Makimautiksat Youth Camp, which aims to promote wellness by getting those aged nine to 12 out on the land.


NTI’s board of directors approved three other spending plans earlier this month aimed at strengthening Inuktut language training and advancing the elimination of tuberculosis.

author: Julia Conley
title: Mike Rogers Receives Last-Minute Donation From Anti-Abortion PAC
content:
While in office, he was a sponsor of four fetal “personhood” bills that aimed to ban nearly all abortions nationwide.

Support justice-driven, accurate and transparent news — make a quick donation to Truthout today!

Michigan voters were clear in 2022 when they voted by a 13-point margin to codify the right to abortion care in the state constitution, and the state’s Republican US Senate candidate, former Rep. Mike Rogers, claimed two years ago that he had no interest in “going back to Washington, DC to undo what the people of Michigan decided to do.”

But a recent campaign contribution from the National Pro-Life Alliance political action committee (PAC) left reproductive rights advocates warning that Rogers has shown throughout his political career that he will fight to stop Michiganders from accessing abortion care — and that extremist groups are counting on him to win the Senate race to ensure abortion is banned nationwide.

Recent filings from the Federal Election Commission show that on October 23, just before Michigan residents began voting early ahead of the November 3 midterms, the National Pro-Life Alliance PAC donated $5,000 to the Rogers for Senate campaign.

The group has lobbied for the passage of the Life at Conception Act, which would ban all abortions with no exceptions for rape, incest, or health risks for the pregnant patient, and previously donated $1,700 to Rogers between 2000-10.

In 2010, when the then-congressman received $1,000 from the group, the National Pro-Life Alliance stipulated that candidates they supported must support the Life at Conception Act.

Shanay Watson-Whittaker, director of Michigan campaigns at Reproductive Freedom for All, told Common Dreams on Tuesday that the “last-minute donation shows how desperate anti-abortion groups are to buy this election — and they’re counting on Mike Rogers to deliver for them.”

“His record gives them every reason to believe he will,” she added.

Despite Rogers’ earlier claims that should he win the Senate seat, he would respect Michiganders’ support for the right to abortion care, he spent his 14 years in office backing a constitutional amendment to enshrine “personhood” in the US Constitution, aiming to ban all abortions from the moment of conception, and supporting a national 20-week ban — “still very much a national ban that could carry disparate harm for people experiencing medical emergencies and fetal conditions,” wrote Kylie Cheung at Jezebel in 2024.

“I oppose abortion at any time except to save the live [sic] of the mother,” Rogers wrote in a candidate questionnaire distributed by the Michigan Catholic Conference, affirming that he supported the Human Life Amendment. He added that he opposed the use of “taxpayer funds for any abortions.”

Rogers was also a sponsor of four fetal “personhood” bills that aimed to ban nearly all abortions nationwide.

Watson-Whittaker urged Michigan voters to keep Rogers’ donation from the National Pro-Life Alliance and his record in mind as they go to the polls in the coming week.

“Michigan voters fought hard to protect reproductive freedom, and these extremist groups want a senator who will help them undermine it in Washington,” said Watson-Whittaker. “We need someone who will fight for our rights, and Rogers has spent his entire career showing us he won’t.”

author: Amy Goodman
title: Egypt Shutters Independent News Site Mada Masr and Detains Its Editor-in-Chief
content:
This “severe blow” to independent media is an “unprecedented escalation,” says a journalist who previously worked there.

Support justice-driven, accurate and transparent news — make a quick donation to Truthout today!

A court in Cairo has ordered the closure of the independent Egyptian news site Mada Masr. The court also ordered the site’s editor-in-chief, Lina Attalah, to be detained until she pays a fine of over $50,000. She was convicted on charges of managing an unlicensed website. Mada Masr is “the flagship independent media outlet in Egypt and a pillar of independent media in the region,” says Sharif Abdel Kouddous of Drop Site News, who previously worked at Mada Masr. The independent outlet was founded in 2013 “in the midst of Egypt’s revolution and counterrevolution” and has “managed to survive all of those years in one of the most hostile media environments” in the world. Still, “what happened today is an unprecedented escalation” because Attalah and Mada Masr had never before been referred to trial.

Kouddous adds that the attack on Mada Masr comes less than a month after Egyptian authorities arrested an entire newsroom at the independent fact-checking outlet Matsadaash. They remain behind bars.

This is a rush transcript. Copy may not be in its final form.

The court also ordered the site’s editor-in-chief, Lina Attalah, to be detained until she pays a fine of over $50,000. She was convicted on charges of managing an unlicensed website. After the court’s ruling, Attalah was taken into custody.

AMY GOODMAN: We’re joined right now by Sharif Abdel Kouddous, the Middle East editor at Drop Site News, previously worked at Mada Masr in Egypt for four years as a journalist and editor.

Sharif, talk about the significance of this breaking news.

SHARIF ABDEL KOUDDOUS: Well, Amy, this is a dark day for journalism, not just in Egypt, but in the entire Arab world. Mada Masr is one of the last remaining independent media outlets reporting the news in Egypt. It’s really the flagship independent media outlet in Egypt and a pillar of independent media in the region.

It was founded in 2013 in the midst of Egypt’s revolution and counterrevolution. It’s managed to survive all of these years in one of the most hostile media environments for the media in the world. It’s had its journalists jailed, foreign staff deported. Its website has been blocked for nearly a decade. Their offices were raided by security forces. There are various forms of intimidation, and the threat of imprisonment is always there. Lina herself has been hauled before interrogation in numerous cases over the years.

But what happened today is an unprecedented escalation. This has never happened before. Lina Attalah or Mada Masr have never been referred to trial before. Then, barely a week, you know, after their being referred to trial, they hold a court session today, where Mada Masr’s defense lawyers are denied a request to even review the case file, that’s given to them in the moment. They’re supposed to review it right there on the spot and present their defense. The court then calls for a recess to deliberate the request, comes back into session, clears the entire courtroom of everyone except for Lina and her lawyer, and then fills it with plainclothes security guards and security officers. And then the court announces it’s rejected all the requests by the defense, including to submit any documentation or hear any witnesses. And the judge then appoints a lawyer for Lina, despite objections, of course. And then, after that, he just summarily reads out the conviction.

And the conviction is fining Lina Attalah herself, as editor-in-chief and co-founder of Mada Masr, to the maximum possible penalty, which is a fine of 3 million Egyptian pounds, which translates to about $50,000, the closure — and the closure of Mada Masr, of the website, and the confiscation of its property. author: Matthew Guariglia
title: New Records Obtained by EFF Expose More Problems with Medicare’s AI Experiment
content:
New records obtained by EFF expose additional issues with Medicare’s AI-driven prior authorization program and show why we need stronger legal limits around government use of

automated decision-making

. 


EFF

sued

 the government back in March for information about the

Wasteful and Inappropriate Service Reduction (WISeR) model

, a new Medicare program that uses AI to evaluate prior authorization requests for certain medical services. We

previously released records

 showing that WISeR has resulted in delays and denials of care, operational chaos, and reports of patient harm. Today, we’re publishing over 800 new pages of records, including:


Requests for information (RFIs) or requests for corrective action plans (CAPs) sent from the Centers for Medicare & Medicaid Services (CMS) to four of the six WISeR vendors, along with the vendors’ responses.


Applications of 66 companies to the WISeR model, including those of the 6 selected companies. 


Task orders and contracts for the evaluation, implementation, and monitoring of the WISeR model.


Documents obtained through EFF’s lawsuit are available

here

.


These newly released documents show that the WISeR rollout was rushed and rocky from the start, highlighting the dangers that arise when governments

treat AI like a silver bullet

 for complex problems. The documents also highlight the need for more transparency about safeguards against inappropriate, AI-driven denials. The public still lacks the information needed to assess whether clinician review is providing meaningful oversight of AI systems and whether appropriate data is being used to evaluate prior authorization requests. 


EFF has

long argued

 that AI has no place in consequential government decisions about peoples’ rights or access to benefits, such as

immigration enforcement

 and

policing

 decisions. That’s because using automated decision-making in these contexts risks decisions that violate people’s rights or deprive them of benefits they’re entitled to based on biased or inappropriate considerations and without proper due process or accountability if there is an error. 


By outsourcing decision-making to private AI companies without sufficient transparency, testing, or legal limits, WISeR jeopardizes seniors’ access to medical care. Congress should step in to place greater legal limits on the use of automated decision-making in Medicare. 


WISeR’s Rollout Was Rushed and Rocky 


CMS launched the WISeR program just six months after

announcing

 it, ignoring calls from

medical providers

 to delay its rollout. In records previously released by EFF, CMS acknowledged this “

extremely condensed timeline

.” 


New records suggest that WISeR’s unusually rapid rollout contributed to widespread problems in the first few months of the program. CMS did not disclose the extent of these issues to the public, even as agency employees privately contacted vendors about potential noncompliance with program requirements. 


In the first three months of the program, CMS sent RFIs or requests for CAPs to at least four of the six WISeR vendors. These requests, which describe delays, technical failures, and a lack of communication with providers, suggest that widespread problems during the program’s rollout were not limited to one vendor or state. 


These letters underscore the severity of the problems with the program. For example, CMS requested information from one vendor, Virtix, about numerous reported issues, including “

determination turnaround times that exceed established guidelines

,” “

denials that appear inaccurate or inconsistent with applicable criteria

,” and “

inadequate customer service

.” CMS’s RFI to Zyter–a vendor that

uses Palantir software infrastructure

–observed that the agency had received reports that “

Zyter is not issuing determination letters in a timely manner

” and communications indicating that it “

may lack adequate processes for responding to and escalating provider/supplier concerns

.” The vendor Innovaccer received two CAP requests and a “Performance Notice of Non-Compliance” over its failure to implement a fully functional portal for WISeR providers and suppliers.

author: Chris Walker
title: Student-Led Movement Could Lower Voting Age to 16 for Local Races in Culver City
content:
Students were motivated to push the proposal due to drastic cuts in funding for their schools that they had no say in.

Support justice-driven, accurate and transparent news — make a quick donation to Truthout today!

A ballot measure in Culver City, California, would lower the voting age for some elections from 18 to 16, allowing teenagers to participate in the decision-making process on many issues that directly affect their lives.

The measure would only apply to certain elections within the Los Angeles suburb’s city limits, including races for school board, elections for city officials, and future ballot measures.

Teenagers in the city have pressed for the measure to be passed before, including in 2022, when it failed by only 16 votes. The proposal gained additional support after last year, when school board budget cuts led to dozens of school employees and teachers being fired, including an assistant superintendent for diversity, equity, and inclusion. Cuts have also been made to funding for arts programs in the district, and students have said basic supplies (including hand soap in restrooms) have been missing.

The school board does allow three “ceremonial” spots to be held by students in the district, but the direction of the cuts was voted on by the larger board overall, whose members are chosen by voters, with no input from students. Those members outvoted the ceremonial ones, leading to the drastic cuts.

The school board, along with the city council, has “been creating policy that alters the lives of our teenagers without giving them a way to voice their opinion,” Culver City High School student Mia Moroz told Bolts magazine.

Moroz, who is also president of Vote 16 Culver City, the student-led group in favor of the ballot proposal, said that the budget moves by the school board have resulted in “teachers who have 42 kids in one classroom and not enough seats to sit down.”

The Culver City Council, recognizing these complaints from students, agreed to place the measure on the fall ballot, in a contentious 3-2 vote in February.

Opponents of the measure call it ill-advised, with some arguing that teenagers are not mature enough, are “easily persuadable,” or aren’t true members of the community because many of them don’t pay taxes.

“I see all of these students who are so often disregarded as being immature, or not knowledgeable, or disengaged. But I see them caring, and I see them acting,” Moroz said, responding to such criticisms.

In an op-ed written jointly by Mayor Freddy Puza and the three members of the city council that backed putting the measure to a vote, the lawmakers noted that young people’s lives are affected by local government decisions.

A “Yes” vote on the measure “is about more than one election,” the mayor and city council members said. “It prepares the next generation of informed voters, strengthens local democracy, and ensures more residents with a stake in Culver City’s future have the opportunity to help shape it for generations to come.”

Only about a dozen municipalities across the U.S. allow those aged 16 or 17 to participate in local elections. The first place to do so, Takoma Park, Maryland, has allowed 16- and 17-year-olds to vote since their measure passed in 2013.

City officials there say the change has led to an increase in civic engagement overall, including for adults, with some children even encouraging their parents to become more active in local democracy.

Lowering the age to vote has “really forced all candidates to think about the things that matter” to teenagers in the community, including “the quality of their schooling,” said Mayor Talisha Searcy, who was initially skeptical of the proposal but has now embraced it as beneficial for the city.

author: Daron Letts
title: Canada’s oceans envoy meets with QIA in Iqaluit to discuss marine protection
content:
This story was updated on Tuesday, Oct. 27, 2026, at 5:10 p.m. ET.


Canada’s new Ocean Envoy Diana Fox Carney, spouse of Prime Minister Mark Carney, talked marine conservation and economic opportunity with Qikiqtani Inuit Association representatives during a 24-hour visit to Iqaluit this week.


“The message I hear, very strongly obviously, is that care for the ocean and the importance of preserving livelihoods and cultural approaches and conservation objectives are critical,” she said during an interview at the Nunavut Fisheries and Marine Training Consortium offices on Tuesday.


“And they must be balanced with effective economic engagement around ocean resources.”


Fox Carney was named to the volunteer position in September by Fisheries Minister Joanne Thompson. In the role she will chair the 12

th

 Our Ocean Conference in Halifax in May 2027.


The international invitation-only gathering will bring together governments, Indigenous leaders, scientists, industry, and non-governmental organizations to hash out strategies for ocean protection and sustainable use.


Fox Carney sought to gather information in advance of the conference this week, during her first visit to the territory.


Her conversation with QIA representatives on Monday was originally scheduled to take place outside on the shore of Koojesse Inlet until high winds moved the meeting indoors.


“This is an initial conversation,” Fox Carney said. “My understanding is that there is a lot to learn.”


She said one of the subjects she learned about during the meeting was the goal to expand preservation of the approximately 85,000-square-kilometre Pikialasorsuaq polynya, year-round open water between Baffin Island and Greenland that is home to various marine species.


Through the

Sinaa agreement

 in 2025, QIA received a $270-million funding commitment from the federal government and other donors for the conservation efforts.


The protection strategy forms part of the federal government’s ongoing commitment to preserve 30 per cent of its marine and terrestrial areas, in accordance with an international agreement achieved at the 2022 United Nations Biodiversity Conference in Montreal, Fox Carney said.


When it comes to preserving the Pikialasorsuaq polynya, she said, “Greenland has not moved as far as we have.”


“An area of such great biodiversity is a priority,” she said.


To date, Canada has protected close to 18 per cent of its marine and terrestrial areas, and the federal government has committed to grow that by another three per cent in 2027, she said.


Fox Carney is working with former governor general Mary Simon, originally from Kangiqsualujjuaq, to organize meetings with Indigenous groups on the first day of the Halifax conference, a first in its history.


Although participation in the meeting is not finalized, Inuit representatives will be invited, she said.


She referred to her meetings with QIA and Simon as “the beginning of the conversation.”


“It was made very clear to me that it’s more than just preserving the resource base so that we can take resources and eat them,” she said. “Conservation is a physical and an emotional concept.”


During her time in Iqaluit, Fox Carney also met with Nunavut MP Lori Idlout, Department of Fisheries and Oceans staff and held a Liberal Party fundraiser at Aqsarniit Lounge on Monday evening.


Representatives from QIA were unavailable for comment before press time.


— With files from Lilli Akpaleeapik


Correction:

 This story was updated to correct the date of the

Our Ocean Conference. It was also corrected to clarify Fox Carney’s view on Greenland’s work to preserve the Pikialasorsuaq polynya.

author: James Crump
title: Met Police Lawyers Told Officer Her PTSD Was Not Severe Because She Was Only Raped Once
content:
Lawyers working for the Met police told a detective who had been raped by a colleague that she could not have severe trauma because she was only attacked once. 


DC Linda Williams sued her employer in 2022 for failing to protect her against serial rapist PC David Carrick, who attacked her while they were working together in south London in 2004. 


But Williams, 60, who waived her right to anonymity to

share her story with the BBC

, says dealing with the Met reduced her tears and was even more traumatising than the rape itself. 


The lawyers were officially representing Met police commissioner Mark Rowley, so Williams – who is still a serving officer – is calling for his resignation. 


“As far as I am concerned, it is Mark Rowley, the commissioner, saying these terrible things, as he was the defendant in the case,” she said. Rowley has failed in his promise to fix a toxic culture within the force, she added. 


The start of her civil case against the Met was “when the suicidal thoughts really came in,” she said, adding that force did not “believe anything” she said and that its behaviour felt “like being raped all over again”.


Williams kept silent about the rape for years because she felt Carrick would not be punished by the Met and that she would then be stigmatised for reporting him. 


She reported Carrick to Hertfordshire Police in 2021 after seeing media coverage that the force had charged him with the rape of another woman. Carrick received 37 life sentences in 2023 after being convicted of sexual offences against Williams and 11 other women.


During four years of legal wrangling, Met lawyers gave several reasons to question the severity of the trauma she was suffering, including the fact she was “only attacked once”, Williams said. “I don’t know how many times you have to be raped to have severe PTSD.”


A document the Met sent to Williams said the fact the “abuse itself was isolated to a single episode” would be a key factor in determining the damages she received. It also argued that for years after the rape, the trauma she went through was “not such as to significantly impact her on a day-to-day basis”.


The Met has now paid Williams an undisclosed sum in compensation without acceptance of liability.


A Met spokesperson said the force “tried to reduce further distress and re-traumatisation to DC Williams’ welfare and has aimed to deal with her claims as quickly and compassionately as possible”.


Williams, who was a rape investigations officer in the early 2000s, said that if she was attacked again she would not report her case to the Met because she has no “faith” in them to handle it correctly. 


Rowley, who has been commissioner since 2022, publicly apologised to Carrick’s victims in 2023.


Two months later, the Met was described as institutionally misogynistic in a report by Baroness Casey, who said the force was a “boys’ club”. 


Sexual assault allegations against officers and staff of the Met

have tripled

 in the five years since Sarah Everard was raped and murdered by serving officer Wayne Couzens.

author: Monthly Review Press
title: In Chicago in November? August Nimtz’ “‘Black Marxism’: A Marxist Critique”
content:
APPEARANCES


In Chicago on November 18th? Join August for a talk at the University of Chicago

Center for Contemporary Theory


In conjunction with

3CT’s Marx + Theory reading group

, led by Anton Ford and Gabriel Winant, August Nimtz will speak for himself as a contemporary of Cedric Robinson’s, as he grounds

Black Marxism: A Marxist Critique

 in an account of his own upbringing in New Orleans and his development throughout the struggles of the 1960s–explaining how and why he came to radically different conclusions.


REGISTER HERE.

This event is free and open to the public, and registration is recommended. Please email 

ccct@uchicago.edu

 if you require any accommodations to enable your full participation.


INTERVIEWS


Coming from Left Field

: “Black Marxism, Class Politics, and the Questions We Cannot Avoid” (Episode 153)


This conversation ranges from the Grenadian Revolution and anti-colonial struggles in Africa to Malcolm X, Black nationalism, identity politics, and the enduring question of whether the left can build an independent political alternative to the Democratic Party. Nimtz also reflects on Lenin’s approach to elections, the meaning of revolutionary parliamentarianism, and why he sees troubling parallels between today’s global conflicts and the period leading up to World War I. This is a wide-ranging, challenging conversation about race, class, imperialism, and the political choices facing the left today….


Opera Mundi and Autonomia Literária

 (Brazil)


Nimtz took a three-week book tour in Brazil, from July 20 to August 8, 2026.  These visits were mainly to promote a Brazilian collection of some of 

his essays

, two of which are from 

Black Marxism

, now being translated for a Brazilian edition. The tour began with three presentations to the Historical Materialism Conference, Rio de Janeiro 2026.  That was followed by seven other presentations in Paraty, Guararema, and São Paulo – to about 600 in person audiences, including the leading Left/Progressive bookfair, 

FLIPEI

.  Two in-depth interviews; 

TUTAMÉIA TV

and 

Opera Mund

i.  (See below for a video from one of these events.)


iMWiL!

, with Jared Ball


“What Cedric Robinson’s

Black Marxism

 Gets Wrong”

, an interview with August Nimtz, by Constantin Berlin (originally published on

Jacobin-Germany

)


“Cedric Robinson’s

Black Marxism: The Making of the Black Radical Tradition

did not receive widespread attention after its original publication in 1983. Since 2000, when it was republished with a new preface and an introduction by historian Robin D. G. Kelley, however, the book has enjoyed widespread appeal and influence in the anglophone humanities and social sciences as well as among activists. Robinson’s proposed theory of “racial capitalism” and his framework of a “black radical tradition” have shaped debates about racial inequalities in capitalist societies and Marxism’s potential for anti-racist politics in recent decades. August Nimtz has engaged with the book’s arguments and trajectory, directly or indirectly, since its original publication. The recently published

collection

,

Black Marxism: A Marxist Critique

, makes accessible, for the first time, a critique that spans four decades….”


REVIEWS


Cosmonaut

: ““Black Marxism” Under Debate, 40 Years On” by Gary Levi


“Cedric Robinson’s 1983

Black Marxism

 is a work that has had a second, and even third life. First revived in academic circles by the proselytizing of his acolyte, acclaimed historian Robin D.G. Kelly, the book was again revived in popular circles by the waves of Black Lives Matters protests that sought in it (along with works of prison abolitionists) a theoretical and historical narrative to broaden the immediate convulsive moment of protest towards a vision of how society might change, and under the impact of what form of mobilization. In this sense, it played a role in BLM protests similar to Graeber’s

Debt

 during Occupy. One couldn’t find a prescription of how to protest in it, nor could one find among most protesters a familiarity with its core ideas, but nonetheless those set into motion found themselves drawn to it, and searching for guidance in its pages….For August Nimtz, at the time a former nationalist and pan-Africanist who had moved towards the interracialism and Trotskyism of the Socialist Workers Party, the answer was straightforward. His 1985 review in

Journal of African Marxists

 was one of the first confrontations …

Segundo apurou a

Pública

, a filha mais velha do senador, de 14 anos, teria deixado a escola no primeiro semestre deste ano. O colégio não informou os motivos quando procurado pela reportagem.


A ausência das estudantes em escolas se dá em meio à suspeita de que Flávio Bolsonaro, derrotado por Lula no segundo turno das eleições presidenciais no último domingo (25), tenha deixado o país

, apesar de o ministro

Alexandre de Moraes, do STF, ter determinado que o candidato derrotado nas urnas entregasse seus passaportes

 à Polícia Federal (PF) e incluí-lo no sistema de monitoramento migratório, o Sonar.


O senador não cumpriu o prazo de entrega, que terminava nesta terça, e teve os passaportes emitidos em seu nome cancelados pela Polícia Federal (PF). Flávio é alvo de investigação no STF que apura suspeitas de lavagem de dinheiro e evasão de divisas.


Mais cedo, a coluna Grande Angular, do Metrópoles, informou, com base em pessoas próximas à família, que Flávio teria partido para os Estados Unidos e que o avião já estava em rota nesta tarde.

 Segundo a coluna, o senador estava sem dar notícias desde o início da manhã: a última mensagem teria sido enviada às 8h ao seu coordenador de campanha, Rogério Marinho (PL-RN), a quem teria dito estar “esfriando a cabeça”, sem responder se havia saído do Brasil. Mais cedo, Marinho havia negado que o aliado tivesse deixado o país.


A hipótese de fuga ganhou força quando o portal argentino Infobae noticiou que o senador teria cruzado a fronteira com a Argentina usando a carteira de identidade, rumo a Puerto Iguazú, de onde seguiria em voo privado para os EUA.

 A decolagem do jato, no entanto, foi retida devido a pendências de documentação de um dos passageiros, informou o jornal argentino Clarín. 


Aeroporto Internacional de Puerto Iguazu, na Argentina


A PF acionou as autoridades argentinas, que inicialmente não confirmaram nem negaram a entrada. Depois, o porta-voz do presidente Javier Milei, Fabián Fernández, negou à Bloomberg que Flávio tenha entrado no país.


O episódio, se confirmado, repete um roteiro de tentativas de evitar consequências judiciais já conhecido na família. O irmão Eduardo Bolsonaro vive nos Estados Unidos, e o pai, Jair Bolsonaro, foi preso pela PF em novembro de 2025 depois de tentar remover a tornozeleira eletrônica.


A reportagem procurou a assessoria do senador, mas não obteve retorno até a publicação. Em caso de manifestação, este espaço será atualizado.


*Informações que poderiam identificar as menores foram omitidas, em respeito ao Estatuto da Criança e do Adolescente.

author: infolibre
title: Ritchy Thibault: Κίτρινο Γιλέκο, Ρομά, προφυλακισμένος  μόνο για αυτά που είπε
content:
ΓΑΛΛΙΑ.


Υπό το Παλαιό Καθεστώς

1

, υπήρχαν οι Σφραγισμένες επιστολές (

Lettres de cachet

): ένα έγγραφο, υπογεγραμμένο από τον μονάρχη και κλεισμένο με τη σφραγίδα του, το οποίο διέτασσε τη φυλάκιση του αποδέκτη της επιστολής χωρίς δίκη. Εκείνη την εποχή, ένας μεγάλος αριθμός ανθρώπων ρίχτηκε στη φυλακή με βάση απλές ομιλίες που δυσαρεστούσαν τον Βασιλιά. Αυτό ακριβώς συμβαίνει σήμερα στον

Ritchy Thibault

, ο οποίος μόλις τέθηκε υπό προσωρινή κράτηση μόνο και μόνο για όσα είπε.


Την 1η Οκτωβρίου, ο 23χρονος νεαρός είχε πάει να στηρίξει τους μαθητές που αγωνίζονταν στο

Seine

–

Saint

–

Denis

. Μπροστά από ένα σχολικό συγκρότημα, είχε εκφωνήσει μια ομιλία κρατώντας τηλεβόα. Είπε συγκεκριμένα

«να βάλουμε φωτιά στο Ελιζέ»

και είχε ανακοινώσει ότι

«στις 17 Οκτωβρίου θα είναι χίλιες φορές χειρότερα από τα Κίτρινα Γιλέκα. Είστε έτοιμοι; Θα κάνουμε επανάσταση;».

 Απόψεις που μοιράζονται

εκατομμύρια άνθρωποι στη χώρα,

 μπροστά στο θέαμα ενός παράνομου καθεστώτος που πυροβολεί παιδιά. Συνελήφθη αμέσως και τέθηκε υπό κράτηση από αστυνομικούς με πολιτικά. Αν έπρεπε να φυλακιστούν όλοι όσοι ονειρεύονται να κάψουν το προεδρικό μέγαρο, θα έπρεπε να συλληφθεί

το συγκρότημα

NTM

 και οι αμέτρητοι θαυμαστές του που τραγουδούν από το 1995

«Πάμε στο Ελιζέ να κάψουμε τους γέρους».

 Και αν έπρεπε να συλληφθούν όλοι όσοι καλούν σε βία, τότε οι αμέτρητοι αρθρογράφοι που δικαιολόγησαν τη γενοκτονία στη Γάζα ή που ζητούν ακόμη πιο βίαιη καταστολή των κοινωνικών αγώνων θα έπρεπε να βρίσκονται πίσω από τα κάγκελα.


Δευτέρα 4 Οκτωβρίου 2026,

 μετά από τέσσερις ημέρες στο κρατητήριο, ο

Ritchy

 δικάστηκε με αυτόφωρο. Μια κατεπείγουσα διαδικασία που δεν αγγίζει ποτέ τους ισχυρούς, όπως ο Σαρκοζί, ο Μπαλκανί ή η Λεπέν. Κατά τη διάρκεια αυτής της συνεδρίασης κεκλεισμένων των θυρών, καθώς η αστυνομία είχε αποβάλει όλους τους υποστηρικτές του νεαρού, οι δικαστές αποφάσισαν να τον προφυλακίσουν στο

Fleury

. Το χειρότερο είναι ότι τέθηκε σε απομόνωση, ένα ακόμη μέτρο εξαίρεσης.


Όμως η μανία καταδίωξης δεν σταματά εδώ: τώρα που η δικαιοσύνη έχει τον ακτιβιστή στα νύχια της, τον δικάζει ενώ βρίσκεται υπό κράτηση για παλιές υποθέσεις. Την Τρίτη 6 Οκτωβρίου, η δικαιοσύνη τον καταδίκασε σε 4 μήνες φυλάκιση με αναστολή επειδή αποδοκίμασε έντονα τον Μακρόν στην Έκθεση Αγροτών. Γεγονότα που ανάγονται στο 2024. Δικάστηκε ερήμην του, πράγμα που σημαίνει ότι δεν μπόρεσε καν να υπερασπιστεί τον εαυτό του στην ίδια του τη δίκη… Αυτό δείχνει το επίπεδο του δικαστικού τσίρκου στη «μακρονία».


Ο

Ritchy

 είναι ένας σύντροφος. Πολύ νωρίς, το 2018, οργανώθηκε στο πλευρό των Κίτρινων Γιλέκων, όταν ήταν ακόμα έφηβος. Ο

Ritchy

 είναι επίσης παιδί των Ρομά, μιας κοινότητας που πέφτει θύμα του κρατικού ρατσισμού και της οποίας έγινε ο εκπρόσωπος. Έχει γράψει μάλιστα το έργο «Κλεφτοκοτάδες» («

Voleurs de poule

»

Libertalia

), ένα βιβλίο ως αγώνας ενάντια στον αντιτσιγγανισμό. Αυτός ο αγωνιστής κάθε μάχης, για περισσότερη δικαιοσύνη και αξιοπρέπεια, δεν μασάει τα λόγια του ενάντια στην εξουσία και τους φασίστες. Σήμερα πληρώνει βαρύ τίμημα για αυτό.


Η ιστορία του

Ritchy

 είναι η ιστορία μιας πρωτοφανούς δικαστικής και αστυνομικής δίωξης. Συνεχής παρακολούθηση, κατ’ οίκον έρευνα, δικαστικοί έλεγχοι, απαγορεύσεις διαδηλώσεων… το κράτος θέλει να τον εξουδετερώσει, επειδή ποτέ δεν χαμήλωσε τα μάτια μπροστά στην καταστολή. Μέσα σε 8 χρόνια, έχει υποστεί περισσότερες από 20 προσωρινές κρατήσεις, που αντιστοιχούν τουλάχιστον σε πάνω από 500 ώρες στέρησης της ελευθερίας του. Πάνω από 6 δίκες, και για τις περισσότερες υποθέσεις, αυτό που του καταλογίζει η Δικαιοσύνη είναι τα λόγια του. Οι αιχμηρές ατάκες του ενάντια στο κατεστημένο και τους ισχυρούς. Κάποιες φορές ιστορικές υπενθυμίσεις, όπως τον Φεβρουάριο του 2024, όταν αποκάλεσε τον Μακρόν «τυφλωτή» και του διαμήνυσε:

«Μην ξεχνάς ποτέ ότι βρισκόμαστε στη χώρα της Γαλλικής Επανάστασης, τη χώρα που αποκεφαλίζει τους μονάρχες!»

 Κάτι που του κόστισε 50 ώρες στο μπουντρούμι… Λίγους μήνες αργότερα, η αστυνομία τον κάλεσε στο τμήμα στο πλαίσιο προκαταρκτικής εξέτασης για «απειλή εγκλήματος ή πλημμελήματος κατά δημοσίου αξιωματούχου» μετά από μήνυση του Μπαρντελά. Είχε δηλώσει σε μια συνέντευξη:

«Ναι, ο φασισμός είναι μια απειλή που πρέπει να εξαλειφθεί».

 Ο ακτιβιστής δεν μπορούσε πλέον ούτε να εκφωνήσει λόγο ούτε να μετακινηθεί χωρίς να παρακολουθείται και, μερικές φορές, να συλλαμβάνεται.


Στις 8 Ιουλίου στο δικαστήριο του Παρισιού, ο

Ritchy Thibault

 δικάστηκε για «προσβολή της …

author: CMI Argentina
title: Difundieron la identidad de ocho personas más entre los restos humanos exhumados en la zona de La Perla
content:
Con este nuevo anuncio ya son 38 las identidades recuperadas e informadas a las familias de las víctimas desde que comenzaron las excavaciones del Equipo Argentino de Antropología Forense (EAAF) en el predio Loma del Torito, a mediados del año pasado. La noticia se enmarca en una causa penal que tramita ante el Juzgado Federal 3 de Córdoba -a cargo del juez Hugo Vaca Narvaja- y que busca recuperar e identificar restos humanos de enterramientos clandestinos, correspondientes a centenares de víctimas que pasaron o permanecieron en cautiverio en el centro clandestino de detención La Perla. La actual campaña se extiende hasta el 10 de diciembre.


La conferencia se llevó a cabo este viernes por la mañana en los tribunales federales de Córdoba en un auditorio colmado de público, entre familiares de víctimas, sobrevivientes del terrorismo de estado, militantes de organismos de derechos humanos, medios de comunicación y autoridades provinciales y municipales.


Tuvo la misma dinámica que los anuncios anteriores: primero, los nombres de las identidades recuperadas, que fueron pronunciados por el propio juez Hugo Vaca Narvaja, titular del Juzgado Federal 3 de Córdoba, a cargo de la causa; luego, la palabra de las familias de las víctimas, que expusieron y compartieron su profunda emoción por haber alcanzado este cierre parcial, insuficiente, pero entrelazado con una larga historia de búsqueda y de luchas; finalmente, las preguntas y comentarios.


Pascual Delfín Ludueña fue uno de los nombres cuyos restos fueron recuperados e identificados. Su sobrina Rosa tomó la palabra durante la conferencia para agradecer a todos los que trabajan en el marco de esta causa y contó que su tío tenía 29 años cuando, el 24 de marzo de 1976, fue secuestrado de su casa por un grupo de uniformados con fajina de color verde.


“Solo había dos mujeres en la casa, además de Pascual: mi abuela y mi tía. Él nunca más volvió pero mi abuela, que enloqueció por tanto sufrimiento, lo llamó todos los días de su vida hasta que murió sin saber absolutamente nada. Por eso esta verdad, aunque sea dolorosa, nos acerca a la justicia y ésta nos aproxima a la paz y a honrar la vida”, dijo Rosa Ludueña, emocionada.


En total fueron 8 identidades recuperadas las que se dieron a conocer: además de Pascual Ludueña, Alejandro Ernesto Jesús Jerez Bodereau, Néstor Albino Acosta, Claudio Norberto Nardini, Cecilia Alicia Pessina de Ávila, Mónica Protti de Guillen, Mercedes del Valle Ramírez, María Luisa Salto y Juan Carlos Soulier.


La familia de Bodereau avisó que no podría estar en la conferencia y, en su lugar, envió una carta: “La Verdad, la Memoria y la Justicia son pilares fundantes para nuestras vidas y están basados en un inmenso amor que es nuestra fortaleza. La felicidad de poder darle un cierre a esta dolorosa búsqueda y que la incertidumbre de saber cuál fue su destino haya tenido una respuesta final, nos genera un sentimiento indescriptible que nos colma de una profunda paz y felicidad a nuestra familia”.


La causa penal en la que se enmarcan las exhumaciones en Loma del Torito y el análisis y cotejo de datos genéticos sobre los restos óseos está caratulada como averiguación de enterramientos clandestinos y las zonas de búsqueda se determinan en base a decenas de testimonios generados desde poco tiempo después de la última dictadura, que señalan los enterramientos en fosas comunes en las inmediaciones del CCD La Perla como destino final de las víctimas que permanecieron allí en cautiverio.


Otra de las personas que tomó la palabra durante la conferencia fue la hermana de Néstor Acosta –militante del Partido Revolucionario de los Trabajadores y trabajador ferroviario-, que describió “estos momentos como muy impactantes. Durante muchos años no supimos nada y hoy, cinco décadas después, podemos decir que Néstor está aquí, presente, con nosotros. Dejó de estar ausente, desaparecido, y eso es muy valioso”.


Por su parte, una de las hermanas de María Luisa Salto contó que la joven “estudiaba medicina en Córdoba y militaba en la Juventud Peronista con la ilusión y las convicciones por una sociedad mejor. Fue secuestrada, torturada, desaparecida y no murió: fue asesinada por un estado de terror, una dictadura cívicomilitar que hizo lo imposible para borrar todas las huellas de sus crímenes”.


“Pero después de 50 años, es unja gran alegría para nuestra familia poder recuperar algo de ella, poder llevar sus restos a Cipolletti para que descanse junto a nuestros …

author: Joanna Moncrieff, MD
title: The Fonagy Report: A Missed Opportunity to Challenge the Neurodevelopmental Narrative
content:
A

n independent review commissioned in the UK to address escalating demand for ADHD and autism diagnosis and treatment has missed an important opportunity to correct misleading notions about the meaning of psychiatric diagnosis and the nature and effectiveness of stimulant treatment.


The

Independent Review into Prevalence and Support for Mental Health Conditions, ADHD and Autism

, led by Peter Fonagy, was published in mid-October.


It was

commissioned to look at the causes of the rising demand for assessments for ADHD and autism

, sometimes referred to as neurodiversity, and to help people get the

“right support”

. The truth is, the  UK’s National Health Service is buckling under the weight of this demand. Many adult mental health teams have had to stop accepting these referrals in order to continue to function. This means people are redirected to private providers at public expense. The report highlights how the NHS is overspending on these assessments by £164 million per year and the Centre for Health and the Public Interest describes the costs of this provision as

“accelerating at an almost exponential rate”.


There are some good points in the Independent Review. It raises fundamental questions about the nature and purpose of diagnosis in mental health and it makes some sensible suggestions about how help and support can be organised around people’s needs without the need for diagnosis.


The executive summary recommends: “There should be a fundamental shift from a ‘diagnosis-dependent’ system to a ‘needs-led plus diagnosis’ system.” And later: “The problem is a system that leans too heavily on diagnosis as the route to help and cannot keep pace”.


The review also highlights how the private sector is cashing in on the public demand for diagnosis at the cost of millions of pounds of public money with no real oversight or accountability. And it stresses that mental health problems are influenced by social and economic conditions and that tackling these and particularly addressing the barriers to participation in school, work and community are key to improving mental health.


However, the Review is also riddled with contradictions and confusion and nothing it suggests is likely to make any difference to the current situation. Ironically, given that rising pressure on the NHS budget was one of the drivers of the Review, if its recommendations are implemented, which is doubtful, they will cost the taxpayer more, not less. It’s difficult not to conclude that the Review was really an exercise in being seen to do something, rather than an effort to bring about significant change.


One of the main problems is that the Review accepts the definition of autism and ADHD as “neurodevelopmental conditions”. It defines these as conditions that are “strongly genetically influenced and present from early life” in the Executive Summary, and elsewhere as “differences in how the brain and nervous system develop that are present from early life, although not always apparent immediately and shape enduring patterns of cognition, attention, communication, behaviour and learning”.


However, as

James Barnes has pointed out

, the Review simultaneously endorses two contradictory conceptions of diagnosis. Alongside the idea that diagnosis identifies a neurological condition, it acknowledges that “diagnosis is based on categories of symptoms rather than established biological mechanisms” and on judgements about their “severity, persistence and impact on functioning”.  Therefore, the diagnosis does

not

 represent a neurodevelopmental disorder. Calling it one simply

assumes

 that symptoms or difficulties that reach a certain threshold must represent a neurological dysfunction or difference.


This assumption is not supported by evidence. Brain imaging studies show that people with an ADHD diagnosis are more likely to show slightly reduced volume in some small areas but there is little consistency between studies in which areas are identified and none have adequately controlled for important confounders such as IQ, birth trauma and socio-economic status that are known to be associated with brain volume and having an ADHD diagnosis. The large

ENIGMA study

, for example, found minuscule differences in some areas of the basal ganglia which have not been confirmed in

subsequent research

. The lead investigator, who at the time of publication hailed the findings as showing that “ADHD is a disorder of the brain”,

later …

title: Αντιφασιστική συγκέντρωση ενάντια στην παρουσία Κασιδιάρη στη Θεσσαλονίκη, Τετάρτη 28/10 16:00 άγαλμα Βενιζέλου
content:
Αντιφασιστική συγκέντρωση ενάντια στην παρουσία Κασιδιάρη


Ούτε σπιθαμή γης στους εχθρούς του ανθρώπου


Αντιφασιστική συγκέντρωση ενάντια στην παρουσία του νεοναζί Κασιδιάρη στην πόλη μας –


Τετάρτη 28/10 – 16:00 στο Άγαλμα Βενιζέλου


ΑΓΩΝΑΣ ΓΙΑ ΖΩΗ ΚΑΙ ΕΛΕΥΘΕΡΙΑ


Συλλογικότητα για τον Κοινωνικό Αναρχισμό- Μαύρο & Κόκκινο μέλος της Αναρχικής Πολιτικής Οργάνωσης – Ομοσπονδίας Συλλογικοτήτων


Όλοι/όλες/όλα στην αντιφασιστική συγκέντρωση για την προσπάθεια εμφάνισης του καταδικασμένου νεοναζί Κασιδιάρη


Ούτε σπιθαμη γης στους νοσταλγούς των ναζί


Και τώρα και πάντα και όπως το 40,


την φτώχεια και τον φασισμό θα πολεμάμε πάντα!


Φασίστες θα σας θάψουμε, όσα ονόματα κι αν αλλάξετε.


Την Τετάρτη 28/10, στις 5μμ στο πάντα φιλόξενο για τους νεοναζί ξενοδοχείο Capsis στην Θεσσαλονίκη, ο πρόσφατα αποφυλακισθέντας φασίστας και πάλαι ποτέ Νο2 της Χρυσής Αυγής Ηλίας Κασιδιάρης, καλεί σε συγκέντρωση τους οπαδούς του. Αυτό το σκουπίδι τολμάει να βγει από την τρύπα του την ημέρα που μνημονεύεται η έναρξη της αντίστασης του αγωνιζόμενου λαού αυτού του τόπου στις δυνάμεις των ιδεολογικών του προγόνων, των φασιστών του Μουσολίνι και αργότερα των Ναζί του 3ου Ράιχ. Ειναι ο πολιτικός και φυσικός απόγονος εκείνων των εγχώριων καθαρμάτων, δοσίλογων και ταγματασφαλητών, που στην διάρκεια της Κατοχής συνεργάστηκαν με τις δυνάμεις του Άξονα, που κατέδιδαν, βασάνιζαν και δολοφονούσαν αγωνιστές και πλούτιζαν από το λαθρεμπόριο ενώ γύρω τους βασίλευε ο θάνατος.


Υπό την σκέπη ενός νέου κόμματος πλέον, της Συμμαχίας Ελλήνων, η οποία – όπως ανακοίνωσαν και οι ίδιοι- μετράει ήδη κοινοβουλευτική παρουσία μέσα από τις μεταπηδήσεις διαφόρων μπροστινών του από αλλά ακροδεξιά κόμματα, ο Κασιδιάρης φιλοδοξεί να επιστρέψει στην κεντρική πολιτική σκηνή. Σε αυτή του την προσπάθεια δεν είναι μόνος. Στην απόπειρά του να χτίσει το προφίλ του δήθεν “αντισυστημικού”, του έχουν παράσχει πολύτιμες υπηρεσίες τα καθεστωτικά ΜΜΕ, που προσπαθώντας δήθεν να τον στοχοποιήσουν ως επικίνδυνο, ουσιαστικά τον ηρωοποιούν στα μάτια μεγάλης μερίδας της κοινωνίας, η οποία έχει σιχαθεί την καθημερινή προπαγάνδα τους και τα αφεντικά τους και αντιλαμβάνεται έτσι τον Κασιδιάρη ως αντίπαλό τους. Το πόσο πολύ “αντισυστημικός” είναι, τόσο αυτός όσο και ο κάθε φασίστας, αποδεικνύεται περίτρανα από αυτούς που του κάνουν πλάτες: Ένας από τους μεγαλύτερους βιομήχανους της χώρας και αθλητικός παράγοντας, ο Δ. Π. Γιαννακόπουλος, έσπευσε να τον στηρίξει πολιτικά, ανοιχτά και δημόσια. Κάτι βέβαια που δεν πρέπει να μας εκπλήσσει, καθώς είναι γνωστό πως οι φασίστες αποτελούν το μακρύ χέρι του Κεφαλαίου σε περιόδους κρίσης.


Αυτό το τελευταίο είναι άλλωστε που συμβαίνει και σε παγκόσμιο επίπεδο, από τις ΗΠΑ και την Λατινική Αμερική, μέχρι την Κεντρική Ευρώπη, όπου το σύστημα έχει ήδη σχηματίσει την εκλεκτή ακροδεξιά του πτέρυγα (πχ το AfD στην Γερμανία και την Λεπέν στην Γαλλία) και την προετοιμάζει να αναλάβει δράση, σε περίπτωση που οι από-τα-κάτω αποφασίσουν να διεκδικήσουν πίσω τις ζωές τους. Η διαίρεση και η αποδυνάμωση της τάξης μας με βάση την φυλή, την θρησκεία, την γλώσσα είναι το αρχικό σχέδιο. Το βίαιο τσάκισμά της είναι η επόμενη επιλογή, σε περίπτωση που το πρώτο πλάνο αποτύχει. Το πιο ξεκάθαρο πρόσφατο παράδειγμα για όλα τα παραπάνω είναι το ξαμόλημα των φασιστικών συμμοριών απέναντι στους εξεγερμένους στην Γαλλία, σε τουλάχιστον 15 διαφορετικές πόλεις, ενώ στην Ιταλία, όπου η ακροδεξιά είναι επίσημα στην κυβέρνηση, διατάχθηκε απαγόρευση κυκλοφορίας και επιστρατεύεται ο στρατός απέναντι στους διαδηλωτές που έχουν βγει στους δρόμους ενάντια στο υψηλό κόστος ζωής.


Το γνωρίζουμε πολύ καλά, ο Κασιδιάρης και οι ομόσταυλοί του σε όλο τον πλανήτη δεν είναι “αντισυστημικοί”. Το αντίθετο. Είναι τα πιο πιστά μαντρόσκυλα του κρατικού-καπιταλιστικού συστήματος. Την δράση τους ενάντια στα πιο αδύναμα κομμάτια της τάξης μας την είδαμε πολύ καλά την περίοδο της ανόδου της ΧΑ, αλλά και αργότερα στα συλλαλητήρια για την Μακεδονία. Το αίμα του Παύλου Φύσσα και του Σαχζάτ Λουκμάν δεν έχει στεγνώσει ακόμη και οι δολοφονίες τους, ανάμεσα σε άλλες, δεν πρόκειται να ξεχαστούν.


Η τάξη μας και το κίνημα πρέπει να τσακίσουν τώρα τους φασίστες, προτού σηκώσουν και πάλι ακόμη περισσότερο το κεφάλι. Θα είμαστε εκεί, απέναντί τους σε κάθε κοινωνικό πεδίο: Στους χώρους εργασίας, στις σχολές και τα σχολεία, στις πλατείες, στις γειτονιές. Δεν θα τους αφήσουμε ούτε χιλιοστό γης.

title: Nosso Povo Tá Na Rua
content:
La notte del ballottaggio tra Lula e Flávio Bolsonaro si conclude con una enorme manifestazione di gioia della classe lavoratrice brasiliana: l’avenida Paulista di São Paulo è piena da scoppiare di gente e di bandiere rosse; nelle favelas delle principali città del paese i fuochi d’artificio scoppiano insieme a colpi di armi da fuoco sparati in aria per festeggiare. La vittoria di Lula al secondo turno è data matematicamente per certa intorno alle 9 di sera, ora brasiliana, con oltre 4 milioni di voti di differenza rispetto al candidato dell’estrema destra e il capovolgimento del risultato del primo turno, tenutosi il 4 ottobre.


«Bora Bora Bora Lula,


Bora Bora Bora Virar


Nosso Povo Tá Na Rua


A Mudança Continua»


Avanti Avanti Avanti Lula,


Avanti Avanti Avanti Ribaltiamo (il risultato),


Il nostro popolo è per strada,


Il cambiamento continua.


(

Bora Lula Bora Pra Rua

, “Avanti Lula Avanti per Strada”, jingle a favore di Lula uscito 4 giorni prima del ballottaggio)


La campagna di Lula per il primo turno è stata considerata da più parti una campagna fredda, imperniata intorno alla storia personale del presidente e alla celebrazione dei risultati del governo, e non è riuscita a stimolare la partecipazione attiva della base sociale storica del Partito dei Lavoratori e della sinistra brasiliana. L’estrema destra bolsonarista, al contrario, aveva condotto una campagna elettorale aggressiva, cercando di organizzare la rabbia contro la crisi sociale e presentandosi come forza di rottura, ma allo stesso tempo tutelando gli interessi economici che producono la crisi e spostando la frustrazione dei brasiliani verso l’ostilità contro altri lavoratori, le donne, le persone LGBTQIA+, i migranti e i popoli indigeni. Bolsonaro Jr prometteva aggressive politiche anti-criminali ed elogiava apertamente le operazioni militari condotte dai governatori bolsonaristi nelle favelas, che avevano causato massacri ed omicidi di massa. Si presentava fieramente come alleato degli Stati Uniti nella regione ed esortava il suo elettorato a dare la spallata finale alla sinistra latino-americana, garantendo che il sostegno servile di Brasilia agli interessi americani nella regione avrebbe portato alla crescita economica del paese. Il bolsonarismo, che condivide i propri interessi economici con la destra liberale, aveva infine stretto alleanze con i grandi proprietari terrieri del centro-sud, le industrie forestali ed i grandi capitali industriali promettendo l’abbattimento di ogni barriera legale alla deforestazione, sdoganando il fracking e lo sfruttamento intensivo dei bacini minerari del paese.


A questo bisogna aggiungere – da un lato – la spudorata ingerenza dell’imperialismo americano nella campagna elettorale, come al solito condotta dagli americani senza carota ma con tanto bastone: dagli endorsement ufficiali di Trump alle minacce di un crollo dei mercati finanziari in caso di vittoria di Lula, fino ad arrivare all’adozione ufficiale da parte del Brasile di sistemi di conteggio dei voti progettati negli USA e dipendenti dalle tecnologie satellitari Starlink di Elon Musk. Dall’altro lato, anche la magistratura brasiliana storicamente legata a doppio filo all’estrema destra aveva fatto il suo, aprendo ad arte – al culmine della campagna elettorale – due inchieste per corruzione contro alcuni ministri del PT e contro lo stesso figlio di Lula. Al primo turno, diversi stati in cui la vittoria di Lula era data per garantita dal PT sono quindi andati al bolsonarismo e l’astensione si è collocata intorno al 20%.


Un dato significativo della prima tornata, tuttavia, risulta essere l’elezione (o la rielezione) con il PT o altri partiti della coalizione (tra cui il PSOL e il PCdoB) di decine di militanti provenienti da differenti settori sociali in lotta, un elemento che conferma come il massiccio e combattivo movimento sociale brasiliano abbia, nel corso degli ultimi anni, puntato sul Lulismo come vetrina elettorale: tra loro, Rick Azevedo, leader del movimento

Vida Além do Trabalho

 (Vita Prima del Lavoro), ex-commesso che si batte da anni per l’abolizione della scala 6×1 (6 giorni di lavoro, 1 di riposo); Rosa Amorim, storica dirigente del

Movimento Sem Terra

; Ana Júlia Ribeiro, dirigente del movimento studentesco in prima linea durante le occupazioni delle scuole del Paraná; Erika Hilton, attivista LGBTQIA+ e storica militante per i diritti delle persone trans e nere.

author: Amy Romer, Local Journalism Initiative Reporter
title: After a ‘mind-blowing’ encounter at a ‘New York’ museum, a Sḵwx̱wú7mesh weaving returns home
content:
On Sept. 14, a ceremony at the Museum of North Vancouver welcomed a tumpline from Sen̓áḵw back to Sḵwx̱wú7mesh territory. The tumpline was collected in 1898 during the Jesup North Pacific Expedition. Photo by Alison Boulier


Sḵwx̱wú7mesh master weaver Chief Janice George had visited New York’s American Museum of Natural History (AMNH) before.


George and her husband, Buddy Joseph, had previously travelled to the museum to examine their collection of Coast Salish weavings.


But when the couple returned in 2024, to research an exhibition George was co-curating at the Burke Museum in “Seattle,” they were surprised to be shown something they hadn’t seen during prior visits.

Among the pieces brought out for them to view was a tumpline — a woven belt used to carry heavy loads. It was beautiful, she remembers thinking, and she admired its master craftsmanship as Joseph searched the museum’s records for information about its origins.

And then he found it. The tumpline was from Sen̓áḵw, the ancient Sḵwx̱wú7mesh village currently being

reimagined

 for 21st century living — and where George was working as a cultural advisor at the time.

“It was just mind-blowing,” George said.


George describes the tumpline as a “woven jewel,” pointing to the fineness of the wool, its vivid colours and the care taken with every detail.


She experiences the tumpline not just as a master weaver, but as a hereditary chief and curator. “It makes me feel emotional to even think about it,” she said.

Rushing to find somewhere to connect the call with her colleagues, she said she felt like the encounter was a message from the ancestors, affirming that she and Joseph were on the right path. 


She excitedly shared what she found — and began working to bring the tumpline back to Sḵwx̱wú7mesh.

At 73 and 69, respectively, George and Joseph have spent years travelling to museums and collections across the world in search of Sḵwx̱wú7mesh weavings. “My relatives call us teenagers because we’re always on the run,” she laughed.

The more belongings the couple are able to locate and bring home, the more future generations can learn from the knowledge, histories and cultural practices carried within them.

“The energy comes with the work,” George said, recalling her husband’s words. “This is work that we’re meant to do.”


After a long journey home, the tumpline is now on temporary display in George’s latest exhibition,

Gifts to be shared, protected and carried forward

, at the Museum of North Vancouver (MONOVA) until March 2027. But while its return to Sḵwx̱wú7mesh territory marks a significant milestone, what happens to the weaving after the exhibition closes remains uncertain.


The Sen̓áḵw tumpline, a woven strap traditionally used to carry baskets of harvested foods, is on display at the Museum of North Vancouver until March 2027. Photo by Alison Boulier


‘It’s unlike anything we’ve seen before’


A tumpline is a long, narrow woven strap used to carry bundles of harvested foods, such as berries, herbs or seafood.


Tied to either side of a basket, the strap rested across the forehead, allowing the wearer to carry the load on their back. Among Sḵwx̱wú7mesh and other Coast Salish peoples, women often made and used tumplines to carry whatever they gathered.


The Sen̓áḵw tumpline was recorded in the AMNH collection in 1898, during the Jesup North Pacific Expedition. Led by anthropologist Franz Boas, the expedition collected Indigenous belongings across the North Pacific region, reflecting a colonial-era approach to studying Indigenous peoples and their cultures.

Visible repairs suggest the tumpline had already been used for some time before it entered the museum’s collection, potentially dating it to the early 19th century or earlier, said George.


Master weaver and hereditary chief Janice George and her husband, Buddy Joseph admire the Sen̓áḵw tumpline during its welcome ceremony at the Museum of North Vancouver on Sept. 14. Photo by Alison Boulier


George believes it was woven from mountain goat wool, possibly spun with hair from woolly dogs that Sḵwx̱wú7mesh and other Coast Salish peoples bred for their fibre. The practice dates back at least 5,000 years, but eventually disappeared as colonialism disrupted Coast Salish communities and cultural traditions.

Depending on when the tumpline was made, its wool may have been dyed with natural materials such as alder or combined with red yarn unravelled from commercially made garments.

author: CMI Argentina
title: El Gobierno expulsó a la científica que detectó la presencia de agroquímicos en personas en Argentina
content:
El Consejo Directivo del INTA armó una causa y exoneró finalmente a Virginia Aparicio, investigadora del proyecto SPRINT que estudió la presencia de agroquímicos en 86% de personas, en ambiente y especies, en Argentina.


Virginia Aparicio, ingeniera agrónoma, doctora en Ciencias Agrarias e investigadora del INTA.


Finalmente, el Consejo Directivo del INTA exoneró este lunes a Virginia Aparicio, la investigadora de la Unidad Integrada Balcarce que coordinó en la Argentina el proyecto SPRINT y midió residuos de agroquímicos en el ambiente y en el cuerpo de voluntarios.


Es la sanción más grave que prevé el empleo público nacional y la deja fuera del INTA y del sector público.


La medida figura en la resolución 366 del organismo, fechada este mismo lunes, y basada en lo tratado en la reunión del 27 de agosto por la Comisión Directiva del organismo, que dio por concluido el sumario abierto en diciembre de 2023.


Su artículo 11 dispone textualmente: “Aplícase a la agente Virginia Carolina APARICIO (Legajo N° 17.205) la sanción de EXONERACIÓN por la violación comprobada de las prohibiciones del artículo 24, incisos e) e i)” de la ley marco de empleo público.


De acuerdo a la resolución, el inciso e) prohíbe usar las facultades del cargo para fines ajenos a la función, y el Consejo Directivo lo aplica a la relación de Aparicio con José Luis Costa, un investigador retirado del INTA.


Según la resolución, “COSTA integraba el grupo familiar de APARICIO en calidad de conviviente”, algo que el organismo da por probado con las declaraciones juradas del legajo de la investigadora, que registran una unión de hecho desde septiembre de 2005.


La causa armada por el INTA contra Aparicio


El texto sostiene que la coordinadora “empleó sus prerrogativas de coordinación para conferir a su conviviente una posición particular de participación, conducción fáctica e inspección de datos reservados, sin autorización del INTA, sin formalización por el órgano decisor del Consorcio ni exteriorización específica del conflicto que permitiera su evaluación independiente”.


Agrega que Costa “se encontraba retirado del INTA y carecía de vínculo institucional vigente”, aunque el documento de información entregado a los voluntarios lo incluía, junto con Aparicio y otro investigador del equipo, entre las personas habilitadas para inspeccionar datos incluso sin codificar.


Virginia Aparicio recibió una notificación de la Dirección General del INTA en 2023, en la que le prohibían difundir los resultados de la investigación SPRINT.


Uso indebido del patrimonio, la otra excusa del INTA


También, el inciso i) castiga el uso indebido del patrimonio estatal y se apoya en el manejo de los fondos europeos, que ingresaron a la contabilidad del INTA. La resolución consigna ingresos por 5.661.483,83 pesos, egresos por 5.527.359,58 y un saldo de 134.124,25. Entre ellos menciona un pago a World Courier de 1.688.445,82 pesos en julio de 2022 por el envío de muestras a los Países Bajos, unos 13.122,95 euros según la cotización del Banco Central.


El propio Consejo Directivo aclara que esos importes no pueden identificarse “por sí solos, con un perjuicio fiscal equivalente, cuya existencia y cuantía no han sido objeto en este procedimiento de una determinación fundada”.


Explica que igual corresponde sancionar porque la prohibición “comprende la utilización indebida de bienes y recursos públicos como supuesto autónomo, sin requerir necesariamente la producción de un perjuicio fiscal, su apropiación, obtención de un beneficio personal o destino a fines particulares”.


Envío de muestras a Holanda


La decisión de centralizar los análisis en el exterior, concluye, fue “adoptada e impulsada por la sumariada APARICIO sin contar con la autorización institucional exigible”. Reconoce además la “ausencia de beneficio económico acreditado” y de antecedentes disciplinarios, pero afirma que esas circunstancias “no permiten atenuar la relevancia de la falta cometida”.


La lista de reproches es más larga. El Consejo Directivo le atribuye haber reemplazado al comité de ética previsto en el acuerdo de subvención por el del Programa Temático Interdisciplinario en Bioética de la Universidad Nacional de Mar del Plata, sin pasar por los órganos del INTA. Señala diferencias entre el protocolo, que preveía 72 participantes repartidos en tres grupos de 24, y la presentación de junio de 2023, que habla de 20 productores, 28 vecinos y 25 consumidores.

author: Chris Walker
title: Alaska Officials Seek Dismissal of DOJ Suit Aiming to Block Election Results
content:
Officials have “taken significant steps to distinguish” two candidates with the same name on the ballot, they said.

Honest, paywall-free news is rare. Please support our boldly independent journalism with a donation of any size.

On Monday, Alaska election officials filed a motion calling for the “immediate” dismissal of a lawsuit, brought forward last week by the U.S. Department of Justice (DOJ), that seeks to invalidate the state’s U.S. Senate race if the Republican candidate loses.

The race features three main candidates. Democrat Mary Peltola is neck and neck in polls with incumbent Sen. Dan Sullivan (R). Meanwhile, a third candidate, also named Dan Sullivan, is running as an independent.

Although the latter Sullivan maintains he is running a legitimate campaign, Alaska officials alleged that he was trying to cause confusion among voters and initially kept him off the ballot. However, the independent sued the state, and won the right to be included in the election after the state Supreme Court found that his candidacy was proper and legal.

Despite the independent already appearing on the primary election ballot and early voting for the general election already starting, the DOJ filed a lawsuit last Thursday, demanding that the state refuse to certify the results if the incumbent Sullivan loses (most likely to Peltola).

“It is vital that Defendants not certify any election result that may be impacted by voter confusion,” the DOJ lawsuit said, adding that one of the conditions demonstrating the outcome could have been “impacted by voter confusion” is if “Senator Sullivan does not win the election.”

Democrats, including Peltola, responded to the suit by requesting it be fast-tracked and, eventually, for a judge to deem it unfounded, especially since elections are largely meant to be administered by the states without federal interference. Shortly after U.S. District Court Judge Sharon Gleason approved fast-tracking the motion, Alaska election officials filed their own paperwork with the court, asking for the DOJ lawsuit to be dismissed outright.

The filing was submitted jointly by Carol Beecher, director of the Division of Elections, and the Elections Boards of the State of Alaska, as well as the State Ballot Counting Review Board for the state, collectively calling themselves “the Division.” The officials recognized the situation was a rare one, but argued that shouldn’t allow the federal government to preemptively intervene in the race’s outcome.

“Although Alaska faces an unusual situation in which two candidates for U.S. Senator share a first and last name, the Division has taken significant steps to distinguish them on the ballot so that voters can easily determine which candidate is which,” the Division’s filing stated, noting that there is a “lack of evidence of any problems (or indeed, any legal cause of action)” described in the DOJ’s lawsuit.

The federal government also “lacks authority to intervene in state elections at all, much less in support of a favored candidate,” the filing said.

The Division pointed out that it has taken steps to minimize confusion among voters, including differentiating the two Sullivans on the ballot by listing one as the incumbent Republican senator, and the other as the independent challenger. Both men also have their middle initials included to alert voters to the fact that they are different candidates.

Beyond those actions, the Division noted that Alaska’s ranked-choice voting system will ensure voters have the opportunity to pick both Sullivans, if one of the choices is their true preference over Peltola.

“If any Sullivan-supporting voter remains uncertain which Sullivan is which despite this clear differentiation on the ballot, the voter can ask for assistance from others or look up information about the candidates using a smart phone or an election pamphlet,” the Division stated. “And if the voter is still uncertain, Alaska’s ranked-choice voting system provides another solution: the voter can rank the Sullivans as his first and second choices. That way, if the voter’s first-ranked Sullivan is eliminated, his vote would transfer to the other Sullivan.”

“The Court should promptly dismiss the complaint with prejudice so that Alaska can proceed to administer its elections consistent with state and federal law and without unwarranted interference by the United States,” the Division’s filing concluded.

title: At least 87 people executed in Iran in 20 days
content:
The wave of executions in Iran continues. According to the “No Execution Tuesdays” campaign, at least 87 people have been executed in just 20 days. Death sentences have also reportedly been handed down to numerous other prisoners. The protest movement, which has been campaigning against the death penalty and the Iranian regime’s execution practices for more than two and a half years, is now continuing its actions in 66 prisons. On Tuesday, the campaign entered its 144th week.


In a statement, participants warned of the scale of state repression as hundreds, possibly even thousands, of prisoners in Iran are awaiting execution. “The regime uses the death penalty not only to kill people but also to spread fear throughout society and silence opposition voices. Each execution also leaves families in deep grief.”


The campaign highlighted the large number of executions carried out during the Iranian month of Mehr, which lasted from September 22 to October 19. According to the campaign, this development demonstrates how systematically the regime uses the death penalty as a tool of intimidation. “Yet history has shown that no gallows can tear the desire for freedom and equality from people’s hearts. No repression can silence forever the voices of those who fight for their rights,” the statement said.


The prisoners appealed to human rights organizations, political and trade union activists, relatives of those sentenced to death, and all democratic forces to strengthen their solidarity. They stressed that the names of those facing execution must not be forgotten through silence and indifference. The campaign called for the public condemnation of all death sentences, an immediate halt to ongoing executions, and an expansion of the collective struggle for the complete abolition of the death penalty in Iran.

title: Convicted rapist Musa Orhan acquitted of charge of inciting suicide
content:
Turkish former non-commissioned officer Musa Orhan, who was sentenced to ten years in prison for raping 18-year-old Kurdish woman İpek Er, has been acquitted in a separate criminal case. On October 22, a court in Batman ruled that it could not be proven that Orhan had incited the young woman to take her own life. The acquittal came despite her suicide note, incriminating witness testimony, and his previous conviction for serious sexual violence. Orhan remains free and has yet to begin serving his prison sentence.


The case of İpek Er sparked outrage far beyond Kurdistan in 2020 and became a symbol of impunity for sexual violence committed by uniformed state personnel. Women’s organizations and the Kurdish women’s movement protested against Orhan’s repeated release from custody and the Turkish judiciary’s handling of the young woman’s case. Even his subsequent conviction did not change the fact that the former soldier remained free.


İpek Er reported being held captive and raped


İpek Er had met Musa Orhan online. In the suicide note she later left behind, she described how the professional soldier, who was stationed in the district of Beşiri at the time, had held her captive for several days, drugged her, and raped her. On July 7, 2020, she filed a criminal complaint with the public prosecutor’s office in the neighboring province of Siirt. Nine days later, the 18-year-old girl attempted suicide and was hospitalized with life-threatening injuries. After 34 days, she died on August 18, 2020. Her suicide note and statements from medical personnel became key pieces of evidence. İpek Er had alerted the doctors and nurses who first examined her after her admission to the violence she had suffered, telling them, “Musa has destroyed me.”


Sentenced to ten years in prison, yet still free


The Turkish judiciary’s handling of Orhan following the disclosure of the rape sparked widespread protests. He was initially detained on July 16, 2020, but was released under judicial supervision after questioning. It was only after İpek Er’s death and amid growing public outrage that he was arrested again on August 19 and subsequently placed in pretrial detention. Around a week later, Orhan was released from custody once more at his lawyer’s request. His dismissal from public service also came only after a decision by the High Disciplinary Board of the Turkish Ministry of Interior. He was subsequently expelled from the Gendarmerie.


In December 2021, a criminal court in Siirt sentenced Orhan to twelve years in prison for aggravated sexual assault. The sentence was reduced to ten years under Article 62 of the Turkish Penal Code, which provides for discretionary sentence reductions. Despite the conviction, the court declined to order his detention and imposed only a travel ban. The regional appeals court in Diyarbakır later upheld the prison sentence by a majority decision. One judge even argued for an acquittal in a dissenting opinion. The Diyarbakır Bar Association’s Women’s Rights Center’s request for a harsher sentence was rejected.


Court finds evidence insufficient


The proceedings that have now concluded concerned whether Orhan could also be held criminally responsible for İpek Er’s suicide. In its closing arguments, the prosecution had requested a conviction for inciting suicide. However, the court concluded that there was no concrete evidence beyond reasonable doubt that Orhan had incited İpek Er to take her own life, encouraged her to do so, or reinforced her decision. It invoked the principle of criminal law that any doubt must be resolved in favor of the defendant.


The court therefore did not consider Orhan’s previous rape conviction, İpek Er’s suicide note, or her statements to hospital staff sufficient grounds for establishing additional criminal liability. The acquittal relates exclusively to the charge of inciting suicide and does not overturn his earlier conviction for sexual violence.


Lawyers for the victim’s family denied time to respond


The court’s handling of the verdict also raises questions. The lawyers representing the victim’s family had requested permission to respond in writing to the prosecution’s closing arguments. The court denied their request for additional time and immediately issued its acquittal. The written reasoning for the verdict was entered into the Turkish judicial system the very next day, October 23. At the same time, the court lifted the travel ban imposed on Orhan in the proceedings …

title: Swedish Social Democratic Party seeks to strengthen cooperation with DEM Party
content:
Following the confirmation of the Swedish election results, DEM Party co-chairs Tülay Hatimoğulları and Tuncer Bakırhan sent a congratulatory message to Swedish Social Democratic Party leader Magdalena Andersson.


Magdalena Andersson, who is currently working to form a government in her country, sent a letter addressed to the DEM Party co-chairs.


The letter, shared by the DEM Party Press Office, reads as follows:


“Thank you for your letter and congratulations on behalf of the Peoples’ Equality and Democracy Party. The election results were very close, and this period requires patience, dialogue, and determination. We are doing everything we can to form a government that works for social justice and equal opportunities—ideals that you, too, continue to champion.


At a time of increasing polarization, we must demonstrate that social democracy can deliver results for ordinary people while offering a genuine alternative to the forces seeking to divide us. We deeply value our friendship with the DEM Party. We stand in solidarity with your demands for peace, justice, and democracy in Turkey and look forward to further strengthening our cooperation, both bilaterally and through our shared international platforms.”
