title: Journalists call for united struggle against repression
content:
Censorship, access restrictions and repressive policies targeting the press and media workers are intensifying, but journalists continue their struggle for a free press in the face of these obstacles. As the public's right to information comes under attack, growing pressure on journalists is deepening restrictions on freedom of expression and press freedom. Free press workers, however, continue to resist these pressures and bring the truth to the public.


Evrensel newspaper reporter Elif Ekin Saltık and Dicle Fırat Journalists Association (DFG) Co-Chair Selman Çiçek spoke to ANF about the mounting pressure on the media. They said the repression affects not only journalists but also democratic politics, freedom of expression and the public's right to information. The journalists pointed out that the longstanding repression of the Kurdish press has now expanded to include other opposition media outlets. They called for solidarity and a united struggle against the obstacles facing free and multilingual journalism.


‘The attacks initially targeted the Kurdish press’


Evrensel newspaper reporter Elif Ekin Saltık said that repression in the media had continued for many years, initially targeting the Kurdish press and the Free Press. Saltık said that all opposition groups were now facing similar measures and that the struggle for press freedom could not be separated from the struggle for democracy, freedom and equality.


 


Saltık said: “The press and media have been under enormous pressure for many years. These pressures were initially directed at the Kurdish press and the Free Press, and they have continued for a very long time. Today, they are directed at all opposition groups. We are in Diyarbakır (Amed) today, outside the courthouse, but journalists in many parts of Turkey are out on the streets, defending the right to information and press freedom and trying to make their voices heard.


We are discussing press freedom today, but we know that the issue is not simply about press freedom. It is also a question of democratisation, freedom and equality. If the Free Press cannot report freely, if media workers and journalists cannot freely bring the truth to the public, then the people's right to information is also being obstructed.


We are living through a period in which journalism is treated as a crime, journalists are detained, imprisoned and arrested, and media outlets are shut down. As I said at the beginning, this is a form of censorship that we have experienced for many years, primarily through the repression of the Free Press. These are the outlets through which we can access genuine news. Today, these pressures have spread to all opposition groups across the country, and they are still continuing.”


‘The public is being prevented from accessing the truth’


Elif Ekin Saltık drew attention to access restrictions imposed on media outlets' websites and social media accounts, saying: “There are countless examples, from the shutdown of Halk TV to restrictions targeting T24, the repeatedly blocked website of Mezopotamya Agency, JINNEWS, the closure of Mezopotamya Agency's social media accounts and censorship of Evrensel newspaper's social media accounts. What is happening across the country shows that an operation is being carried out to prevent genuine news from reaching the public. They want to silence truthful reporting and stop the truth from reaching people.


 


The issue of the fund scandal has become so widely exposed recently that they can no longer contain it. That is why they are trying even harder to restrict the media and the press. Defending press freedom today means not only defending the right to information but also defending democracy. It means ensuring that democratic politics can function and that people can express their opinions freely.


A process is also underway. In the context of this process, it is extremely important to establish a language of peace, practise peace journalism and ensure that everyone can exercise their right to information through the free press. That is why we are out on the streets today. It is not only journalists who are taking to the streets; citizens are also out there defending their right to information and their right to access the truth.”


‘The struggle for a free press will not be silenced’


Saltık said that defending press freedom was not solely the responsibility of journalists and that every section of society had a role to play in this struggle …

author: Unknown
title: MSD condemns the attack in Gire Spi: Return of IDPs is an inherent right
content:
The Syrian Democratic Council (MSD) strongly condemned the recent attacks against forcibly displaced Kurdish families returning to Tal Abyad (Gire Spi) in the Raqqa countryside. Returning civilians—including women and children—faced death threats, physical assaults, and property destruction. These violent acts were accompanied by racist slogans targeting Kurdish national identity.


MSD stated that this incident is a grave crime against unarmed civilians, a flagrant violation of the January 29 agreement, and a direct threat to social peace and the right to safe return.


The MSD holds the Syrian Transitional Government fully responsible for protecting civilians, safeguarding their property, and immediately stopping these abuses to prevent their recurrence. It calls for an independent, impartial, and public investigation to reveal the facts, hold both perpetrators and instigators accountable regardless of affiliation, and end systemic impunity. Furthermore, the MSD demands decisive action against hate speech and racial incitement to ensure that no citizen is targeted based on national identity.


The MSD said it is monitoring the rising anger and tension in Hasakah with grave concern, remarking that this public outrage is fully understandable given the severe threats and violations faced by returning families. While calling for restraint and de-escalation to preserve social peace, the MSD stresses that calm must not come at the expense of justice or accountability. “Addressing the fallout of these attacks requires providing redress for victims, prosecuting those responsible, and addressing the root causes of tension under the rule of law,” the statement said.


The MSD reaffirms that the return of forcibly displaced persons to their homes is an inherent right, not a privilege granted by any faction: “A safe, dignified, and voluntary return requires concrete security guarantees, the protection of property, and fair compensation for suffered losses. Protecting civilians, delivering justice, and guaranteeing the right of return remain foundational pillars for building a united Syria based on equal citizenship and full recognition of all its communities.”

author: webdev@democracynow.org (Democracy Now!)
title: "Dark Day for Journalism": Egypt Shutters Independent News Site Mada Masr, Detains Editor
content:
A court in Cairo has ordered the closure of the independent Egyptian news site

Mada Masr

. The court also ordered the site’s editor-in-chief, Lina Attalah, to be detained until she pays a fine of over $50,000. She was convicted on charges of managing an unlicensed website.

Mada Masr

 is “the flagship independent media outlet in Egypt and a pillar of independent media in the region,” says Sharif Abdel Kouddous of

Drop Site News

, who previously worked at

Mada Masr

. The independent outlet was founded in 2013 “in the midst of Egypt’s revolution and counterrevolution” and has “managed to survive all of those years in one of the most hostile media environments” in the world. Still, “what happened today is an unprecedented escalation” because Attalah and

Mada Masr

 had never before been referred to trial.


Kouddous adds that the attack on

Mada Masr

 comes less than a month after Egyptian authorities arrested an entire newsroom at the independent fact-checking outlet

Matsadaash

. They remain behind bars.

author: Miriam Lafontaine
title: Coast guard prepares to survey Arctic using Israeli-made drone
content:
The Canadian Coast Guard is preparing to test the Arctic surveillance capacity of a large Israeli-manufactured drone.


Coast guard staff began testing the Hermes 900 Starliner earlier this year at the Canadian Forces Base in Greenwood, N.S., before it was disassembled and shipped from there to Iqaluit on Oct. 1.


The testing will part of an effort to study whether the drone can fit well into the coast guard’s fleet of smaller drones, said Mark McKeeman, the director of the coast guard’s remotely piloted aircraft program.


“Were still in the contract delivery stages with the manufacturer, so they have to prove that the aircraft is capable of operating in some of the conditions in the Arctic,” he said.


One of the things the Hermes 900 Starliner will be tested for is its ability to operate at 72 degrees north, which is about the same latitude as Pond Inlet.


Canada signed a contract to obtain the drone from the Israeli arms dealer Elbit Systems in 2020, at a cost of $36 million.


Transport Canada was initially assigned to manage its use as part of Canada’s National Aerial Surveillance Program, which was transferred over to the coast guard on April 1.


The program now has a mandate to assert Canada’s presence and sovereignty in the Arctic, McKeeman said.


Climate change is bringing an extended shipping season to the Arctic, he noted, and more shipping traffic demands more monitoring.


Should the drone join the government’s fleet, it would monitor shipping and ice cover, respond to pollution events such as oil spills, and patrol for foreign actors attempting to illegally enter Canadian waters, McKeeman said.


The drone, which is red, has a 15-metre wingspan and is about 8.3 metres long, is stationed at a hanger in Iqaluit’s airport.


He said his team had initially hoped to get the drone airborne early this month, but the mission was called off because of low cloud cover. Now testing should begin in May or June.


McKeeman said if everything goes well, the Department of National Defence could explore purchasing more of the drones.


Canada’s Department of National Defence has awarded Elbit Systems contracts for many years. As recently as 2025, the department awarded a $1.9 million sole-source contract to a Elbit Systems Deutschland, a German subsidy of the company, for the purchase of networking equipment.


Meanwhile, a 2025 UN report

named

 the company in a report investigating how the private sector profits from and is complicit in Israel’s genocide in Palestine.


The Hermes 900 Starliner is among drones long-used by the Israeli military since at least 2014. The Israeli military has also used it during the Israeli-Hamas war, which started in October 2023.


NDP Edmonton MP Heather McPherson, also the party’s critic for foreign affairs and international trade, said the federal government has a moral obligation to cut its ties with the company.


“The Canadian government has a responsibility to live up to the same standards that they have set for other companies in this countries, and that means they should not be engaging with companies who are complicit in human rights abuses in the West Bank and Gaza,” she said in an interview.


In 2024, Canada paused the approval of new direct export permits for military goods to Israel.


Jad Eleid, a Montreal-based organizer with the Palestinian Youth Movement, said that the federal government should instead implement a two-way arms embargo, which would end the awarding of contracts to Israeli companies.


“Complicity with genocide is not always about sending bombs and bullets: it’s about purchasing from companies that use the same surveillance technology that allows the bombing of our people,” said Eleid, who is from Lebanon.


The Hermes 900 StarLiner was alleged to have been used in 2024 to target civilians in Lebanon, according to

media reports

 from the time.


Eleid said a loophole in Canada’s export regime also still allows for the export of parts as long as they get to the United States first before being shipped to Israel.


In March, Jenny Kwan, another NDP MP from Vancouver, attempted to pass a bill to close that loophole. It was rejected then, with 295 MP voting against it and 22 voting in favour.


Nunatsiaq News asked Liberal Nunavut MP Lori Idlout for her thoughts on Canada conducting business with an Israeli defence contractor but did not receive a response.

author: webdev@democracynow.org (Democracy Now!)
title: "Anti-Fascist Economics": Isabella Weber on How Inequality Fuels Extremism & Erodes Democracy
content:
With the U.S. midterm elections just a week away, the affordability crisis — intensified by President Trump’s tariffs and war on Iran — has emerged as a major campaign issue. Across the country, families are struggling to make ends meet, while oil and gas companies have reported record profits during recent periods of price shocks.


Economist Isabella Weber’s new book,

Anti-Fascist Economics: In Defense of Affordability, Dignity, and Democracy

, warns economic insecurity can fuel the rise of authoritarian movements, and argues protecting democracy requires making life affordable for everybody.


Anti-fascist economics is “not about getting rid of the market,” says Weber. “It’s about having public players that behave differently, and by behaving differently, changing the dynamic of the market as a whole and literally creating an alternative so that people are not dependent on often very concentrated and private providers as the only choice,” she explains, providing current examples of governments enacting such policies from New York City to Mexico City to Rome.

author: Jenna Mahale
title: Over 20k Sign Petition Demanding Inquiry Into UK Role in Gaza Genocide
content:
Jeremy Corbyn has backed fresh calls for an independent inquiry into the UK’s role in Israel’s atrocities in Gaza.


The former Labour leader is supporting

a parliamentary petition

 calling for a probe into “any British involvement in Israeli operations” in the enclave, “including the sale, supply or use of weapons, surveillance aircraft and Royal Air Force bases.”

 


The petition, launched last week by trade unionist and Your Party organiser Jennifer Forbes, has amassed over 20,000 signatures. “We believe the UK has played a vital role in Israeli military operations in Gaza,” it reads.


It calls for a “fully independent” inquiry that would have the power to “question government ministers and officials involved in decision-making processes” about weapons sales, intelligence gathering and the use of RAF bases. 


It would also seek to establish what legal advice was sought by the government “in assessing whether a genocide has taken place in Gaza.”


Andy Burnham’s government last week rejected Corbyn’s call for an inquiry, arguing an investigation was unnecessary due to the “extensive mechanisms already available for parliamentary accountability and oversight”.


In response, Corbyn

wrote on Instagram

: “If the government has nothing to hide, then why block our efforts to expose the truth?”


Because the petition has already passed the threshold of 10,000 signatures, the government must now give a formal response. If it reaches 100,000 signatures it can be debated in parliament. 


In June, MPs debated

Israeli influence on British politics

 after more than 118,000 people signed a separate petition calling for an inquiry. 


Ayoub Khan, Independent MP for Birmingham Perry Barr, was among those who

backed the earlier petition

. “With every decision this government has made, it’s not only reasonable to ask questions about political influence in Britain, it’s necessary,” he said.

author: Aline Melo
title: Parlamentares dos EUA cobram Meta por tratamento desigual a Lula
content:
Uma carta assinada por 13 parlamentares democratas dos Estados Unidos cobra explicações de Mark Zuckerberg, CEO da Meta, sobre denúncias de tratamento desigual às campanhas de Luiz Inácio Lula da Silva (PT) e Flávio Bolsonaro (PL) nas plataformas da empresa durante as eleições presidenciais brasileiras de 2026.

Enviada em 22 de outubro, a carta ocorre em meio a denúncias de restrições a conteúdos políticos, redução de alcance de publicações e diferenças no funcionamento de ferramentas de inteligência artificial, episódios que levantaram suspeitas sobre a atuação de empresas estrangeiras no processo eleitoral brasileiro.


Entre os signatários estão o senador Bernie Sanders e os deputados Pramila Jayapal, Greg Casar, Maxwell Frost, Jesús G. (conhecido como Chuy García), Jonathan L. Jackson, Summer L. Lee, Mark Pocan, Mike Quigley, Delia C. Ramirez, Jan Schakowsky, Rashida Tlaib e Nydia M. Velázquez. 


Os parlamentares afirmam estar preocupados com os diversos relatos que surgiram ao longo das eleições brasileiras de que as plataformas da Meta estariam restringindo ou reduzindo a distribuição de conteúdos ligados à campanha de Lula, enquanto ampliavam ou recomendavam publicações associadas a Flávio Bolsonaro e seus aliados. Segundo os signatários, as diferenças de tratamento poderiam criar condições desiguais na disputa eleitoral.


Entre os episódios citados está a

desativação

, em 23 de setembro, da conta de anúncios da campanha de Lula no Facebook, 11 dias antes do primeiro turno. Embora a conta tenha sido restabelecida após 24 horas, os parlamentares afirmam que a Meta não apresentou uma justificativa detalhada para a medida. A carta também menciona restrições ao impulsionamento de anúncios da campanha no Instagram entre 9 e 10 de outubro, que, segundo uma estimativa da própria campanha, teriam impedido cerca de 1,3 milhão de pessoas de visualizar as publicações.


O documento cita ainda uma reportagem da

Folha de S.Paulo

 sobre comunicações internas da Meta que indicariam que funcionários da empresa tinham conhecimento de recomendações algorítmicas que promoviam o perfil de Flávio Bolsonaro e um canal do WhatsApp associado à sua campanha, prática que é proibida pelo Tribunal Superior Eleitoral (TSE).


A carta também menciona um levantamento da organização Ctrl Z,

divulgado

 pela

Agência Pública

, que documentou mais de mil casos de restrições e banimentos nas plataformas da Meta na primeira quinzena do mês. Entre os conteúdos cuja orientação política pôde ser identificada, nove em cada dez eram favoráveis a Lula ou progressistas. O levantamento registrou casos de perda de alcance, restrições às funcionalidades de contas e remoção de publicações.


Os parlamentares dos Estados Unidos pedem que Zuckerberg esclareça quais medidas foram adotadas, quais regras orientam a moderação de conteúdo político em eleições estrangeiras e se a empresa mantém comunicações com integrantes do governo Donald Trump sobre o Judiciário brasileiro, a regulamentação das plataformas e as eleições de 2026.


O documento também questiona como a Meta pretende garantir que restrições automatizadas às contas de anúncios dos candidatos sejam analisadas por pessoas em até duas horas. Por fim, os signatários perguntam se a empresa permitirá que um auditor independente examine dados internos de moderação e distribuição de conteúdo político relacionado às eleições brasileiras.


Os parlamentares estabeleceram o dia 4 de novembro como prazo para o envio das respostas por escrito, sem retorno até o momento de publicação dessa nota. 


Alertas da sociedade civil 


Para Luã Cruz, diretor de Litigância Estratégica da Ctrl+Z, os episódios reforçam os alertas sobre os riscos de concentrar o debate político nas plataformas controladas pelas Big Techs.

“A sociedade civil brasileira de direitos digitais tem alertado há anos sobre o problema de deixar todo o sistema de discussão política pública dentro de ferramentas que são controladas por empresas estrangeiras. As eleições mostraram isso justamente por ser um momento delicado”

, afirma.


Segundo Luã, as denúncias reuniram evidências de diferentes formas de interferência, desde anúncios com desinformação e pagamentos em moeda estrangeira até o descumprimento de regras eleitorais e a derrubada de conteúdos progressistas: “Isso reforça de maneira mais aguda que a gente não pode depender delas”, diz.


O diretor ressalta que as plataformas continuam sendo importantes para a comunicação política – …

title: Serbia: la lista degli studenti stravince le elezioni. Il movimento chiude l’era Vucic, 12 anni di corruzione e ultranazionalismo
content:
Svolta elettorale storica in 

Serbia

, dove si è registrata un’affluenza record alle urne.


da

Radio Onda d’Urto


Vucic ammette la sconfitta alle elezioni, 

stravinte dalla Lista degli studenti

. La svolta chiude 12 anni di dominio ultranazionalista di Vucic, passato da vicepremier e premier a presidente dopo la fondazione, nel 2008, del Partito progressista serbo (SNS).


La Lista studentesca è destinata a ottenere 

140 seggi su 250 del Parlamento

, mentre la formazione dello sconfitto Vucic ne avrà circa 105. Le proiezioni attribuiscono agli studenti circa il 52% dei voti contro il 39% di Vucic, dopo anni di potere segnati da corruzione e a quasi due anni dalle 

proteste di massa

, nate dal crollo di una pensilina alla stazione di Novi Sad nel 2024 (16 morti).


Scene di esultanza in strada a Belgrado. Da qui Radio Onda d’Urto ha sentito 

Massimo Moratti, corrispondente dalla capitale della Serbia per l’Osservatorio Balcani Caucaso d’Europa ed esperto in diritti umani. 


L’intervista anche a Giorgio Fruscione, ricercatore dell’ISPI – Istituto per gli Studi di Politica Internazionale.

title: Bostancı'da otobüste kadına şiddet: Saldırgan yolculara da biber gazı sıktı
content:
İstanbul'un Kadıköy ilçesine bağlı Bostancı semtinde bir otobüste kadına yönelik fiziksel şiddet yaşandı. Otobüste bulunan bir kişi bir kadına vurdu. Saldırıya tanık olan diğer yolcuların duruma tepki göstermesi üzerine otobüste gerginlik çıktı.

Duruma müdahale eden yolcular, şiddetin failine tepki gösterdi. Ancak tepkiler üzerine saldırısını sürdüren kişi, bu kez çantasından çıkardığı biber gazını otobüsün içine sıktı.

Kadına yönelik fiziksel şiddetle başlayan olay, yolcuların müdahalesinin ardından toplu taşıma aracındaki diğer kişilerin de güvenliğini tehdit eden bir duruma dönüştü.

Olayın ardından saldırgan hakkında herhangi bir adli işlem yapılıp yapılmadığına ilişkin ise henüz bilgi bulunmuyor.

31 yıldır emeğin sesi olan Evrensel, gücünü sadece okurlarından alıyor. Emeğin sesinin daha gür çıkması için sen de güç ver.

author: webdev@democracynow.org (Democracy Now!)
title: Trump Is Already Undermining Confidence in Midterm Election Results from Alaska to California: ACLU
content:
A competitive Senate race has gripped the once reliably Republican state of Alaska. If Democratic challenger Mary Peltola wins the election against incumbent Republican Senator Dan Sullivan, it could tip the balance of power in Washington. Attorneys for Peltola and the Democratic Senatorial Campaign Committee have submitted a motion to dismiss a Department of Justice lawsuit filed last week that seeks to block the certification of the election results in Alaska if Sullivan loses. President Trump confirmed on Friday he had ordered the

DOJ

 to file the lawsuit, which alleges that the appearance of another candidate on the ballot with a similar name, Daniel J. Sullivan Jr., would mislead voters. The Alaska Supreme Court ruled ahead of the primary that Sullivan Jr., a retired schoolteacher who is running unaffiliated, could appear on the ballot.


The

ACLU

 — on behalf of two Alaska voters, the League of Women Voters of Alaska and Common Cause — has moved to intervene in the case and has also filed a motion asking the court to dismiss it.


“There is no merit to this claim,” says Sophia Lin Lakin, director of the ACLU’s Voting Rights Project. “We’ve asked the court to consider sanctions, because the courts shouldn’t be used to launder baseless claims into distrust in our elections. There should be consequences for that.”

author: anred
title: Anatomía de la victoria digital de Lula
content:
Lula da Silva celebra en São Paulo su victoria electoral y su cuarto mandato como presidente de Brasil, el 25 de octubre de 2026. Foto: Natacha Pisarenko / AP-LaPresse.


Luiz Inácio Lula da Silva ha conquistado la presidencia de Brasil tras librar una batalla electoral sin precedentes en dos frentes simultáneos: en la arena política, contra el embate de la dinastía Bolsonaro; y en el terreno invisible de las plataformas digitales, contra las lógicas, sesgos y restricciones de los propios algoritmos, en particular los de Meta. No es una dicotomía. Son ámbitos complementarios y con profundas ramificaciones. Lo que históricamente se resolvía en los estrados obreros, en la mística de los mítines masivos y en la liturgia de los debates televisados se convirtió esta vez en una carrera de obstáculos cibernética de proporciones gigantescas. El equipo progresista compitió con el terreno inclinado por limitaciones en los motores de búsqueda de Instagram, trabas sistemáticas a su pauta publicitaria y fallos algorítmicos que amenazaban con invisibilizar su mensaje. Su ajustado triunfo electoral no fue solo el desenlace de un programa de gobierno convincente, sino la demostración de cómo una movilización popular híbrida, armada con ironía, inteligencia artificial y canales ciudadanos descentralizados, logró desbordar el cerco técnico de las grandes corporaciones de Silicon Valley para devolver la política a la calle. 

Por Miquel Pellicer, para Jot Down.


De la misma forma que vivimos tiempos de guerras híbridas, las campañas electorales se tornaron HÍ-BRI-DAS. Una campaña electoral híbrida es aquella que borra la frontera entre el mundo analógico y el digital, coordinando ambos espacios como un único campo de batalla sincronizado. Al igual que en la doctrina militar de las

guerras híbridas

 (donde no se combate solo con tanques convencionales, sino combinando tropas de tierra con ciberguerra, desinformación, presiones económicas y propaganda psicológica), una campaña política híbrida no separa el mitin en la plaza de la guerra algorítmica en las pantallas.


El choque frontal con el gigante de Silicon Valley


El conflicto entre el lulismo y la multinacional de

Mark Zuckerberg

 no nació de manera fortuita al calor de la contienda electoral, sino que constituyó el punto culminante de un largo y áspero pulso institucional.

Tal como documentan

 en su artículo los analistas

Antoni Gutiérrez-Rubí

 y

Felipe Carrerá Martínez

 en las páginas de

Agenda Pública

, las tensiones se remontan a los violentos sucesos de enero de 2023, cuando una turba asaltó la plaza de los Tres Poderes espoleada por una marea de desinformación que circuló libremente por las redes sociales. Aquel trauma impulsó al Gobierno recién investido y a los magistrados del Supremo Tribunal Federal a diseñar mecanismos para exigir responsabilidades legales a las empresas tecnológicas por la viralización de contenidos fraudulentos.


La relación entre ambas partes terminó de resquebrajarse a principios de 2025, cuando Meta decidió cancelar de manera unilateral sus protocolos de verificación de veracidad en Brasil, abriendo una crisis que provocó que la Abogacía General de la Unión interpusiera demandas judiciales por la proliferación de estafas que suplantaban la imagen del Estado.


Con este telón de fondo, el aterrizaje en la arena electoral derivó en una abierta acusación de interferencia política. La campaña de Lula denunció formalmente que sus perfiles estaban siendo sometidos a un silenciamiento encubierto. Ya no se trató de denunciar a Rusia o Estados Unidos, sino a Silicon Valley. Lula denunció, a las puertas de la segunda vuelta, a Meta por

«interferir en las elecciones»

. El método no es tan grosero como el de

Elon Musk

 y su apoyo a la ultraderecha global. Sea Estados Unidos, Alemania o Brasil. Meta siempre está ahí. Como si fuera un espectador secundario. Como si fuera el

Alfred Hitchcock

 que pasea circunstancialmente por sus películas de forma anecdótica, pero la realidad es diferente. El historial de Meta en las elecciones es palmario. Ya no solo con Cambridge Analytica en las elecciones estadounidenses de 2016, sino en repetidas ocasiones, como vimos en estas páginas:

 «Cambridge Analytica, la empresa que enseñó a manipular democracias»

. En Brasil, volviendo al presente, por ejemplo, cuando los usuarios escribían el nombre del presidente en el buscador de Instagram, el sistema arrojaba cuentas fantasma o perfiles irrelevantes …

title: Sarıgül soruşturmasında “itirafçı Emir Sarıgül” iddiası
content:
Gazeteci Fatih Altaylı, Mustafa Sarıgül’ün oğulları Ömer ve Emir Sarıgül’ün de aralarında bulunduğu kişilere yönelik mal varlığını aklama soruşturmasıyla ilgili yargı ve iş dünyasında konuşulduğunu belirttiği bir iddiayı köşesine taşıdı. Altaylı, soruşturmanın derinleşmesini sağladığı öne sürülen bir itirafçının bulunduğunu ve bu kişinin Emir Sarıgül olduğu iddiasının gündeme geldiğini yazdı.

Altaylı, iddiayı doğrulanmış bir bilgi olarak değil, kulislerde konuşulanlar üzerinden aktardı. Yazısında, Emir Sarıgül’ün sorgusu sırasında ailesinin mali ilişkileri hakkında ayrıntılı bilgiler verdiğinin öne sürüldüğünü belirtti. İddiaya göre bu bilgilerin soruşturmayı yürüten savcıların işini kolaylaştırdığı ileri sürülüyor. Altaylı, söz konusu bilgilerin neden paylaşılmış olabileceğine ilişkin yorumların da Emir Sarıgül’ün babasına tepki duyduğu iddiasına dayandırıldığını aktardı.

Altaylı, yazısında soruşturmanın Almanya bağlantılı şirketler ve Titanic otellerinin sahiplerine kadar uzandığı yönündeki iddialara da yer verdi. Soruşturmaya yeni isimlerin dahil olabileceğini öne sürdü.

İstanbul Cumhuriyet Başsavcılığı'nın açıklamasına göre soruşturma, Alman vatandaşları K.P. ve M.B.’nin yurt içinde ve dışında kurulan şirketler aracılığıyla kaynağı belirsiz yüksek miktarda paranın aklandığı iddiasıyla yaptığı başvurular üzerine başlatıldı.

Başsavcılık açıklamasında müştekilerin; 80 milyon avroluk sözleşme düzenlendiği, 100 milyon avroluk havale gerçekleştirildiği, 1 milyar avroluk fonun kamu gücü ve nüfuzu kullanılarak kredi yoluyla yurt dışına çıkarılmasının vaat edildiği ve 1,5 milyon avroluk tekne satışı yapıldığı yönünde iddialarda bulunduğu belirtildi.

Müştekilerin, konuya ilişkin bilgi ve belgeleri gazeteci Murat Ağırel’e ilettiği, belgelerin ilgili kişilere aktarılmasının ardından tehdit edildiklerini öne sürdükleri de savcılık açıklamasında yer aldı.

Açıklamada, müşteki ifadeleri, sunulan ses ve görüntü kayıtları ile soruşturma kapsamında elde edilen delillerin birlikte değerlendirilmesi sonucunda Emir Sarıgül, Ömer Sarıgül, Aylin Kotil, Volkan Aslanbaş, Cavidan Tanrah Artuner ve Murat Ağırel hakkında gözaltı kararı verildiği bildirildi. Mustafa Sarıgül hakkındaki iddiaların ise ayrı değerlendirilmek üzere Ankara Cumhuriyet Başsavcılığı'na gönderileceği kaydedildi.

Soruşturmanın ilk aşamasında gözaltına alınan kişilerden adliyeye sevk edilen 17 kişinin 15’i tutuklandı; Cemil Vasken Barın ile Uğur Kurtulan adli kontrol şartıyla serbest bırakıldı. Emir Sarıgül de 21 Ekim’de çıkarıldığı sulh ceza hâkimliğince tutuklandı.

Soruşturmanın sonraki aşamalarında da yeni gözaltı ve tutuklamalar gerçekleşti. Beşir Ömer Demir, Çağlar Sezgin, Cihan Tunç, Atakan Eren ve Ümit İlker Avcı’nın gözaltına alındığı operasyonda Cihan Tunç, Ümit İlker Avcı ve Çağlar Sezgin tutuklandı; Demir ve Eren hakkında adli kontrol kararı verildi.

Bir başka operasyon kapsamında gözaltına alınan 15 kişiden üçü tutuklandı. Tutuklananlar arasında Sofu Altınbaş, Ramazan Argün ve İbrahim Avcı da yer aldı.

Fatih Altaylı’nın yazısında yer verdiği Emir Sarıgül’ün itirafçı olduğu iddiasına ilişkin ise savcılık tarafından kamuoyuna açıklanmış bir doğrulama bulunmuyor. Soruşturma sürüyor.

31 yıldır emeğin sesi olan Evrensel, gücünü sadece okurlarından alıyor. Emeğin sesinin daha gür çıkması için sen de güç ver.

title: “Soffia il vento dei ’20!” Torino, Campus Einaudi occupato
content:
Pubblichiamo la piattaforma di rivendicazioni uscita dall’

Assemblea di CPS – Culture, Politica e Società

 del campus Einaudi di Torino che da ieri è stato occupato a seguito di una partecipatissima assemblea generale universitaria e della contestazione all’inaugurazione dell’anno accademico al quale era stato invitato un noto sionista, Maurizio Massari. Studenti e studentesse universitarie dichiarano di voler rimanere in occupazione sino a quando le richieste non saranno accolte. Inoltre, viene diramato un appello volto a diffondere una mobilitazione universitaria permanente e a seguire l’iniziativa in tutte le università.


L’assemblea studentesca del Campus Einaudi dichiara il polo occupato, avanzando le seguenti rivendicazioni:


Al Governo chiediamo:


La sottrazione dell’Italia dall’accordo firmato con la NATO nel quale si impegna a raggiungere un investimento pari al 5% del PIL nel comparto della difesa entro il 2035 e la sottrazione dal piano ReArm Europe.


Reinvestimento dei suddetti fondi destinati al bellico in istruzione, ricerca e sanità.


Il ripristino del taglio delle accise sui carburanti di 24,4 centesimi complessivi.


Il congelamento degli affitti, il blocco degli sfratti, l’impossibilità di commutare i contratti di locazione da lungo a breve termine.


La modifica del Codice degli appalti, affinché ci sia una progressiva internalizzazione dellз lavoratorз, a partire dalle università.


Un maggiore investimento nel Fondo di Finanziamento Universitario.


Al Ministero dell’Università e della Ricerca chiediamo:


Che il 96% dei 33mila studentati costruiti coi fondi PNRR, attualmente in mano ai privati, vengano posti sotto l’ente pubblico, uscendo dal circuito del mercato immobiliare. Chiediamo inoltre che vengano resi disponibili gli altri 27mila posti letto promessi dal PNRR e non ancora realizzati.


La modifica dei criteri di premialità nella distribuzione dei finanziamenti all’Università. 


Ad Edisu e alla Regione Piemonte chiediamo: 


Che i criteri di vivibilità standard all’interno dei posti letto che Edisu prende in concessione dalle strutture private vengano rispettati.


Lo stanziamento di un fondo specifico per il premio di laurea, affinché non venga ricavato da avanzi di altre erogazioni.


Che i rinunciatari al posto letto possano accedere alla borsa di studio da fuori sede caricando il contratto di locazione.


All’Università degli Studi di Torino chiediamo:


Trasparenza nella vigilanza dell’accordo tra Confindustria e UniTO affinché vengano rispettate le clausole dell’Osservatorio sulla consapevolezza dei Rischi d’uso nelle Attività universitarie (ORA).


La rescissione di tutte le collaborazioni e accordi con le aziende belliche (Thales Alenia Space e Leonardo). 


Una presa di posizione contro i tagli al Fondo di Finanziamento Ordinario, facendo pressione su MUR e CRUI (Conferenza Rettori Universitari Italiani).


Che parte dei fondi ottenuti vengano vincolati alla riduzione del precariato universitario, per lз ricercatorз e tecnichз-amministrativз.


L’investimento nell’affitto di aule affinché non venga ridotto il numero di corsi ad accesso libero.


Il rimborso spese per lз tirocinanti curriculari.


APPELLO A TUTTE LE UNIVERSITA’ D’ITALIA


Da ieri martedì 27 ottobre, il Campus Luigi Einaudi è dichiarato occupato.

Le lezioni saranno sospese, ma verranno organizzati laboratori, conferenze, seminari, discussioni e lezioni alternative insieme a precari e docenti. L’obiettivo è duplice: evidenziare problematiche dando risposte politiche e favorire un processo di formazione collettiva attraverso lo strumento dell’occupazione.


Due assemblee, partecipate da centinaia di persone, hanno portato alla conclusione che è necessario, come studenti e studentesse dell’università di Torino, dare un segnale chiaro a cui tutte e tutti sono invitati e tenuti a partecipare.


Nel corso delle ultime settimane l’Italia e l’Europa sono state scosse da fortissime mobilitazioni popolari e giovanili. Dalla Francia alla Grecia, studenti e studentesse, universitari e universitarie, giovani delle periferie, sono usciti dalla letargia nella quale i governi li avrebbero preferiti, e hanno espresso il loro potere. Nelle scuole, nelle università, nelle piazze.


A Torino più di 30 scuole sono state occupate e cortei da migliaia di persone hanno attraversato, con determinazione, le strade della città. I lavoratori, dall’ex ILVA ai porti, si mobilitano verso la convergenza del 30 ottobre. Adesso tocca a …
